##### shared/utils/agentTypes.ts
“Agent Types - Types and converters for the AI pricing agent The "Agent" format is a simplified, AI-friendly format used by the pricing agent. It uses string literals like "single_use" instead of enums, making it easier for LLMs to generate and for users to read. This module provides: - TypeScript interfaces for the agent format - Converters: AgentFeature ↔ Feature, AgentProduct ↔ ProductV2”

“============ INTERFACES ============”
Type AgentFeatureType: one of "static", "boolean", "single_use", "continuous_use", "credit_system", or "ai_credit_system".

Type AgentFeature: ID, name (optional), type, display (optional), credit schema (optional), and model markups (optional) (+2 more).
Type AgentProductItem: feature ID (optional), included usage (optional), interval (optional), price (optional), tiers (optional), and usage model (optional) (+1 more).
Type AgentFreeTrial: length, duration, unique fingerprint (optional), and card required (optional).
Type AgentProduct: ID, name, is add on (optional), is default (optional), group (optional), and items (optional) (+1 more).
Type AgentPricingConfig: features and products.

“============ AGENT → SHARED CONVERTERS ============”
To map agent type to feature type — given agent type; gives back a FeatureType:
  Depending on agent type:
    • If it is "boolean" or "static":
      Give back feature type's boolean.
    • If it is "credit_system":
      Give back feature type's credit system.
    • If it is "ai_credit_system":
      Give back feature type's ai credit system.
    • For anything else:
      Give back feature type's metered.

To map agent type to usage type — given agent type; gives back a FeatureUsageType (or nothing):
  Depending on agent type:
    • If it is "single_use":
      Give back feature usage type's single.
    • If it is "continuous_use":
      Give back feature usage type's continuous.
    • For anything else:
      Give back nothing.

“Convert AgentFeature → Feature (shared DB type)”
Agent feature → feature — given agent feature; gives back a Feature:
  Map agent type to usage type (agent feature's type) → usage type.
  Let config be an empty object.
  If usage type is set, set config's usage type to usage type.
  If agent feature's credit schema is set:
    Set config's schema to agent feature's credit schema, each passed through API credit schema item to DB.
  If agent feature's type is "credit_system", set config's usage type to feature usage type's single.
  If agent feature's type is "ai_credit_system", copy everything from build ai credit system config into config.
  Give back an object with:
    • internal ID: agent feature's ID
    • org ID: ""
    • created at: the current time
    • env: app env's sandbox
    • ID: agent feature's ID
    • name: agent feature's name, or agent feature's display's plural if that's missing, or agent feature's ID if that's missing
    • type: map agent type to feature type (agent feature's type)
    • config: config if the keys of config is not empty (otherwise nothing)
    • display: agent feature's display, or nothing if that's missing
    • archived: false
    • event names: an empty list
    • model markups: agent feature's model markups, or nothing if that's missing

“Convert AgentProductItem → ProductItem (shared DB type)”
Agent item → product item — given item; gives back a ProductItem:
  Give back an object with:
    • feature ID: item's feature ID, or nothing if that's missing
    • included usage: depending on whether item's included usage is "inf":
      • if so: infinite
      • if not: item's included usage, or nothing if that's missing
    • interval: item's interval
    • price: item's price, or nothing if that's missing
    • billing units: item's billing units, or nothing if that's missing
    • usage model: item's usage model
    • tiers: item's tiers, with each t turned into an object with:
      • to: infinite if t's to is "inf", otherwise t's to
      • amount: t's amount

“Convert AgentProduct → ProductV2 (shared DB type)”
Agent product → product v2 — given product; gives back a ProductV2:
  Give back an object with:
    • internal ID: product's ID
    • ID: product's ID
    • name: product's name
    • description: nothing
    • is add on: product's is add on, or false if that's missing
    • is default: product's is default, or false if that's missing
    • version: 1
    • group: product's group, or nothing if that's missing
    • env: app env's sandbox
    • free trial: nothing
    • items: product's items, each passed through agent item to product item
    • created at: the current time

“============ SHARED → AGENT CONVERTERS ============”
To map feature type to agent type — given feature; gives back an AgentFeatureType:
  If feature's type is ai credit system, give back "ai_credit_system".
  If feature's type is feature type's credit system, give back "credit_system".
  If feature's type is feature type's boolean, give back "boolean".
  If feature's type is feature type's metered:
    Let usage type be feature's config's usage type.
    If usage type is "continuous_use" or usage type is feature usage type's continuous, give back "continuous_use".
    Give back "single_use".
  Give back "static".

“Convert Feature → AgentFeature”
Feature → agent feature — given feature; gives back an AgentFeature:
  Let agent feature be an object with:
    • ID: feature's ID
    • name: feature's name
    • type: map feature type to agent type (feature)
  If feature's display's singular is set or feature's display's plural is set:
    Set agent feature's display to an object with:
      • singular: feature's display's singular, or feature's name if that's missing
      • plural: feature's display's plural, or feature's name if that's missing
  If feature's type is feature type's credit system and feature's config's schema is set:
    Set agent feature's credit schema to feature's config's schema, each passed through DB credit schema item to API.
  If feature's type is ai credit system:
    Set agent feature's model markups to feature's model markups.
    Set agent feature's default markup to feature's config's default markup.
    Set agent feature's provider markups to feature's config's provider markups.
  Give back agent feature.

“Convert ProductItem → AgentProductItem”
Product item → agent item — given item; gives back an AgentProductItem:
  Let agent item be an empty object.
  If item's feature ID is set, set agent item's feature ID to item's feature ID.
  If item's included usage is set and item's included usage is set:
    Set agent item's included usage to "inf" if item's included usage is infinite, otherwise item's included usage.
  If item's interval is set, set agent item's interval to item's interval.
  If item's price is set and item's price is set, set agent item's price to item's price.
  “Copy tiers if present (tiered pricing)”
  If item's tiers is set and item's tiers is not empty:
    Set agent item's tiers to item's tiers, with each t turned into an object with:
      • to: "inf" if t's to is infinite, otherwise t's to
      • amount: t's amount
  If item's usage model is set, set agent item's usage model to item's usage model.
  If item's billing units is set, set agent item's billing units to item's billing units.
  Give back agent item.

“Convert ProductV2 → AgentProduct”
Product v2 → agent product — given product; gives back an AgentProduct:
  Let agent product be an object with ID: product's ID and name: product's name.
  If product is add on, set agent product's is add on to true.
  If product is default, set agent product's is default to true.
  If product's group is set, set agent product's group to product's group.
  If product's items is set and product's items is not empty:
    Set agent product's items to product's items, each passed through product item to agent item.
  If product's free trial is set:
    Set agent product's free trial to an object with:
      • length: the number of product's free trial
      • duration: product's free trial's duration
      • unique fingerprint: product's free trial's unique fingerprint
      • card required: product's free trial's card required
  Give back agent product.

“Convert ProductV2[] and Feature[] → AgentPricingConfig”
To convert to agent config — given products and features; gives back an AgentPricingConfig:
  Give back an object with:
    • features: features, each passed through feature to agent feature
    • products: products, each passed through product v2 to agent product

##### shared/utils/authAccessControl.ts
“Better-auth AccessControl configuration for the organization plugin. This gates better-auth's OWN built-in org endpoints (invite-member, update-member-role, cancel-invitation, etc.). It is ORTHOGONAL to our product scope system in `scopeDefinitions.ts` — scopes gate product routes via `scopeCheckMiddleware`; AC gates better-auth's internal SDK endpoints. Role permissions (for better-auth's own endpoints): - owner     → full access (stock) - admin     → full access except org delete (stock) - developer → no member/invitation management; read-only AC - sales     → no member/invitation management; read-only AC - member    → same as stock better-auth "member" (basically nothing) This file is shared between server (`server/src/utils/auth.ts`) and client (`vite/src/lib/auth-client.ts`) so TypeScript inference on `authClient.organization.inviteMember({ role })` includes our custom role names.”
Create access control (default statements), and call the result ac.

“Developer role: zero permissions on better-auth's internal org endpoints. Developers cannot invite, update, or remove members via better-auth's SDK. Product-level operations (creating API keys, pushing plans etc.) are governed by our own scope system.”
Let developer role be ac's new role:
  • organization: an empty list
  • member: an empty list
  • invitation: an empty list
  • team: an empty list
  • ac: a list of "read"

“Sales role: same as developer for AC purposes. No better-auth org management permissions.”
Let sales role be ac's new role:
  • organization: an empty list
  • member: an empty list
  • invitation: an empty list
  • team: an empty list
  • ac: a list of "read"

“All roles, keyed by role name. The stock `owner`, `admin`, and `member` are re-exported from better-auth so we have a single source of truth when configuring the plugin.”
Let roles be an object with:
  • owner: owner ac
  • admin: admin ac
  • developer: developer role
  • sales: sales role
  • member: member ac

##### shared/utils/chatState.ts
Let chat install state schema be a schema for an object with provider, org ID, user ID, env, mode, and scopes (+2 more).
Type ChatInstallState: a z.infer.

To encode — given value:
  Give back the from value as JSON [Buffer] as text.

To sign — given payload and secret:
  Give back update create crypto hmac ("sha256" and secret) (payload)'s digest ("base64url").

To create chat install state — given secret and the rest as state:
  Encode (state), and call the result payload.
  Give back "{payload}.{sign (payload and secret)}".

To verify chat install state — given state and secret:
  Split state split on "." into payload and signature.
  If payload is missing or signature is missing, give back nothing.
  Let expected be the from sign (payload and secret) [Buffer].
  Let actual be the from signature [Buffer].
  If any of these is true:
    • the number of expected is not the number of actual
    • crypto's timing safe equal (expected and actual) gives back nothing
  then:
    Give back nothing.
  Try the following:
    Parse chat install state schema (the from payload and "base64url" [Buffer] as text parsed from JSON), and call the result parsed.
    Give back parsed if parsed's expires at is future, otherwise nothing.
  If anything fails:
    Give back nothing.

##### shared/utils/cursorUtils.ts
“Decoded cursor with verbose property names for code readability”
Type DecodedCursorV1: timestamp and ID.

“Encodes cursor into compact base64url string Format: version|timestamp|id (e.g., "1|1764746499167|evt_xxx") Uses pipe-delimited format for optimal performance and 25% size reduction vs JSON Uses base64url encoding for URL safety”
To encode cursor — given timestamp and ID; gives back text:
  Let raw be "1|{timestamp}|{ID}".
  Give back the from raw [Buffer] as text.

“Decodes base64url cursor string to extract timestamp and ID Expects format: version|timestamp|id”
To decode cursor — given cursor string; gives back a DecodedCursorV1:
  Try the following:
    Let decoded be the from cursor string and "base64url" [Buffer] as text.
    Let parts be decoded split on "|".
    If the number of parts is not 3, fail with an error: "Invalid cursor structure".
    Split parts into version, timestamp, and ID.
    If version is not "1", ID is missing, or timestamp is missing, fail with an error: "Invalid cursor structure".
    Parse int [Number] (timestamp and 10), and call the result parsed timestamp.
    If parsed timestamp is not a valid number, fail with an error: "Invalid cursor timestamp".
    Give back an object with timestamp: parsed timestamp and ID.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Fail with an error: "Invalid cursor format".

##### shared/utils/displayUtils.ts
To get feature name — given feature, plural, units, and capitalize (default false):
  If feature is missing, give back "".
  Let feature name start as feature's name, or "" if that's empty.
  If feature's display is set:
    Start with no final plural yet.
    “Case 1: If units and nullish plural”
    If plural is set:
      Set final plural to plural.
    Otherwise:
      Set final plural to whether units is not 1.
    If final plural is set:
      Set feature name to feature's display's plural, or feature name if that's empty.
    Otherwise:
      Set feature name to feature's display's singular, or feature name if that's empty.
  If capitalize is true:
    Set feature name to feature name split on " ", after these steps:
      1. Turn each word into the character at 0 in word in uppercase plus word from position 1 onward
      2. Join them with " "
  Give back feature name.

To get feature name with capital — given feature:
  If feature's name is set and feature's name is not empty:
    Give back "{the character at 0 in feature's name in uppercase}{feature's name from position 1 onward}".
  Give back feature's name.

To get singular and plural — given feature and capitalize (default false):
  Give back an object with:
    • singular: get feature name (feature, no plural, and capitalize)
    • plural: get feature name (feature, plural, and capitalize)

Number with commas — given x:
  Format a new intl's number format ("en-US" and maximum fraction digits: 20) (x), and give back the result.

Usage → feature name — given usage and feature:
  Get singular and plural (feature), and take its singular and plural.
  If usage is 1, give back singular.
  Give back whether plural is true.

To get feature invoice description — given feature, usage, billing units (default 1), product name, is prepaid (default false), and from unix:
  Get singular and plural (feature), and take its singular and plural.
  Let usage string be number with commas (usage, rounded up).
  Let result start as "".
  If is prepaid, billing units is set, and billing units is more than 1:
    Set result to "{usage string} x {billing units} {plural}".
  Otherwise:
    If usage is 1:
      Set result to "{usage string} {singular}".
    Otherwise:
      Set result to "{usage string} {plural}".
  If product name is set, set result to "{product name} - {result}".
  If from unix is set, set result to "{result} (from {format (from unix and "d MMM yyyy")})".
  Give back result.

  Give back context, but with:
    • expand set to all results, combined, of turning each entry in the expand into:
      For each current prefix in prefixes:
        If entry is current prefix, give back a list of "".
        If entry starts with "{current prefix}.":
          Give back a list of entry from position the number of current prefix plus 1 onward.
      Give back an empty list.

To filter plan and feature expand — given expand and target; gives back a T:
  Expand includes, and call the result expand balance feature:
    • expand
    • includes: a list of customer expand's balances feature and check expand's balance feature

      Set target's balances' entry for feature ID's feature to nothing.
  Expand includes (expand and includes: a list of customer expand's subscriptions plan), and call the result expand subscription plan.
  If expand subscription plan is missing and target's subscriptions is set:
    For each position i in target's subscriptions:
      Set target's subscriptions' entry for i's plan to nothing.
  Expand includes (expand and includes: a list of customer expand's purchases plan), and call the result expand scheduled subscription plan.
  If expand scheduled subscription plan is missing and target's scheduled subscriptions is set:

      Set target's scheduled subscriptions' entry for i's plan to nothing.
  Give back target.

##### shared/utils/infisical.ts
To init infisical (async):
  Let client ID be the INFISICAL_CLIENT_ID environment variable.
  Let client secret be the INFISICAL_CLIENT_SECRET environment variable.
  Let project ID be the INFISICAL_PROJECT_ID environment variable.
  Let environment be the INFISICAL_ENVIRONMENT environment variable.
  If any of these is true:
    • client ID is missing
    • client secret is missing
    • project ID is missing
    • environment is missing
  then:
    Stop here.
  Fetch, and call the result auth:
    • "https://app.infisical.com/api/v1/auth/universal-auth/login"
    • method: "POST"
    • headers: an object with "Content-Type": "application/json"
    • body: an object with client ID and client secret as JSON
  If auth's ok is missing, fail with an error: "Infisical auth failed: {auth's status}".
  From auth's JSON, take access token.
  Let params be a new URL search params:
    • environment
    • workspace ID: project ID
    • secret path: the INFISICAL_SECRET_PATH environment variable, or "/" if that's missing
    • include imports: "true"
    • recursive: "true"
  Fetch, and call the result secrets:
    • "https://app.infisical.com/api/v3/secrets/raw?{params}"
    • headers: an object with authorization: "Bearer {access token}"
  If secrets' ok is missing, fail with an error: "Infisical secrets failed: {secrets' status}".
  Let body be secrets' JSON.
  Let loaded start as 0.
  For each secret in body's secrets, plus all the secrets across body's imports:
    If process's env's entry for secret's secret key is missing:
      Set process's env's entry for secret's secret key to secret's secret value.
      Increase loaded by 1.
  Log "Infisical loaded {loaded} secrets".

Type IntervalConfig: an object.
Type EntIntervalConfig: an object.
Type BillingAndEntIntervalConfig: an object.

Entitlement interval → value — given interval and interval count:

    • [entitlement interval's minute]: 1

    • [entitlement interval's week]: 1 times 60 times 24 times 7
    • [entitlement interval's month]: 1 times 60 times 24 times 30

    • [entitlement interval's year]: 1 times 60 times 24 times 365

  Let base value be interval to base value's entry for interval.
  Give back base value times interval count, or 1 if that's missing.

    • [billing interval's semi annual]: 180 times 24 times 60 times 60
    • [billing interval's year]: 365 times 24 times 60 times 60
  Give back interval to seconds' entry for interval, or 30 times 24 times 60 times 60 if that's missing.

Entitlement intervals same — given interval a and interval b:
  Let value a be the value of interval a's interval (given interval a's interval count).
  Let value b be the value of interval b's interval (given interval b's interval count).
  Give back whether value a is value b.

Entitlement intervals different — given interval a and interval b:
  Give back whether there is no entitlement intervals same (interval a and interval b).

Billing and entitlement intervals same — given billing interval, billing interval count, entitlement interval, and entitlement interval count:
  If any of these is true:
    • billing interval is billing interval's one off
    • entitlement interval is entitlement interval's lifetime
  then:
    Give back whether all of these are true:

    • billing interval as text is entitlement interval as text
    • billing interval count, or 1 if that's missing is entitlement interval count, or 1 if that's missing

Billing and entitlement intervals different — given params:
  Give back whether there is no billing and entitlement intervals same (params).

##### shared/utils/productDisplayUtils.ts
“Types”
Type DisplayResult: primary text and secondary text (optional).

Type FormatTiersParams: item, currency (optional), amount format options (optional), and use flat amount (optional).

“Helpers”
To get reset interval display — given item; gives back text (or nothing):
  If item's interval is missing, give back nothing.
  Format interval, and give back the result:
    • interval: item's interval
    • interval count: item's interval count, or nothing if that's missing

To get billing interval display — given item; gives back text (or nothing):
  Let interval be the billing interval of item.
  If interval is missing, give back nothing.
  Format interval (interval and interval count: the billing interval count of item), and give back the result.

To get included usage text — given item and feature; gives back text:
  Get feature name (feature and units: item's included usage) → feature name.
  If item's included usage is infinite, give back "Unlimited {feature name}".
  If item's included usage is missing or item's included usage is 0, give back "0 {feature name}".
  Give back "{number with commas (item's included usage)} {feature name}".

Is single use feature? — given feature; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether feature's config's usage type is feature usage type's single.

“Volume-based tiers where pricing is a flat amount per tier band (not per-unit).”
Is volume flat amount item? — given item; gives back true/false:
  If item's tier behavior is not tier behavior's volume based, give back whether false.
  If item's tiers is missing or item's tiers is empty, give back whether false.
  Give back whether all of these are true:
    • every t in item's tiers satisfies: t's amount is 0
    • item's tiers has a t where t's flat amount, or 0 if that's missing is positive

“Tier Formatting”
To format tiers — given item, currency, amount format options, and use flat amount (default false); gives back text (or nothing):
  Let tiers be item's tiers.
  If tiers is missing, give back nothing.
  To format — given amount:
    Format amount (currency, amount, and amount format options), and give back the result.
  To get amount — given tier:
    If use flat amount is true:
      Give back tier's flat amount, or 0 if that's missing.
    Otherwise:
      Give back tier's amount.
  If the number of tiers is 1, Format (get amount (the first of tiers)), and give back the result.
  Get amount (the first of tiers), and call the result first price.
  Get amount (the last of tiers), and call the result last price.
  Give back "{format (first price)} - {format (last price)}".

“Feature Item Display (no pricing, just entitlement)”
To get feature item display — given item, feature, entity feature, and full display (default false); gives back a DisplayResult:
  If feature is missing:
    Give back an object with primary text: item's feature ID, or "Loading..." if that's empty.
  “Boolean features just show the name”
  If feature's type is feature type's boolean, give back an object with primary text: feature's name.
  Get included usage text (item and feature), and call the result primary text.
  “Determine secondary text: per-entity scope + interval. e.g. "per user per month" when entity_feature_id is set, otherwise "per month".”
  Start with no secondary text yet.
  If full display is true:
    Let parts be an empty list.
    If item's entity feature ID is set and entity feature is set:
      Get feature name (feature: entity feature and units: 1), and call the result entity name.
      If entity name is set, add "per {entity name}" to parts.
    Get reset interval display (item) → interval display.
    If interval display is set:
      Add interval display to parts.
    Otherwise, if feature is single use and item's included usage is not infinite:
      Add "one-off" to parts.
    If parts is not empty, set secondary text to parts joined with " ".
  Give back an object with primary text: primary text and secondary text: secondary text.

“Price Item Display (flat price, no feature)”
To get price item display — given item and currency; gives back a DisplayResult:
  Format amount (currency and amount: item's price), and call the result primary text.
  Get billing interval display (item), and call the result secondary text.
  Give back an object with primary text: primary text and secondary text: secondary text.

“Feature + Price Item Display (usage-based pricing)”
To get feature price item display — given feature, item, currency, is main price (default false), amount format options, and full display (default false); gives back a DisplayResult:
  If feature is missing, fail with an error: "Feature {item's feature ID} not found".
  “Build included usage string (e.g., "100 credits")”
  Let included usage be item's included usage.
  Let has included usage mean included usage is set and included usage is positive.
  Get feature name (feature and units: item's included usage), and call the result included feature name.
  Let included usage string start as "".
  If has included usage, set included usage string to "{number with commas (included usage)} {included feature name}".
  Let volume flat amount mean item is volume flat amount.
  “For volume flat-amount items, tier.amount is always 0 — the real price lives in tier.flat_amount, so we must pass useFlatAmount: true.”
  Start with no price string yet.
  If volume flat amount is true:
    Set price string to format tiers, or "" if that's missing:
      • item
      • currency
      • amount format options
      • use flat amount
  Otherwise, if item's tiers is set:
    Set price string to format tiers (item, currency, and amount format options), or "" if that's missing.
  Otherwise:
    Set price string to depending on whether item's price is set:
      • if so: format amount (currency, amount: item's price, and amount format options)
      • if not: ""
  “Build billing unit string (e.g., "credit" or "100 credits")”
  Let billing units be item's billing units, or 1 if that's missing.
  Get feature name (feature and units: billing units), and call the result billing feature name.
  Let per unit string be "{number with commas (billing units)} {billing feature name}" if billing units is more than 1, otherwise billing feature name.
  “Build interval string”
  Let show interval mean is main price or full display is true.
  Let interval string start as "".
  If show interval is true:
    Get billing interval display (item) → interval display.
    If interval display is set:
      Set interval string to interval display.
    Otherwise, if feature is single use:
      Set interval string to "one-off".
  “Format output based on what we have”
  If has included usage:
    If volume flat amount is true:
      Get feature name (feature and units: 2) → feature name.
      Give back an object with:
        • primary text: included usage string
        • secondary text: "then {price string} for {feature name} {interval string}" without surrounding spaces
    Give back an object with:
      • primary text: included usage string
      • secondary text: "then {price string} per {per unit string} {interval string}" without surrounding spaces
  If volume flat amount is true:
    Get feature name (feature and units: 2) → feature name.
    If show interval is true:
      Give back an object with:
        • primary text: price string
        • secondary text: "for {feature name} {interval string}" without surrounding spaces
    Give back an object with:
      • primary text: "{price string} for {feature name}" without surrounding spaces
      • secondary text: nothing
  If show interval is true:
    Give back an object with:
      • primary text: price string
      • secondary text: "per {per unit string} {interval string}" without surrounding spaces
  Give back an object with:
    • primary text: "{price string} per {per unit string}" without surrounding spaces
    • secondary text: nothing

“Main Entry Point”
To get product item display — given item, features, currency (default "usd"), full display (default false), and amount format options; gives back a DisplayResult:
  To find feature:
    Give back the first f in features where f's ID is item's feature ID.
  To find entity feature:
    If item's entity feature ID is set:
      Give back the first f in features where f's ID is item's entity feature ID.
    Otherwise:
      Give back nothing.
  If item is feature:
    Get feature item display, and give back the result:
      • item
      • feature: find feature
      • entity feature: find entity feature
      • full display
  If item is price, Get price item display (item and currency), and give back the result.
  If item is feature price:
    Get feature price item display, and give back the result:
      • item
      • feature: find feature
      • currency
      • full display
      • amount format options
  Give back an object with primary text: "couldn't detect item type" and secondary text: nothing.

##### shared/utils/scopeDefinitions.ts
“Canonical list of resources protected by scopes. Keep `apiKeys` in camelCase — this matches how the resource is referenced throughout the codebase.”
Let resources be a list of:
  • "organisation"
  • "customers"
  • "features"
  • "plans"
  • "rewards"
  • "balances"
  • "billing"
  • "migrations"
  • "analytics"
  • "apiKeys"
  • "platform"

Type ResourceType: (typeof RESOURCES)[number].

“Modern scope actions.”
Type ScopeActionType: one of "read" or "write".

“All resources that support writing — i.e. every resource except analytics. We compute this via a conditional type so that the resulting `ScopeString` union is exact: it contains `${WritableResource}:write` but never `analytics:write`.”
Type WritableResource: an Exclude.

“Meta-scopes: not tied to a specific resource. - `superuser` — internal Autumn-staff scope. Gates admin-dashboard routes (e.g. `/admin/*`). Manually injected on requests where the better-auth session's `user.role === "admin"` (global admin, not org admin) or the session is an impersonation. - `owner` — org owner scope. Gates owner-only destructive actions (e.g. delete organisation, transfer ownership). The `admin` meta-scope does NOT satisfy an `owner` requirement — owner is strictly narrower. - `admin` — universal bypass for product-level scopes. A caller with this scope passes every scope check that does not explicitly require `superuser`, `owner`, or `public` (see {@link checkScopes}). Granted to the org owner/admin roles so they can do anything non-destructive across the product. - `public` — explicit declaration that a route requires NO scopes. When a route declares `scopes: [Scopes.Public]` the scope-check middleware short-circuits regardless of what the caller has (or doesn't have). Used for: - truly unauthenticated endpoints (e.g. checkout links, hosted invoice redirects) where authorisation comes from possession of a URL-embedded token, not from a session/key; - authenticated-but-universally-accessible endpoints (e.g. feedback submission, org feature flags, saved views) where the upstream auth middleware has already validated the session and no per-action gating is desired. Prefer `public` over the old empty-scopes fail-open: declaring it explicitly makes intent visible in the route file and at the call site in the picker. Future work can replace the fail-open with fail-closed on empty scopes without breaking these routes.”
Let meta scopes be a list of "superuser", "owner", "admin", and "public".

Type MetaScope: (typeof META_SCOPES)[number].

“Exact template-literal union of every valid scope string. Includes modern R/W scopes plus the meta-scopes. Intentionally NOT `${ResourceType}:${ScopeActionType}`, because that would erroneously include `"analytics:write"`.”
Type ScopeString: `${ResourceType}:read`, `${WritableResource}:write`, or a MetaScope.

“Namespaced constants for every modern scope string. Use these in handlers and route definitions rather than stringly-typed literals, e.g. `Scopes.Customers.Write`.”
Let scopes be an object with:
  • organisation: an object with read: "organisation:read" and write: "organisation:write"
  • customers: an object with read: "customers:read" and write: "customers:write"
  • features: an object with read: "features:read" and write: "features:write"
  • plans: an object with read: "plans:read" and write: "plans:write"
  • rewards: an object with read: "rewards:read" and write: "rewards:write"
  • balances: an object with read: "balances:read" and write: "balances:write"
  • billing: an object with read: "billing:read" and write: "billing:write"
  • migrations: an object with read: "migrations:read" and write: "migrations:write"
  • analytics: an object with read: "analytics:read"
  • API keys: an object with read: "apiKeys:read" and write: "apiKeys:write"
  • platform: an object with read: "platform:read" and write: "platform:write"
  • superuser: "superuser"
  • owner: "owner"
  • admin: "admin"
  • public: "public"

“Flat list of every modern R/W scope derived from {@link Scopes}. Order is stable: for each resource we emit `:read` then `:write` (when it exists), in the order defined by {@link RESOURCES}.”

Type LegacyScope: (typeof LEGACY_SCOPES)[number].

“Maps legacy CRUDL scopes (and the bare `"apiKeys"` token) onto their modern R/W equivalents. Convention: `create | update | delete` → `:write`, `list` → `:read`. The legacy bare `"apiKeys"` token implied full access, so it maps to `apiKeys:write` (which transitively grants `apiKeys:read` via {@link expandScopes}).”

“Parse a modern R/W scope string into its resource and action parts. Returns `{ resource: null, action: null }` for OpenID scopes, legacy CRUDL scopes, and malformed inputs. Callers that need to handle legacy scopes semantically should normalise them first via {@link LEGACY_SCOPE_ALIASES}.”

“Check if a scope is a meta-scope.”
Is meta scope? — given scope; gives back scope is MetaScope:
  Give back whether scope is in meta scopes.

“Normalise an arbitrary list of granted scopes into a set of known scopes. Steps: 1. Legacy CRUDL scopes are rewritten via {@link LEGACY_SCOPE_ALIASES}. 2. OpenID and unknown scopes are dropped. 3. Meta-scopes expand hierarchically. The hierarchy is: superuser > owner > admin > product-scopes so: - `superuser` in grant → expands to: superuser, owner, admin, and every modern R/W scope - `owner`     in grant → expands to: owner, admin, and every modern R/W scope - `admin`     in grant → expands to: admin, and every modern R/W scope - `public`    in grant → expands to: public (no hierarchy involvement — it's a route-side declaration) Equivalently, satisfaction semantics at the requirement end: - A `superuser` requirement is satisfied ONLY by `superuser`. - An `owner`     requirement is satisfied by `superuser` or `owner`. - An `admin`     requirement is satisfied by `superuser`, `owner`, or `admin`. - A product-scope requirement is satisfied by admin / owner / superuser / the exact scope. This is the single source of truth for the hierarchy — `checkScopes`, `isScopeSubset`, and `makeScopeChecker` all rely on this expansion rather than re-implementing the hierarchy. 4. For every `:write`, the corresponding `:read` is added (write implies read).”
To expand scopes — given scopes; gives back a set of ScopeString:
  Let expanded be an empty set.
  For each raw in scopes:
    Let scope start as raw.
    “Legacy → modern”
    Let modern scope be legacy scope aliases' entry for scope.
    If modern scope is set, set scope to modern scope.
    “Meta-scope hierarchy: superuser > owner > admin. `public` does not participate in the hierarchy — it's a route-side declaration meaning "no scopes required".”
    If scope is meta:
      Add scope to expanded.
      If scope is "superuser":
        Add "owner" to expanded.
        Add "admin" to expanded.
      Otherwise, if scope is "owner":
        Add "admin" to expanded.
      Move on to the next one.
    Skip it if scope is not modern.
    Add scope to expanded.
    “Write implies read”
    If scope ends with ":write":
      Let resource be the first negative the number of ":write" of scope.
      Let read scope be "{resource}:read".
      Add read scope to expanded.
  “`admin` (by itself, or via expansion from owner/superuser) grants every product-scope. This is the product-level catch-all.”
  If "admin" is in expanded:
    For each scope in modern scopes:
      Add scope to expanded.
  Give back expanded.

“Check whether a set of granted scopes satisfies a route's requirement. `granted` may contain legacy scopes; normalisation (and write→read expansion and meta-scope hierarchy expansion) happens internally via {@link expandScopes}. All other behaviour falls out of the expansion in `expandScopes`: superuser > owner > admin > product-scopes. Requirement-side satisfaction is literal `expanded.has(scope)` membership.”

  Let any list be request's any, each passed through normalise required scope.

“Scope checker with memoised expansion. Call this once per auth boundary (request, session load, useScopes hook) and pass the result around instead of re-running `expandScopes` on every check. Semantics are driven entirely by the hierarchy expansion in {@link expandScopes}: - `has("customers:read")` on an admin grant → true (admin expands to every modern product scope). - `has("owner")` on an admin grant → false (admin does NOT grant owner). - `has("owner")` on a superuser grant → true (superuser → owner → admin). - `has("superuser")` on an owner grant → false (owner does NOT grant superuser — superuser is strictly narrower). ##### shared/utils/usageWindowUtils/buildUsageWindowKey.ts

##### shared/utils/usageWindowUtils/getUsageWindowAnchorTimestamp.ts
“Entitlement reset intervals that are a whole multiple of each window interval. An entitlement on one of these only moves its `next_reset_at` on a window boundary, so it phases the window without ever shifting it. Weeks do not divide months or years, so a weekly window only follows a weekly reset.”
Let reset intervals aligned to window be an object with:
  • [entitlement interval's day]: a list of:
    • entitlement interval's day
    • entitlement interval's week
    • entitlement interval's month
    • entitlement interval's quarter
    • entitlement interval's semi annual
    • entitlement interval's year
  • [entitlement interval's week]: a list of entitlement interval's week
  • [entitlement interval's month]: a list of:
    • entitlement interval's month
    • entitlement interval's quarter
    • entitlement interval's semi annual
    • entitlement interval's year
  • [entitlement interval's year]: a list of entitlement interval's year

To reset interval aligns to window — given reset interval and window interval; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether reset interval is in reset intervals aligned to window's entry for window interval, or false if that's missing (only if reset interval is set).

“The timestamp a usage window's bounds align to. The anchor entitlement's `next_reset_at` is used only when its reset interval is a whole multiple of the window's, so the window rolls WITH the entitlement's cycle (and a plan change that restarts the cycle restarts the window). An entitlement that resets more often than the window (daily credits under a monthly cap) would drag the window forward on every reset and zero its counter, so it anchors to its fixed `reset_cycle_anchor` instead, else null (UTC calendar). The pending `billing_cycle_anchor_resets_at` is no anchor for that case: it is cleared when the move lands, which would shift the bounds and zero the count.”
To get usage window anchor timestamp — given anchor customer entitlement and window interval; gives back a number (or nothing):
  If anchor customer entitlement is missing, give back nothing.
  Reset interval aligns to window, and call the result reset aligns to window:
    • reset interval: anchor customer entitlement's entitlement's interval
    • window interval
  If reset aligns to window is set:
    Give back anchor customer entitlement's next reset at, or anchor customer entitlement's customer product's billing cycle anchor resets at if that's missing, or nothing if that's missing.
  Give back anchor customer entitlement's reset cycle anchor, or nothing if that's missing.

##### shared/utils/usageWindowUtils/getUsageWindowBounds.ts
Let lifetime window end be the largest possible number.

          • from: year start

          • interval count: 6
    • If it is entitlement interval's year:
      Give back start of year (from) as a timestamp.
    • For anything else:
      Give back now.

“Current usage-window bounds for an interval. When a billing-cycle `anchor` is given, bounds align to the customer's cycle (so a "daily" cap rolls on their billing time-of-day, not UTC midnight). Without an anchor, falls back to UTC calendar alignment. `lifetime` never resets. Each window spans one interval.”

    If all of these are true:

      • cycle end at is a real number

    then:
      Give back an object with window start at: cycle start at and window end at: cycle end at.
  Start of window (interval and now), and call the result window start at.

##### shared/utils/usageWindowUtils/findUsageWindowAnchor/findUsageWindowAnchor.ts

	customer.

“Finds the usage window's ANCHOR entitlement: a bounds/billing-cycle reference only (counters are customer-scoped rows, never entitlement-owned). It supplies billing-cycle alignment for the window bounds and is stamped on counter rows at creation as provenance. Owner preference: the capped feature's own entitlements first, then (for non-credit features) entitlements of credit systems that contain it. Null when no eligible entitlement exists -- the cap stays enforceable with calendar-aligned bounds.”
To find usage window anchor — given full subject, feature ID, is credit system, in statuses, and scope type (default "customer"); gives back an object with anchor customer entitlement ID and anchor customer entitlement (optional):
  Let own entitlements be the customer entitlements of full subject (given feature IDs: a list of feature ID and in statuses).
  Let funding entitlements be depending on whether is credit system:
    • if so: an empty list
    • if not: the customer entitlements of full subject (given funds feature ID: feature ID and in statuses), keeping only those where customer entitlement's entitlement's feature's ID is not feature ID
  For each candidate entitlements in a list of own entitlements and funding entitlements:
    Skip it if candidate entitlements is empty.
    Pick anchor customer entitlement ID → anchor customer entitlement ID:
      • candidates: candidate entitlements, each passed through to anchor candidate
      • scope type
    If anchor customer entitlement ID is set:
      Give back an object with:
        • anchor customer entitlement ID
        • anchor customer entitlement: the first customer entitlement in candidate entitlements where customer entitlement's ID is anchor customer entitlement ID
  Give back an object with anchor customer entitlement ID: nothing.

##### shared/utils/usageWindowUtils/findUsageWindowAnchor/pickAnchorCustomerEntitlementId.ts
“A candidate customer entitlement for owning a usage-window counter, reduced to just the fields the canonical pick depends on. Deliberately decoupled from the deduction set and its ordering so the chosen anchor is stable regardless of deduction order, filters, or reverse_deduction_order.”
Type AnchorCandidate: an object.

“Deterministically picks the single customer entitlement that owns a usage window, so one logical counter is never split across entitlements. Customer-scope counters must live on a customer-level entitlement (returns null if only entity-scoped ones exist, so the caller can fail closed rather than split the cap per entity). Entity-scope prefers an entity-owned one.”
To pick anchor customer entitlement ID — given candidates and scope type; gives back text (or nothing):
  Start with no eligible yet.
  If scope type is "customer":
    Set eligible to candidates, keeping only those where candidate is not entity scoped.
  Otherwise:
    Let entity scoped be candidates, keeping only those where candidate is entity scoped.
    Set eligible to entity scoped if entity scoped is not empty, otherwise candidates.
  If eligible is empty, give back nothing.
  Let sorted be a copy of eligible, sorted by this rule:
    If a's status rank is not b's status rank, give back a's status rank minus b's status rank.
    If a's is plan backed is not b's is plan backed, give back negative 1 if a is plan backed, otherwise 1.
    If a's is add on is not b's is add on, give back 1 if a is add on, otherwise negative 1.
    If a's created at is not b's created at, give back a's created at minus b's created at.
    Give back negative 1 if a's ID is less than b's ID, otherwise 1.
  Give back the first of sorted's ID.

##### shared/utils/usageWindowUtils/convertUsageWindow/getUsageWindowDimension.ts
“Which dimension a usage limit on `feature` counts against: - any credit-system feature (classic or AI token-based) caps the credit POOL (`balance` dimension, counted in credits drained); - any other feature caps that feature's own usage (`metered_feature` dimension, counted in tracked units).”
To get usage window dimension — given feature; gives back an object with dimension type and dimension feature ID:
  Let is credit system mean feature's type is any credit system.
  Give back an object with:
    • dimension type: "balance" if is credit system, otherwise "metered_feature"
    • dimension feature ID: nothing if is credit system; otherwise feature's ID

##### shared/utils/usageWindowUtils/convertUsageWindow/usageLimitToUsageWindowLimit.ts
“Non-null = the cap is the entity's own: its counter is entity-scoped.”
Type UsageWindowEntityScope: an object.

“Resolves one stored usage-limit entry into the enforceable UsageWindowLimit handed to the deduction script. The entry's ResetInterval converts to the internal EntInterval here -- the single edge between the API/storage vocabulary and the window internals. Under `anchor: 'billing_cycle'` bounds align to the anchor entitlement's cycle when one exists, else UTC calendar; `anchor: 'utc'` skips the lookup and always uses the UTC calendar.”
Usage limit → usage window limit — given full subject, usage limit, feature, now, in statuses, and entity scope (default nothing); gives back an UsageWindowLimit (or nothing):
  “No catalog internal_id => unstorable counter row (NOT NULL FK); the cap is unenforceable, so skip it.”
  If feature's internal ID is missing, give back nothing.
  Reset intv to entitlement intv (reset intv: usage limit's interval), and call the result interval.
  If interval is missing, give back nothing.
  Get usage window dimension (feature), and take its dimension type and dimension feature ID.
  Let scope type be "entity" if entity scope is set, otherwise "customer".
  Let anchor mode be usage limit's anchor, or "billing_cycle" if that's missing.
  From depending on whether anchor mode is "utc", take anchor customer entitlement ID and anchor customer entitlement:
    • if so: an object with:
      • anchor customer entitlement ID: nothing
      • anchor customer entitlement: nothing
    • if not: find usage window anchor:
      • full subject
      • feature ID: feature's ID
      • is credit system: whether dimension type is "balance"
      • in statuses
      • scope type
  Get usage window bounds, and take its window start at and window end at:
    • interval
    • now
    • anchor: get usage window anchor timestamp (anchor customer entitlement and window interval: interval)
  Let filter key be an usage limit filter key (usage limit's filter).
  Give back an object with:
    • feature ID: feature's ID
    • internal feature ID: feature's internal ID
    • internal customer ID: full subject's customer's internal ID
    • key: build usage window key:
      • scope type
      • internal entity ID: entity scope's internal entity ID, or nothing if that's missing
      • dimension type
      • dimension feature ID
      • interval
      • window start at
      • filter key
    • dimension type: dimension type
    • dimension feature ID: dimension feature ID
    • scope type: scope type
    • entity ID: entity scope's entity ID, or nothing if that's missing
    • internal entity ID: entity scope's internal entity ID, or nothing if that's missing
    • filter key: filter key, or nothing if that's empty
    • filter properties: usage limit's filter's properties, or nothing if that's missing
    • interval
    • window start at: window start at
    • window end at: window end at
    • limit: usage limit's limit
    • anchor customer entitlement ID: anchor customer entitlement ID
    • anchor mode: anchor mode

##### shared/utils/usageWindowUtils/convertUsageWindow/usageWindowLimitToWebhookBlock.ts

Is usage limit interval? — given interval; gives back interval is UsageLimitInterval:

    • window end at: limit's window end at

##### shared/utils/usageWindowUtils/convertUsageWindow/usageWindowsToRolls.ts
“Decides, per counter row, whether it needs rolling. A count is only valid within the window stamped on it (isSameUsageWindow); the anchor is provenance, so an anchor-only re-point keeps the count: expired | window moved | anchor moved | result --------+--------------+--------------+--------------------------------- no      | no           | no           | no roll (the common case) no      | no           | yes          | re-point anchor, count kept no      | drifted      | any          | re-bound, count kept (isSameUsageWindow) no      | yes          | any          | re-bound, count zeroed (plan change) yes     | any          | any          | re-bound, count zeroed (period over) yes     | (no limit)   | --           | bounds kept, count zeroed (entity rows, v1) "Window moved" compares the row's bounds against its limit's CURRENT derivation (anchor ent's cycle). Entity-scoped rows have no resolvable limit in v1, so their bounds can't re-derive -- but an expired count must still zero.”
Usage windows → rolls — given usage windows, limits, and now; gives back a list of UsageWindowRoll:
  Let rolls be an empty list.
  For each usage window in usage windows:
    Let expired mean usage window's window end at as a number is at or before now.
    Find usage window limit by window (limits and usage window), and call the result limit.
    Let target be depending on whether limit is set:
      • if so: an object with:
        • window start at: limit's window start at
        • window end at: limit's window end at
        • anchor customer entitlement ID: limit's anchor customer entitlement ID
      • if not: an object with:
        • window start at: usage window's window start at as a number
        • window end at: usage window's window end at as a number
        • anchor customer entitlement ID: usage window's anchor customer entitlement ID, or nothing if that's missing
    Let bounds changed mean any of these is true:
      • usage window's window start at as a number is not target's window start at
      • usage window's window end at as a number is not target's window end at
    Let window moved mean usage window is not same (given window: target).
    Let anchor moved mean usage window's anchor customer entitlement ID, or nothing if that's missing is not target's anchor customer entitlement ID.
    Skip it if expired is false, bounds changed is false, and anchor moved is false.
    Add an object with to rolls:
      • ID: usage window's ID
      • feature ID: usage window's feature ID
      • internal entity ID: usage window's internal entity ID, or nothing if that's missing
      • filter key: usage window's filter key, or nothing if that's missing
      • zero usage: whether expired is true or window moved is true
      • everything in target
  Give back rolls.

##### shared/utils/usageWindowUtils/classifyUsageWindow/isSameUsageWindow.ts
“Stripe stamps a subscription's anchor seconds after we stamp its product's start, so one cycle's recomputed bounds can drift by that much.”
Let usage window bound tolerance ms be 30,000.

Type UsageWindowBounds: an object.

“Whether a counter row still counts in a window: its bounds match, but for that recomputation drift.”
Is same usage window? — given usage window and window; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether all of these are true:
    • the absolute value of usage window's window start at as a number minus window's window start at is at or before usage window bound tolerance ms
    • the absolute value of usage window's window end at as a number minus window's window end at is at or before usage window bound tolerance ms

##### shared/utils/usageWindowUtils/classifyUsageWindow/usageWindowMatchesLimit.ts
“Whether a counter row and a resolved limit describe the same counter: same feature (by internal id when both carry one), same scope (null entity = customer scope), same filter identity (null/'' both mean the unfiltered aggregate counter).”
Usage window matches limit — given usage window and limit; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether all of these are true:
    • depending on whether usage window's internal feature ID is set and limit's internal feature ID is set is set:
      • if so: whether usage window's internal feature ID is limit's internal feature ID
      • if not: whether usage window's feature ID is limit's feature ID
    • usage window's internal entity ID, or nothing if that's missing is limit's internal entity ID
    • usage window's filter key, or "" if that's empty is limit's filter key, or "" if that's empty

Let options by type be a lookup table built from Stripe tax ID options, each turned into a list of "{option's country code}:{option's type}" and option.

“Resolves a stored Stripe tax id back to its picker option, if the country is known.”
To find Stripe tax ID option — given type and country code; gives back a StripeTaxIdOption (or nothing):
  If country code is set:
    Let exact be options by type's entry for "{country code in uppercase}:{type}".
    If exact is set, give back exact.
  Give back the first option in Stripe tax ID options where option's type is type.

##### shared/utils/stripeUtils/classifyStripeResource/isPreviewStripeId.ts
Let preview Stripe price ID prefix be "price_PREVIEW_".
Let preview Stripe product ID prefix be "prod_PREVIEW_".

Is preview Stripe ID? — given Stripe ID:
  Give back whether any of these is true:
    • Stripe ID starts with preview Stripe price ID prefix
    • Stripe ID starts with preview Stripe product ID prefix

##### shared/utils/rewardUtils/promoCodeUtils.ts
Let alphanumeric regex be /^[a-zA-Z0-9]+$/.
Let max promo code length be 500.

To get global max redemption — given promo code:
  Give back promo code's global max redemption, or promo code's max redemptions if that's missing.

To normalize promo codes — given promo codes; gives back a list of PromoCode:
  Let normalized be promo codes, after these steps:
    1. Keep only those where promo code's code is not empty

      Let global max redemption be global max redemption, or max redemptions if that's missing.

        • everything in promo code

          • if so: an object with global max redemption: global max redemption
          • if not: an empty object
  For each promo code in normalized:
    If promo code's code does not match alphanumeric regex:
      Fail with an error: "Promotional code can only contain letters and numbers (a-z, A-Z, 0-9)" [error code's invalid reward].
    If the number of promo code's code is more than max promo code length:
      Fail with an error: "Promotional code cannot exceed 500 characters" [error code's invalid reward].
    If all of these are true:
      • promo code's global max redemption is set
      • any of these is true:
        • promo code's global max redemption is not a whole number
        • promo code's global max redemption is less than 1
    then:
      Fail with an error: "Max redemptions must be a positive whole number" [error code's invalid reward].
  Give back normalized.

    If candidate is not usage, give back whether false.
    Let new config be candidate's config.
    “Match by feature”
    If new config's feature ID is not old config's feature ID, give back whether false.
    If new config's internal feature ID is not old config's internal feature ID, give back whether false.
    “Match by billing behavior”
    Get billing type (new config), and call the result new biling type.
    Get billing type (old config), and call the result old biling type.
    If new biling type is not old biling type, give back whether false.
    “Optionally match by tier structure”
    If there is no tiers match (old config's usage tiers and new config's usage tiers), give back whether false.
    Give back whether true.

“Main matching function with type-specific logic”
To find best match — given old price and new prices; gives back a Price (or nothing):
  “First, filter by basic characteristics”
  Let candidates be new prices, keeping only those where all of these are true:
    • new price's config's type is old price's config's type
    • new price's config's interval is old price's config's interval
    • new price's config's interval count is old price's config's interval count
  If candidates is empty, give back nothing.
  If the number of candidates is 1, give back the first of candidates.
  “If multiple candidates, use type-specific matching”
  If old price is fixed price:
    Find matching fixed price (old price and candidates), and give back the result.
  Otherwise, if old price is usage:
    Find matching usage price (old price and candidates), and give back the result.
  “Fallback to first candidate”
  Give back the first of candidates.

Type RewardMigrationResult: will migrate count and will not migrate count.
Type RewardPriceAnalysisResult: valid price count and invalid price count.

  Let will migrate count start as 0.
  Let will not migrate count start as 0.
  “Filter rewards to only those we care about and that have discount configs with price_ids”

    • reward's type is in reward types to check
    • reward's discount config's price IDs is set
    • reward's discount config's price IDs is not empty
  For each reward in relevant rewards:
    Skip it if reward's discount config's price IDs is missing.
    For each price ID in reward's discount config's price IDs:
      Let old price be the first p in old prices where p's ID is price ID.
      Skip it if old price is missing.
      Find best match (old price and new prices), and call the result matching new price.
      If matching new price is set:
        Increase will migrate count by 1.
      Otherwise:
        Increase will not migrate count by 1.
  Give back an object with will migrate count and will not migrate count.

  Let valid price count start as 0.
  Let invalid price count start as 0.

  “Check each price ID in the reward”

    For each price ID in reward's discount config's price IDs:

        Increase valid price count by 1.
      Otherwise:
        Increase invalid price count by 1.

##### shared/utils/productV2Utils/productItemUtils/convertItemUtils.ts

##### shared/utils/productV2Utils/productItemUtils/sortPlanItems.ts
Let boolean collapse threshold be 5.

“Priority bucket for a plan item within a category group. Lower number = rendered first.”

  If item is feature price, give back 0 if item's usage model is usage model's prepaid, otherwise 1.
  If item is boolean feature, give back 3.
  “Metered feature without pricing (has included_usage or interval)”
  Give back 2.

To compare items — given a and b; gives back a number:
  Get item priority (a), and call the result priority a.
  Get item priority (b), and call the result priority b.
  If priority a is not priority b, give back priority a minus priority b.
  “Within the same priority, group by feature_id so duplicates stay adjacent”
  Let feature a be a's feature ID, or "" if that's missing.
  Let feature b be b's feature ID, or "" if that's missing.
  Give back how feature a compares alphabetically to feature b.

“Sort plan items into a consistent display order: 1. Non-entity items first (no entity_feature_id) 2. Entity-scoped items last, grouped by entity_feature_id Within each group the sub-order is: a. Priced features (prepaid before pay-per-use) b. Metered features without pricing c. Boolean features Items sharing the same feature_id are kept adjacent. Does not mutate the input array.”
To sort plan items — given items; gives back a list of ProductItem:
  Let non entity be an empty list.
  Let entity groups be an empty lookup table.
  For each item in items:
    If item's entity feature ID is set:
      Let group be entity groups' entry for item's entity feature ID.
      Add item to group.
      Record group under item's entity feature ID in entity groups.
    Otherwise:
      Add item to non entity.
  Non entity, sorted using compare items.
  Let sorted entity keys be a copy of entity groups' keys, sorted alphabetically by value.
  Let sorted entity items be an empty list.
  For each key in sorted entity keys:
    Let group be entity groups' entry for key.
    Skip it if group is missing.
    Group, sorted using compare items.
    Add everything in group to sorted entity items.
  Give back non entity, plus sorted entity items.

“Split already-sorted items into those rendered inline and boolean overflow items that should be collapsed behind an accordion. The first `BOOLEAN_COLLAPSE_THRESHOLD` boolean items stay visible; any beyond that are returned in `collapsedBooleanItems`.”
To split boolean items — given items; gives back an object with visible items and collapsed boolean items:
  Let boolean count start as 0.
  Let visible items be an empty list.
  Let collapsed boolean items be an empty list.
  For each item in items:
    If item is boolean feature:
      Increase boolean count by 1.
      If boolean count is at most boolean collapse threshold:
        Add item to visible items.
      Otherwise:
        Add item to collapsed boolean items.
    Otherwise:
      Add item to visible items.
  Give back an object with visible items and collapsed boolean items.

##### shared/utils/productV2Utils/productItemUtils/convertProductItem/planItemIntervals.ts

    • For anything else:

##### shared/utils/productUtils/priceToInvoiceAmount.ts
“Prices an arbitrary quantity against a usage price's tier schedule. This is the single entry point for converting a raw unit count into dollars — it does NOT know whether that count represents included allowance, prepaid purchased units, or paid overage. The caller is responsible for passing the correct quantity for the billing context: - **Included usage** (free allowance): pass the size of the free bucket to find out its monetary value (used internally for proration math). - **Prepaid** (`UsageInAdvance`): pass the quantity the customer is buying upfront. The result is the immediate charge. - **Pay-per-use overage** (`UsageInArrear`): pass only the units consumed *above* any included free allowance — i.e. `totalUsage − includedFree`. Do NOT pass raw total usage here; the caller must subtract the free tier first. optionally `billing_units`. included allowance when called in an overage context.”
To get amount for quantity — given price and quantity:
  Let config be price's config.
  Let billing units be config's billing units, or 1 if that's empty.
  Give back the line amount of tiers (price, overage: quantity, and billing units).

Item → invoice amount — given item, quantity, and overage:
  Let amount start as 0.
  If item is price, set amount to item's price.
  If quantity is set and overage is set:
    Fail with an error: "itemToInvoiceAmount: quantity or overage is required, autumn item: {item's feature ID}".
  Let price be an object with:
    • tier behavior: item's tier behavior
    • config: an object with:
      • usage tiers: item's tiers, or a list of an object with to: infinite and amount: item's price if that's empty
      • billing units: item's billing units, or 1 if that's empty
  If item's usage model is usage model's prepaid:
    Get amount for quantity (price and quantity), and put the result in amount.
  Otherwise:
    Get amount for quantity (price and quantity: overage), and put the result in amount.
  Give back amount.

Price → invoice amount — given price, item, quantity, product quantity, overage, proration, and now:
  “1. If fixed price, just return amount”
  Let amount start as 0.
  If price is set:
    If price is fixed:
      Set amount to price's config's amount times product quantity, or 1 if that's missing.
    Otherwise:
      Let config be price's config.
      Get billing type (config) → billing type.
      If quantity is set and overage is set:
        Fail with an error: "getAmountForPrice: quantity or overage is required, autumn price: {price's ID}".
      If billing type is billing type's usage in advance:
        Get amount for quantity (price and quantity), and put the result in amount.
      Otherwise:
        Get amount for quantity (price and quantity: overage), and put the result in amount.
  Otherwise:
    Set amount to the invoice amount of item (given quantity and overage).
  If proration is set:
    Calculate proration amount, and give back the result:
      • period end: proration's end
      • period start: proration's start
      • now: now, or the current time if that's empty
      • amount
      • allow negative
  Give back amount.

##### shared/utils/productUtils/priceUtils/getPriceForOverage.ts
“Returns the dollar cost for a given overage quantity on a price. "Overage" is the portion of usage that is **not** covered by included free allowance. How it is calculated depends on the billing model: - **Included usage (free tier):** no overage is charged; the free bucket is consumed first and this function is not called for those units. - **Prepaid** (`UsageInAdvance`): the customer purchased units upfront. Overage here is any consumption beyond what was prepaid — typically priced via `tiersToLineAmount` at the end of the period, not this function. - **Pay-per-use** (`UsageInArrear`): overage is `totalUsage − includedFree`. Pass that net quantity as `overage`; this function prices it against the graduated tier schedule. - **Fixed** (`FixedCycle` / `OneOff`): no usage tiers apply; returns the flat `config.amount` regardless of the `overage` argument. Ignored for fixed-price billing types. Must be pre-subtracted by the caller.”
To get price for overage — given price and overage:
  Let usage config be price's config.
  Get billing type (usage config) → billing type.
  If billing type is billing type's fixed cycle or billing type is billing type's one off:
    Let config be price's config.
    Give back config's amount.
  Let billing units be usage config's billing units, or 1 if that's empty.
  Give back the line amount of tiers (price, overage, and billing units).

##### shared/utils/productUtils/priceUtils/convertPrice/priceToStripePrepaidV2Tiers.ts
“Builds the Stripe tier array for a V2 prepaid price. For both graduated and volume prices with an allowance, a free $0 leading tier is inserted and all paid-tier boundaries are shifted up by the allowance. Stripe receives total packs (purchased + allowance) as the quantity. - **Graduated**: Stripe splits charges across tier bands. The free tier covers the included units at $0, so only units above the allowance incur cost. - **Volume**: if total quantity exceeds the free tier, the ENTIRE quantity (including the included portion) is charged at the matching paid tier's rate. This is intentional — volume pricing does not subtract included usage before applying the rate.”
Price → Stripe prepaid v2 tiers — given price, entitlement, org, and currency (as target currency); gives back a list of Stripe.PriceCreateParams.Tier:
  If price is not prepaid, fail with an error: "priceToStripePrepaidV2Tiers requires a prepaid price, got price {price's ID}".
  Let config be price's config.
  Let org default be the currency of org in lowercase.
  Let currency be target currency, or config's base currency if that's missing, or org default if that's missing in lowercase.
  Let usage tiers be a price config for currency (config, currency, and org default)'s usage tiers, or config's usage tiers if that's missing.
  Let tiers be an empty list.
  “Insert a free leading tier and shift paid-tier boundaries up by the allowance. Applies to both graduated and volume pricing.”
  If entitlement's allowance is set, add an object with unit amount decimal: "0" and up to: entitlement's allowance to tiers.
  For each tier in usage tiers:
    Let Autumn unit amount be tier's amount, or 0 if that's missing divided by config's billing units, or 1 if that's missing.
    Let Stripe unit amount decimal be the Stripe amount decimal of Autumn (amount: Autumn unit amount and currency).
    Let up to start as "inf".
    If tier is not final:
      Set up to to depending on whether entitlement's allowance is set:
        • if so: tier's to plus entitlement's allowance
        • if not: tier's to
    Let Stripe tier be an object with unit amount decimal: Stripe unit amount decimal and up to: up to.
    If tier's flat amount is set:
      Set Stripe tier's flat amount decimal to the Stripe amount decimal of Autumn (amount: tier's flat amount and currency).
    Add Stripe tier to tiers.
  “Divide all tiers by billing units”
  Give back tiers, with each tier turned into tier, but with:
    • up to set to depending on whether index is the number of tiers minus 1 or tier's up to is "inf":
      • if so: "inf"
      • if not: tier's up to divided by config's billing units, or 1 if that's missing's ceil
    • unit amount decimal set to tier's unit amount decimal, or 0 if that's missing times config's billing units, or 1 if that's missing as text

##### shared/utils/planV1Utils/diff/applyDiff.ts
Type ApplyDiffOutput: an object.
Type ApiPlanItem: ApiPlanV1["items"][number].
Type ApiPlanItemPrice: a NonNullable.
Type ApiPlanItemRollover: a NonNullable.

To apply price — given base and diff; gives back ApiPlanV1["price"]:
  If diff is missing, give back base.
  If diff is missing, give back nothing.
  Give back an object with everything in diff.

To remove items — given items and remove filters; gives back ApiPlanV1["items"]:
  Give back items, keeping only those where remove filters has no filter where plan item matches filter (given item and filter).

To API plan item price — given price; gives back an ApiPlanItemPrice (or nothing):
  If price is missing, give back nothing.
  Give back price, but with:
    • billing units set to price's billing units, or 1 if that's missing
    • max purchase set to price's max purchase, or nothing if that's missing

To API plan item rollover — given rollover; gives back an ApiPlanItemRollover (or nothing):
  If rollover is missing, give back nothing.
  Give back rollover, but with max set to rollover's max, or nothing if that's missing.

To API plan item — given params; gives back an ApiPlanItem:
  Give back params, but with:
    • included set to params' included, or 0 if that's missing
    • unlimited set to params' unlimited, or false if that's missing
    • reset set to params' reset, or nothing if that's missing
    • price set to a to API plan item price (params' price)
    • rollover set to a to API plan item rollover (params' rollover)

Is free non reset entitlement? — given item; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether item's price is missing and item's reset is missing.

To apply items — given base items and diff; gives back ApiPlanV1["items"]:
  Let items start as a copy of base items.
  If diff's remove items is set, Remove items (items and diff's remove items), and put the result in items.
  If diff's add items is set:
    Let entitlement keys be an empty set.
    For each item in items:
      If item is free non reset entitlement, add compose match key (item) to entitlement keys.
    For each add item in diff's add items:
      Compose match key (add item) → key.
      Skip it if add item is free non reset entitlement and key is in entitlement keys.
      Add a to API plan item (add item) to items.
      If add item is free non reset entitlement, add key to entitlement keys.
  Give back items.

“applyItems in CreatePlanItemParams space — same remove/add semantics, without ApiPlan normalization.”
To apply plan item params diff — given items, add items, and remove items; gives back a list of CreatePlanItemParamsV1:
  Let next start as a copy of items.
  If remove items is set:
    Set next to next, keeping only those where remove items has no filter where plan item matches filter (given item and filter).
  If add items is set:
    Let entitlement keys be the unique values of next, after these steps.
    For each add item in add items:
      If add item is free non reset entitlement:
        Compose match key (add item) → key.
        Skip it if key is in entitlement keys.
        Add key to entitlement keys.
      Add add item to next.
  Give back next.

“applyItems only guards free entitlements; replaying a diff onto a drifted plan can collide priced slots too. First occurrence (the base plan's) wins.”
To dedupe items by match key — given items; gives back ApiPlanV1["items"]:
  Let seen be an empty set.
  Give back items, keeping only the items that pass this check:
    Compose match key (item) → key.
    If key is in seen, give back whether false.
    Add key to seen.
    Give back whether true.

To apply free trial — given base and diff; gives back ApiPlanV1["free_trial"]:
  If diff is missing, give back base.
  If diff is missing, give back nothing.
  Give back an object with everything in diff.

To apply license upsert — given existing and upsert; gives back an ApiPlanLicenseV1:
  Let customize be nothing if upsert's customize is missing; otherwise upsert's customize, or existing's customize if that's missing.
  Give back an object with:
    • license plan ID: upsert's license plan ID
    • version: existing's version, or 1 if that's missing
    • included: upsert's included, or existing's included if that's missing, or 0 if that's missing
    • prepaid only: upsert's prepaid only, or existing's prepaid only if that's missing, or false if that's missing
    • everything in an object with customize if customize is set, otherwise an empty object
    • everything in an object with plan: existing's plan if existing's plan is set, otherwise an empty object

“Only emit `licenses` when the diff has a license lane — content-only round-trips must not grow a licenses key.”
To apply licenses — given base and diff; gives back a list of ApiPlanLicenseV1 (or nothing):
  If diff's upsert licenses is missing and diff's remove licenses is missing, give back nothing.
  Let removed be the unique values of the license plan IDs of diff's remove licenses.
  Let pending be a lookup table built from diff's upsert licenses, each turned into a list of entry's license plan ID and entry.
  Let next be an empty list.
  For each license in base's licenses:
    Skip it if license's license plan ID is in removed.
    Let upsert be pending's entry for license's license plan ID.
    If upsert is set:
      Add apply license upsert (existing: license and upsert) to next.
      Remove license's license plan ID from pending.
      Move on to the next one.
    Add license to next.
  For each upsert in diff's upsert licenses:
    Skip it if upsert's license plan ID is not in pending.
    Add apply license upsert (upsert) to next.
  Give back next.

To apply diff — given base and diff; gives back an ApplyDiffOutput:
  Let output be an object with:
    • price: apply price (base's price and diff's price)
    • items: apply items (base's items and diff)
    • free trial: apply free trial (base's free trial and diff's free trial)
  Apply licenses (base and diff) → licenses.
  If licenses is missing, give back output.
  Give back output, but with licenses set to licenses.

“Public customize (PUT `items` or PATCH add/remove) applied onto a plan.”
To apply customize to plan — given plan and customize; gives back a DiffablePlanV1:
  Apply diff, and call the result applied:
    • base: plan
    • diff: an object with:
      • everything in depending on whether customize's price is set:
        • if so: an object with price: customize's price
        • if not: an empty object
      • everything in depending on whether customize's add items is set:
        • if so: an object with add items: customize's add items
        • if not: an empty object
      • everything in depending on whether customize's remove items is set:
        • if so: an object with remove items: customize's remove items
        • if not: an empty object
      • everything in depending on whether customize's free trial is set:
        • if so: an object with free trial: customize's free trial
        • if not: an empty object
      • everything in depending on whether customize's upsert licenses is set:
        • if so: an object with upsert licenses: customize's upsert licenses
        • if not: an empty object
      • everything in depending on whether customize's remove licenses is set:
        • if so: an object with remove licenses: customize's remove licenses
        • if not: an empty object
  Give back an object with:
    • everything in plan
    • price: applied's price
    • items: depending on whether customize's items is set:
      • if so: customize's items, each passed through to API plan item
      • if not: applied's items
    • free trial: applied's free trial
    • everything in depending on whether applied's licenses is set:
      • if so: an object with licenses: applied's licenses
      • if not: an empty object

##### shared/utils/invoices/invoiceLineItems/logInvoiceLineItems.ts

      Let amount be "${the absolute value of li's amount rounded to 2 decimal places}".
      Log "  │  {branch} [{dir}] {feat}{prorated}  {amount}".

##### shared/utils/intervalUtils/addBillingInterval.ts
“Validate unix timestamp”
To add billing interval — given from unix and interval config:
  From interval config, take interval and interval count (default 1).
  Let from date be a new UTC date (from unix).
  Depending on interval:
    • If it is billing interval's week:
      Give back add weeks (from date and 1 times interval count) as a timestamp.
    • If it is billing interval's month:
      Give back add months (from date and interval count) as a timestamp.
    • If it is billing interval's quarter:
      Give back add months (from date and 3 times interval count) as a timestamp.
    • If it is billing interval's semi annual:
      Give back add months (from date and 6 times interval count) as a timestamp.
    • If it is billing interval's year:
      Give back add years (from date and 1 times interval count) as a timestamp.
    • For anything else:
      Fail with an error: "Invalid billing interval: {interval}".

        • in statuses
