##### shared/utils/featureUtils/creditRates/creditRateToCost.ts
“A rate as either a schema row or a rate card carries it: flat credits per feature amount, or graduated tiers.”
Type CreditRate: { feature_amount?: number } & (
	| { cre.

To get graduated credit cost at usage — given feature ID, credit system ID, schema item, and usage:
  Let feature amount be schema item's feature amount, or 1 if that's missing.
  If feature amount is not a real number or feature amount is zero or less:
    Fail with an invalid credit rate card:
      • feature ID
      • credit system ID
      • message: "Credit rate-card billing units must be greater than zero"
  If schema item's tiers is empty:
    Fail with an invalid credit rate card:
      • feature ID
      • credit system ID
      • message: "Graduated credit rate cards require at least one tier"
  Let bounded usage be the result of max [Decimal] (usage and 0).
  Let previous boundary start as 0.
  Let total cost start as 0.
  For each tier (at position index) in schema item's tiers:
    If tier's credit amount is not a real number or tier's credit amount is negative:
      Fail with an invalid credit rate card:
        • feature ID
        • credit system ID
        • message: "Credit tier costs must be finite and non-negative"
    Let is last tier mean index is the number of schema item's tiers minus 1.
    If tier's to is "inf":
      If is not last tier:
        Fail with an invalid credit rate card:
          • feature ID
          • credit system ID
          • message: "Only the final credit tier may have an infinite boundary"
      Let tier units be the result of max [Decimal] (bounded usage minus previous boundary and 0).
      Give back total cost plus tier units divided by feature amount times tier's credit amount.
    If tier's to is not a real number or tier's to is at most previous boundary:
      Fail with an invalid credit rate card:
        • feature ID
        • credit system ID
        • message: "Credit tier boundaries must be strictly increasing"
    If is last tier:
      Fail with an invalid credit rate card:
        • feature ID
        • credit system ID
        • message: "The final credit tier must have an infinite boundary"
    Let boundary be tier's to.
    Let tier units be the result of max [Decimal]:
      • the result of min [Decimal] (bounded usage and boundary) minus previous boundary
      • 0
    Set total cost to total cost plus tier units divided by feature amount times tier's credit amount.
    Set previous boundary to boundary.
    If bounded usage is at most boundary, give back total cost.
  Fail with an invalid credit rate card:
    • feature ID
    • credit system ID
    • message: "The final credit tier must have an infinite boundary"

“Credits `amount` units cost at this rate, from `currentUsage` on for graduated tiers.”
Credit rate → cost — given feature ID, credit system ID, rate, amount, and current usage:
  If rate's tier behavior is "graduated":
    Get graduated credit cost at usage, and call the result before cost:
      • feature ID
      • credit system ID
      • schema item: rate
      • usage: current usage
    Get graduated credit cost at usage, and call the result after cost:
      • feature ID
      • credit system ID
      • schema item: rate
      • usage: the larger of 0 and current usage plus amount
    Give back after cost minus before cost.
  Give back rate's credit amount divided by rate's feature amount, or 1 if that's missing times amount.

##### shared/utils/featureUtils/creditRates/getCreditRateFundedUnits.ts

  Give back lower bound.

##### shared/utils/cusProductUtils/featureOptionUtils/convertFeatureOptions.ts
“Computes the Stripe subscription-item quantity for a V2 prepaid price. Always returns total packs (purchased + allowance) for both graduated and volume pricing. The V2 Stripe price has a free leading tier that covers the allowance, so Stripe needs the full quantity to bill correctly. For **volume** prices: if total quantity exceeds the free tier, the ENTIRE quantity (including included) is charged at the matching paid tier's rate. This is the intended behavior — volume pricing does not subtract included usage before applying the tier rate.”
Feature options → v2 Stripe quantity — given feature options, price, and entitlement:
  Let packs excluding allowance mean feature options' upcoming quantity, or feature options' quantity if that's missing is set.
  Let allowance in packs be price utils' convert's to allowance in packs (price and entitlement).
  If packs excluding allowance is false, give back allowance in packs.
  Give back packs excluding allowance plus allowance in packs.

##### shared/utils/cusProductUtils/convertCusProduct/cusProductToConvertedFeatureOptions.ts
Usage → converted feature options — given customer product, entitlement, and new price; gives back a FeatureOptions (or nothing):
  Find customer entitlement by feature, and call the result customer entitlement:
    • customer entitlements: customer product's customer entitlements
    • feature: entitlement's feature
  If customer entitlement is missing, give back nothing.
  Let usage be the usage of a list of:
    • customer entitlement, but with customer product set to customer product
  Let new allowance be entitlement's allowance, or 0 if that's missing.
  Let new billing units be new price's config's billing units, or 1 if that's missing.
  Let paid usage be the larger of 0 and usage minus new allowance.
  Round usage to nearest billing unit (usage: paid usage and billing units: new billing units), and call the result rounded paid usage.
  Give back an object with:
    • internal feature ID: entitlement's feature's internal ID
    • feature ID: entitlement's feature's ID
    • quantity: rounded paid usage divided by new billing units

“Converts purchased packs from an old customer product to packs in new billing units. Allowance (included usage) is NOT factored in here — it's handled by getStartingBalance.”
Customer product → converted feature options — given customer product, entitlement, and new price; gives back a FeatureOptions (or nothing):
  Let feature be entitlement's feature.
  Let current option be the feature options of customer product (given feature).
  “if (nullish(currentOption?.quantity)) return undefined;”
  Find prepaid customer price by feature (customer prices: customer product's customer prices and feature), and call the result old customer price.
  “if (!oldCusPrice) return undefined;”
  If current option's quantity is missing or old customer price is missing:
    Give back the converted feature options of usage (customer product, entitlement, and new price).
  Let old customer entitlement be the customer entitlement of old customer price (given customer entitlements: customer product's customer entitlements).
  Let old billing units be old customer price's price's config's billing units, or 1 if that's missing.
  Let new billing units be new price's config's billing units, or 1 if that's missing.
  “1. Multiply by old billing units to get actual quantity”
  Let actual quantity be current option's quantity times old billing units.
  “2. Round to nearest new billing unit”
  Round usage to nearest billing unit (usage: actual quantity and billing units: new billing units), and call the result rounded quantity.
  “3. Add current allowance”
  Let old allowance be old customer entitlement's entitlement's allowance, or 0 if that's missing.
  Let quantity with old allowance be rounded quantity plus old allowance.
  “4. Subtract new allowance”
  Let new allowance be entitlement's allowance, or 0 if that's missing.
  Let quantity without new allowance be the larger of 0 and quantity with old allowance minus new allowance.
  “5. Round to nearest new billing unit”
  Round usage to nearest billing unit, and call the result rounded quantity without new allowance:
    • usage: quantity without new allowance
    • billing units: new billing units
  “3. Divide by new billing units”
  Let converted quantity be rounded quantity without new allowance divided by new billing units.
  “Clamp to 0 minimum - if new allowance exceeds old total, no additional packs needed”
  Let final quantity be the larger of 0 and converted quantity.
  Give back an object with:
    • internal feature ID: feature's internal ID
    • feature ID: feature's ID
    • quantity: final quantity

##### shared/utils/cusEntUtils/sortCusEntsForDeduction.ts

    If all of these are true:
      • customer entitlement filters' customer entitlement IDs is set
      • customer entitlement filters' customer entitlement IDs is not empty
    then:
      Let a in list mean a's ID is in customer entitlement filters' customer entitlement IDs.
      Let b in list mean b's ID is in customer entitlement filters' customer entitlement IDs.
      If a in list is true and b in list is false, give back negative 1.
      If a in list is false and b in list is true, give back 1.
    Let a entitlement be a's entitlement.
    Let b entitlement be b's entitlement.
    “0. Sort customer-level vs entity-level based on tracking context If entityId is provided: entity-level goes first (deduct entity's own resources first) If entityId is null: customer-level goes first (deduct customer resources first)”
    Let a is entity mean a is entity.
    Let b is entity mean b is entity.
    If (a is entity is true) differs from (b is entity is true):

      Otherwise:

    then:
      Give back 1.

      • a entitlement's feature's type is not feature type's credit system
      • b entitlement's feature's type is feature type's credit system

      Give back negative 1.

      • a entitlement's allowance type is allowance type's unlimited
      • b entitlement's allowance type is not allowance type's unlimited
    then:
      Give back negative 1.
    If all of these are true:
      • a entitlement's allowance type is not allowance type's unlimited
      • b entitlement's allowance type is allowance type's unlimited
    then:
      Give back 1.
    “If one has a next_reset_at, it should go first”
    Let next reset first be 1 if reverse order is true, otherwise negative 1.
    If a's next reset at is set and b's next reset at is missing, give back next reset first.
    “If b has a next_reset_at, it should go first”
    If a's next reset at is missing and b's next reset at is set, give back negative next reset first.
    “3. Sort by interval”
    Let a value be the value of a entitlement's interval (given a entitlement's interval count).
    Let b value be the value of b entitlement's interval (given b entitlement's interval count).
    If a entitlement's interval is set, b entitlement's interval is set, and a value is not b value:
      If reverse order is true:

      Otherwise:
        Give back a value minus b value.
    If a's expires at is not b's expires at:

    “0a. If both are entity products (attached to entities), sort by entity_id for consistent ordering”

    Let b is product entity mean b's customer product's internal entity ID is set.
    If a is product entity is true and b is product entity is true:

      Let b entity ID be b's customer product's entity ID.
      If a entity ID is set, b entity ID is set, and a entity ID is not b entity ID:

    “Check if a is main product (add-ons go after main products)”

    If a is add on is missing and b is add on is set, give back negative 1.
    “2.5. Sort by usage_allowed (prepaid goes before pay-per-use) Prepaid (usage_allowed=false) should be deducted first since it can't go negative”

##### shared/utils/cusEntUtils/rolloverUtils/performMaximumClearing.ts
Perform maximum clearing — given rows and customer entitlement:
  Let rollover config be customer entitlement's entitlement's rollover.
  If rollover config is missing, give back an object with to delete: an empty list and to update: an empty list.
  Let effective max be the effective rollover max of customer entitlement.
  If effective max is missing, give back an object with to delete: an empty list and to update: an empty list.
  Rows, sorted by this rule:
    If a expires at and b expires at, give back a's expires at minus b's expires at.
    If a expires at and b does not expire at, give back negative 1.
    If a does not expire at and b expires at, give back 1.
    Give back 0.
  Let entitlement be customer entitlement's entitlement.
  Let entity mode mean entitlement's entity feature ID is set.
  If entity mode is false:
    Let total rollover balance be the total balance across rows.
    Let to deduct start as total rollover balance minus effective max.
    If to deduct is less than 0, give back an object with to delete: an empty list and to update: an empty list.
    Let to update be an empty list.
    Let to delete be an empty list.
    For each row in rows:
      Let current balance be row's balance.
      Let new balance start as current balance.
      If current balance is at least to deduct:
        Set new balance to new balance minus to deduct.
        Set to deduct to 0.
        “Drop fully-drained rows instead of keeping zero-balance zombies.”
        If new balance is zero:
          Add row's ID to to delete.
        Otherwise:
          Add row, but with balance set to new balance to to update.
      Otherwise:
        Set new balance to 0.
        Set to deduct to to deduct minus current balance.
        Add row's ID to to delete.
      Stop the loop if to deduct is at most 0.
    Give back an object with to delete and to update.
  Let entity ID to total be an empty object.
  For each row in rows:
    For each key entity ID in row's entities:
      Set entity ID to total's entry for entity ID to entity ID to total's entry for entity ID, or 0 if that's empty plus row's entities' entry for entity ID's balance.
  Let to update be an empty list.
  Let to delete be an empty list.
  For each row in rows:
    Let update be a deep copy of row.
    Let should update mean false.
    For each key entity ID in entity ID to total:
      Let entity total be entity ID to total's entry for entity ID.
      Let to deduct be entity total minus effective max.
      Skip it if to deduct is at most 0 or row's entities' entry for entity ID is missing.
      Let current balance be row's entities' entry for entity ID's balance.
      Let new balance start as current balance.
      If current balance is at least to deduct:
        Set new balance to new balance minus to deduct.
        “Remaining running total after the full deduction (== effectiveMax), keeping the same invariant as the else-branch below.”
        Set entity ID to total's entry for entity ID to entity total minus to deduct.
        Set should update to true.
        Set update's entities' entry for entity ID to an object with ID: entity ID, balance: new balance, and usage: 0.
      Otherwise:
        Set new balance to 0.
        “Carry the remaining running total (not the residual deduction) so the next row recomputes toDeduct correctly.”
        Set entity ID to total's entry for entity ID to entity total minus current balance.
        Set should update to true.
        Set update's entities' entry for entity ID to an object with ID: entity ID, balance: 0, and usage: 0.
    If every entity in the values in update's entities satisfies: entity's balance is 0:
      Add row's ID to to delete.
    Otherwise, if should update:
      Add update to to update.
  Give back an object with to delete and to update.

##### shared/utils/cusEntUtils/resetUtils/getNextResetAt.ts

##### shared/utils/billingUtils/invoicingUtils/filterUnchangedPricesFromLineItems.ts
“Filters out line item pairs where a refund and charge item have the same price ID and their amounts cancel out (sum to 0).”
To filter unchanged prices from line items — given line items; gives back a list of LineItem:
  “Split by direction”
  Let refund items be line items, keeping only those where item's context's direction is "refund".
  Let charge items be line items, keeping only those where item's context's direction is "charge".
  Let remaining refund items be an empty list.
  Let matched charge indices be an empty set.
  For each refund item in refund items:
    Let refund price ID be refund item's context's price's ID.
    “Find a matching charge item with the same price ID”
    Let matching charge index be the position of the first charge item in charge items where all of these are true (or -1):
      • index is not in matched charge indices
      • charge item's context's price's ID is refund price ID
    If matching charge index is not negative 1:
      Let matching charge item be charge items' entry for matching charge index.
      Let net amount be the absolute value of refund item's amount plus matching charge item's amount.
      If net amount is less than billing amount epsilon:
        Add matching charge index to matched charge indices.
        Move on to the next one.
    “No canceling match found - keep this refund item”
    Add refund item to remaining refund items.
  “Filter out matched charge items”
  Let remaining charge items be charge items, keeping only those where index is not in matched charge indices.
  Give back remaining refund items, plus remaining charge items.

##### shared/utils/billingUtils/invoicingUtils/lineItemUtils/billingLineItemMatchesStripeLineItem.ts

##### shared/utils/billingUtils/invoicingUtils/lineItemUtils/filterBillingLineItemsByStripeLineItem.ts
“Filters ALL matching Autumn LineItems for a Stripe InvoiceLineItem. Used for multi-entity scenarios where one Stripe line item represents charges for multiple customer products. Returns all matches at the highest priority level found: 1. ExactLineItemId (returns single item) 2. CustomerPriceId (can be multiple for multi-entity) 3. StripePriceId (can be multiple for multi-entity) 4. StripeProductId (can be multiple for multi-entity) A metadata match names only one entity's customer price, yet Stripe merges every entity sharing the same Stripe price into one line. Siblings that match this line by stripe_price_id are kept so the merged line is attributed to all of them. Product-level matches are not siblings: per-entity inline prices get their own Stripe line each.”
To filter billing line items by Stripe line item — given Stripe line item, Autumn line items, and subscription item metadata; gives back a list of LineItem:
  “Score each line item”
  Let scored items be Autumn line items, after these steps:
    1. Turn each line item into an object with:
      • line item
      • priority: a billing line item matches Stripe line item (line item, Stripe line item, and subscription item metadata)
    2. Keep only those where item's priority is not line item match priority's no match
  If scored items is empty, give back an empty list.
  “Find the highest priority (lowest number)”
  Let highest priority be the smaller of all of the priorities of scored items.
  Let top matches be scored items, after these steps:
    1. Keep only those where item's priority is highest priority
    2. Take each one's line item
  If highest priority is not line item match priority's customer price ID, give back top matches.
  Let merged price IDs be the unique values of each li's context's price's ID, for each li in top matches.
  Let siblings on same Stripe price be scored items, after these steps:
    1. Keep only those where all of these are true:
      • item's priority is line item match priority's Stripe price ID
      • the ID of item's line item's context's price is in merged price IDs
    2. Take each one's line item
  Give back top matches, plus siblings on same Stripe price.

##### shared/utils/billingUtils/invoicingUtils/lineItemUtils/findBillingLineItemByStripeLineItem.ts

CustomerPriceId (autumn_customer_price_id metadata) 3. StripePriceId (price config) 4. StripeProductId (product processor)”

##### shared/utils/billingUtils/invoicingUtils/lineItemUtils/graduatedTiersToLineAmount.ts
“Core graduated tiered pricing calculation used across all billing contexts: included usage (free allowances), prepaid purchased quantities, and paid overage. Graduated pricing splits usage across tier bands — each band is charged at its own rate. For example, if tier 1 covers 0–100 units at $1 and tier 2 covers 100+ at $0.50, then 150 units costs (100 × $1) + (50 × $0.50) = $125. - **Included usage** (free allowance): pass `usage = includedQuantity`. The result represents the monetary value of the free bucket — used to compute how much of the prepaid charge is "used up" vs remaining. - **Prepaid quantity** (usage_in_advance): pass `usage = quantityPurchased`. The result is what the customer is charged upfront for the units they bought. - **Paid overage** (usage_in_arrear / pay-per-use): pass `usage = overageUnits` (raw usage minus any included or prepaid allowance). The result is the end-of-period charge for units consumed beyond the free/prepaid bucket. quantity for prepaid, overage units for arrear billing, or free-bucket size for included-usage valuation. Must be non-negative unless `allowNegative` is true. for "per 1k tokens"). Defaults to 1. value and the result is negated. Used for downgrade credits / proration refunds. Defaults to false.”
Graduated tiers → line amount — given tiers, usage, billing units (default 1), and allow negative (default false); gives back a number:
  If tiers is missing, fail with an error: "[graduatedTiersToLineAmount] usage_tiers required for usage-based prices".
  Let is negative mean allow negative is true and usage is negative.
  Let absolute usage be the absolute value of usage if allow negative is true, otherwise usage.
  Round usage to nearest billing unit (usage: absolute usage and billing units), and call the result rounded usage.
  Let amount start as 0.
  Let remaining start as rounded usage.
  Let last tier to start as 0.
  For each tier in tiers:
    Stop the loop if remaining is at most 0.
    Let is final tier mean tier's to is infinite or tier's to is negative 1.
    Let tier size be depending on whether is final tier:
      • if so: remaining
      • if not: the result of min [Decimal] (remaining and tier's to minus last tier to)
    Let rate be tier's amount divided by billing units.
    Set amount to amount plus rate times tier size.
    Set remaining to remaining minus tier size.
    If is not final tier, set last tier to to tier's to.
  Let final amount be amount rounded to 10 decimal places.
  Give back negative final amount if is negative, otherwise final amount.

##### shared/utils/billingUtils/invoicingUtils/lineItemUtils/tiersToLineAmount.ts
“Translates usage into a dollar amount using the price's tier behaviour. - **Graduated**: `overage` should be net of allowance. Each tier band is charged at its own rate. `allowance` param is unused. - **Volume**: `overage` should be total usage (purchased + allowance). `allowance` is passed through to prepend a free $0 tier and shift boundaries. If total exceeds the free tier, the ENTIRE quantity (including included) is charged at the matching tier's rate. Callers (e.g. `usagePriceToLineItem`) are responsible for adjusting `overage` before calling — volume adds allowance to overage, graduated does not.”
Tiers → line amount — given price, overage, allowance (default 0), billing units (default 1), and currency; gives back a number:
  Let tiers be a price amounts for currency (config: price's config and currency)'s usage tiers, or price's config's usage tiers if that's missing.
  Let is volume mean price's tier behavior is tier behavior's volume based.
  If tiers is missing, fail with an error: "[tiersToLineAmount] usage_tiers required for usage-based or prepaid prices".
  If is volume:
    Give back the line amount of tiers:
      • usage: overage
      • billing units
      • allow negative
      • allowance
  Give back the line amount of tiers (given usage: overage, billing units, and allow negative).

##### shared/utils/billingUtils/invoicingUtils/lineItemUtils/volumeTiersToLineAmount.ts
“Volume-based tier pricing: the ENTIRE usage is charged at the rate of whichever single tier it falls into (unlike graduated, which splits across bands). When `allowance` > 0, a free $0 tier is prepended and paid-tier boundaries are shifted up. If usage <= allowance, cost is $0. If usage exceeds the allowance, the ENTIRE usage (including the free portion) is charged at the matching paid tier's rate. This is intentional — volume pricing does not subtract included usage before applying the rate.”
Volume tiers → line amount — given tiers, usage, allowance (default 0), billing units (default 1), and allow negative (default false); gives back a number:
  If tiers is missing, fail with an error: "[volumeTiersToLineAmount] usage_tiers required for volume-based prices".
  Let is negative mean allow negative is true and usage is negative.
  Let absolute usage be the absolute value of usage if allow negative is true, otherwise the larger of 0 and usage.
  Round usage to nearest billing unit (usage: absolute usage and billing units), and call the result rounded usage.
  Let amount start as 0.
  Add allowance to tiers (tiers and allowance), and call the result tiers with allowance.
  For each tier in tiers with allowance:
    Let is final tier mean tier's to is infinite or tier's to is negative 1.
    Let tier boundary be infinity if is final tier, otherwise tier's to.
    “If the usage is within this current tier,”
    If rounded usage is at most tier boundary:
      “Assume the total amount is THIS tier's cost * the usage”
      Let rate be tier's amount divided by billing units.
      Set amount to rate times rounded usage.
      “Add the flat fee for this tier if present”
      If tier's flat amount is set, set amount to amount plus tier's flat amount.
      “Do not consider each tier individually, just use the total amount for this tier.”
      Stop the loop.
  Let final amount be amount rounded to 10 decimal places.
  Give back negative final amount if is negative, otherwise final amount.

        • amount: round to currency (amount: source attribution's credits and currency)

Smallest billable unit — given currency; gives back a Decimal:
  If currency in lowercase is in Stripe three decimal currencies:
    Give back 0.01.
  Otherwise:
    Give back 1 divided by a Stripe minor unit factor (currency).

Rounding residual — given line; gives back a Decimal:
  Give back line's amount minus line's credits.

“Rounding each source line to the cent can drift their sum away from the rounded target. The lines rounded furthest give back one unit each, so none goes negative.”
Absorb rounding drift — given lines, target total, and currency:
  Let drift start as sum amounts (lines) minus target total.
  If drift is zero, stop here.
  Let step be a smallest billable unit (currency) times 1 if drift is negative, otherwise negative 1.
  Let furthest rounded first be a copy of lines, sorted by this rule:
    • compare first and second by depending on whether step is negative
  For each line in furthest rounded first:
    If drift is zero, stop here.
    Round to currency (amount: line's amount plus step and currency), and put the result in line's amount.
    Set drift to add step to drift.

To invoice credit customer entitlement to line items — given customer entitlement, context, features, idempotency scope, and fully offset overage (default false); gives back a list of LineItem:
  Let invoice credit feature be customer entitlement's entitlement's feature.
  Let source lines be the credit source lines of customer entitlement (given features and currency: context's currency).
  Let overage be the invoice overage of customer entitlement.
  Let credits applied be depending on whether fully offset overage is true:
    • if so: sum credits (source lines)
    • if not: the result of max [Decimal] (sum credits (source lines) minus overage and 0)
  Let rounded credits applied be depending on whether credits applied is zero:
    • if so: 0
    • if not: round to currency (amount: credits applied and currency: context's currency)
  Let rounded overage be depending on whether fully offset overage is true:
    • if so: 0
    • if not: round to currency (amount: overage and currency: context's currency)
  Absorb rounding drift:
    • lines: source lines
    • target total: rounded overage plus rounded credits applied
    • currency: context's currency
  Let line items be source lines, with each line turned into a with stable invoice credit ID:
    • line item: build line item:
      • context: context, but with:
        • feature set to line's feature, or invoice credit feature if that's missing
        • direction set to "charge"
      • amount: line's amount
      • description: "{line's label}, {format credit quantity formatter (line's units)} units"
      • no should prorate
      • usage: line's units
    • idempotency scope
    • position: "{customer entitlement's ID}_{line's attribution key}"
  If credits applied is zero, give back line items.
  Build line item, and call the result offset line item:
    • context: context, but with feature set to invoice credit feature and direction set to "refund"
    • amount: rounded credits applied
    • description: "Credits applied"
    • no should prorate
  Add a with stable invoice credit ID to line items:
    • line item: offset line item
    • idempotency scope
    • position: "{customer entitlement's ID}_applied"
  Give back line items.

##### shared/utils/billingUtils/cycleUtils/getCycleEnd.ts
“Get the next cycle end after `now`, aligned to the anchor. Uses mathematical calculation instead of iteration: 1. Calculate how many full cycles have passed since anchor 2. The next cycle end is (cyclesPassed + 1) cycles from anchor this value, returns the floor instead. Use this when billing cannot start before a certain date (e.g., trial end date for long trials). Example: Trial ends 4 Aug (anchor), now is 16 Jan, monthly interval. Without floor: returns 4 Feb (next monthly boundary after now). With floor=4 Aug: returns 4 Aug (billing can't start before trial ends).”
To get cycle end — given anchor, interval, interval count (default 1), now, and floor; gives back a number:
  “EDGE CASE: anchor might be slightly before now due to network latency.”

  Let now date be a new UTC date (now).
  Get cycle interval functions (interval) → interval functions.
  If interval functions is missing:
    Fail with an error: "[internal] failed to get interval functions to calculate cycle end for interval: {interval}".
  From interval functions, take add and difference.
  Let intervals passed be a difference (now date and anchor date).
  Let cycles passed start as intervals passed divided by interval count, rounded down.
  “Same clamped-boundary correction as getCycleStart: land on the cycle that brackets `now`, then the end is the next boundary after it (always > now).”
  Keep repeating while add (anchor date and cycles passed plus 1 times interval count) as a timestamp is at or before now:
    Add 1 to cycles passed.
  Keep repeating while add (anchor date and cycles passed times interval count) as a timestamp is after now:
    Subtract 1 from cycles passed.
  Let result be add (anchor date and cycles passed plus 1 times interval count) as a timestamp.
  “If floor is provided and result is before floor, return floor”
  If floor is set and result is less than floor, give back floor.
  Give back result.

##### shared/utils/billingUtils/cycleUtils/getCycleStart.ts
“Get the start of the current cycle that contains `now`, aligned to the anchor. Uses mathematical calculation instead of iteration: 1. Calculate how many full cycles have passed since anchor 2. The cycle start is cyclesPassed cycles from anchor this value, returns the floor instead. Use this when the subscription/entity didn't exist before a certain date (e.g., subscription creation date). Example: Subscription starts 1 Jan, anchor is 15 Jan, now is 5 Jan. Without floor: returns 15 Dec (previous cycle boundary). With floor=1 Jan: returns 1 Jan (subscription start).”

  Keep repeating while add (anchor date and cycles passed plus 1 times interval count) as a timestamp is at or before now:
    Add 1 to cycles passed.
  Keep repeating while add (anchor date and cycles passed times interval count) as a timestamp is after now:
    Subtract 1 from cycles passed.
  Let result be add (anchor date and cycles passed times interval count) as a timestamp.
  “If floor is provided and result is before floor, return floor”
  If floor is set and result is less than floor, give back floor.
  Give back result.

##### shared/utils/balanceAllocationUtils/allocationMath.ts
Type AllocationUsage: an object.

“Relative float noise in a stored scale; without it, 12000 × ⅔ floors to 7999. Lua uses the same value.”
Let allocation float tolerance be 1e-9.

Claimed of — given requested and usage:
  Give back the result of min [Decimal] (usage and requested).

“Largest scale ≤ 1 at which every entity's unused share still fits in what's left of the pot.”
To solve allocation scale — given shared remaining and entries; gives back a number:
  Let live be entries, keeping only those where entry's requested is positive.
  Let remaining be the result of max [Decimal] (0 and shared remaining).
  Let unused at full scale be live combined into one value, starting from 0; for each entry (with the running total sum):
    • the running total becomes sum plus entry's requested minus the claimed of entry
  If unused at full scale is at most remaining, give back 1.
  “Each entity starts holding unused credits once scale passes claimed / requested.”
  Let by threshold be live, after these steps:
    1. Turn each entry into an object with:
      • requested: entry's requested
      • claimed: the claimed of entry
      • threshold: the claimed of entry divided by entry's requested
    2. ␀them, sorted by this rule:
      • compare a and b by a's threshold's compared to (b's threshold)
  Let active requested start as 0.
  Let active claimed start as 0.
  For each entry (at position index) in by threshold:
    Set active requested to active requested plus entry's requested.
    Set active claimed to active claimed plus entry's claimed.
    Let next threshold be by threshold's entry for index plus 1's threshold, or 1 if that's missing.
    Let scale be remaining plus active claimed divided by active requested.
    If scale is at most next threshold, give back the result of max [Decimal] (scale and entry's threshold).
  Give back 1.

“The share an entity holds right now: its request scaled down, rounded to whole credits, never below usage.”
Allocation granted — given requested, usage, and scale; gives back a number:
  If scale is at least 1, give back requested.
  Let scaled be requested times scale plus requested times allocation float tolerance's floor.
  Give back the result of max [Decimal] (the claimed of requested and usage and scaled).

“What a deduction may take from shared rows: the entity's own unused share, then credits nobody holds.”
Allocation gate — given own, scale (as stored scale), held unused, and shared remaining; gives back an object with own unused and unallocated:
  “A cut solved before the pot grew stops binding once every unused promise fits again.”
  Let scale be 1 if held unused is at most shared remaining, otherwise stored scale.
  Let own unused be depending on whether own is set:
    • if so: the result of max [Decimal]:
      • 0
      • an allocation granted (everything in own and scale) minus own's usage
    • if not: 0
  If scale is less than 1, give back an object with own unused: own unused and unallocated: 0.
  Let unallocated be the result of max [Decimal] (0 and shared remaining minus held unused).
  Give back an object with own unused: own unused and unallocated: unallocated.

“First-call usage nobody was counting: absorbed from the end of the list so the first entries stay whole.”
To pack allocation gap — given gap and entries; gives back a lookup of text to number:
  Let left start as the result of max [Decimal] (0 and gap).
  Let usage be an empty object.
  For each entry in a copy of entries' reverse:
    Let absorbed be the result of min [Decimal] (left and entry's amount).
    Set usage's entry for entry's entity ID to absorbed.
    Set left to left minus absorbed.
  Give back an object built from entries, with each entry turned into a list of:
    • entry's entity ID
    • usage's entry for entry's entity ID, or 0 if that's missing

“The shared row whose cycle allocations follow: the pinned row while it exists, else the pool, else the soonest to reset.”
To pick allocation parent — given shared rows and pinned ID; gives back a T (or nothing):
  Let resetting be shared rows, keeping only those where row's next reset at is set.
  Let pinned be the first row in resetting where row's ID is pinned ID if pinned ID is set (otherwise nothing).
  If pinned is set, give back pinned.
  Let pooled be the first row in resetting where row is pooled balance.
  If pooled is set, give back pooled.
  Give back the first of a copy of resetting, sorted by this rule:
    • compare a and b by a's next reset at, or 0 if that's missing minus b's next reset at, or 0 if that's missing, or how a's ID compares alphabetically to b's ID if that's empty

##### shared/utils/auth/oauthRequestBody.ts

    • fields set to an object built from a new URL search params (raw body)'s entries

“Keys are emitted in a stable order because the token endpoint's refresh replay key hashes this body: a client retrying the same refresh has to produce the same bytes. Form encoding carries only strings, so non-string values are dropped there but survive in JSON.”

    1. ␀them, sorted

  Let params be a new URL search params.
  For each key and value in sorted entries:
    If value is text, record value under key in params.
  Give back a new request (request and body: params).

##### shared/models/productModels/priceModels/priceConfig/buildPriceCurrencies.ts
Type CurrencyAmount: an object.
Type CurrencyTierAmount: an object.
Type BaseTier: an object.
Type ItemTier: an object.

To key — given currency:
  Give back currency in lowercase.

“Flat (fixed) price: each currency becomes a per-currency amount block.”
To build fixed price currencies — given additional currencies; gives back a lookup of text to PriceCurrencyConfig (or nothing):
  If additional currencies is empty, give back nothing.
  Let currencies be an empty object.
  For each currency and amount in additional currencies:
    Set currencies' entry for a to key (currency) to an object with amount.
  Give back currencies.

“Usage price: each currency becomes a full usage_tiers set whose boundaries are copied from the base (already subtracted) tiers, so they can never drift. `itemTiers` drives the tiered case; `flatCurrencies` the single-tier (prepaid) case. Returns undefined when no currency is present, so callers omit the map.”
To build usage price currencies — given base tiers, item tiers, and flat currencies; gives back a lookup of text to PriceCurrencyConfig (or nothing):
  If item tiers is not empty:
    Let keys be everything in a to key (each c's currency), for each c in each tier's additional currencies, for each tier in item tiers without duplicates.
    If keys is empty, give back nothing.
    Let currencies be an empty object.
    For each key in keys:
      Set currencies' entry for key to an object with:
        • usage tiers: base tiers, with each base turned into the result of:
          Let entry be the first c in item tiers' entry for index's additional currencies where a to key (c's currency) is key.
          Give back an object with:
            • to: base's to
            • amount: entry's amount, or 0 if that's missing
            • everything in depending on whether entry's flat amount is set:
              • if so: an object with flat amount: entry's flat amount
              • if not: an empty object
    Give back currencies.
  If flat currencies is not empty and base tiers is not empty:
    Let currencies be an empty object.
    For each currency and amount in flat currencies:
      Set currencies' entry for a to key (currency) to an object with:
        • usage tiers: a list of an object with to: the first of base tiers' to and amount
    Give back currencies.
  Give back nothing.

“Fixed price: per-currency amount blocks -> flat additional_currencies.”
Fixed currencies → API — given currencies; gives back a list of object (or nothing):
  If currencies is missing, give back nothing.
  Let entries be the key/value pairs of currencies.
  If entries is empty, give back nothing.
  Give back entries, with each item turned into an object with currency and amount: block's amount, or 0 if that's missing.

“Usage price: per-currency usage_tiers -> per-tier additional_currencies arrays, aligned by index to the base tiers (index i = the currencies for base tier i).”
Usage currencies → tiers — given currencies and tier count; gives back a list of list of object (or nothing):
  If currencies is missing or tier count is zero or less, give back nothing.
  Let entries be the key/value pairs of currencies.
  If entries is empty, give back nothing.
  Let per tier be an object with length: tier count as a list, each turned into an empty list.
  For each currency and block in entries:
    For each tier in block's usage tiers:
      If index is less than tier count:
        Add an object with to per tier's entry for index:
          • currency
          • amount: tier's amount
          • everything in depending on whether tier's flat amount is set:
            • if so: an object with flat amount: tier's flat amount
            • if not: an empty object
  Give back per tier.

##### shared/models/productModels/priceModels/priceConfig/priceCurrencyView.ts

To resolve base currency — given config and org default; gives back text:
  Give back config's base currency, or org default if that's missing in lowercase.

Is base currency? — given config, currency, and org default; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether currency in lowercase is resolve base currency (config and org default).

Price config for currency — given config, currency, and org default; gives back a PriceCurrencyConfig:
  If currency is base (given config and org default):
    Give back an object with amount: config's amount and usage tiers: config's usage tiers.
  Let block be config's currencies' entry for currency in lowercase.
  Give back an object with amount: block's amount and usage tiers: block's usage tiers.

Price amounts for currency — given config and currency; gives back a PriceCurrencyConfig:
  If currency is missing, give back an object with amount: config's amount and usage tiers: config's usage tiers.
  Give back a price config for currency:
    • config
    • currency
    • org default: config's base currency, or currency if that's missing

Price has currency amounts — given config, currency, org default, and is fixed; gives back true/false:
  If currency is base (given config and org default), give back whether true.
  Let block be config's currencies' entry for currency in lowercase.
  If block is missing, give back whether false.
  If is fixed:
    Give back whether block's amount is set.
  Otherwise:
    Give back whether block's usage tiers is not empty.

  • "stripe_price_id"

  Let blocks be a list of:
    • config
    • everything in the values in config's currencies, or an empty object if that's missing
  Give back all results, combined, of turning each block in blocks into slots, after these steps:
    1. Turn each slot into each block's entry for slot
    2. Keep only those where ID is set

To get price currency Stripe ID — given config, currency, org default, and slot; gives back text (or nothing):
  If currency is base (given config and org default), give back config's entry for slot, or nothing if that's missing.
  Give back config's currencies' entry for currency in lowercase's entry for slot, or nothing if that's missing.

To set price currency Stripe ID — given config, currency, org default, slot, and ID:

    Set config's entry for slot to ID, or nothing if that's missing.

    Let right per day be an usage limit per day (right).
    If left per day is not right per day, give back right if right per day is less than left per day, otherwise left.
  Let left anchor be left's anchor, or "billing_cycle" if that's missing.
  Let right anchor be right's anchor, or "billing_cycle" if that's missing.
  If left anchor is not right anchor, give back left if left anchor is "utc", otherwise right.
  Give back left.

  Give back whether parse int [Number] (high and 16) times 65,536 plus parse int [Number] (low and 16) is private ipv4.

“True when the URL literally points at this machine or a private network. Svix delivers from the internet, so such an endpoint could never be reached.”

##### shared/api/versionUtils/ApiVersionClass.ts
“ApiVersionClass - Encapsulates version comparison logic Provides semantic comparison methods (gt, lt, gte, lte, eq) for API versions. Only accepts valid versions from the ApiVersion enum. const v1 = new ApiVersionClass(ApiVersion.V1_1); const v2 = new ApiVersionClass(ApiVersion.V1_2); v2.gt(v1); // true v1.gte(ApiVersion.V1_1); // true”
Class API version class:
  Field version.
  Field metadata.
  Field sorted versions.
  When created — given version:
    If version is not in API versions, fail with an error: "Invalid API version: {version}".
    Set this's version to version.
    Get version metadata (version), and put the result in this's metadata.
    Get versions sorted, and put the result in this's sorted versions.
  “Get the current version”
  Value — gives back an ApiVersion:
    Give back this's version.
  “Get version metadata”
  Meta — gives back a VersionMetadata:
    Give back this's metadata.
  “Get the CalVer representation (for headers)”
  Calver — gives back text:
    Give back this's metadata's calver.
  “Get the SemVer representation”
  Semver — gives back an ApiVersion:
    Give back this's version.
  “Get the index of this version in the sorted list”
  To get index — given version; gives back a number:
    Give back the position of version in this's sorted versions (or -1).
  “Greater than”
  Gt — given other; gives back true/false:
    Let other version be other's value if other is an API version class, otherwise other.
    Give back whether get this index (this's version) is more than get this index (other version).
  “Greater than or equal”
  Gte — given other; gives back true/false:
    Let other version be other's value if other is an API version class, otherwise other.
    Give back whether get this index (this's version) is at least get this index (other version).
  “Less than”
  Lt — given other; gives back true/false:
    Let other version be other's value if other is an API version class, otherwise other.
    Give back whether get this index (this's version) is less than get this index (other version).
  “Less than or equal”
  Lte — given other; gives back true/false:
    Let other version be other's value if other is an API version class, otherwise other.
    Give back whether get this index (this's version) is at most get this index (other version).
  “Equal”
  Eq — given other; gives back true/false:
    Let other version be other's value if other is an API version class, otherwise other.
    Give back whether this's version is other version.
  “Not equal”
  Neq — given other; gives back true/false:
    Give back whether this is not other.
  “Check if this version is deprecated”
  Is deprecated? — gives back true/false:
    Give back whether this's metadata's deprecated is set.
  “Get the version to migrate to (if deprecated)”
  To get migration version — gives back an ApiVersion (or nothing):
    Give back this's metadata's migrate to version, or nothing if that's empty.
  “String representation”
  To string — gives back text:
    Give back this's version.
  “JSON representation”
  To JSON — gives back text:
    Give back this's version.

##### shared/api/versionUtils/convertVersionUtils.ts
“CalVer → SemVer (supports .clover suffix for future non-breaking changes)”
Cal ver → sem ver — given calver; gives back an ApiVersion (or nothing):
  Give back calver to semver map's entry for calver, or nothing if that's empty.

“SemVer → CalVer”
Sem ver → cal ver — given semver; gives back text:
  Let meta be version registry's entry for semver.
  If meta is missing, fail with an error: "Unknown version: {semver}".
  Give back meta's calver.

“Legacy float → SemVer”
Legacy → sem ver — given legacy version; gives back an ApiVersion (or nothing):
  Depending on legacy version:
    • If it is legacy version's v1 or 0.2:
      Give back API version's v0 2.
    • If it is 0.1:
      Give back API version's v0 1.
    • If it is legacy version's v1 1 or 1.1:
      Give back API version's v1 1.
    • If it is legacy version's v1 2 or 1.2:
      Give back API version's v1 2.
    • If it is legacy version's v1 4 or 1.4:
      Give back API version's v1 beta.
    • For anything else:
      Give back nothing.

“SemVer → Legacy float”
Sem ver → legacy — given semver; gives back a number (or nothing):
  Depending on semver:
    • If it is API version's v0 1:
      Give back 0.1.
    • If it is API version's v0 2:
      Give back legacy version's v1.
    • If it is API version's v1 1:
      Give back legacy version's v1 1.
    • If it is API version's v1 2:
      Give back legacy version's v1 2.
    • If it is API version's v1 beta:
      Give back legacy version's v1 4.
    • For anything else:
      Give back nothing.

“Parse version string (CalVer, SemVer, or legacy) Supports .clover suffix: "2025-04-17.clover" Supports partial SemVer: "2" → "2.0.0", "2.0" → "2.0.0"”
To parse version — given version string; gives back an ApiVersion (or nothing):
  “CalVer with optional .clover suffix”
  If version string matches /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}(\.clover)?$/, give back the sem ver of version string.
  “SemVer (X.Y.Z) - normalize partial versions Supports "2" → "2.0.0", "2.0" → "2.0.0", "2.0.0" → "2.0.0"”
  If version string matches /^\d+(\.\d+)*$/:
    Let parts be version string split on ".".
    Let normalized version be "{the first of parts, or "0" if that's empty}.{item #2 of parts, or "0" if that's empty}.{item #3 of parts, or "0" if that's empty}".
    If normalized version is in the values in API version, give back normalized version.
  “Check for exact match (for special versions like "beta")”
  If version string is in the values in API version, give back version string.
  “Legacy float”
  Parse float [Number] (version string), and call the result float version.
  If float version is a valid number, give back the sem ver of float version.
  Give back nothing.

“Convert Unix timestamp (milliseconds since epoch) to ApiVersionClass Based on organization creation date - returns ApiVersionClass with comparison methods”
Created at → version — given created at; gives back an ApiVersionClass:
  Let v2 4 be "2026-09-04T00:00:00Z" as a date as a timestamp.
  Let v2 3 be "2026-05-13T00:00:00Z" as a date as a timestamp.
  Let v2 2 be "2026-03-18T00:00:00Z" as a date as a timestamp.
  Let v1 2 be "2025-05-05" as a date as a timestamp.
  Let v1 1 be "2025-04-17" as a date as a timestamp.
  Let v0 2 be "2025-01-30" as a date as a timestamp.
  Start with no version yet.
  If created at is missing or created at is at or after v2 4:
    Set version to API version's v2 4.
  Otherwise, if created at is at or after v2 3:
    Set version to API version's v2 3.
  Otherwise, if created at is at or after v2 2:
    Set version to API version's v2 2.
  Otherwise, if created at is at or after v1 2:
    Set version to API version's v1 2.
  Otherwise, if created at is at or after v1 1:
    Set version to API version's v1 1.
  Otherwise, if created at is at or after v0 2:
    Set version to API version's v0 2.
  Otherwise:
    Set version to API version's v0 1.
  Give back a new API version class (version).

##### shared/api/versionUtils/versionRegistryUtils.ts
“CalVer → SemVer lookup map”
Let calver to semver map be the values in version registry combined into one value, starting from an empty object; for each meta (with the running total total so far):
  Set total so far's entry for meta's calver to meta's semver.
  Set total so far's entry for "{meta's calver}.clover" to meta's semver.
  Give back total so far.

To get version metadata — given version; gives back a VersionMetadata:
  Give back version registry's entry for version.

Is valid version? — given params; gives back params is { version: ApiVersion }:
  Give back whether params' version is in API versions.

To get versions sorted — gives back a list of ApiVersion:
  Give back the values in version registry, after these steps:
    1. ␀them, sorted by released at (smallest first)
    2. Take each one's semver

To get versions between — given from and to; gives back a list of ApiVersion:
  Get versions sorted → sorted.
  Let from index be the position of from in sorted (or -1).
  Let to index be the position of to in sorted (or -1).
  If from index is negative 1 or to index is negative 1, fail with an error: "Invalid version range: {from} to {to}".
  Give back sorted from position from index up to to index plus 1.

To get versions for request transform — given from and to; gives back a list of ApiVersion:
  Get versions sorted → sorted.

##### shared/api/versionUtils/versionChangeUtils/applyVersionChanges.ts

  Let print logs mean false.

  Give back transformed data.

##### shared/api/products/mappers/attachItemCurrencies.ts
To key — given currency:
  Give back currency in lowercase.

“V1-layer: read additional_currencies off the original plan item and attach them onto the built ProductItem (per-tier amounts merged by index), stamping base_currency only when currencies are present. Validates here (we have ctx) that no additional currency equals the base, and that each currency tier's flat_amount shape mirrors the base tier. Deliberately NOT done in the V0 hop: ApiPlanItemV0 is part of the public apiPlanV0 response and planItemV1ToV0 is reused by the V1->V0 downgrade.”
To attach item currencies — given product item and plan item; gives back a ProductItem:
  Let price be plan item's price.
  If price is missing, give back product item.
  Let flat currencies be price's additional currencies.
  Let tier currencies present mean price's tiers has a tier where the number of tier's additional currencies, or 0 if that's missing is positive.
  If flat currencies is empty and tier currencies present is false, give back product item.
  Let base currency be a to key (the org's default currency, or "usd" if that's empty).
  To assert not base currency — given currency:
    If a to key (currency) is base currency:
      Fail with an error: "additional_currencies cannot include the base currency '{base currency}' (feature: {plan item's feature ID})" [product error code's invalid product item] (status 400).
  If flat currencies is not empty:
    For each currency in flat currencies:
      Assert not base currency (currency).
    Give back product item, but with:
      • additional currencies set to flat currencies
      • base currency set to base currency
  Let base tiers be product item's tiers.
  Let v1 tiers be price's tiers.
  Let tiers be base tiers, with each base tier turned into the result of:
    Let currency entries be v1 tiers' entry for index's additional currencies.
    Let base has flat mean base tier's flat amount is set.
    For each entry in currency entries:
      Assert not base currency (entry's currency).
      If (entry's flat amount is set) differs from (base has flat is true):
        Fail with an error: "additional currency '{entry's currency}' tier must {"" if base has flat is true, otherwise "not "}use flat_amount to match the base tier (feature: {plan item's feature ID})" [product error code's invalid product item] (status 400).
    Give back base tier, but with additional currencies set to currency entries.
  Give back product item, but with tiers set to tiers and base currency set to base currency.

##### shared/api/migrations/filters/arrayFilter.ts

##### shared/api/migrations/filters/customerFilter.ts
“Filter over Autumn customers. Migration-scoped — stable contract decoupled from `ApiCustomerV5`. `plan` and `item` are array-navigation: a bare filter is implicit `$some`. Use `{ $every: ... }` or `{ $none: ... }` for stricter checks. `item` is sugar for `plan: { item: ... }` — matches customers with at least one active plan that has at least one matching item. Sibling with `plan` it AND's (each must independently have a match). `$and` / `$or` compose independent customer-level predicates: each branch is its own `CustomerFilter` (typically a single `plan` quantifier), so `$and: [{ plan: free }, { plan: pro }]` means "has free AND also has pro" — two separate existence checks, not one plan that is both.”
Type PlanFilterValue: a z.infer.

##### shared/api/migrations/filters/matcher.ts
“Mongo-style matchers for migration filters. Rules: - Bare value = equality (Mongo convention). `feature_id: "credits"` ≡ `feature_id: { $eq: "credits" }`. - `null` is a valid bare value: `price: null` matches null fields. - Object form lets the caller use operators ($in, $ne, $gt, $regex, ...). - Operator keys are prefixed with `$` to disambiguate from nested-object filters. Keys without `$` are treated as field names on the resource.”

##### shared/api/migrations/filters/planFilter.ts
“Filter over a plan. Migration-scoped: stable contract decoupled from `ApiPlanV1`. Customer-rooted filters automatically scope to relevant customer-product status (`cp.status IN RELEVANT_STATUSES`). `price` is the plan's BASE price (customer_price linked to a price with `entitlement_id IS NULL`). Use `price: null` for free plans, `price: { $ne: null }` for paid plans. `paid` / `recurring` are DERIVED filters — boolean shortcuts that compile to EXISTS expressions: - `paid: true`     → has at least one customer_price (base or item) - `recurring: true`→ has at least one customer_price whose price's interval is not 'one_off' - `addon: false`   → product.is_add_on is false Note: `recurring: true` is a strict subset of `paid: true`. Every recurring plan is paid (a recurring price is still a price), but a paid plan may be one-off. Combine them only when you mean it — e.g. `paid: true, recurring: false` selects one-off-paid plans. `item` is array-navigation: a bare `PlanItemFilter` is implicit `$some`. `$or` joins sibling filters with OR instead of the default AND. Sibling fields outside `$or` continue to be ANDed with the OR group.”
Let plan price filter inner be a schema for an object with .

##### shared/api/migrations/filters/match/nullableFieldMatches.ts
“Evaluate a `nullableObjectFilter(...)` value against a field. Mirrors the three-branch shape of the schema: - bare `null`               → match if value is null/undefined - `{ $eq: null }`           → same - `{ $ne: null }`           → match if value is non-null - inner shape               → value must be non-null AND `innerMatches` returns true `innerMatches` is the caller-supplied nested matcher (e.g. for a nested `PlanItemFilter`). It only sees non-null values.”

  If filter is missing, give back whether is null.
  If filter is an object and filter is set:
    If filter has a "$eq" key and filter's eq is missing, give back whether is null.
    If filter has a "$ne" key and filter's ne is missing, give back whether is not null.
    “Anything else with `$eq`/`$ne` keys is shape-invalid for a nullable wrapper — fall through to the inner matcher.”
    Let only null keys mean all of these are true:
      • every k in the keys of filter satisfies: k is "$eq" or k is "$ne"
      • the keys of filter is not empty
    If only null keys is true, give back whether true.
  If is null, give back whether false.
  Give back inner matches (filter and value).

##### shared/api/migrations/compiler/registry/registryTypes.ts
“Field registry — the single source of truth mapping each logical filter field to its physical SQL shape. Adding a filter field = adding a registry entry. Compiler stays untouched. Two field kinds: - `leaf`: a column or expression. Used for direct comparisons. - `nav`: a 1:N relation. Compiles to `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM <from> WHERE <correlation> AND <ambient> AND <child>)`. Ambient predicates: each scope can declare predicates that get auto-injected when the scope is entered. Two flavors: - `context` source: value pulled from an ambient context (e.g. orgId, env). Pushed as a `?` param. - `values` source: static list known at registry-construction time (e.g. `cp.status IN ACTIVE_STATUSES`). Each element is pushed as a `?` param so quoting/escaping is the driver's responsibility.”
Type AmbientPredicate: an object.

Type LeafField: an object.
Type NavScope: an object.
Type NavField: an object.
Type FieldDef: a LeafField or a NavField.
Type RootScope: an object.

“Values supplied to ambient predicates with `source.kind === "context"`.”
Type AmbientContext: a lookup of text to anything.

“Compile an IR tree into a parameterized SQL fragment. The root scope's ambient predicates are emitted at the top of the WHERE clause; every nested scope's ambient predicates are auto-injected into its EXISTS subquery.”
Ir → SQL — given ir, root, and ambient; gives back a CompiledSql:
  Let params be an empty list.
  Compile ambient (predicates: root's ambient, ambient, and params), and call the result root ambient.
  Compile node, and call the result ir SQL:
    • node: ir
    • fields: root's fields
    • params
    • ambient
  Let parts be a list of everything in root ambient and ir SQL, keeping only those where s is not empty.
  Give back an object with SQL: parts joined with " AND " and params.

To compile ambient — given predicates, ambient, and params; gives back a list of text:
  If predicates is missing, give back an empty list.
  Give back predicates, with each pred turned into the result of:
    If pred's source's kind is "context":
      Let value be ambient's entry for pred's source's key.
      If value is missing, fail with an error: "Missing ambient value for key "{pred's source's key}" (column {pred's column})".
      Add value to params.
      Give back "{pred's column} = ?".
    If pred's source's values is empty, give back "FALSE".
    Let placeholders be pred's source's values, after these steps:
      1. Turn each v into the result of these steps:
        Add v to params.
        Give back "?".
      2. Join them with ", "
    Give back "{pred's column} IN ({placeholders})".

To compile node — given node, fields, params, and ambient; gives back text:
  If node's kind is "leaf", Compile leaf (leaf: node, fields, and params), and give back the result.
  If node's kind is "and":
    If node's children is empty, give back "TRUE".
    Let parts be node's children, with each c turned into compile node:
      • node: each c
      • fields
      • params
      • ambient
    Give back "({parts joined with " AND "})".
  If node's kind is "or":
    If node's children is empty, give back "FALSE".
    Let parts be node's children, with each c turned into compile node:
      • node: each c
      • fields
      • params
      • ambient
    Give back "({parts joined with " OR "})".
  “nav”
  Let def be fields' entry for node's name.
  If def is missing, fail with an error: "Unknown nav field: {node's name}".
  If def's kind is not "nav", fail with an error: "Field "{node's name}" is not a nav".
  Give back whether def's scope exists for (given child: node's child, quantifier: node's quantifier, params, and ambient).

Exists for scope? — given scope, child, quantifier, params, and ambient; gives back text:
  Compile ambient (predicates: scope's ambient, ambient, and params), and call the result ambient preds.
  Compile node, and call the result child SQL:
    • node: child
    • fields: scope's fields
    • params
    • ambient
  Let conditions be a list of scope's correlation, everything in ambient preds, and child SQL, keeping only those where s is not empty and s is not "TRUE".
  Let where clause be conditions joined with " AND " if conditions is not empty, otherwise "TRUE".
  Let keyword be "NOT EXISTS" if quantifier is "none", otherwise "EXISTS".
  Give back "{keyword} (SELECT 1 FROM {scope's from} WHERE {where clause})".

To compile leaf — given leaf, fields, and params; gives back text:
  Let def be fields' entry for leaf's field.
  If def is missing, fail with an error: "Unknown leaf field: {leaf's field}".
  If def's kind is not "leaf", fail with an error: "Field "{leaf's field}" is not a leaf".
  Let col be def's SQL.
  If leaf's op is "exists", give back "{col} IS NOT NULL" if leaf's value is set, otherwise "{col} IS NULL".
  If leaf's op is "eq":
    If leaf's value is missing, give back "{col} IS NULL".
    Add leaf's value to params.
    Give back "{col} = ?".
  If leaf's op is "ne":
    If leaf's value is missing, give back "{col} IS NOT NULL".
    Add leaf's value to params.
    Give back "{col} <> ?".
  If leaf's op is "regex" or leaf's op is "startsWith":
    Let build be regex SQL if leaf's op is "regex", otherwise starts with SQL.
    Build (column: col, field: leaf's field, and value: leaf's value), and call the result match.
    Add everything in match's params to params.
    Give back match's SQL.
  If leaf's op is "in" or leaf's op is "nin":
    If leaf's value is not a list, fail with an error: "${leaf's op} expects an array on field "{leaf's field}"".
    Let keyword be "IN" if leaf's op is "in", otherwise "NOT IN".
    If leaf's value is empty, give back "FALSE" if leaf's op is "in", otherwise "TRUE".
    Let placeholders be leaf's value, after these steps:
      1. Turn each v into the result of these steps:
        Add v to params.
        Give back "?".
      2. Join them with ", "
    Give back "{col} {keyword} ({placeholders})".
  If any of these is true:
    • leaf's op is "gt"
    • leaf's op is "gte"
    • leaf's op is "lt"
    • leaf's op is "lte"
  then:
    If leaf's value is missing or leaf's value is a list:
      Fail with an error: "${leaf's op} requires a scalar value on field "{leaf's field}"".
    Let symbol be an object with's entry for leaf's op:
      • gt: ">"
      • gte: ">="
      • lt: "<"
      • lte: "<="
    Add leaf's value to params.
    Give back "{col} {symbol} ?".
  Fail with an error: "Unsupported op: {leaf's op}".

##### shared/api/migrations/compiler/irToSql/stringMatchSql.ts
“SQL for the two string matchers, each returning its own bound params so the caller never threads a mutable array through the branch.”
Type StringMatchSql: an object.

As pattern — given op, field, and value; gives back text:
  If value is not text, fail with an error: "${op} expects a string on field "{field}"".
  Give back value.

“Smallest string greater than every value starting with `prefix`: bump the last character that can be bumped. Null when every character is already the maximum code point, leaving the range open-ended.”
Prefix upper bound — given prefix; gives back text (or nothing):
  Let chars be prefix as a list.
  Start with let index = chars.length - 1, repeat while index is zero or more, then decrease index by 1 each time:
    Let code be chars' entry for index's code point at (0), or 0 if that's missing.
    If code is less than 1,114,111:
      Give back chars, after these steps plus a from code point [String] (code plus 1):
        1. The first index of ␀them
        2. Join them with ""
  Give back nothing.

“A prefix match as a range rather than LIKE, which cannot use a btree index under a non-C collation. The uncollated bounds drive the index seek; the C-collated pair is the exact prefix test, because en_US sorts 'aB' and 'a-bz' inside ['ab','ac') without carrying the prefix.”
Starts with SQL? — given column, field, and value; gives back a StringMatchSql:
  Let prefix be an as pattern (op: "startsWith", field, and value).
  If prefix is "", give back an object with SQL: "TRUE" and params: an empty list.
  Let byte column be "{column} COLLATE "C"".
  Let upper bound be a prefix upper bound (prefix).
  If upper bound is missing:
    Give back an object with:
      • SQL: "({column} >= ? AND {byte column} >= ?)"
      • params: a list of prefix and prefix
  Give back an object with:
    • SQL: "({column} >= ? AND {column} < ? AND {byte column} >= ? AND {byte column} < ?)"
    • params: a list of prefix, upper bound, prefix, and upper bound

“Rejects an invalid pattern here rather than letting Postgres raise it mid-preview or mid-run.”
Regex SQL — given column, field, and value; gives back a StringMatchSql:
  Let pattern be an as pattern (op: "regex", field, and value).
  Try the following:
    A new reg exp (pattern).
  If anything fails:
    Fail with an error: "$regex on field "{field}" is not a valid regular expression".
  Give back an object with SQL: "{column} ~ ?" and params: a list of pattern.

##### shared/api/migrations/compiler/ir/irTypes.ts
“Intermediate Representation (IR) for migration filters. The filter pipeline is: Filter (Zod, public DSL) → IR (canonical AST) → SQL (Drizzle fragment) The IR is the compiler-friendly middle layer. It collapses every spelling of the public DSL (`feature_id: "x"` ≡ `{ $eq: "x" }`, `price: null` ≡ `{ $eq: null }`) into one canonical shape, so the compiler only handles one form per concept.”
Type LeafOp: one of "eq", "ne", "in", "nin", "exists", "gt", "gte", "lt", "lte", "startsWith", or "regex".

Type LeafValue: text, a number, true/false, readonly string[], or readonly number[] (or nothing).
Type IRLeaf: an object.
Type IRAnd: an object.
Type IROr: an object.
Type Quantifier: one of "some" or "none".
Type IRNav: an object.
Type IRNode: an IRLeaf, an IRAnd, an IROr, or an IRNav.

##### shared/api/migrations/compiler/filterToIr/filterToIr.ts
“Top-level entry: take a validated `CustomerFilter` plus a resolution context (features, products) and produce IR ready for compilation. The parser walks the filter shape, recurses into each scope (customer → plan → item), and converts each field-matcher pair into one or more IR leaves. AND is always implicit between sibling fields. Bare nested filters become `nav` nodes with implicit `$some` quantifier. Internal layout (each one-thing-per-file): scopes/   per-scope dispatchers (customer, plan, plan.item) navs/     scope-to-scope transitions (plan, item; routes scope variants) fields/   per-field parsers + parseLeaf + makeExistenceParser factory helpers/  wrapAnd, isQuantifierWrapper”
To filter to ir — given filter; gives back an IRNode:
  Parse customer filter (filter), and give back the result.

“Plan-rooted entry: validated `PlanFilter` → IR. Used when the migration targets the catalog directly rather than a customer's plan instance.”
To plan filter to ir — given filter; gives back an IRNode:
  Parse plan filter (filter), and give back the result.

##### shared/api/migrations/compiler/filterToIr/resolutionContext.ts
“Public IDs that map 1:1 to internal IDs are translated at parse time, before the IR is built. This keeps the compiler pure — it only ever sees resolved internal IDs for those fields. Currently only `feature_id` is translated (features are not versioned, so the mapping is 1:1). `plan_id` is NOT translated — a public plan_id maps to many internal_product_ids (one per version), so we resolve it via a JOIN to `products` instead. Unknown IDs throw at parse time, never silently miss.”
Type ResolutionContext: an object.

##### shared/api/migrations/compiler/filterToIr/scopes/parseCustomerFilter.ts
To parse customer filter — given filter; gives back an IRNode:
  Let children be an empty list.
  If filter's customer ID is set, add parse leaf (field: "customer_id" and raw value: filter's customer ID) to children.
  If filter's plan is set, add parse plan nav (raw: filter's plan) to children.
  “`item` is sugar for `plan: { item: ... }` — wraps the item nav in a plan nav so the IR stays canonical (no separate scope/registry entry).”
  If filter's item is set:
    Add an object with to children:
      • kind: "nav"
      • name: "plan"
      • quantifier: "some"
      • child: parse item nav (raw: filter's item)
  If filter's and is set:
    For each branch in filter's and:
      Add parse customer filter (filter: branch) to children.
  If filter's or is set:
    If filter's or is empty, fail with an error: "$or requires at least one branch".
    Add an object with to children:
      • kind: "or"
      • children: parse customer filter (filter: each branch), for each branch in filter's or
  Wrap and (children), and give back the result.

##### shared/api/migrations/compiler/filterToIr/fields/makeExistenceParser.ts
“Factory for nullable-existence field parsers. The pattern is identical across `price`, `rollover`, and any future field where the only phase-1 questions are "is this column null?" / "is it non-null?": field: null           → exists(false) field: { $eq: null }  → exists(false) field: { $ne: null }  → exists(true) `scopePath` is the dotted public path used in error messages (e.g. "plan.item.rollover"). The IR `field` is the bare name.”
To make existence parser — given field and scope path; gives back a function:
  Give back a function of raw that:
    If raw is missing:
      Give back an object with:
        • kind: "leaf"
        • field
        • op: "exists"
        • value: false
    If raw is not an object, fail with an error: "{scope path} must be null or an object".
    Let ops be raw.
    Let has only null ops mean all of these are true:
      • every k in the keys of ops satisfies: k is "$eq" or k is "$ne"
      • every v in the values in ops satisfies: v is missing or v is missing
    If has no only null ops, fail with an error: "{scope path} filtering on nested fields is not supported in phase 1".
    If ops has a "$ne" key and ops' ne is missing:
      Give back an object with:
        • kind: "leaf"
        • field
        • op: "exists"
        • value: true
    If ops has a "$eq" key and ops' eq is missing:
      Give back an object with:
        • kind: "leaf"
        • field
        • op: "exists"
        • value: false
    Fail with an error: "{scope path} requires $eq: null or $ne: null".

##### shared/api/migrations/compiler/filterToIr/fields/parseLeaf.ts
“Parse a single field's matcher value into one IR leaf or a small AND of leaves. Handles the supported operators: eq, ne, in, nin, exists, gt, gte, lt, lte, startsWith, regex. Spelling normalization: - bare value         → eq - { $eq: x }         → eq - { $ne: null }      → exists (true) - { $eq: null }      → eq null - { $in: [...] }     → in - { $gt: n }         → gt   (and same for $gte / $lt / $lte) - { $startsWith: s } → startsWith - { $regex: s }      → regex Multiple operators on one field are combined with AND.”
To parse leaf — given field and raw value; gives back an IRNode:
  If raw value is bare value, Make leaf (field, "eq", and raw value), and give back the result.
  Let ops be raw value.
  Let leaves be an empty list.
  If ops has a "$eq" key, add make leaf (field, "eq", and ops' eq) to leaves.
  If ops has a "$ne" key:
    If ops' ne is missing:
      Add make leaf (field, "exists", and true) to leaves.
    Otherwise:
      Add make leaf (field, "ne", and ops' ne) to leaves.
  If ops has a "$in" key, add make leaf (field, "in", and ops' in) to leaves.
  If ops has a "$nin" key, add make leaf (field, "nin", and ops' nin) to leaves.
  If ops has a "$gt" key, add make leaf (field, "gt", and ops' gt) to leaves.
  If ops has a "$gte" key, add make leaf (field, "gte", and ops' gte) to leaves.
  If ops has a "$lt" key, add make leaf (field, "lt", and ops' lt) to leaves.
  If ops has a "$lte" key, add make leaf (field, "lte", and ops' lte) to leaves.
  If ops has a "$startsWith" key, add make leaf (field, "startsWith", and ops' starts with) to leaves.
  If ops has a "$regex" key, add make leaf (field, "regex", and ops' regex) to leaves.
  If leaves is empty, fail with an error: "No supported operator found on field "{field}"".
  If the number of leaves is 1, give back the first of leaves.
  Give back an object with kind: "and" and children: leaves.

Is bare value? — given v; gives back true/false:
  If v is missing, give back whether true.
  Let t be the type of v.
  Give back whether t is "string", t is "number", or t is "boolean".

To make leaf — given field, op, and value; gives back an IRLeaf:
  Give back an object with:
    • kind: "leaf"
    • field
    • op
    • value: translate value (field and value)

    Give back feature's internal ID.
