##### shared/api/entities/changes/V1.2_EntityChange.ts
“V1_2_EntityChange: Transforms entity response TO V0 format (pre-V2.0) Applied when: targetVersion <= V1_2 Breaking changes introduced in V2.0: 1. Products renamed to Plans: - V1+: "subscriptions" field contains ApiSubscription objects - V0: "products" field contains ApiCusProductV3 objects 2. Simplified feature schema: - V1+: "balances" field with minimal fields + optional feature object - V0: "features" field with verbose fields and all metadata 3. Features remain as record (no change from V1.1): - Both V1 and V0: Record<string, ApiCusFeature> Input: ApiEntityV1 (V2.0+ format) Output: ApiEntityV0 (V1.2 format)”
Let v1 2 entity change be a define version change:
  • new version: API version's v2 0
  • old version: API version's v1 beta
  • description: a list of:
    • "Products renamed to plans in SDK"
    • "Simplified feature and plan schemas"
    • "Added optional nested objects for expanded data"
  • affected resources: a list of affected resource's entity
  • new schema: API entity v1 schema
  • old schema: API entity v0 schema
  • legacy data schema: entity legacy data schema
  • transform response: a function of input and legacy data that:
    “Step 1: Transform plans V1 → V0 (products)”
    Let v0 customer products be (only if input's subscriptions is set) input's subscriptions, with each subscription turned into the result of:
      Let customer plan legacy data be legacy data's customer product legacy data's entry for subscription's plan ID, but with features set to the features, or an empty list if that's empty if legacy data's customer product legacy data's entry for subscription's plan ID is set (otherwise nothing).
      Transform subscription to customer product v3 (input: subscription and legacy data: customer plan legacy data), and give back the result.
    Let scheduled customer products be (only if input's scheduled subscriptions is set) input's scheduled subscriptions, with each subscription turned into the result of:
      Let customer plan legacy data be legacy data's customer product legacy data's entry for subscription's plan ID, but with features set to the features, or an empty list if that's empty if legacy data's customer product legacy data's entry for subscription's plan ID is set (otherwise nothing).
      Transform subscription to customer product v3 (input: subscription and legacy data: customer plan legacy data), and give back the result.
    Let final customer products be one list combining:
      • v0 customer products, or an empty list if that's empty
      • scheduled customer products, or an empty list if that's empty
    “Step 2: Transform features V1 → V0”
    Start with no v0 features yet.
    If input's balances is set:
      Set v0 features to an empty object.
      For each key feature ID and value feature in input's balances:
        Transform balance to customer feature v3 (input: feature), and put the result in v0 features' entry for feature ID.
    “Step 3: Return V0 entity format”
    Give back an object with:
      • Autumn ID: input's Autumn ID
      • ID: input's ID
      • name: input's name
      • customer ID: input's customer ID
      • feature ID: input's feature ID
      • created at: input's created at
      • env: input's env
      • products: final customer products
      • features: v0 features
      • invoices: transform invoice to v0 (input: each invoice), for each invoice in input's invoices, or nothing if that's missing

##### shared/api/entities/changes/V2.0_EntityChange.ts
“V2.0_EntityChange: Transforms entity response TO V1 format from V2 format Applied when: targetVersion <= V2.0 (request is for V2.0 or older) Breaking changes introduced in V2.1: 1. Subscription schema changes: - V2.1+: Single "subscriptions" array with ApiSubscriptionV1 (auto_enable, ApiPlanV1) - V2.0: Split arrays "subscriptions" + "scheduled_subscriptions" with ApiSubscription (default, ApiPlanV0) 2. Subscription merging: - V2.1+: Each customer product is a separate entry (unmerged) - V2.0: Same plan_id + status are merged (quantities summed) Input: ApiEntityV2 (V2.1+ format) Output: ApiEntityV1 (V2.0 format)”
Let v2 0 entity change be a define version change:
  • name: "V2_0 Entity Change"
  • new version: API version's v2 1
  • old version: API version's v2 0
  • description: a list of "Subscription schema transforms (V1 to V0) - plan field versioning"
  • affected resources: a list of affected resource's entity
  • new schema: API entity v2 schema
  • old schema: API entity v1 schema
  • affects response
  • transform response: a function of input that:
    “Merge subscriptions first (V2.1 returns unmerged, V2.0 expects merged)”
    Let merged subscriptions be the v0 of input's subscriptions.
    “Merge purchases as subscriptions”
    Let purchases as subscriptions be the subscriptions v0 of input's purchases.
    Let active subscriptions v0 be merged subscriptions, keeping only those where subscription's status is "active".
    Let scheduled subscriptions v0 be merged subscriptions, keeping only those where subscription's status is "scheduled".
    Let balances v0 be an empty object.
    If input's balances is set:
      For each key feature ID and value balance in input's balances:
        Set balances v0's entry for feature ID to the v0 of balance.
    If input's flags is set:
      For each key feature ID and value flag in input's flags:
        Flag v0 to balance v0 (input: flag), and put the result in balances v0's entry for feature ID.
    “Return V0 entity format (without purchases field)”
    From input, take purchases and the rest as rest.
    Give back rest, but with:
      • subscriptions set to active subscriptions v0, plus purchases as subscriptions
      • scheduled subscriptions set to scheduled subscriptions v0
      • balances set to balances v0

##### shared/api/customers/utils/apiSubjectToUsageLimitHeadroom.ts
“Remaining usage-window headroom for a check, in the EVALUATED feature's units (credits when the evaluated feature is a credit system). Considers both the cap on the evaluated feature itself and -- when checking a credit-system member -- the metered cap on the original feature, converted via its credit cost. Filtered caps only apply when the check's `properties` match. Null when no armed cap applies.”
API subject → usage limit headroom — given API subject, feature, original feature, and properties; gives back a number (or nothing):
  “Entity subjects see inherited customer entries via mergeCustomerBillingControlsForCheck; entity's own entry wins per feature.”
  Let billing controls be API subject's billing controls.
  Let usage limits be billing controls' usage limits if billing controls is set and billing controls has a "usage_limits" key (otherwise nothing).
  If usage limits is missing or usage limits is empty, give back nothing.
  Let headrooms be an empty list.
  Applicable caps — given feature ID:
    Give back usage limits, keeping only those where all of these are true:
      • usage limit's feature ID is feature ID
      • usage limit's enabled is set
      • usage limit filter matches properties (given usage limit's filter's properties, or nothing if that's missing and properties)
  For each cap on evaluated in applicable caps (feature's ID):
    Add the result of max [Decimal] to headrooms:
      • 0
      • cap on evaluated's limit minus cap on evaluated's usage, or 0 if that's missing
  If original feature is set and original feature's ID is not feature's ID:
    Let schema item be the first item in feature's config's schema where item's metered feature ID is original feature's ID.
    If schema item is set:
      For each cap on original in applicable caps (original feature's ID):
        Let headroom units be the result of max [Decimal]:
          • 0
          • cap on original's limit minus cap on original's usage, or 0 if that's missing
        Add headroom units times schema item's credit amount, or 1 if that's missing divided by schema item's feature amount, or 1 if that's missing to headrooms:
  If headrooms is empty, give back nothing.
  Give back the result of min [Decimal] (all of headrooms).

##### shared/api/customers/cusFeatures/utils/apiBalanceV2Utils.ts
Type FullAggregatedFeatureBalanceWithOptionsPrepaid: FullAggregatedFeatureBalance & {
		prepa.

To merge aggregated balance into API balance v2 — given API balance and aggregated feature balance; gives back an ApiBalanceV1:
  If aggregated feature balance is missing, give back API balance.
  If API balance's unlimited is set or aggregated feature balance's unlimited is set:
    “Unlimited cusEnts still deduct: their raw balance drifts negative as a usage counter. The aggregate row covers only entity-level cusEnts — a set disjoint from the in-memory customer-level ones — so ADD its usage to the in-memory value, and only negate the aggregate balance when the aggregate itself is unlimited (a finite aggregate balance is a remaining amount, not a usage counter).”
    Let aggregated unlimited usage be depending on whether aggregated feature balance's unlimited is set:
      • if so: the values in aggregated feature balance's entities, or an empty object if that's missing combined into one value, starting from aggregated feature balance's balance, or 0 if that's missing; for each entity balance (with the running total total)'s neg:
        • the running total becomes add entity balance's balance, or 0 if that's missing to total
      • if not: 0
    Let usage be add API balance's usage to aggregated unlimited usage.
    Give back API balance, but with:
      • granted set to 0
      • remaining set to 0
      • usage set to usage
      • unlimited set to true
      • overage allowed set to false
      • breakdown set to API balance's breakdown
  Let aggregated allowance be aggregated feature balance's allowance total, or 0 if that's missing.
  Let aggregated prepaid grant from options be aggregated feature balance's prepaid grant from options, or 0 if that's missing.
  Let aggregated adjustment be aggregated feature balance's adjustment, or 0 if that's missing.
  Let aggregated balance be aggregated feature balance's balance, or 0 if that's missing.
  Let aggregated rollover balance be aggregated feature balance's rollover balance, or 0 if that's missing.
  Let aggregated rollover usage be aggregated feature balance's rollover usage, or 0 if that's missing.
  Let aggregated rollover grant be aggregated rollover balance plus aggregated rollover usage.
  Let aggregated next reset at be aggregated feature balance's next reset at, or nothing if that's missing.
  Let next reset at be depending on whether API balance's next reset at is missing:
    • if so: aggregated next reset at
    • if not: depending on whether aggregated next reset at is missing:
      • if so: API balance's next reset at
      • if not: the smaller of API balance's next reset at and aggregated next reset at
  “Aggregate rows do not retain the full per-entity/per-product breakdown, so the top-level summary is merged from the coarse aggregate values only.”
  Let base granted be add aggregated adjustment to aggregated allowance plus aggregated prepaid grant from options.
  Let granted be base granted plus aggregated rollover grant.
  “Main remaining is floored at 0 (matches legacy behaviour). Rollover remaining is added on top, since rollover balances are independent of main balance sign.”
  Let main remaining be the result of max [Decimal] (0 and aggregated balance).
  Let remaining be main remaining plus aggregated rollover balance.
  “Usage mirrors the entity-view formula: (granted - main balance) + rollover usage.”
  Let usage be add aggregated rollover usage to base granted minus aggregated balance.
  Give back API balance, but with:
    • granted set to API balance's granted plus granted
    • remaining set to API balance's remaining plus remaining

##### shared/api/customers/cusFeatures/mappers/balanceV1ToV0.ts
Balance breakdown v1 → v0 — given input; gives back an ApiBalanceBreakdown:
  Let overage be input's overage, or 0 if that's missing.
  Let purchased balance be input's prepaid grant plus overage.
  Give back an object with:

    • purchased balance: purchased balance

    • usage: input's usage

    • reset: input's reset
    • prepaid quantity: input's prepaid grant
    • expires at: input's expires at

“Transform ApiBalanceV1 (V2.1 format) to ApiBalance (V2.0 format) In V1 format: - `granted` = total granted amount - `remaining` = current balance - `next_reset_at` = when balance resets In V0 format: - `granted_balance` = granted amount - `purchased_balance` = purchased/prepaid amount (calculated from breakdown) - `current_balance` = remaining balance - `reset` = reset interval object”
Balance v1 → v0 — given input; gives back an ApiBalance:
  “Calculate purchased_balance from breakdown”
  Let purchased balance be the purchased balance of input.
  Let prepaid quantity be the prepaid quantity of input.
  “V0 granted_balance = V1 granted - prepaid_quantity V1 granted includes both included + prepaid, but V0 splits them”
  Let granted balance be input's granted minus prepaid quantity.
  “Get plan_id from breakdown”
  Let breakdown plan IDs be the plan IDs of input's breakdown without duplicates.
  “Build reset object from breakdown”
  Let unique intervals be each b's reset's interval, for each b in input's breakdown without duplicates.
  Let reset be depending on whether unique intervals has more than 1 item:
    • if so: an object with interval: "multiple", interval count: nothing, and resets at: nothing
    • if not: the first of input's breakdown's reset, but with resets at set to input's next reset at if the first of input's breakdown's reset is set (otherwise nothing)
  Give back an object with:
    • feature ID: input's feature ID
    • feature: input's feature
    • unlimited: input's unlimited
    • granted balance: granted balance
    • purchased balance: purchased balance
    • current balance: input's remaining
    • usage: input's usage
    • overage allowed: input's overage allowed
    • max purchase: input's max purchase
    • reset: reset
    • plan ID: nothing if breakdown plan IDs has more than 1 item; otherwise the first of breakdown plan IDs, or nothing if that's missing
    • breakdown: the v0 of each b in input's breakdown
    • rollovers: input's rollovers

##### shared/api/customers/cusFeatures/changes/V1.2_CusFeatureChange.ts

  Let prepaid quantity start as 0.

  “6. Expires at”

    • usage limit
    • expires at

  Let legacy credit schema be the v0 of input's feature's credit schema.

##### shared/api/common/epochUtils.ts
“Converts epoch ms to DateTime string format (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS)”
Epoch → date time — given epoch ms; gives back text:
  Let date be epoch ms as a date.
  Get date UTC full year → year.
  Let month be get date UTC month plus 1 as text padded to 2 characters.
  Let day be get date UTC date as text padded to 2 characters.
  Let hours be get date UTC hours as text padded to 2 characters.
  Let minutes be get date UTC minutes as text padded to 2 characters.
  Let seconds be get date UTC seconds as text padded to 2 characters.
  Give back "{year}-{month}-{day} {hours}:{minutes}:{seconds}".

Epoch → date time millis — given epoch ms; gives back text:
  Let date be epoch ms as a date.
  Get date UTC full year → year.
  Let month be get date UTC month plus 1 as text padded to 2 characters.
  Let day be get date UTC date as text padded to 2 characters.
  Let hours be get date UTC hours as text padded to 2 characters.
  Let minutes be get date UTC minutes as text padded to 2 characters.
  Let seconds be get date UTC seconds as text padded to 2 characters.
  Let millis be get date UTC milliseconds as text padded to 3 characters.
  Give back "{year}-{month}-{day} {hours}:{minutes}:{seconds}.{millis}".

Tinybird timestamp → epoch ms — given ts string; gives back a number:
  If ts string ends with "Z", give back ts string as a date as a timestamp.
  Give back "{ts string with " " replaced by "T"}Z" as a date as a timestamp.

Tinybird timestamp → epoch micros — given ts string; gives back a number:
  Let normalized be depending on whether ts string ends with "Z":
    • if so: the first negative 1 of ts string
    • if not: ts string with " " replaced by "T"
  Let dot index be the position of "." in normalized (or -1).
  If dot index is negative 1, give back "{normalized}Z" as a date as a timestamp times 1000.
  Let head be the first dot index of normalized.
  Let frac be the first 6 of normalized from position dot index plus 1 onward's pad end (6 and "0").
  Let base ms be "{head}Z" as a date as a timestamp.
  Give back base ms times 1000 plus frac as a number.

Epoch micros → date time — given epoch micros; gives back text:
  Let ms be epoch micros divided by 1000, rounded down.
  Let micros be epoch micros minus ms times 1000.
  Let date be ms as a date.
  Get date UTC full year → year.
  Let month be get date UTC month plus 1 as text padded to 2 characters.
  Let day be get date UTC date as text padded to 2 characters.
  Let hours be get date UTC hours as text padded to 2 characters.
  Let minutes be get date UTC minutes as text padded to 2 characters.
  Let seconds be get date UTC seconds as text padded to 2 characters.
  Let subscription be get date UTC milliseconds times 1000 plus micros as text padded to 6 characters.
  Give back "{year}-{month}-{day} {hours}:{minutes}:{seconds}.{subscription}".

##### shared/api/common/queryHelpers.ts
“Helper to handle query string arrays that can be either: - Single value: ?expand=invoices → "invoices" - Comma-separated: ?expand=invoices,rewards → ["invoices", "rewards"] (requires queryMiddleware) - Multiple values: ?expand=invoices&expand=products → ["invoices", "products"] Normalizes all to array format for consistent Zod validation Note: Comma-separated parsing requires the queryMiddleware to be applied first. The middleware uses the `qs` library to parse query strings with comma support. ```ts const schema = z.object({ expand: queryStringArray(z.enum(CusExpand)).optional(), }); ```”
To query string array — given schema:
  Give back z's preprocess:
    • a function of value that:
      “Convert single string to array, splitting on commas if present "active" → ["active"], "active,trialing" → ["active", "trialing"]”
      If value is text, give back each v without surrounding spaces, for each v in value split on ",".
      Give back value.
    • a schema for a list of schema

“Helper to handle query string integers that come in as strings and need to be converted to numbers. Query parameters are always strings, so this helper parses them to integers for validation. ```ts const schema = z.object({ limit: queryInteger({ min: 1, max: 100 }).default(10), offset: queryInteger({ min: 0 }).default(0), }); ``` Helper to handle query string integer arrays that can be either: - Single value: ?version=1 → [1] - Comma-separated: ?version=1,2,3 → [1, 2, 3] - Multiple values: ?version=1&version=2 → [1, 2] Parses string values to integers for consistent validation.”
To query integer array:
  Give back z's preprocess:
    • a function of value that:
      If value is a number, give back a list of value.
      If value is text, give back each v without surrounding spaces as a whole number, for each v in value split on ",".
      If value is a list, give back value, each turned into v as a whole number if v is text, otherwise v.
      Give back value.
    • a schema for a list of a number (whole number)

To query integer — given options:
  Let schema start as a schema for a number (whole number).
  If options' min is set:
    Set schema to schema's min:
      • options' min
      • message: options' error, or "must be at least {options' min}" if that's empty
  If options' max is set:
    Set schema to schema's max:
      • options' max
      • message: options' error, or "must be at most {options' max}" if that's empty
  Give back z's preprocess:
    • a function of value that:
      “If already a number, return as-is”
      If value is a number, give back value.
      “Parse string to integer”
      If value is text:
        Parse int [Number] (value and 10), and call the result parsed.
        Give back value if parsed is not a valid number, otherwise parsed.
      Give back value.
    • schema

To query boolean:
  Give back z's preprocess:
    • a function of value that:
      If value is text:
        If value is "false" or value is "0", give back whether false.
        If value is "true" or value is "1", give back whether true.
      Give back value.
    • a schema for true/false

  “Remove filters can omit billing_method even when priced, so check the source items by feature_id rather than the lossy filter.”

  Give back an object with:
    • everything in an object with price: diff's price if diff's price is set, otherwise an empty object
    • everything in depending on whether diff's add items is set:
      • if so: an object with add items: diff's add items
      • if not: an empty object
    • everything in depending on whether diff's remove items is set:
      • if so: an object with remove items: diff's remove items
      • if not: an empty object
    • everything in depending on whether diff's update items is set:
      • if so: an object with update items: diff's update items
      • if not: an empty object
    • everything in depending on whether diff's upsert licenses is set:
      • if so: an object with upsert licenses: diff's upsert licenses
      • if not: an empty object

To plan matcher — given IDs:
  Give back the first of IDs if the number of IDs is 1, otherwise an object with in: IDs.

With custom guard — given include custom and plan filter:
  Give back plan filter if include custom is true, otherwise plan filter, but with custom set to false.

Versioned plan filter — given targets:
  Let IDs by version be an empty lookup table.
  For each target in targets:
    Let IDs be IDs by version's entry for target's version.
    Add target's ID to IDs.
    Record IDs under target's version in IDs by version.
  Let groups be IDs by version's entries as a list, with each item turned into an object with plan ID: plan matcher (IDs) and version.
  Give back the first of groups if the number of groups is 1, otherwise an object with or: groups.

To group targets by customize — given targets; gives back a list of object:
  Let groups be an empty lookup table.
  For each target in targets:
    Skip it if target's customize is missing.
    Let customize be a migratable plan diff (target's customize).
    Skip it if the keys of customize is empty.
    Let key be customize as JSON.
    Let group be groups' entry for key.
    If group is set:
      Add target to group's targets.
    Otherwise:
      Record an object with customize and targets: a list of target under key in groups.
  Give back a copy of groups' values.

##### shared/api/balances/check/changes/V0.2_CheckChange.ts
“V0_2_CheckChange: Transforms check response TO V0_2 format Applied when: targetVersion <= V0_2 Breaking changes introduced in V0.2 (that we reverse here): 1. Structure: Single check result object → balances array format - V0.2+: Single object with allowed, feature_id, balance, unlimited, etc. - V0_2: { allowed, balances: [{ feature_id, required, balance, unlimited, usage_allowed }] } 2. Boolean features: No balance fields → balance: null 3. Unlimited features: Return unlimited: true, usage_allowed based on overage_allowed 4. Metered features: Return required_balance and balance Input: CheckResult (V0.2+ format) Output: CheckResponseV0 (V0_2 balances array format)”
Let v0 2 check change be a define version change:
  • name: "V0.2 Check Change"
  • new version: API version's v1 1
  • old version: API version's v0 2
  • description: a list of:
    • "Check response transformed to balances array format"
    • "Single check result object → { allowed, balances: [...] }"
  • affected resources: a list of affected resource's check
  • new schema: check response v1 schema
  • old schema: check response v0 schema
  • legacy data schema: check legacy data schema
  • affects response
  • transform response: a function of input and legacy data that:
    From input, take allowed, feature ID, required balance, balance, unlimited, and overage allowed.
    If legacy data is missing, fail with an error: "Legacy data is required".
    From legacy data, take no customer entitlements and feature to use.
    “No customer entitlements”
    If no customer entitlements is set and allowed is missing:
      Give back an object with allowed: false and balances: an empty list.
    “Build the balance object based on feature type”
    Let balance object be an object with feature ID.
    If feature to use's type is feature type's boolean:
      Give back an object with:
        • allowed
        • balances: a list of an object with feature ID and balance: nothing
    “Case 1: Boolean/Static features (no balance, no unlimited, no overage)”
    If all of these are true:
      • balance is missing
      • unlimited is missing
      • overage allowed is missing
      • required balance is missing
    then:
      Set balance object's balance to nothing.
      Give back an object with allowed and balances: a list of balance object.
    “Case 2: Unlimited features”
    If unlimited is set:
      Set balance object's balance to nothing.
      Set balance object's unlimited to true.
      Set balance object's usage allowed to overage allowed, or false if that's empty.
      Set balance object's required to nothing.
      Give back an object with allowed and balances: a list of balance object.
    “Case 3: Overage allowed (usage allowed but not unlimited)”
    If overage allowed is set:
      Set balance object's balance to balance.
      Set balance object's unlimited to false.
      Set balance object's usage allowed to true.
      Set balance object's required to nothing.
      Give back an object with allowed and balances: a list of balance object.
    “Case 4: Metered features with balance tracking”
    Set balance object's required to required balance, or nothing if that's missing.
    Set balance object's balance to balance.
    Give back an object with allowed and balances: a list of balance object.

##### server/tinybird/scripts/backfill_base.ts
“Shared utilities and config for all epoch-ms-chunked Tinybird backfill scripts.”

“CONSTANTS”
Let max retries be 3.

Let retry delay ms be 5000.
Let delay between chunks ms be 2000.
Let default chunk days be 30.

“TYPES”
Type Chunk: start epoch ms and end epoch ms.

Type TableConfig: label, copy pipe name, datasource, and start epoch ms.

“UTILITIES”
To exec capture — given cmd; gives back text:
  Try the following:
    Give back exec sync without surrounding spaces.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Give back error's stdout without surrounding spaces, or "" if that's missing.

Let tb API URL be the TINYBIRD_API_URL environment variable, or "https://api.us-west-2.aws.tinybird.co" if that's missing.
Let tb token be the TINYBIRD_TOKEN environment variable.

If tb token is missing:
  Log an error "TINYBIRD_TOKEN env var is not set. Export it before running backfill scripts.".
  Exit the process with code 1.

“Query Tinybird SQL API directly — returns parsed rows as an array of objects.”
Tb SQL — given query; gives back a list of Record (async):
  Let query with format be "{trim query end} FORMAT JSONEachRow".
  Let URL be "{tb API URL}/v0/sql?q={encode uri component (query with format)}".
  Fetch (URL and headers: an object with authorization: "Bearer {tb token}"), and call the result response.
  If response's ok is missing:
    Let body be response's text.
    Fail with an error: "Tinybird SQL API error {response's status}: {body}".
  Let text be response's text.
  “JSONEachRow returns one JSON object per line”
  Give back text split on "
", after these steps:
    1. Turn each l into l without surrounding spaces
    2. Keep only those where l is not empty
    3. Turn each l into l parsed from JSON

To exec — given cmd:
  Exec sync (cmd, encoding: "utf-8", and stdio: "inherit").

Sleep — given ms (async):
  Give back a promise.

“Extract a single numeric value from the first row/column of a tbSql result.”
To extract number — given rows and col; gives back a number (or nothing):
  Let value be the first of rows' entry for col.
  If value is missing or value is missing, give back nothing.
  Let number be value as a number.
  Give back nothing if number is na n, otherwise number.

To format epoch ms — given epoch ms; gives back text:
  Give back epoch ms as a date as an ISO date string.

“Returns the MAX created_at among backfill ('read') rows, or null if none.”
To get max created at — given datasource; gives back a number (or nothing) (async):
  Let rows be a tb SQL:
    • query: "SELECT max(created_at) AS val FROM {datasource} WHERE __action = 'read'"
  Extract number (rows and col: "val"), and call the result number.
  Give back number if number is set and number is positive, otherwise nothing.

“Returns count of non-deleted rows in the datasource.”
To get row count — given datasource; gives back a number (async):
  Let rows be a tb SQL:
    • query: "SELECT count() AS val FROM {datasource} FINAL WHERE __action != 'delete'"
  Give back extract number (rows and col: "val"), or 0 if that's missing.

“CHUNK GENERATION (FORWARD — oldest → newest)”
To generate chunks forward — given start epoch ms, end epoch ms, and chunk days; gives back a list of Chunk:
  Let chunks be an empty list.
  Let chunk ms be chunk days times 24 times 60 times 60 times 1000.
  Let current start as start epoch ms.
  Keep repeating while current is less than end epoch ms:
    Let next be the smaller of current plus chunk ms and end epoch ms.
    Add an object with start epoch ms: current and end epoch ms: next to chunks.
    Set current to next.
  Give back chunks.

“COPY JOB EXECUTION”
To wait for copy jobs (async):
  Let max attempts be 60.
  Count attempt from 0 while attempt is less than max attempts:
    Exec capture, and call the result waiting:

##### server/tinybird/scripts/backfill_deductions_mv.ts
“Idempotent DOWNWARD backfill for events_deductions_hourly_mv. The MV deploys with BACKFILL skip (the deploy-time repopulate decodes the deductions JSON over ALL of `events` in one query and blows the deployment cap), so history is filled here in bounded chunks via the events_deductions_hourly_mv_backfill copy pipe on on-demand compute. - Fills downward: seam → yesterday → ... → target - Idempotent: resumes from min(hour) in the MV. The first forward-materialized bucket IS the seam, so no hardcoded cutoff — but it means the MV must have at least one forward row before the first run (else there is no seam to fill below, and the script refuses rather than guess). - All-time by default: custom_range is unbounded so any date can be queried. TARGET_DATE sits before the first deduction was ever written (~May 2026), so earlier windows would copy zero rows by construction anyway. Usage: bun scripts/backfill_deductions_mv.ts bun scripts/backfill_deductions_mv.ts --chunk-hours 12 bun scripts/backfill_deductions_mv.ts --target-date "2025-06-01 00:00:00" bun scripts/backfill_deductions_mv.ts --dry-run”

“CONFIGURATION”
Let copy pipe be "events_deductions_hourly_mv_backfill".

Let datasource be "events_deductions_hourly_mv".

“Before the first deduction was ever written to events. Earlier windows copy zero rows by construction — this is a data-existence floor, NOT a serving window: custom_range queries are unbounded. Override with --target-date if deductions ever get backfilled onto older events.”
Let target date be "2026-04-01 00:00:00".

“The deductions ARRAY JOIN fans out and pays a double JSONExtract per field, so default chunks are a day, not the wide chunks the no-fan-out backfills use.”
Let default chunk hours be 24.

Let max retries be 3.
Let retry delay ms be 5000.
Let delay between chunks ms be 2000.

“TYPES / ARGS”
Type Args: chunk hours, target date, and dry run.

Type Chunk: start and end.

To parse args — gives back an Args:
  Let args be an object with:
    • chunk hours: default chunk hours
    • target date: target date
    • dry run: false
  Count i from 2 while i is less than the number of process's argv:
    Let arg be process's argv's entry for i.
    If arg is "--chunk-hours" and process's argv's entry for i plus 1 is set:
      Set args' chunk hours to process's argv's entry for increase i by 1 as a whole number.
      If args' chunk hours is not a whole number or args' chunk hours is zero or less:
        Log an error "--chunk-hours must be a positive integer".
        Exit the process with code 1.
    Otherwise, if arg is "--target-date" and process's argv's entry for i plus 1 is set:
      Set args' target date to process's argv's entry for increase i by 1.
    Otherwise, if arg is "--dry-run":
      Set args' dry run to true.
    Otherwise, if arg is "--help" or arg is "-h":
      Log "
Idempotent DOWNWARD backfill for {datasource}

Options:
  --chunk-hours <n>     Hours per chunk (default: {default chunk hours})
  --target-date <date>  Oldest date to backfill to (default: {target date},
                        before the first deduction was ever written)
  --dry-run             Show the chunks without running anything

How it works:
  1. Derives the EXACT seam live, no flags: take the earliest MV bucket
     H = min(hour), read how many deduction rows the MV holds for it, then
     find the min timestamp of the LAST that-many deduction rows in raw
     events for that hour — the precise point forward materialization took
     over. Anything before it was inserted pre-promote and needs backfilling.
     Once a bucket has been backfilled it is complete, so the derived seam
     collapses to exactly H and continuation runs resume hour-aligned.
  2. Generates [start, end) chunks from there DOWN to the target. Chunks
     need no hour alignment: the read pipes re-sum per bucket, so a
     backfilled partial hour and a forward-materialized partial hour add up.
  3. Runs each through 'tb --cloud copy run {copy pipe} --on-demand-compute'.

Safe to re-run at any time, safe to change chunk size between runs.
".
      Exit the process with code 0.
  Give back args.

“stdin is ALWAYS ignored: with it piped, any interactive tb prompt (workspace, auth, region) renders invisibly and the script hangs forever. Ignored, the prompt read fails and the error surfaces instead. Queries also carry a timeout for the same reason; copy runs don't (chunks legitimately run long).”
Let query timeout ms be 300,000.

“Seam on the first run, resume point on every later one.”
To get min hour — gives back text (or nothing):

  Give back timestamp.

“The exact timestamp where forward materialization took over, derived live. The MV's earliest bucket H only contains what materialized forward (first run) or a complete backfilled hour (continuations). Either way, the min timestamp of the LAST mv-count deduction rows in raw events for that hour is the precise upper bound the backfill must fill up to: mid-bucket on a fresh deploy, exactly H once the bucket is complete. Relies on live traffic being timestamp-ordered at ingest; sub-second truncation of the boundary loses at most the pre-promote sliver inside the seam second.”
To derive seam — given min hour; gives back text:
  Let bucket start be the hour of min hour.
  Add hours (bucket start and 1), and call the result bucket end.
  Log "  Deriving the exact seam within that bucket...".
  Extract count, and call the result mv count:
    • a tb SQL:
      • "SELECT toInt64(sum(deduction_count)) FROM {datasource} WHERE hour = toDateTime('{bucket start}')"
  If mv count is 0:
    “The bucket came from min(hour), so it MUST contain rows — zero means the count query failed. Falling back to the hour boundary would silently skip everything between it and the actual promote time.”
    Log an error (with "
Refusing to run: the MV count query for the seam bucket failed or" followed by "
returned zero, which is impossible for the min(hour) bucket." plus "
Re-run when tb is responsive.").
    Exit the process with code 1.
  Extract timestamp, and call the result seam:
    • a tb SQL:
      • "SELECT min(t) FROM (" plus "SELECT timestamp AS t FROM events " plus "ARRAY JOIN JSONExtractArrayRaw(toString(deductions), 'list') AS d " plus "WHERE timestamp >= toDateTime('{bucket start}') " plus "AND timestamp < toDateTime('{bucket end}') " plus "AND JSONExtractString(JSONExtractString(d), 'balance_id') != '' " plus "ORDER BY t DESC LIMIT {mv count})"
  If seam is missing:
    Log an error (with "
Refusing to run: the seam query returned nothing (timeout or error)." followed by "
Falling back to the hour boundary would silently drop every event" plus "
inserted between it and the promote moment. Re-run when tb is" plus "
responsive.").
    Exit the process with code 1.
  “Truncate to whole seconds (the copy-pipe DateTime params carry no fraction). Flooring can only lose the pre-promote sliver within the seam second — never double-count.”
  Give back the first of seam split on ".".

To get row count — gives back a number:

##### server/tinybird/scripts/backfill_events.ts

“TARGET: The oldest event in Postgres. Backfill stops here.”
Let target date be "2025-01-30 00:00:00".

Let delay between chunks ms be 3000.

      Set args' chunk hours to process's argv's entry for increase i by 1 as a whole number.
    Otherwise, if arg is "--start-date" and process's argv's entry for i plus 1 is set:
      Set args' start date to process's argv's entry for increase i by 1.

      Set args' dry run to true.

  --chunk-hours <n>     Hours per chunk (default: {default chunk hours})
  --start-date <date>   Override end point (oldest date to backfill to)
  --dry-run             Show what would be done without executing
  --help, -h            Show this help message

How it works:
  1. Queries Postgres for MIN(timestamp) - the oldest event (our target)
  2. Queries Tinybird for MIN(timestamp) below cutoff - our current progress
  3. Generates chunks from resume point DOWN to target
  4. Processes chunks in reverse chronological order

Idempotency:
  - Safe to re-run at any time
  - Safe to change chunk size between runs
  - Automatically resumes from where it left off

Examples:
  bun scripts/backfill_events.ts
  bun scripts/backfill_events.ts --chunk-hours 12
  bun scripts/backfill_events.ts --dry-run
".
      Exit the process with code 0.
  Give back args.

##### server/tinybird/scripts/backfill_rollovers.ts
“Offset-based idempotent backfill for rollovers from Postgres to Tinybird. Rollovers have no created_at so we can't chunk by date. Pages through the full table with LIMIT + OFFSET ordered by id. Stops when a page returns fewer rows than page_size. Usage: bun scripts/backfill_rollovers.ts bun scripts/backfill_rollovers.ts --page-size 1000 bun scripts/backfill_rollovers.ts --offset 10000 bun scripts/backfill_rollovers.ts --dry-run”

“CONFIGURATION”
Let datasource be "rollovers".

Let copy pipe be "rollovers_backfill".
Let default page size be 5000.

“ARGUMENT PARSING”
To parse args — gives back an object with page size, offset override (optional), and dry run:
  Let args be an object with:
    • page size: default page size
    • offset override: nothing
    • dry run: false
  Count i from 2 while i is less than the number of process's argv:
    Let arg be process's argv's entry for i.
    If arg is "--page-size" and process's argv's entry for i plus 1 is set:
      Set args' page size to process's argv's entry for increase i by 1 as a whole number.
    Otherwise, if arg is "--offset" and process's argv's entry for i plus 1 is set:
      Set args' offset override to process's argv's entry for increase i by 1 as a whole number.
    Otherwise, if arg is "--dry-run":
      Set args' dry run to true.
    Otherwise, if arg is "--help" or arg is "-h":
      Log "
Offset-based backfill for rollovers

Usage: bun scripts/backfill_rollovers.ts [options]

Options:
  --page-size <n>   Rows per page (default: {default page size})
  --offset <n>      Start from this offset (default: 0)
  --dry-run         Print plan without executing
  --help, -h        Show this help
".
      Exit the process with code 0.
  Give back args.

    • query: "SELECT count() AS val FROM {datasource} FINAL WHERE __action != 'delete'"

To run page — given offset, page size, and retries (default max retries); gives back true/false (async):
  Count attempt from 1 while attempt is at most retries:
    Try the following:
      Wait for copy jobs.
      Exec:
        • cmd: "TB_VERSION_WARNING=0 tb --cloud copy run {copy pipe} --param offset="{offset}" --param page_size="{page size}" --wait"

    If anything fails (call the problem error):
      Let message be error's message, or error as text if that's empty.

“MAIN”

".

  Log "Starting offset: {offset}

    Log "DRY RUN — would run pages starting at offset" (with offset).
    Exit the process with code 0.
  Let page number start as 0.
  Keep repeating (until something stops it):
    Increase page number by 1.
    Log "=== Page {page number}: offset={offset} ===".
    Let start time be the current time.
    Run page (offset and page size: args' page size), and call the result success.
    Let duration be the current time minus start time divided by 1000, rounded.
    If success is missing:
      Log "✗ Page {page number} FAILED after {duration}s".
      Log "To resume from this point, re-run with:".

      Stop the loop.
    Run sleep (ms: delay between chunks ms).

##### server/src/utils/backoffDelayMs.ts
“Equal jitter: half the ceiling is always waited, so a caller riding out a dead connection keeps a guaranteed floor, and the other half is spread so several callers that failed together don't return in step.”
Backoff delay ms — given attempt, base delay ms, max delay ms, and jitter (default true):
  Let ceiling be the smaller of base delay ms times 2 to the power of attempt minus 1 and max delay ms.
  If jitter is true:
    Give back ceiling divided by 2 plus a random number times ceiling divided by 2.
  Otherwise:
    Give back ceiling.

##### server/src/utils/createRatePacer.ts

  To take slot (async):
    Let now be the current time.
    Let slot be next slot if next slot is after (given now), otherwise now.
    Add milliseconds (slot and min interval ms), and put the result in next slot.
    Let wait ms be difference in milliseconds (slot and now).
    If wait ms is positive, a promise.
  Give back an object with take slot.

Type RatePacer: a ReturnType.

##### server/src/utils/memory/memorySpikeProbe.ts
“arrayBuffers separates transport/buffer growth from ordinary object churn.”
Type MemorySnapshotMB: an object.

Type MemorySpikeReport: MemorySnapshotMB & {
	inFlightCount: num.
Let default ceiling mb be 4500.
Let default rise mb be 1500.
Let default baseline samples be 30.
Let default interval ms be 2000.
Let default max reports be 3.
Let max requests logged be 20.

To mb — given bytes; gives back a number:
  Give back bytes divided by 1024 divided by 1024 times 10, rounded divided by 10.

“Fires on a rapid RISE above the recent baseline, not just an absolute size — a process going 2GB to 4.4GB is the event; a steadily fat one is not.”
To create memory spike probe — given read memory mb, list in flight requests (as read in flight), report, ceiling mb, rise mb, baseline samples, max reports, and max requests logged:
  Let armed mean true.
  Let reports sent start as 0.
  Let history be an empty list.
  To sample:
    Read memory mb, and call the result memory.
    Let baseline mb be the smaller of all of history if history is not empty, otherwise memory's rss mb.
    Add memory's rss mb to history.
    If the number of history is more than baseline samples, take the first item off history.
    Let spiking mean memory's rss mb minus baseline mb is at least rise mb or memory's rss mb is at least ceiling mb.
    “Re-arm as soon as the condition clears, so one event yields one report.”
    If spiking is false, set armed to true.
    If any of these is true:
      • spiking is false or armed is false
      • reports sent is at least max reports
    then:
      Stop here.
    Set armed to false.
    Add 1 to reports sent.

##### server/src/utils/memory/forkRecycling/recyclePolicy.ts
Let mb be 1024 times 1024.

“JSC never returns allocator-retained pages, so forks only shed memory by dying; recycling above this RSS is the bound the engine cannot provide.”
Let fork recycle defaults be an object with:
  • rss threshold bytes: 2000 times mb
  • min age ms: 30 times 60,000
  • check interval ms: 30,000
  • drain timeout ms: 30,000
  • drain grace ms: 5000
  • max delay ms: 5 times 60,000
  • blackout before ms: 2 times 60,000
  • blackout after ms: 3 times 60,000

“Rolled once per fork: a private post-eligibility wait de-phases same-boot cohorts so a burst can't harvest a whole fleet's boots into one minute.”
To roll eligibility delay ms — given max delay ms and random (default math's random); gives back a number:
  Give back a random times max delay ms, rounded.

Let hour ms be 60 times 60,000.

Is within hourly blackout? — given now, before ms, and after ms; gives back true/false:
  Let into hour be now modulo hour ms.
  Give back whether into hour is less than after ms or into hour is at least hour ms minus before ms.

Ms until hourly blackout end — given now, before ms, and after ms; gives back a number:
  Let into hour be now modulo hour ms.
  If into hour is less than after ms, give back after ms minus into hour.
  If into hour is at least hour ms minus before ms, give back hour ms minus into hour plus after ms.
  Give back 0.

Should request recycle? — given rss bytes, threshold bytes, age ms, and min age ms; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether rss bytes is at least threshold bytes and age ms is at least min age ms.

“Sub-second timings would hot-loop checks or defeat the drain bounds, so intervals floor at 1s (thresholds/ages just need to be positive).”
Positive or — given raw and fallback; gives back a number:
  Let value be raw as a number.
  Give back value if value is a real number and value is positive, otherwise fallback.

Interval or — given raw and fallback; gives back a number:
  Give back the larger of 1000 and a positive or (raw and fallback).

“Zero is meaningful here: it disables the delay/blackout entirely.”
Non negative or — given raw and fallback; gives back a number:
  Let value be raw as a number.
  Give back value if value is a real number and value is zero or more, otherwise fallback.

“Serving forks per task — single-threaded loops, so this is capacity. Cap 6: above it, forks x ~2.3GB worst case (default 2000MB threshold + overshoot) + primary can OOM a 16GB task; revisit if the threshold drops.”
To get server fork count — gives back a number:
  Let value be the SERVER_FORK_COUNT environment variable as a number.
  If value is not a whole number or value is less than 1, give back 4.
  Give back the smaller of 6 and value.

    • drain grace ms: a non negative or:
      • the FORK_RECYCLE_DRAIN_GRACE_MS environment variable

##### server/src/utils/memory/forkRecycling/recycleCoordinator.ts
Type RecycleCycle: an object.

Let default replacement boot timeout ms be 120,000.

“Above the drainer's own max-drain (10min) + graceful-shutdown backstop.”
Let default drain completion timeout ms be 12 times 60,000.

“One recycle in flight at a time, and an invariant every path must hold: the serving fork count returns to N — no surplus, no deficit.”

  Let requested worker IDs be an empty set.
  Let expected exit worker IDs be an empty set.
  “Replacements killed for hanging: their eventual exit needs no respawn.”
  Let discarded worker IDs be an empty set.
  “Crash respawns still booting: drains wait for these so a recycle never stacks on top of reduced capacity.”
  Let booting respawn IDs be an empty set.
  Let respawn boot deadlines be an empty lookup table.
  Untrack booting respawn — given worker ID; gives back true/false:
    Let deadline be respawn boot deadlines' entry for worker ID.
    If deadline is set, Clear timeout (deadline).
    Remove worker ID from respawn boot deadlines.
    Give back remove worker ID from booting respawn IDs.
  Respawn tracked — given worker ID:

    If new worker ID is missing, stop here.
    Add new worker ID to booting respawn IDs.
    “A respawn that hangs before `listening` would defer drains forever.”
    Let deadline be after replacement boot timeout msms, do the following:
      If there is no untrack booting respawn (new worker ID), stop here.

        • "[ForkRecycle] Crash respawn {new worker ID} not listening after {replacement boot timeout ms}ms; killing and replacing it"
      Add new worker ID to discarded worker IDs.
      Kill worker (new worker ID).
      Respawn tracked (new worker ID).
      Release deferred drain if clear.
    Unref deadline.
    Record deadline under new worker ID in respawn boot deadlines.
  “Keyed by drained worker, not by cycle: a cycle can be replaced while its old fork is still draining, and that fork still needs its deadline.”
  Let drain completion deadlines be an empty lookup table.
  To clear drain completion deadline — given worker ID:
    Let deadline be drain completion deadlines' entry for worker ID.
    If deadline is set, Clear timeout (deadline).
    Remove worker ID from drain completion deadlines.
  To send drain now — given cycle:
    Set cycle's drain sent to true.
    Set cycle's drain deferred to false.

      • "[ForkRecycle] Replacement {cycle's replacement ID} listening; draining {cycle's old worker ID}"
    Send drain (cycle's old worker ID).
    “A lost drain message (or wedged drainer) must not hold the queue forever. The replacement is already serving, so past the worker's own drain bounds the old fork is killed and its exit completes the cycle.”
    Let deadline be after drain completion timeout msms, do the following:
      Remove cycle's old worker ID from drain completion deadlines.
      Log:
        • "[ForkRecycle] Worker {cycle's old worker ID} did not exit within {drain completion timeout ms}ms of its drain; killing it (replacement already serving)"
      Kill worker (cycle's old worker ID).
    Unref deadline.
    Record deadline under cycle's old worker ID in drain completion deadlines.
  To release deferred drain if clear:
    If booting respawn IDs' size is positive, stop here.
    If active cycle's drain deferred is true and active cycle's drain sent is false, Send drain now (active cycle).
  To clear boot deadline:
    If boot deadline is set, Clear timeout (boot deadline).
    Set boot deadline to nothing.
  To start cycle — given old worker ID:
    Fork replacement, and call the result replacement ID.
    Set active cycle to an object with:
      • old worker ID
      • replacement ID
      • drain sent: false
      • drain deferred: false
      • old exited: false
    Log:
      • "[ForkRecycle] Replacing worker {old worker ID}; replacement {replacement ID} booting"
    Set boot deadline to after replacement boot timeout msms, do the following:
      If active cycle is missing or active cycle's replacement ID is not replacement ID, stop here.
      If active cycle's drain sent is true, stop here.
      “Alive but never listening (hung init): without this deadline the cycle would hold the recycle queue forever.”
      Log:
        • "[ForkRecycle] Replacement {replacement ID} not listening after {replacement boot timeout ms}ms; killing and aborting recycle of {old worker ID}"
      Add replacement ID to discarded worker IDs.
      From active cycle, take old exited.
      Remove old worker ID from requested worker IDs.
      If old exited is true:
        Respawn tracked (replacement ID).
      Otherwise:
        Send abort (old worker ID).
      Kill worker (replacement ID).
      Start next pending cycle.
    Unref boot deadline.
  To start next pending cycle:
    Clear boot deadline.
    Set active cycle to nothing.
    Let next be take the first item off pending worker IDs.
    If next is set, Start cycle (next).
  Give back an object with:
    • handle recycle request, a function of worker ID that:
      If worker ID is in requested worker IDs, stop here.
      Add worker ID to requested worker IDs.
      If active cycle is set:
        Add worker ID to pending worker IDs.
        Stop here.
      Start cycle (worker ID).
    • handle worker listening, a function of worker ID that:
      If there is an untrack booting respawn (worker ID):
        Release deferred drain if clear.
        Stop here.
      If active cycle is missing or active cycle's replacement ID is not worker ID, stop here.
      If active cycle's drain sent is true, stop here.
      If active cycle's old exited is true:
        “The worker this replacement was for already crashed; the replacement simply takes its slot.”

        Start next pending cycle.
        Stop here.
      Clear boot deadline.
      If booting respawn IDs' size is positive:
        “A crash respawn is still booting; draining now would dip below N.”

        Log:
          • "[ForkRecycle] Replacement {worker ID} listening; deferring drain of {active cycle's old worker ID} until {booting respawn IDs' size} crash respawn(s) boot"

      Send drain now (active cycle).
    • handle worker exit, a function of worker ID that:
      Clear drain completion deadline (worker ID).
      “Every branch below must see a dead worker gone from the queue and its latch, or a later cycle forks a replacement for a fork that no longer exists. Branches still clear OTHER workers' latches themselves.”
      Let pending index be the position of worker ID in pending worker IDs (or -1).
      If pending index is not negative 1, run pending worker IDs' splice (pending index and 1).
      Remove worker ID from requested worker IDs.
      “A crash respawn dying while booting falls through to the plain-crash branch below (which respawns again); the deferred-drain release runs only after that branch has tracked the new respawn.”
      Let was booting respawn be an untrack booting respawn (worker ID).
      Let was expected be the result of a function that:
        If worker ID is in discarded worker IDs:
          “A hung replacement we already killed and accounted for.”
          Remove worker ID from discarded worker IDs.
          Give back whether true.
        If worker ID is in expected exit worker IDs:
          Remove worker ID from expected exit worker IDs.
          If active cycle's old worker ID is worker ID, Start next pending cycle.
          Log ("[ForkRecycle] Worker {worker ID} recycled").

        If active cycle's old worker ID is worker ID:
          If active cycle's drain deferred is true:
            “Replacement is already listening (drain deferred): the crash completes the cycle outright — a deferred drain to a dead worker would wait forever on an exit that already happened.”

            Start next pending cycle.
            Give back whether false.
          “Crashed before its drain: the already-booting replacement is its respawn, so forking again here would leave a surplus worker.”
          Set active cycle's old exited to true.
          Log:
            • "[ForkRecycle] Worker {worker ID} died mid-recycle; replacement {active cycle's replacement ID} adopts its slot"

            “Old worker is already draining and stays an expected exit; the dead replacement's slot is the one that needs refilling.”

            Give back whether false.
          “Died while booting. If the old worker still serves, no capacity was lost — abort and let it ask again later. If the old worker had crashed too, this replacement WAS its slot: refill it.”
          Log:
            • "[ForkRecycle] Replacement {worker ID} died before listening; aborting recycle of {old worker ID}"

          If active cycle's old exited is true:
            Respawn tracked (worker ID).
          Otherwise:
            Send abort (old worker ID).
          Start next pending cycle.
          Give back whether false.
        Respawn tracked (worker ID).
        Give back whether false.
      If was booting respawn, Release deferred drain if clear.
      Give back whether was expected.

##### server/src/utils/cacheUtils/normalizeFromSchema.ts
“Normalize data from Redis cache to fix cjson quirks. Different Redis providers handle cjson.encode differently: - Empty objects {} may become empty arrays [] - null values may become undefined - Empty arrays [] may become empty objects {} This function dynamically normalizes data based on a Zod schema structure.”
To get schema type — given schema; gives back text (or nothing):
  Give back schema's def's type.

To unwrap schema — given schema; gives back a z.ZodTypeAny:
  Get schema type (schema) → type.
  Let def be schema's def.
  If type is "optional", Unwrap schema (def's inner type), and give back the result.
  If type is "nullable", Unwrap schema (def's inner type), and give back the result.
  If type is "effects", Unwrap schema (def's schema), and give back the result.
  If type is "default", Unwrap schema (def's inner type), and give back the result.
  If type is "lazy" and def's getter is set, Unwrap schema (def's getter), and give back the result.
  Give back schema.

Is nullable? — given schema; gives back true/false:
  Get schema type (schema) → type.
  Let def be schema's def.
  If type is "nullable", give back whether true.
  If type is "optional", type is "effects", or type is "default":
    Let inner schema be def's inner type, or def's schema if that's empty.
    Give back whether inner schema is nullable.
  If type is "lazy" and def's getter is set, give back whether def's getter is nullable.
  Give back whether false.

Is empty object? — given value; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether all of these are true:
    • value is set
    • value is set
    • value is an object
    • value is not a list
    • the keys of value is empty

“Normalize cjson empty table to array.”
To normalize to array — given value; gives back a list of anything:
  If value is a list, give back value.
  If value is set, value is an object, and the keys of value is empty, give back an empty list.
  Give back an empty list.

“Dynamically normalize data based on Zod schema structure.”
To normalize from schema — given schema and data; gives back a T:
  If data is missing and schema is nullable, give back nothing.
  Unwrap schema (schema), and call the result unwrapped.
  Get schema type (unwrapped) → type.
  If type is "record":
    If data is a list and data is empty, give back an empty object.
    If data is set, data is an object, and data is not a list:
      Let value schema be unwrapped's def's value type.
      Let normalized be an empty object.
      For each key key in data:
        Normalize from schema (schema: value schema and data: data's entry for key), and put the result in normalized's entry for key.
      Give back normalized.
  If type is "array":
    If data is empty object, give back an empty list.
    If data is a list:
      Let item schema be unwrapped's def's element.
      Give back normalize from schema (schema: item schema and data: each item), for each item in data.
  If type is "object":
    “Upstash Lua cjson collapses empty `{}` to `[]`; treat as empty object so nested defaults still get applied on round-trip.”
    Let object data be an empty object if data is a list and data is empty, otherwise data.
    If object data is missing, object data is not an object, or object data is a list, give back data.
    Let shape be unwrapped's def's shape.
    Let normalized be an object with everything in object data.
    For each key key in shape:
      Normalize from schema (schema: shape's entry for key and data: normalized's entry for key), and put the result in normalized's entry for key.
    Give back normalized.
  Give back data.

##### server/src/queue/utils/deriveSqsQueueArn.ts

    Split local match into (skip), account ID, and queue name.
    Give back "arn:aws:sqs:{default aws region}:{account ID}:{queue name}".
  Fail with an error: "Cannot derive an SQS ARN from queue URL: {queue URL}".

##### server/src/queue/blueGreen/blueGreenGate.ts
“True iff this process should run worker/cron work right now. Fail-open everywhere except an explicit serviceArn mismatch: - **Non-AWS host** (no ECS metadata) → true. Lets the same code run on Railway / local / any non-ECS host. - **ECS metadata didn't surface a service ARN** (rare) → true. - **No `flightcontrolBlueArn` in S3 record** → true. - **`flightcontrolBlueArn === identity.serviceArn`** → true. - **Otherwise** → false (the only stop case). Service ARN is the sole gate signal. It's stable across deploys (unlike task definition revisions or image SHAs) — a fresh deploy to a service doesn't desync the gate.”
Is active slot? — given service name (as bg service name); gives back true/false:
  If has no aws task identity, give back whether true.
  Get active slot config (service name: bg service name) → config.
  If config's flightcontrol blue arn is missing, give back whether true.
  Get aws task identity → identity.
  If identity's service arn is missing, give back whether true.
  Give back whether identity's service arn is config's flightcontrol blue arn.

“Same logic as isActiveSlot, but returns a structured reason for diagnostics.”
To describe slot gate — given service name (as bg service name):
  If has no aws task identity, give back an object with allow poll: true and reason: "blue-green-disabled".
  Get active slot config (service name: bg service name) → config.
  If config's flightcontrol blue arn is missing, give back an object with allow poll: true and reason: "no-active-record".
  Get aws task identity → identity.
  If identity's service arn is missing, give back an object with allow poll: true and reason: "service-arn-unresolved".
  If identity's service arn is config's flightcontrol blue arn:
    Give back an object with:
      • allow poll: true
      • reason: "active"
      • matched on: "service-arn"
      • identity
  Give back an object with:
    • allow poll: false
    • reason: "idle"
    • identity
    • expected service arn: config's flightcontrol blue arn

##### server/src/queue/blueGreen/initBlueGreen.ts
“Wire blue-green into the worker process: 1. Resolve AWS task identity (idempotent — `awsTaskIdentity` also fires a fire-and-forget at module load, so identity is usually ready by the time this runs). 2. Start polling the S3 active-slot pointer. 3. Start the per-instance heartbeat writer. Polling is started here (not via the global edge-config registry) because `initBlueGreen` runs after `startAllEdgeConfigPolling` in the worker boot path. No-op when identity can't be resolved (local dev / non-ECS).”

  Resolve aws task identity → identity.

  Start blue green heartbeat (service name: "workers").
  If has aws task identity:
    Log "[BlueGreen] Worker identity resolved: serviceArn={identity's service arn, or "unknown" if that's missing} sha={identity's image sha, or "unknown" if that's missing}. Slot gate active.".

To shutdown blue green:
  Stop blue green heartbeat.
  Stop blue green slot store polling (service name: "workers").

    Fail with an error: "The dashboard webhook at this URL was just given the id {current's uid}; run the sync again" [error code's ambiguous webhook URL] (status 409).

    • run: a function giving back patch Svix's endpoint:
      • app ID
      • endpoint ID

      • URL: params' URL

      • disabled: params' disabled
  Give back the webhook of endpoint.

##### server/src/internal/stripeRead/actions/stripeGet/capStripeResponse.ts
Let max response bytes be 200,000.
Let truncation note be "Response exceeded {max response bytes} bytes and was truncated; narrow the request with params (limit, filters) or fewer pages.".
Type StripeList: an object.
Let list objects be the unique values of a list of "list" and "search_result".

Byte length — given value:
  Give back a byte length [Buffer] (value as JSON, or "" if that's missing).

Is Stripe list? — given body; gives back body is StripeList:
  Give back whether all of these are true:
    • body is an object
    • body is set
    • body's object as text is in list objects
    • body's data is a list

To truncate list — given list:
  Let budget be max response bytes minus a byte length (everything in list and data: an empty list) minus 500.
  Let kept be an empty list.
  Let used start as 0.
  For each item in list's data:
    Add a byte length (item) plus 1 to used.
    Stop the loop if used is more than budget.
    Add item to kept.
  Give back list, but with:
    • data set to kept
    • has more set to true
    • truncated set to true
    • truncation note set to truncation note

Cap Stripe response — given body; gives back anything:
  If a byte length (body) is at most max response bytes, give back body.
  If body is Stripe list, Truncate list (list: body), and give back the result.
  Give back an object with:
    • truncated: true
    • truncation note: truncation note
    • partial JSON: the first max response bytes divided by 2 of body as JSON

##### server/src/internal/stripeRead/actions/stripeGet/stripeGet.ts

  If first is not paginated list, give back a cap Stripe response (body: redact Stripe response (body: first)).

    • cards: a list of card

Let max cards be 3.

##### server/src/internal/slackUnfurl/slack/verify.ts
Let five minutes seconds be 60 times 5.

“Slack request signing: v0 HMAC-SHA256 over `v0:{timestamp}:{rawBody}`, with a 5-minute replay window. MUST run over the raw, unparsed body — so callers pass the exact string they read off the request.”
To verify slack signature — given raw body, timestamp, signature, and now seconds; gives back true/false:
  If timestamp is missing or signature is missing:
    Warn "[slack-unfurl] verify: missing timestamp/signature header".
    Give back whether false.
  “Fail closed: an empty secret would make the HMAC publicly computable.”
  If env's slack signing secret is missing:
    Warn "[slack-unfurl] verify: ALU_SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET unset".
    Give back whether false.
  Let ts be timestamp as a number.
  If ts is not a real number:
    Warn "[slack-unfurl] verify: non-numeric timestamp".
    Give back whether false.
  If the absolute value of now seconds minus ts is after five minutes seconds:
    Warn "[slack-unfurl] verify: stale timestamp (delta={now seconds minus ts}s) — check clock".
    Give back whether false.
  Let expected be "v0={update create hmac ("sha256" and env's slack signing secret) ("v0:{timestamp}:{raw body}")'s digest ("hex")}".
  Let a be the from expected [Buffer].
  Let b be the from signature [Buffer].
  Let ok be a timing safe equal (a and b) (only if the number of a is the number of b).
  If ok is missing:
    Warn "[slack-unfurl] verify: digest mismatch — SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET likely wrong (secret loaded, len={the number of env's slack signing secret})".
  Give back ok.

##### server/src/internal/slackUnfurl/render/cardToken.ts

  If anything fails:
    Give back nothing.
  Let a be the from expected [Buffer].
  Let b be the from sig [Buffer].
  If the number of a is not the number of b or there is no timing safe equal (a and b), give back nothing.
  Try the following:
    Let parsed be the from payload and "base64url" [Buffer] as text parsed from JSON.
    If parsed's org ID is not text or parsed's items is not a list, give back nothing.
    Let items be an empty list.
    For each item in the first max items of parsed's items:
      If all of these are true:
        • item's customer ID is text
        • item's env is app env's live or item's env is app env's sandbox
      then:
        Add an object with customer ID: item's customer ID and env: item's env to items.
    If items is empty, give back nothing.

  If anything fails, ignore it.
  Give back nothing.

##### server/src/internal/slackUnfurl/render/usageChartSvg.ts
“Build a compact area/line chart as an inline SVG data URI. takumi rasterises SVG images, so this gives a real smooth area chart (line + gradient fill) rather than chunky bars.”

</linearGradient></defs>

</svg>".
  Give back "data:image/svg+xml;utf8,{encode uri component (svg)}".

To round — given value; gives back a number:
  Give back value times 10, rounded divided by 10.

To get card data live — given org ID, customer ID, and env; gives back a CustomerCardData (or nothing) (async):
  “env comes from the URL path (/sandbox/... = sandbox, else live), so we resolve exactly that env. Every query is org+env-scoped → tenant-safe.”

  “Pin to the latest API version — otherwise getApiCustomerV2 emits this org's legacy response shape (e.g. v1.2) with no subscriptions/balances/flags keys.”

  “Invoices + expand each subscription's plan so we get real prices.”
  Set the expand to a list of customer expand's invoices and customer expand's subscriptions plan.
  “Aggregated subject (rolls entity-scoped products/entitlements/flags up to the customer) — this is what getApiCustomerV2 is built to consume.”
  Start with no full subject yet.
  Try the following:
    Load subject (customer ID), and put the result in full subject.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):

    Give back nothing.

  Let feature IDs be the keys of API customer's balances, or an empty object if that's missing.

  “Prices live at entity level for entity-scoped plans, so the customer view flattens them. Collect each entity's plan prices to widen the range.”

  Log (with "[slack-unfurl] resolved {customer ID} (org={org ID} env={env}): " plus "entities={entity count} subs={the number of API customer's subscriptions, or 0 if that's missing} " plus "balances={the number of feature IDs} flags={the number of the keys of API customer's flags, or an empty object if that's missing} " plus "invoices={the number of API customer's invoices, or 0 if that's missing} usagePoints={the number of usage's points, or 0 if that's missing}").

    • API customer

To fetch usage — given customer ID, full customer, and feature IDs; gives back an UsageSeries (or nothing) (async):
  If feature IDs is empty or full customer is missing, give back nothing.
  Let params be an object with:
    • customer ID: customer ID
    • interval: "7d"
    • event names: feature IDs
    • bin size: "day"
    • aggregate all: false
    • customer: full customer
  Try the following:
    Do these at the same time:
      • aggregate event actions (params) → formatted
      • get event actions count and sum (params) → totals
    Let points be formatted's data, with each row turned into an object with:
      • label: format period (row's period)
      • value: sum numeric except (row and "period")
    Let total be the total of totals' entry for each ID's sum, or totals' entry for each ID's count if that's missing, or 0 if that's missing across feature IDs.
    If every point in points satisfies: point's value is 0 and total is 0, give back nothing.
    Give back an object with:
      • feature label: the first of feature IDs if the number of feature IDs is 1, otherwise "Usage"
      • total
      • points
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Warn "[slack-unfurl] usage fetch failed: {error as text}".
    Give back nothing.

To sum numeric except — given row and exclude; gives back a number:
  Let total start as 0.
  For each key key and value value in row:
    Skip it if key is exclude.
    If value is a number:
      Add value to total.
    Otherwise, if value is text, value is not "", and value as a number is a valid number:
      Add value as a number to total.
  Give back total.

To format period — given period; gives back text:
  Let date be period as text as a date.
  If date as a timestamp is not a valid number, give back period as text.
  Give back date's to locale date string ("en-US", month: "short", and day: "numeric").

To format number — given value; gives back text:
  Give back value's to locale string ("en-US") if value is a real number, otherwise value as text.

Prettify — given ID; gives back text:
  Give back ID with /[_-]+/g replaced by " " with /\b\w/g replaced by a function of char giving back char in uppercase.

To plan status — given subscription; gives back a PlanStatus:
  If subscription's past due is set, give back "past_due".
  If subscription's canceled at is set, give back "canceled".
  If subscription's trial ends at is set, give back "trialing".
  Give back "active".

To format currency — given total and currency; gives back text:
  Let code be currency, or "usd" if that's missing in uppercase.
  Try the following:
    Format a new intl's number format ("en-US", style: "currency", and currency: code) (total), and give back the result.
  If anything fails:
    Give back "{format number (total)} {code}".

To plan price label — given subscription; gives back text:
  Let price be subscription's plan's price.
  If price is missing, give back "Add-on" if subscription's add on is set, otherwise "Free".
  If price's display's primary text is set:
    Give back a list of price's display's primary text and price's display's secondary text, after these steps:
      1. Drop empty values
      2. Join them with " "
  Give back "{format currency (price's amount and nothing)}/{price's interval}".

Type PriceEntry: an object.

Subscription price entry — given subscription; gives back a PriceEntry:
  Give back an object with:
    • amount: subscription's plan's price's amount, or 0 if that's missing
    • label: plan price label (subscription)

“Single price if every plan in the group prices the same, else "low – high".”
Price range label — given entries; gives back text:
  Let unique labels be the labels of entries without duplicates.
  If unique labels has at most 1 item, give back the first of unique labels, or "—" if that's missing.
  Let sorted be a copy of entries, sorted by amount (smallest first).
  Let low be the first of sorted.
  Let high be the last of sorted.
  Give back low's label if low's label is high's label, otherwise "{low's label} – {high's label}".

“Per-entity plan prices keyed by plan name. Entity-scoped plans price at the entity level, so the customer view flattens them — we query each entity's subject to recover the real prices and widen the range. Sequential to avoid racing on the shared ctx.”
To fetch entity plan prices — given customer ID and entities; gives back a map of text to list of PriceEntry (async):
  Let by name be an empty lookup table.
  For each entity in entities:
    Let entity ID be entity's ID.
    Skip it if entity ID is missing.
    Try the following:
      Load subject (customer ID and entity ID) → subject.
      Skip it if subject is missing.
      Get API customer v2 (full subject: subject), and call the result entity API.
      For each subscription in entity API's subscriptions:
        Let name be subscription's plan's name, or subscription's plan ID if that's missing.
        Let list be by name's entry for name.
        Add a subscription price entry (subscription) to list.
        Record list under name in by name.
    If anything fails (call the problem error):
      Warn "[slack-unfurl] entity {entity ID} price fetch failed: {error as text}".
  Give back by name.

To group plans — given subscriptions and entity prices; gives back a list of GroupedPlan:
  “Collapse by plan name. Count comes from the customer view; the price range spans both customer- and entity-level prices (lowest to highest).”
  Let groups be an empty lookup table.
  For each subscription in subscriptions:
    Let name be subscription's plan's name, or subscription's plan ID if that's missing.
    Let existing be groups' entry for name.
    If existing is set:
      Add 1 to existing's count.
      Add a subscription price entry (subscription) to existing's prices.
    Otherwise:
      Record an object with under name in groups:
        • name
        • count: 1
        • status: plan status (subscription)
        • prices: a list of a subscription price entry (subscription)
  Give back a copy of groups' values, with each group turned into the result of:
    Let entity list be entity prices' entry for group's name.
    Let prices be entity list if entity list is set and entity list is not empty, otherwise group's prices.
    Give back an object with:
      • name: group's name
      • count: group's count
      • status: group's status
      • price label: a price range label (prices)

To map balances — given balances; gives back a list of BalanceBar:
  Give back the key/value pairs of balances, with each item turned into the result of:
    If balance's unlimited is set:
      Give back an object with:
        • feature: a prettify (balance's feature ID, or feature ID if that's missing)
        • unlimited: true
        • fraction: 1
        • label: "Unlimited"
        • over: false
        • overage label: nothing
    Let granted be balance's granted.
    Let raw remaining be balance's remaining.
    Let overage be depending on whether raw remaining is negative:
      • if so: negative raw remaining
      • if not: the larger of 0 and balance's usage, or 0 if that's missing minus granted
    Let remaining be the larger of 0 and raw remaining.
    Let fraction be remaining divided by granted if granted is positive, otherwise 0.
    Give back an object with:
      • feature: a prettify (balance's feature ID, or feature ID if that's missing)
      • unlimited: false
      • fraction: the larger of 0 and the smaller of 1 and fraction
      • label: "{format number (remaining)} / {format number (granted)}"
      • over: whether overage is positive
      • overage label: "+{format number (overage)} over" if overage is positive (otherwise nothing)

To map to card — given org ID, API customer, entity count, usage, and entity prices; gives back a CustomerCardData:
  “plan_id -> display name, from the (expanded) subscriptions.”
  Let plan name by ID be an empty lookup table.
  For each subscription in API customer's subscriptions:
    Record subscription's plan's name, or a prettify (subscription's plan ID) if that's missing under subscription's plan ID in plan name by ID.
  Let invoices be a copy of API customer's invoices, after these steps:
    1. ␀them, sorted by this rule:
      • compare a and b by b's created at, or 0 if that's missing minus a's created at, or 0 if that's missing
    2. The first 3 of ␀them
    3. Turn each invoice into an object with:
      • products: invoice's plan IDs, after these steps, or "—" if that's empty:
        1. Turn each ID into plan name by ID's entry for ID, or a prettify (ID) if that's missing
        2. Join them with ", "
      • status: invoice's status, or nothing if that's missing
      • total label: format currency (invoice's total and invoice's currency)
      • created at: depending on whether invoice's created at is set:
        • if so: invoice's created at as a date as an ISO date string
        • if not: ""
  Give back an object with:
    • org ID
    • customer ID: API customer's ID, or "" if that's missing
    • name: API customer's name, or API customer's ID if that's missing, or "Customer" if that's missing
    • email: API customer's email, or nothing if that's missing
    • created at: API customer's created at as a date as an ISO date string
    • entity count
    • plans: group plans (API customer's subscriptions and entity prices)
    • balances: map balances (API customer's balances, or an empty object if that's missing)
    • feature flags: the keys of API customer's flags, or an empty object if that's missing, each passed through prettify
    • usage
    • invoices
