##### server/src/internal/sandboxes/copySandbox.ts
“Copies plans (products) + features from one named sandbox into another. Both sandboxes are sub-orgs of the master org (`is_sandbox=true`, `created_by = masterOrg.id`), each its own organization living in `AppEnv.Sandbox`. The caller (a master-org dashboard session) must own BOTH sandboxes; `getOwnedSandbox` applies the same 404-masking ownership check as `assertSandboxAccess`, so a missing or non-owned id is indistinguishable from a 404 and we never touch any org's live catalog.”
To copy sandbox for org — given master org, from sandbox ID, from org, from env (as from env arg), to sandbox ID, product IDs, and feature IDs; gives back an object with from sandbox and to sandbox (async):
  If from sandbox ID is set and from sandbox ID is to sandbox ID:
    Fail with an error: "Source and target sandboxes must be different" [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
  “Target is always an owned named sandbox. Source is either another owned sandbox or — for a copy started from the default sandbox / production — the master org at the caller's current env. Ownership failures fold into a uniform 404 so ids/ownership can't be probed.”
  Get owned sandbox (master org and sandbox ID: to sandbox ID), and call the result to sandbox.
  Start with no source org yet.
  Start with no from env yet.
  If from sandbox ID is set:
    Get owned sandbox (master org and sandbox ID: from sandbox ID), and put the result in source org.
    Set from env to app env's sandbox.
  Otherwise, if from org is set and from env arg is set:
    “The only non-sandbox source is the caller's own master org; never copy from an unrelated org into a sandbox this master owns.”
    If from org's ID is not master org's ID:
      Fail with an error: "Invalid copy source" [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
    Set source org to from org.
    Set from env to from env arg.
  Otherwise:
    Fail with an error: "No copy source specified" [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
  Let to env be app env's sandbox.
  Do these at the same time:
    • list [FeatureService] (org ID: source org's ID and env: from env) → from features
    • list [FeatureService] (org ID: to sandbox's ID and env: to env) → to features
  “No filter => whole-catalog copy. Any filter => copy only the requested products + features, plus every feature the requested products reference so a copied plan never lands with a dangling feature reference.”
  Let selective mean product IDs is set or feature IDs is set.
  Let features to copy start as from features.
  Let product IDs to copy start as product IDs.
  If selective is true:
    Let requested product IDs be product IDs.
    List full [ProductService] (org ID: source org's ID and env: from env), and call the result from products.
    “A requested product/feature that isn't in the source would otherwise no-op and still toast success; surface it instead.”
    Let source product IDs be the unique values of the IDs of from products.
    Let missing products be requested product IDs, keeping only those where ID is not in source product IDs.
    If missing products is not empty:
      Fail with an error: "Plan{"s" if missing products has more than 1 item, otherwise ""} not found in source: {missing products joined with ", "}" [error code's product not found] (status 404).
    Let requested feature IDs be feature IDs.
    Let source feature IDs be the unique values of the IDs of from features.
    Let missing features be requested feature IDs, keeping only those where ID is not in source feature IDs.
    If missing features is not empty:
      Fail with an error: "Feature{"s" if missing features has more than 1 item, otherwise ""} not found in source: {missing features joined with ", "}" [error code's feature not found] (status 404).
    “A requested variant pulls its base (via handleCopyProducts); a requested base pulls its variants here; the set's license plans come along too. Every pulled-in plan needs its item features copied.”
    Resolve source base plan IDs (from products and from products all: from products), and call the result base plan ID by variant ID.
    Let requested product ID set be the unique values of requested product IDs.
    Let pulled in variant IDs be an empty list.
    Let wanted product IDs be the unique values of requested product IDs.
    For each variant ID and base plan ID in base plan ID by variant ID:
      If base plan ID is in requested product ID set:
        Add variant ID to pulled in variant IDs.
        Add variant ID to wanted product IDs.
      If variant ID is in requested product ID set, add base plan ID to wanted product IDs.
    List plan license repo with license plan ID by parents, and call the result license links:
      • parent internal product IDs: from products, after these steps:
        1. Keep only those where product's ID is in wanted product IDs
        2. Take each one's internal ID
    For each link in license links:
      Add link's license plan ID to wanted product IDs.
    Let wanted feature IDs be the unique values of requested feature IDs.
    For each product in from products:
      Skip it if product's ID is not in wanted product IDs.
      Map to product v2 (product and features: from features), and take its items.
      For each item in items:
        If item's feature ID is set, add item's feature ID to wanted feature IDs.
    Add credit system metered feature IDs (features: from features and feature IDs: wanted feature IDs).
    Set features to copy to from features, keeping only those where f's ID is in wanted feature IDs.
    Set product IDs to copy to requested product IDs, plus pulled in variant IDs without duplicates.
  “Features first: products reference them, and credit systems reference metered features (handleCopyFeatures orders the batches accordingly).”
  Handle copy features:
    • to context: context, but with:
      • org set to to sandbox
      • env set to to env
      • features set to to features
    • from features: features to copy
  Handle copy products:
    • from org: source org
    • from env
    • to org: to sandbox
    • to env
    • product IDs: product IDs to copy
    • from features
  Invalidate products cache (org ID: to sandbox's ID and env: to env).
  Give back an object with from sandbox: source org and to sandbox.

##### server/src/internal/sandboxes/resetSandbox.ts
Let sandbox only message be "Only sandboxes can be reset".

“Empties the sandbox the caller's key belongs to: its migration drafts, customers, plans and features. Keys, settings and Stripe are left alone.”
To reset sandbox (async):
  From context, take org and env.
  If env is not app env's sandbox, fail with an error: sandbox only message [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
  Try the following:
    “One transaction: a failure part-way must not leave the sandbox holding customers whose plans are gone, with no way to retry back to the start.”
    Run transaction:
      • a function of transaction that:
        Let tx be transaction.
        “Drafts first: they reference the plans the product delete is about to take.”
        Delete migration drafts (context: context, but with DB set to tx).
        “Then the three deletes in FK order — customers hold products, products hold features; deleting a feature first would fail on the references to it.”
        Safe delete by org ID [CusService] (org ID: org's ID and env: app env's sandbox).
        Safe delete by org ID [ProductService] (org ID: org's ID and env: app env's sandbox).
        Safe delete by org ID [FeatureService] (org ID: org's ID and env: app env's sandbox).
  Either way, finally:
    “Even a rolled-back reset may have read rows into these caches, so they are dropped on both paths rather than left serving a stale catalog.”
    Invalidate products cache (org ID: org's ID and env: app env's sandbox).
    “Every secret key caches the org's features beside it, so a wiped sandbox would keep answering with the old catalog until that cache expires.”
    Clear org cache (org ID: org's ID and env: app env's sandbox).

##### server/src/internal/sandboxes/resolveSandboxActor.ts
Let owner role be "owner".

“A secret key without a user falls back to the org's owner — provisioning a sandbox needs a real user (Stripe, key owner).”
To find owner user — given org ID; gives back a User (or nothing) (async):
  Let rows be look up rows from member:
    • joined with user table on member's user ID is user table's ID
    • where all of these are true:
      • member's organization ID is org ID
      • member's role is owner role
    • sorted by the result of asc (member's created at)
    • at most 1 row(s)
  Give back the first of rows' user.

To resolve sandbox actor — given org, user, and auth type; gives back a User (async):
  If auth type is auth type's dashboard and user is set, give back user.
  If auth type is auth type's secret key:
    “A key minted through `atmn login` remembers who minted it; the org owner is the fallback for keys that carry no user.”
    If user is set, give back user.
    Find owner user (org ID: org's ID), and call the result owner.
    If owner is missing:
      Fail with an error: "This organization has no owner to act as. Create a sandbox from the dashboard instead." [error code's invalid request] (status 401).

“POST /sandboxes.copy Dashboard-only RPC that copies plans (products) + features into a named sandbox. The source is another owned sandbox, or — via fromMaster — the master org at the caller's current env (so you can seed a sandbox from the default sandbox or from production). Ownership is enforced inside copySandboxForOrg via the 404-masking getOwnedSandbox check, so a non-owned endpoint reads as a 404.”

  • handler: a function of c that:

    If from sandbox ID is to sandbox ID:
      Fail with an error: "Source and target sandboxes must be different" [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
    Copy sandbox for org:
      • master org
      • from sandbox ID
      • from org: master org if from master is set (otherwise nothing)
      • from env: env if from master is set (otherwise nothing)
      • to sandbox ID
      • product IDs
      • feature IDs
    Give back c's JSON (success).

##### server/src/internal/rewards/rewardUtils.ts
To construct reward — given internal ID, reward, org ID, env, and features (default an empty list):
  If reward's ID is missing or reward's name is missing:
    Fail with an error: "Reward ID and name are required" [error code's invalid reward].
  If reward's type is reward type's free product and reward's free product ID is missing:
    Fail with an error: "Select a free product" [error code's invalid reward].
  If reward's type is reward type's feature grant:
    If reward's entitlements is empty:
      Fail with an error: "Feature grant reward requires at least one entitlement" [error code's invalid reward].
    For each entitlement in reward's entitlements:
      If entitlement's internal feature ID is missing:
        Fail with an error: "Each entitlement must have a feature" [error code's invalid reward].
      Find feature by internal ID (features and internal ID: entitlement's internal feature ID), and call the result feature.
      “Boolean features grant on/off access, so they carry no allowance”
      Let is boolean mean feature's type is feature type's boolean.
      If all of these are true:
        • is not boolean
        • entitlement's allowance is missing or entitlement's allowance is negative
      then:
        Fail with an error: "Each entitlement must have a non-negative allowance" [error code's invalid reward].
  If get reward cat (reward) is reward category's discount, Parse [DiscountConfigSchema] (reward's discount config).
  Normalize promo codes (reward's promo codes) → promo codes.
  Let config data start as an empty object.
  If reward's type is reward type's free product:
    Set config data to an object with:
      • free product ID: reward's free product ID
      • discount config: nothing
      • entitlements: nothing
  Otherwise, if reward's type is reward type's feature grant:
    Set config data to an object with:
      • entitlements: reward's entitlements
      • discount config: nothing
      • free product ID: nothing
      • free product config: nothing
  Otherwise, if reward's type is reward type's percentage discount:
    Set config data to an object with:
      • discount config: reward's discount config
      • free product ID: nothing
      • entitlements: nothing
  Let new reward be an object with:
    • everything in reward
    • everything in config data
    • internal ID: internal ID, or generate ID ("rew") if that's empty
    • created at: the current time
    • org ID: org ID
    • env
    • promo codes: promo codes
  Give back new reward.

To get reward cat — given reward:
  If reward's type is reward type's free product or reward's type is reward type's feature grant:
    Give back reward category's free product.
  Give back reward category's discount.

Enum CouponType: AddInvoiceBalance, AddBillingCredits, and Standard.

To get coupon type — given reward:
  If reward is missing, give back nothing.
  Let config be reward's discount config.
  If config is missing, give back nothing.
  If config's apply to all is set and config should rollover:
    Give back coupon type's add invoice balance.
  Otherwise, if config should rollover:
    Give back coupon type's add billing credits.
  Give back coupon type's standard.

To get original coupon ID — given coupon ID:
  If coupon ID is missing, give back nothing.
  Let index be the position of "_roll_" in coupon ID (or -1).
  If index is not negative 1, give back coupon ID's substring (0 and index).
  Give back coupon ID.

To init reward Stripe prices — given prices (async):
  Get unique, and call the result internal product IDs:
    • prices, after these steps:
      1. Take each one's internal product ID
      2. Keep only those that pass not nullish
  List by internal IDs [ProductService] (internal IDs: internal product IDs), and call the result products.
  Let uninitialised be products, keeping only those where product has missing Stripe resources for.
  For every product in uninitialised, all at the same time:
    init product in Stripe (product and include live)
  “initProductInStripe writes the new ids onto its own rows, not the caller's.”
  For each price in prices:
    Let product be the first p in products where p's internal ID is price's internal product ID.
    Skip it if product is missing.
    Set price's product to product.
    Let initialised be the one in product's prices whose ID is price's ID.
    If initialised is set, set price's config to initialised's config.

To format reward — given reward:
  If reward is missing, give back "".
  Let discount string be depending on whether reward's type is reward type's percentage discount:
    • if so: "{reward's discount config's discount value}%"
    • if not: "{reward's discount config's discount value} off"
  If reward's discount config's apply to all is set:
    Give back "{discount string} off all products".
  Otherwise, if reward's discount config's price IDs is set:
    Give back "{discount string} off prices: {reward's discount config's price IDs joined with ", "}".
  Give back discount string.

To get amount after reward — given amount, reward, subscription discounts, and currency:
  If there is a first d in subscription discounts where all of these are true:
    • d's source's coupon is set
    • d's source's coupon is not text
    • d's source's coupon's ID is reward's ID
  then:
    Give back amount.
  If reward's type is reward type's percentage discount:
    Let discount value be reward's discount config's discount value, or 0 if that's missing.
    Let Autumn discount value be the Autumn amount of Stripe (amount: discount value and currency).
    Let discount ratio be 1 minus Autumn discount value.
    Give back amount times discount ratio.
  Otherwise, if reward's type is reward type's fixed discount:
    Let discount amount be reward's discount config's discount value, or 0 if that's missing.
    Give back amount minus discount amount.
  Give back amount.

Discount applies → price — given discount, product, and price:
  Let coupon be discount's source's coupon.
  If coupon is missing or coupon is text, give back whether true.
  Let applies to be coupon's applies to's products.
  If applies to is missing, give back whether true.
  If price is fixed, give back whether applies to has a Stripe product ID where Stripe product ID is product's processor's ID.
  Give back whether applies to has a Stripe product ID where Stripe product ID is price's config's Stripe product ID.

To get unused amount after discount — given amount, discount amounts, and ratio:
  Let amount after discount start as the absolute value of amount.
  For each discount amount in discount amounts:
    Let applied discount be discount amount's amount, or 0 if that's empty divided by 100 times ratio.
    Set amount after discount to amount after discount minus applied discount.
  Give back amount after discount.

To get amount after Stripe discounts — given price, amount, product, Stripe discounts, and currency:
  Let amount after discount start as amount.
  For each discount in Stripe discounts:
    Skip it if there is no price of discount applies (discount, product, and price).
    Let coupon be discount's source's coupon.
    Skip it if coupon is missing or coupon is text.
    If coupon's percent off is set:
      Let ratio be 1 minus coupon's percent off divided by 100.
      Set amount after discount to amount after discount times ratio.
    Otherwise, if coupon's amount off is set:
      “must do some ratio ting here...”
      Let Autumn discount amount be the Autumn amount of Stripe (amount: coupon's amount off and currency).
      Set amount after discount to amount after discount minus Autumn discount amount.
  Give back amount after discount.

“Build a RewardProgram object from creation input”
To construct reward program — given reward program data, org ID, and env:
  Let reward program be reward program data, but with:
    • internal ID set to generate ID ("rs")
    • unlimited redemptions set to false
    • created at set to the current time
    • org ID set to org ID
    • env set to env
  Give back reward program.

“═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ Referral helpers (moved from referralUtils.ts) ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════”
Let referral response codes be an object with:
  • owns product: "has_product_already"
  • success: "success"
  • unknown: "unknown"
  • not configured: "not_configured"
  • internal error: "internal_error"

“Generate a random 6-character alphanumeric referral code”
To generate referral code:
  Let chars be "ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789".
  Let code length be 6.
  Let code start as "".
  Count i from 0 while i is less than code length:
    Add the character at a random number times the number of chars, rounded down in chars to code.
  Give back code.

“Whether the referrer receives the reward”
Received by referrer — given received by:
  Give back whether received by is reward received by's referrer or received by is reward received by's all.

“Whether the redeemer receives the reward”
Received by redeemer — given received by:
  Give back whether received by is reward received by's all.

##### server/src/internal/rewards/actions/redeemPromoCode.ts

    • internal customer ID: full customer's internal ID
    • reward internal ID: reward's internal ID
  If existing redemption is set:
    Fail with an error: "Customer "{customer ID}" has already redeemed this reward" [error code's customer already redeemed referral code] (status 400).
  “4.5. First-time restriction (no Stripe customer → necessarily first-time)”
  If promo code's first time transaction is set and full customer's processor's ID is set:
    Create Stripe client (org and env) → Stripe client.
    Assert first time Stripe customer:
      • Stripe client
      • Stripe customer ID: full customer's processor's ID
      • promo code: code

  “6. Record the redemption”

      • ID: generate ID ("rr")

      • reward internal ID: reward's internal ID

      • referral code ID: nothing
      • internal reward program ID: nothing
      • triggered: true
      • applied: true
      • redeemer applied: true
      • created at: the current time
      • updated at: the current time
  “8. Return result”

    • reward ID: reward's ID
    • entitlements granted: reward's entitlements, with each entitlement turned into the result of:
      Find feature by internal ID, and call the result feature:
        • features: the features
        • internal ID: entitlement's internal feature ID

        • feature ID: feature's ID, or entitlement's internal feature ID if that's missing
        • balance: entitlement's allowance, or 0 if that's missing

##### server/src/internal/rewards/actions/triggerCheckoutReward.ts
“Process checkout-triggered reward redemptions (called from job queue)”
To run Trigger checkout reward — given payload (async):
  From context, take org and env.
  Try the following:
    From payload, take customer, product, and subscription ID.
    Create Stripe client (org and env) → Stripe client.
    “Check if redemption exists”
    Get redemption repo by customer (internal customer ID: customer's internal ID and no triggered), and call the result redemptions.
    For each redemption in redemptions:
      If any of these is true:
        • redemption is missing
        • redemption's reward program's when is not reward Trigger event's checkout
      then:
        Log "No redemption found or reward program not set to checkout, skipping".
        “BUG FIX: was `return` which exited the entire function — should be `continue`”
        Move on to the next one.
      From redemption, take reward program and referral code.
      From reward program, take reward.
      Log "--------------------------------".
      Log "CHECKING FOR CHECKOUT REWARD, ORG: {org's slug}".
      Log "Redeemed by: {customer's name} ({customer's ID}) for referral program: {reward program's ID}".
      Log "Referral code: {referral code's code} ({referral code's ID})".
      Log "Products: {reward program's product IDs joined with ", "}, {reward program's reward's free product ID}".
      If product's ID is not in reward program's product IDs:
        Log "Product {product's name} ({product's ID}) not included in referral program, skipping".
        Skip it if reward program's reward's free product ID is not product's ID.
      “Check for trial”
      Let has trial mean false.
      If subscription ID is set:
        Retrieve Stripe client's subscriptions (subscription ID), and call the result subscription.
        Set has trial to whether subscription's status is "trialing".
      If has trial:
        Log "Subscription is on trial, not triggering reward".
        “BUG FIX: was `return` which exited the entire function — should be `continue`”
        Move on to the next one.
      “Get redemption count”
      Get referral code repo redemption count (referral code ID: referral code's ID) → redemption count.
      If redemption count is at least reward program's max redemptions:
        Log "Max redemptions reached, not triggering latest redemption".
        “BUG FIX: was `return` which exited the entire function — should be `continue`”
        Move on to the next one.

An interval variant simply means a product is a quarterly, semi-annual, or annual version of a base monthly product. 

If the given product is a variant of another product (which we'll call the base variant), please return the id of the base variant in the base_variant_id field.

To determine if a product is an interval variant, please follow these guidelines:

1. Look at the name of the product. If it contains a word like "annual", "yearly", etc. and the name resembles another product, it's a variant.
- Example of this: "Pro (Annual)" is a variant of "Pro".

2. If the product has a similar name to another product, but interval is different, it's probably a variant.

4. If the current product is not a variant of any existing product, return null.
".

<product_to_detect>

  {filtered existing products, after these steps}

{variables}"

##### server/src/internal/products/product-items/supersedeUnlimitedItems.ts
Is unlimited item? — given item:
  Give back whether item's included usage is infinite.

“A free grant with a countable allowance, which an unlimited grant would hide. Priced items are excluded: an unlimited grant plus a metered overage price is a legitimate shape, and the grant is what keeps that usage unbilled.”
Grants finite allowance? — given item:
  Give back whether item is not unlimited and item is feature.

“Global and entity-scoped grants for one feature are independent balances.”
Item → grant scope — given item:
  If item's feature ID is set:
    Give back "{item's feature ID}|{item's entity feature ID, or "" if that's missing}".
  Otherwise:
    Give back "".

“Drops an unlimited item when the same feature also has a finite grant. Duplicate validation only catches same-interval collisions, so an unlimited lifetime grant survives beside a finite monthly one. The customer then reads as unlimited and the finite allowance is unreachable, which makes setting an allowance on a previously-unlimited feature look like a no-op.”
Supersede unlimited items — given items; gives back a list of ProductItem:
  Let finite scopes be the unique values of items, after these steps.
  If finite scopes' size is 0, give back items.
  Give back items, keeping only those where item is not unlimited or the grant scope of item is not in finite scopes.

##### server/src/internal/products/prices/billingIntervalUtils.ts
To subtract billing interval unix — given unix timestamp, interval, and interval count (default 1):
  Let date be a new UTC date (unix timestamp).
  Let subtracted date start as date.
  Depending on interval:
    • If it is billing interval's week:
      Set subtracted date to subscription weeks (date and 1 times interval count).
    • If it is billing interval's month:
      Set subtracted date to subscription months (date and 1 times interval count).
    • If it is billing interval's quarter:
      Set subtracted date to subscription months (date and 3 times interval count).
    • If it is billing interval's semi annual:
      Set subtracted date to subscription months (date and 6 times interval count).
    • If it is billing interval's year:
      Set subtracted date to subscription years (date and 1 times interval count).
    • For anything else:
      Fail with an error: "Invalid billing interval: {interval}".
  Give back subtracted date as a timestamp.

To add billing interval unix — given unix timestamp, interval, and interval count (default 1):
  If interval is missing or interval count is missing, give back unix timestamp.
  Let date be a new UTC date (unix timestamp).
  Let added date start as date.
  Depending on interval:
    • If it is billing interval's week:
      Add weeks (date and 1 times interval count), and put the result in added date.
    • If it is billing interval's month:
      Add months (date and interval count), and put the result in added date.
    • If it is billing interval's quarter:
      Add months (date and 3 times interval count), and put the result in added date.
    • If it is billing interval's semi annual:
      Add months (date and 6 times interval count), and put the result in added date.
    • If it is billing interval's year:
      Add years (date and 1 times interval count), and put the result in added date.
    • For anything else:
      Fail with an error: "Invalid billing interval: {interval}".
  Give back added date as a timestamp.

To get next start of month unix — given interval and interval count:
  Add interval for proration, and call the result next billing cycle:
    • unix timestamp: the current time
    • interval config: an object with interval and interval count
  “Subtract till it hits first”
  Let date be a new UTC date (next billing cycle).
  Start of month (date), and call the result first day of month.
  Set hours (first day of month and 12), and call the result twelve o clock.
  Give back twelve o clock as a timestamp.

To get aligned interval unix — given align with unix, interval, interval count, now, and always return:
  “alignWithUnix = addSeconds(alignWithUnix, 20).getTime();”
  Let next cycle anchor unix start as align with unix.
  Set now to now, or the current time if that's empty.
  Add interval for proration, and call the result natural billing date:
    • unix timestamp: now
    • interval config: an object with interval and interval count
  Let max iterations be 10,000.
  Let iterations start as 0.
  Let print logs mean false.
  If print logs is true:
    Log "Natural billing date:" (with format unix to date time (natural billing date)).
    Log "Next cycle anchor unix:" (with format unix to date time (next cycle anchor unix)).
  Keep repeating (until something stops it):
    Subtract billing interval unix (unix timestamp: next cycle anchor unix, interval, and interval count), and call the result subtracted unix.
    If print logs is true, log "Subtracted unix:" (with format unix to date time (subtracted unix)).
    Stop the loop if subtracted unix is at or before now.
    Set next cycle anchor unix to subtracted unix.
    Increase iterations by 1.
    If iterations is more than max iterations, fail with an error: "Max iterations reached".
  Let billing cycle anchor unix start as next cycle anchor unix.
  If print logs is true:
    Log "Next cycle anchor:" (with format unix to date time (next cycle anchor unix)).
    Log "Now:" (with format unix to date time (now)).
    Log "--------------------------------".
  Let anchor and natural diff be difference in seconds (natural billing date and next cycle anchor unix).
  “For insurance, also means you can't set billing cycle anchor to a minute in the future...”
  Let anchor and now diff be the absolute value of difference in seconds (now and next cycle anchor unix).
  If anchor and natural diff is less than 60 or anchor and now diff is before 20:
    If always return is true:
      Give back natural billing date.
    Otherwise:
      Set billing cycle anchor unix to nothing.
  Give back billing cycle anchor unix.

To subtract from unix till aligned — given target unix and original unix:
  Let target date be a new UTC date (target unix).
  Let original date be a new UTC date (original unix).
  “Get target date components”
  Get date (target date), and call the result target day.
  Get hours (target date), and call the result target hours.
  Get minutes (target date), and call the result target minutes.
  Get seconds (target date), and call the result target seconds.
  Get date (original date), and call the result original day.
  “Create aligned date using date-fns functions”
  Let aligned date start as original date.
  “If target day is greater than original day, subtract a month”
  If target day is more than original day, set aligned date to subscription months (aligned date and 1).
  “Calculate last day of the month to handle month length differences”
  Get a new UTC date (get aligned date full year, get aligned date month plus 1, and 0) date, and call the result last day of month.
  “Apply target day (capped to last day of month) and time components”
  Set date (aligned date and the smaller of target day and last day of month), and put the result in aligned date.
  Set hours (aligned date and target hours), and put the result in aligned date.
  Set minutes (aligned date and target minutes), and put the result in aligned date.
  Set seconds (aligned date and target seconds), and put the result in aligned date.
  Get time (aligned date), and give back the result.

“Subtracts an interval from a period end, preserving anchor-based end-of-month behavior Uses the anchor date (unixTimestamp) to determine if end-of-month logic should apply e.g. Sep 30 anchor -> Aug 30, Jul 30, Feb 28/29 (follows Stripe behavior)”
To subtract interval for proration — given unix timestamp, interval, and interval count (default 1):
  Let anchor date be a new UTC date (unix timestamp).
  Get date (anchor date), and call the result anchor day.
  To preserve time — given d:
    Let preserved start as a new UTC date (d as a timestamp).
    Set preserved to a new UTC date (set hours (preserved and get hours (anchor date)) as a timestamp).
    Set preserved to a new UTC date (set minutes (preserved and get minutes (anchor date)) as a timestamp).
    Set preserved to a new UTC date (set seconds (preserved and get seconds (anchor date)) as a timestamp).
    Give back preserved.
  To set to anchor day or end of month — given d:
    Get a new UTC date (get d full year, get d month plus 1, and 0) date, and call the result last day of target month.
    “If the anchor day doesn't exist in the target month, go to the last day of that month This follows Stripe's behavior: Sep 30 -> Feb 28, Jul 31 -> Feb 28, etc.”
    Let target day be the smaller of anchor day and last day of target month.
    Give back a new UTC date (set date (d and target day) as a timestamp).
  Depending on interval:
    • If it is billing interval's week:
      Let subscription be a new UTC date:
        • subscription weeks (anchor date and 1 times interval count) as a timestamp
      Get time (subscription), and give back the result.

      Preserve time (subscription), and put the result in subscription.
      Get time (subscription), and give back the result.
    • If it is billing interval's quarter:
      Let subscription start as a new UTC date:
        • subscription months (anchor date and 3 times interval count) as a timestamp
      Set to anchor day or end of month (subscription), and put the result in subscription.
      Preserve time (subscription), and put the result in subscription.
      Get time (subscription), and give back the result.
    • If it is billing interval's semi annual:

        • subscription months (anchor date and 6 times interval count) as a timestamp
      Set to anchor day or end of month (subscription), and put the result in subscription.
      Preserve time (subscription), and put the result in subscription.
      Get time (subscription), and give back the result.
    • If it is billing interval's year:

        • subscription years (anchor date and 1 times interval count) as a timestamp

      Preserve time (subscription), and put the result in subscription.
      Get time (subscription), and give back the result.
    • For anything else:
      Fail with an error: "Invalid billing interval: {interval}".

##### server/src/internal/products/prices/billingIntervalUtils2.ts
To add interval to anchor — given interval config, anchor unix, and now:
  Set now to now, or the current time if that's empty.
  Let next interval start as anchor unix.
  Count i from 0 while i is less than 50:
    If next interval is after now, give back next interval.
    Add interval for proration (unix timestamp: next interval and interval config), and put the result in next interval.
  Add interval for proration (unix timestamp: anchor unix and interval config), and give back the result.

Is less than equals? — given a and b:
  “Check if a is <= now. return true if a is ~ same as b (maybe by a couple of hours?)”
  Let a unix be a as a timestamp.
  Let b unix be b as a timestamp.
  If a unix is less than b unix plus to milliseconds' hours (1), give back whether true.
  Give back whether false.

To subtract interval from anchor — given anchor, interval config, and now:
  Let current anchor start as anchor.
  Set now to now, or the current time if that's empty.
  Count i from 0 while i is less than 50:
    Subtract interval for proration, and call the result new anchor:
      • unix timestamp: current anchor
      • interval: interval config's interval
      • interval count: interval config's interval count, or 1 if that's missing
    “Return anchor before it goes below now”
    If a new UTC date (new anchor) is less than equals (given b: a new UTC date (now)), give back current anchor.
    Set current anchor to new anchor.
  Give back now.

“Finds the period start by advancing from anchor until reaching the period that contains targetEnd Returns the start of the period that ends at or after targetEnd”
To get period start for end — given anchor, interval config, and target end:
  Let period start start as anchor.
  Add interval for proration (unix timestamp: anchor and interval config), and call the result period end.
  “Keep advancing until we find the period containing targetEnd”
  Let max iterations be 50.
  Let iterations start as 0.
  Keep repeating while period end is before target end and iterations is less than max iterations:
    Set period start to period end.
    Add interval for proration (unix timestamp: period end and interval config), and put the result in period end.
    Increase iterations by 1.
  Give back period start.

To get aligned unix — given anchor, interval config, and now:
  Set now to now, or the current time if that's empty.
  If anchor is at or before now:
    Add interval to anchor (interval config, anchor unix: anchor, and now), and give back the result.
  Subtract interval from anchor (anchor, interval config, and now), and give back the result.

##### server/src/internal/products/prices/priceUtils/convertPrice.ts

    Give back billing interval's one off.
  Otherwise, if interval is billing interval's quarter:

    Give back "{billing interval's month}-{final count}".
  Otherwise, if interval is billing interval's semi annual:

##### server/src/internal/products/handlers/handleCopyEnvironment/handleCopyProducts.ts
“Copies products from one (org, env) into another (org, env). Generalised from the original sandbox→live copy so the source and target may be different organizations (e.g. two sandbox sub-orgs of the same master org). Processor-specific ids (price/entitlement ids, price_config) are stripped so the target gets a clean copy, and the write context is rebuilt around an explicit `toOrg`/`toEnv`.”

  “1. Load both sides”

    • provided from features, or list [FeatureService] (org ID: from org's ID and env: from env) if that's missing → from features
    • list [FeatureService] (org ID: to org's ID and env: to env) → to features
    • list full [ProductService] (org ID: from org's ID and env: from env) → from products all
    • list full [ProductService] (org ID: to org's ID and env: to env) → to products
  “undefined => copy every product (original behavior); a list (incl. empty) => only those ids.”
  Let requested from products be depending on whether product IDs is set:
    • if so: from products all, keeping only those where p's ID is in product IDs
    • if not: from products all
  “2. Build the copy set: variants pull their bases in, parents pull their license plans in. A same-id target plan is never pulled over.”
  Resolve source base plan IDs (from products: requested from products and from products all), and call the result base plan ID by variant ID.
  Let from products be with license plan products:
    • from products: with pulled in plans:
      • from products: requested from products
      • from products all
      • to products
      • plan IDs: a copy of base plan ID by variant ID's values
    • from products all
    • to products
  Let to context be context, but with org set to to org, features set to to features, and env set to to env.
  Let target IDs be the unique values of the IDs of to products.
  Let from products v2 be a to copy ready products v2 (products: from products and features: from features).
  “3. Copy bases first: a variant's link resolves against the target env, so its base must exist there before the variant is copied.”
  Let base products v2 be from products v2, keeping only those where p's ID is not in base plan ID by variant ID.
  For every from product v2 in base products v2, all at the same time:
    upsert copied plan (to context, from product v2, and target IDs)
  “4. Copy variants, linked to their bases in the target env”
  Let variant products v2 be from products v2, keeping only those where p's ID is in base plan ID by variant ID.
  Copy env variant plans:
    • to context
    • variant products v2
    • base plan ID by variant ID
    • target IDs
  “5. Init created variants in Stripe after their base's family exists. inIds bypasses the products cache — the copy ops' invalidations land async, so a plain listFull can still see the pre-copy (empty) snapshot.”

    • to context
    • from products
    • to products
    • copied to products

      • if so: a copy of entries, sorted by this rule:
        • compare a and b by how a's feature ID, or "" if that's missing as text compares alphabetically to b's feature ID, or "" if that's missing as text
      • if not: entries

##### server/src/internal/product/actions/previewUpdatePlan/detectVariantConflicts.ts
Interval of — given item; gives back text:
  Give back item's price's interval, or item's reset's interval if that's missing, or "none" if that's missing.

Base prices equal — given a and b; gives back true/false:
  If a is missing and b is missing, give back whether true.
  If a is missing or b is missing, give back whether false.
  Give back whether all of these are true:
    • a's amount is b's amount
    • a's interval is b's interval
    • a's interval count, or 1 if that's missing is b's interval count, or 1 if that's missing

To group by feature — given items; gives back a map of text to list of ApiPlanItemV1:
  Let map be an empty lookup table.
  For each item in items:
    Let list be map's entry for item's feature ID.
    Add item to list.
    Record list under item's feature ID in map.
  Give back map.

To filter for item — given item; gives back a PlanItemFilter:
  Let filter be an object with feature ID: item's feature ID.
  If item's price's billing method is set, set filter's billing method to item's price's billing method.
  Let interval be item's price's interval, or item's reset's interval if that's missing.
  If interval is set, set filter's interval to interval.
  Let interval count be item's price's interval count, or item's reset's interval count if that's missing.
  If interval count is set, set filter's interval count to interval count.
  Give back filter.

“Conflicts the variant owner should resolve manually before propagating: - different_interval: variant holds the feature at an interval the edit doesn't touch — propagation adds a duplicate item. - value_divergence: variant customized the feature's value relative to the base — propagation would silently overwrite it. - base_price_divergence: variant customized its base price — a base price edit would overwrite it.”
To detect variant conflicts — given current base plan, edited base plan, diff, variant plan, and features; gives back a list of PlanUpdatePreviewVariantConflict:
  Let changed feature IDs be the unique values of one list combining.
  Group by feature (edited base plan's items), and call the result edited by feature.
  Group by feature (variant plan's items), and call the result variant by feature.
  Let base old by match key be a lookup table built from current base plan's items, each turned into a list of compose match key (item) and item.
  Let edited by match key be a lookup table built from edited base plan's items, each turned into a list of compose match key (item) and item.
  “Match keys whose item the edit actually changes — only these get overwritten on propagate. A customization on an untouched item (e.g. the variant's included amount when only the price changed) is left intact.”
  Let changed match keys be an empty set.
  For each key and edited item in edited by match key:
    Let base old be base old by match key's entry for key.
    If base old is missing or there is no items equal (edited item and base old), add key to changed match keys.
  For each key in base old by match key's keys:
    If key is not in edited by match key, add key to changed match keys.
  Let conflicts be an empty list.
  For each feature ID in changed feature IDs:
    “Feature removed from the base entirely — propagating the removal is clean, so it's never a conflict.”
    Let edited list be edited by feature's entry for feature ID.
    Skip it if edited list is empty.
    Let variant list be variant by feature's entry for feature ID.
    Skip it if variant list is empty.
    “clean add into variant”
    Find feature by ID (features and feature ID), and call the result feature.
    Let edited intervals be the unique values of edited list, each passed through interval of.
    Let variant intervals be the unique values of variant list, each passed through interval of.
    Let shares interval mean a copy of variant intervals has a iv where iv is in edited intervals.
    If shares interval is false:
      “Unpriced non-consumables have no real interval, so propagation maps cleanly; a priced item propagates as a duplicate at the edit's interval.”
      Let has priced item mean any of these is true:
        • edited list has a item where item's price is set
        • variant list has a item where item's price is set
      Let is clean non consumable entitlement mean feature is set, feature is not consumable, and has no priced item.
      If is not clean non consumable entitlement:
        Add an object with to conflicts:
          • item filter: filter for item (the first of variant list)
          • feature name: feature's name
          • reason: "different_interval"
      Move on to the next one.
    Let divergent item be the first item in variant list that passes this check:
      If compose match key (item) is not in changed match keys, give back whether false.
      Let base old be base old by match key's entry for compose match key (item).
      Give back whether base old is set and there is no items equal (item and base old).
    If divergent item is set:
      Add an object with to conflicts:
        • item filter: filter for item (divergent item)
        • feature name: feature's name
        • reason: "value_divergence"
  If all of these are true:
    • diff's price is set
    • there is no base prices equal (variant plan's price and current base plan's price)
  then:
    Add an object with reason: "base_price_divergence" to conflicts.
  Give back conflicts.

##### server/src/internal/orgs/orgUtils/getOrgWithFeaturesCached.ts
Type OrgWithFeatures: a NonNullable.

“Read-through cache around `OrgService.getWithFeatures`. Queue workers call this once per message and async `balances.track` enqueues one message per API request, so the uncached path was running ~1,140 times a second against Postgres — 3.08M lookups in 45 minutes, 8.4% of database time — for a row that barely changes. Redis is strictly an accelerator: every op goes through `tryRedisOp`, which swallows failures, so an outage reads as a cache miss and falls through to Postgres. That must hold — if a Redis error escaped here, `createWorkerContext` would catch it, treat the org as missing, and silently acknowledge queued jobs without recording usage.”
To get org with features cached — given org ID, env, skip cache (default false), and request ID; gives back an OrgWithFeatures (or nothing) (async):
  To load:
    Get with features [OrgService] (org ID and env), and give back the result.
  If skip cache is false:
    Read through org with features, and give back the result:
      • context: get misc cache context
      • org ID
      • env
      • load
      • request ID
  Load, and call the result fresh.
  If fresh is missing, give back nothing.
  Set cached org with features:
    • context: get misc cache context
    • org ID
    • env
    • data: fresh
    • request ID
  Give back fresh.

Invalid domain error:

“Accepts "stripe.com", "https://www.stripe.com/pricing", etc. and returns "stripe.com".”

To get aspect ratio — given logo:
  From logo's resolution, or an empty object if that's missing, take width, height, and aspect ratio.
  If aspect ratio is set, give back aspect ratio.
  If width is set and height is set, give back width divided by height.
  Give back 1.

“The org logo renders as a small square, so prefer square icons (favicons / app icons) over wide wordmarks, then prefer the highest resolution.”
To pick best logo — given logos:
  To score logo — given logo:
    Let is icon be 1 if logo's type is "icon", otherwise 0.
    Let squareness be negative the absolute value of log [Math] (get aspect ratio (logo)).
    Let width be logo's resolution's width, or 0 if that's missing.
    Give back an object with is icon, squareness, and width.
  Give back the first of a copy of logos, after these steps:
    1. Keep only those where logo's URL is allowed logo URL
    2. ␀them, sorted by this rule:
      Score logo (a), and call the result score a.
      Score logo (b), and call the result score b.
      Give back score b's is icon minus score a's is icon, or score b's squareness minus score a's squareness if that's empty, or score b's width minus score a's width if that's empty.

“Logo URLs come from Context.dev's own CDN. Only download from there, and never follow redirects, so a logo URL can't steer this server-side fetch at an internal address (SSRF) whose response would land in a public bucket.”
Is allowed logo host? — given hostname:
  Give back whether logo cdn host suffixes has a suffix where hostname is suffix from position 1 onward or hostname ends with suffix.

  Try the following:
    Let parsed be a new URL (URL).

  If anything fails:
    Give back whether false.

  Give back an error: "Couldn't download a logo for that website" [error code's invalid request] (status 404).

Logo too large error:
  Give back an error: "Logo is larger than 10MB" [error code's invalid request] (status 400).

“Reads the body but aborts as soon as it exceeds MAX_LOGO_BYTES.”
To read body with limit — given response (async):
  Get response's body reader → reader.
  If reader is missing, fail with a logo download failed error.
  Let chunks be an empty list.
  Let total bytes start as 0.
  Keep repeating (until something stops it):
    Read reader, and take its done and value.
    Stop the loop if done is set.
    Add value's byte length to total bytes.
    If total bytes is more than max logo bytes:
      Cancel reader.
      Fail with a logo too large error.
    Add value to chunks.
  Let bytes be a new uint8 array (total bytes).
  Let offset start as 0.
  For each chunk in chunks:
    Record offset under chunk in bytes.
    Add chunk's byte length to offset.
  Give back bytes.

To download logo — given URL (async):
  If URL is not allowed logo, fail with a logo download failed error.
  Start with no response yet.
  Try the following:
    Fetch, and put the result in response:
      • URL
      • redirect: "error"
      • signal: a timeout [AbortSignal] (logo download timeout ms)
  If anything fails:
    Fail with a logo download failed error.
  Let content type be response's headers' entry for "content-type", or "" if that's missing.
  If response's ok is missing or content type does not start with "image/", fail with a logo download failed error.
  Let declared length be response's headers' entry for "content-length" as a number.
  If declared length is more than max logo bytes:
    Cancel response's body.
    Fail with a logo too large error.
  Read body with limit (response), and call the result bytes.
  Give back an object with bytes and content type.

##### server/src/internal/orgs/handlers/stripeHandlers/handleOAuthCallback.ts
Let failure messages be an object with:
  • access denied: "Stripe connection was cancelled. Please try again when you are ready."
  • OAuth authorization failed: "Stripe did not authorize the connection. Please try again."
  • missing parameters: "The Stripe callback is missing required parameters. Please restart the connection."
  • invalid state: "This connection request is not valid. Please restart the connection."
  • state expired: "This connection link has expired. Please restart the connection."
  • state already used: "This connection link was already used. Please restart the connection."
  • org not found: "The organization could not be found. Please restart the connection."
  • account ID not found: "Stripe did not return an account. Please restart the connection."
  • account already connected: "This Stripe account is already connected to another organization in this environment."
  • account mismatch: "This Stripe account does not match the account connected through your secret key."
  • account mismatch check failed: "The account connected through your secret key could not be verified. Please check your key and try again."
  • OAuth callback failed: "The Stripe connection could not be completed. Please try again."

“Handles Stripe OAuth callback Uses Redis state for both standard and platform flows”
To handle o auth callback — given c (async):
  Query c's request → query.
  From query, take code, state, and error.
  “Get database connection”
  “Build frontend redirect URL (default)”
  Let frontend URL be the CLIENT_URL environment variable, or "http://localhost:3000" if that's empty.
  Let redirect URL start as a new URL (frontend URL).
  Record "stripe" under "tab" in redirect URL's search params.
  To fail — given failure and details:
    For each key key and value value in details:
      Record value under key in redirect URL's search params.
    Record "false" under "success" in redirect URL's search params.
    Record failure under "error" in redirect URL's search params.
    Record failure messages' entry for failure under "message" in redirect URL's search params.
    Redirect c (redirect URL as text), and give back the result.
  If state is missing, Fail ("missing_parameters"), and give back the result.
  Try the following:
    “Consume OAuth state from Redis”
    Consume o auth state (state key: state), and call the result Redis state.
    If Redis state is missing:
      “A signed return URL outlives the stored state, so send the user back there”
      Read o auth state return (state) → state return.
      If state return is missing, Fail ("invalid_state"), and give back the result.
      Set redirect URL to a new URL (state return's redirect uri).
      Let age ms be the current time minus state return's issued at.
      Fail, and give back the result:
        • "state_expired" if age ms is more than OAuth state TTL seconds times 1000, otherwise "state_already_used"
    If Redis state's provider is "revenuecat", Fail ("invalid_state"), and give back the result.
    “Extract state data”
    From Redis state, take organization slug, env (as env string), redirect uri, and master org ID.
    Let env be app env's live if env string is "live", otherwise app env's sandbox.
    Let is platform flow mean master org ID is set.
    “Use custom redirect URI if provided (platform flow)”
    If is platform flow:
      Set redirect URL to a new URL (redirect uri).
    Otherwise:
      Set redirect URL to depending on whether redirect uri is set:
        • if so: a new URL (redirect uri)
        • if not: a new URL:
          • "{frontend URL}{"/sandbox" if env is app env's sandbox, otherwise ""}/settings?tab=stripe"
    “Handle OAuth error from Stripe, now that the caller's return URL is trusted”
    If error is set:
      Fail, and give back the result:
        • "access_denied" if error is "access_denied", otherwise "oauth_authorization_failed"
    If code is missing, Fail ("missing_parameters"), and give back the result.
    “Fetch the organization by slug”
    Get by slug [OrgService] (slug: organization slug), and call the result org.
    “Platform state may only connect orgs its master still owns”
    Let ownership changed mean is platform flow and org's created by is not master org ID.
    If org is missing or ownership changed is true:
      Log an error "Organization not found:" (with organization slug).
      Fail ("org_not_found"), and give back the result.
    Init master Stripe (env) → Stripe.
    Let response be Stripe's OAuth's token (grant type: "authorization_code" and code).
    Let account ID be response's Stripe user ID.
    If account ID is missing:
      Log an error "Account ID not found".
      Fail ("account_id_not_found"), and give back the result.
    “Check if account ID is already connected to another organization (reconnecting is fine)”
    Find by Stripe account ID [OrgService] (account ID, env, and exclude org ID: org's ID), and call the result existing org.
    If existing org is set:
      Log an error "Account {account ID} is already connected to org {existing org's ID}".
      “Platform flow only learns about conflicts inside its own platform”
      If is platform flow:
        If existing org's created by is not master org ID, Fail ("account_already_connected"), and give back the result.
        Let public org be a to platform org (org: existing org and master org ID).
        Fail, and give back the result:
          • "account_already_connected"
          • connected org name: public org's name
          • connected org slug: public org's slug
      “Standard flow returns detailed error”
      Create Stripe client (org: existing org and env), and call the result master.
      “The conflict is still reported if the account can no longer be read”
      Let account be retrieve master's accounts (account ID) (and if that fails, nothing instead).
      Fail, and give back the result:
        • "account_already_connected"
        • account ID
        • account name: account's company's name, or "" if that's empty
        • connected org name: existing org's name, or "" if that's empty
        • connected org slug: existing org's slug, or "" if that's empty
    “Both channels must point at the same Stripe account, else OAuth webhooks (this account) would be processed against secret-key billing state.”
    Let secret key connected mean org is Stripe connected (given env and through secret key: true).
    If secret key connected is true:
      Try the following:
        Create Stripe client (org, env, and through secret key), and call the result secret key client.
        Retrieve secret key client's accounts, and call the result secret key account.
        If secret key account's ID is not account ID:
          Fail, and give back the result:
            • "account_mismatch"
            • account ID
            • secret key account ID: secret key account's ID
      If anything fails (call the problem error):
        Log an error "Failed to verify account match against secret key for org {org's ID} ({org's slug}):" (with error).
        Fail ("account_mismatch_check_failed"), and give back the result.
    “Fails if the grant was revoked after the token exchange”
    Retrieve Stripe's balance (Stripe account: account ID).
    “Update organization with Stripe Connect account”
    Update Stripe connect [OrgService] (org ID: org's ID, account ID, and env).
    Log "Successfully connected Stripe account for org {org's ID}".
    “Redirect to success”
    Record "true" under "success" in redirect URL's search params.
    Redirect c (redirect URL as text), and give back the result.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Log an error "Error in OAuth callback:" (with error).
    Fail ("oauth_callback_failed"), and give back the result.

    • product name: expanded product's name, or nothing if that's missing

“Two lookups, no free-text search: an exact price id, or every price under a product id. Stripe cannot match price ids by substring, so anything else would return unrelated prices — those queries never reach Stripe.”

##### server/src/internal/orgs/handlers/stripeHandlers/handleSearchStripeProducts.ts
Let Stripe product ID prefix be "prod_".

“Stripe's `name~` substring search requires at least 3 characters.”
Let min name search length be 3.

Let local filter list limit be 100.

Is Stripe product ID? — given search:
  Give back whether search without surrounding spaces starts with Stripe product ID prefix.

Escape Stripe search value — given value:
  Give back value with /\\/g replaced by "\\" with /'/g replaced by "\'".

Create route, and call the result handle search Stripe products:
  • scopes: a list of scopes' plans' read
  • query: Stripe product search params schema
  • handler: a function of c that:
    Let context be c's entry for "ctx".
    From context, take org and env.
    From c's request's valid ("query"), take search and limit.
    Let normalized search be search without surrounding spaces, or "" if that's missing.
    If org is not Stripe connected (given env):
      Give back c's JSON:
        • parse [StripeProductSearchResponseSchema] (no Stripe connected and Stripe products: an empty list)
    Create Stripe client (org and env) → Stripe client.
    Let products by ID be an empty lookup table.
    To retrieve product (async):
      If normalized search is not Stripe product ID, stop here.
      Try the following:
        Retrieve Stripe client's products (normalized search), and call the result product.
        If product has a "deleted" key and product's deleted is set, stop here.
        Let catalog product be the catalog product of product.
        Record catalog product under catalog product's ID in products by ID.
      If anything fails (call the problem error):
        Warn "[stripe.products.search] Stripe product {normalized search} not found: {error}".
    To add products — given products:
      For each product in products:
        Let catalog product be the catalog product of product.
        Record catalog product under catalog product's ID in products by ID.
    To list active products — given list limit (async):
      List Stripe client's products (active and limit: list limit), and call the result listed.
      Give back listed's data.
    To search products (async):
      Try the following:
        “Product IDs only ever match exactly, via retrieveProduct. Listing or name-searching here would return unrelated products.”
        If normalized search is Stripe product ID, stop here.
        If normalized search is missing:
          Add products (list active products (limit)).
          Stop here.
        If the number of normalized search is less than min name search length:
          List active products (local filter list limit), and call the result listed.
          Let lowercased search be normalized search in lowercase.
          Add products:
            • listed, after these steps:
              1. Keep only those where lowercased search is in product's name in lowercase
              2. The first limit of ␀them
          Stop here.
        Search Stripe client's products, and call the result searched:
          • query: "active:'true' AND name~'{an escape Stripe search value (normalized search)}'"
          • limit
        Add products (searched's data).
      If anything fails (call the problem error):
        Warn "[stripe.products.search] Failed to search products: {error}".
    Do these at the same time:
      • retrieve product
      • search products
    Give back c's JSON:
      • parse [StripeProductSearchResponseSchema]:
        • Stripe connected
        • Stripe products: products by ID's values as a list

##### server/src/internal/orgs/handlers/memberHandlers/handleRemoveMember.ts
Create route, and call the result handle remove member:
  • scopes: an object with any: a list of scopes' admin and scopes' owner
  • body: a schema for an object with member ID and user ID
  • handler: a function of c that:
    Let context be c's entry for "ctx".
    From c's request's valid ("json"), take member ID and user ID.
    From context, take org.
    “First check if the member exists by memberId”
    Find the query's member first, and call the result existing member:
      • where: all of these are true:
        • member's ID is member ID
        • member's organization ID is org's ID
    If existing member is missing:
      “Try to find by userId as fallback”
      Find the query's member first, and call the result member by user ID:
        • where: all of these are true:
          • member's user ID is user ID
          • member's organization ID is org's ID
      If member by user ID is missing:
        Fail with an error: "Member not found in this organization" ["MEMBER_NOT_FOUND"] (status 404).
      “Use the member found by userId”
      Set existing member to member by user ID.
    Let removing owner mean "owner" is in existing member's role split on ",".
    If removing owner is true and scopes' owner is not in the scopes:
      Fail with an error: "Only owners can remove another owner" ["FORBIDDEN"] (status 403).
    If removing owner is true:
      Find the query's member many (where: member's organization ID is org's ID), and call the result org members.
      Let owner count be the number of org members where "owner" is in org member's role split on ",".
      If owner count is at most 1, fail with an error: "An organization must keep at least one owner" ["LAST_OWNER"] (status 400).
    “Remove member from database using the found member”
    Delete from member:
      • where all of these are true:
        • member's ID is existing member's ID
        • member's organization ID is org's ID
    “Revoke all sessions for this user in this organization”
    Try the following:
      Delete from auth session:
        • where all of these are true:
          • auth session's user ID is existing member's user ID
          • auth session's active organization ID is org's ID
    If anything fails (call the problem error):
      Warn "Session revocation failed: {error}".
    Give back c's JSON (message: "Member removed successfully").

##### server/src/internal/misc/trmnl/handlers/handleGenerateTrmnlScreen.ts

      • params: an object with:
        • event names: a list of top event

        • aggregate all: true
        • bin size: "day"

    If total events is missing, set total events to "Unknown".
    “Revenue: stubbed to 0 for now (Tinybird only stores events today)”
    Let monthly revenue be an object with total payment volume: 0 and label: "N/A".
    “Get timeseries data for the chart”
    Aggregate event actions, and take its formatted (as results):
      • params: an object with:
        • event names: a list of top event
        • interval: "30d"
        • aggregate all: true
        • bin size: "day"
    “Total customers: stubbed to 0 for now (Tinybird only stores events today)”
    Let total customers be 0.
    Let data be results' data.
    “Access hideRevenue from the trmnl context set by middleware”
    Let hide revenue be org's hide revenue, or false if that's missing.
    Give back c's JSON:
      • row data: "[{data, after these steps}]"
      • revenue: number with commas (monthly revenue's total payment volume)
      • total events: number with commas (total events)
      • total customers: number with commas (total customers)
      • top event: feature name, or "Unknown" if that's empty
      • hide revenue

##### server/src/internal/misc/slackConnect/slackConnectClient.ts
“Comma-separated Slack user ids added to every new channel. Defaults to whoever installed the admin bot, so a new channel is never unattended.”
Let team user IDs be the AUTUMN_SUPPORT_SLACK_TEAM_USER_IDS environment variable, or "" if that's missing split on ",", after these steps:
  1. Turn each user ID into user ID without surrounding spaces
  2. Drop empty values

Let slack channel prefix be "autumn-".

“Slack caps channel names at 80 characters.”
Let max channel name length be 80.

Let invalid channel name chars be /[^a-z0-9_-]+/g.

“Each request can name a new channel, so cap how many one org can create.”
Let max slack channels per org be 2.

“The per-org support channels live in Autumn's own workspace, so they're driven by the internal admin install of the Slack agent app (Admin → Slack admin bot). That install requests `SLACK_CONNECT_ADMIN_SCOPES` on top of the agent's scopes; returns null until it's installed with them.”
Type SlackConnectClient: an object.

To get slack connect client — gives back a SlackConnectClient (or nothing) (async):
  If process's env's slack client ID is missing, give back nothing.
  Find the query's chat installations first (where: chat installations' provider is get slack admin provider), and call the result installation.
  If installation is missing, give back nothing.
  Let granted be the unique values of installation's scopes.
  Let has scopes mean every scope in slack connect admin scopes satisfies: scope is in granted.
  If has no scopes, give back nothing.
  Let installer user ID be installation's installed by provider user ID.
  Give back an object with:
    • slack: a new web client (a decrypt chat token (token: installation's bot access token))
    • team user IDs: depending on whether team user IDs is not empty or installer user ID is missing:
      • if so: team user IDs
      • if not: a list of installer user ID

To slack channel name — given name:
  Let sanitized be name in lowercase with invalid channel name chars replaced by "-".
  Let prefixed be sanitized if sanitized starts with slack channel prefix, otherwise "{slack channel prefix}{sanitized}".
  Give back the first max channel name length of prefixed.

“Thrown when the requested name belongs to a channel the org doesn't own.”
Class Slack channel name taken error (extends error):

“Thrown when the org already has `MAX_SLACK_CHANNELS_PER_ORG` channels.”
Class Slack channel limit error (extends error):

“Stamped into the channel purpose so a typed name can't reuse another org's channel. It's also the only record of which channels an org owns.”
Org channel purpose — given org ID:
  Give back "Shared support channel with Autumn ({org ID})".

Type SlackChannel: NonNullable<ConversationsListResponse["c.

To get slack error code — given error; gives back text (or nothing):
  If error is not an object, error is missing, or error has no "data" key, give back nothing.
  From error, take data.
  Give back data's error.

“Every public channel in the workspace, archived ones included.”
To list public channels — given client; gives back a list of SlackChannel (async):
  Let channels be an empty list.
  Start with no cursor yet.
  Do the following at least once:
    List client's slack's conversations (types: "public_channel", limit: 1000, and cursor), and call the result response.
    For each channel in response's channels:
      Add channel to channels.
    Set cursor to response's response metadata's next cursor, or nothing if that's empty.
  …and keep repeating while cursor is set.
  Give back channels.

“Renames and archives a channel whose setup failed before it was stamped, so its name is free for the next request instead of being held by a channel no org owns. Best effort: the caller rethrows the setup error.”
To release unstamped channel — given client and channel ID (async):
  Try the following:
    Rename client's slack's conversations:
      • channel: channel ID
      • name: "{slack channel prefix}unused-{channel ID in lowercase}"
    Archive client's slack's conversations (channel: channel ID).
  If anything fails, ignore it.

Unarchive channel — given client and channel ID (async):
  Try the following:
    Run client's slack's conversations' unarchive (channel: channel ID).
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    If get slack error code (error) is not "not_archived", fail with error.

“Returns the channel if the org owns it (unarchiving it if needed), throws if someone else holds the name, and returns undefined if the name is free.”
To reuse owned channel — given client, channel, name, and purpose; gives back text (or nothing) (async):
  If channel is missing, give back nothing.
  If channel's ID is missing or channel's purpose's value is not purpose:
    Fail with a slack channel name taken error: "#{name} is already taken".
  “An archived channel still holds its name; bring it back.”
  If channel is archived, Unarchive channel (client and channel ID: channel's ID).
  Give back channel's ID.

“The channel purpose doubles as the ownership record, so both the reuse check and the per-org limit read it from Slack instead of a DB row.”
To get or create channel — given client, name, and org ID; gives back text (async):
  Let purpose be an org channel purpose (org ID).
  List public channels (client) → channels.
  Reuse owned channel, and call the result owned channel ID:
    • client
    • channel: the first channel in channels where channel's name is name
    • name
    • purpose
  If owned channel ID is set, give back owned channel ID.
  Let org channels be channels, keeping only those where channel's purpose's value is purpose.
  If the number of org channels is at least max slack channels per org:
    Let names be org channels, after these steps:
      1. Turn each channel into "#{channel's name}"
      2. Join them with ", "
    Fail with a slack channel limit error: "Your organization already has {the number of org channels} Slack channels with Autumn ({names}). Request an invite to one of those instead".
  Start with no channel ID yet.
  Try the following:
    Create client's slack's conversations (name), and call the result response.
    Set channel ID to response's channel's ID.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    If get slack error code (error) is not "name_taken", fail with error.
    “Either a concurrent request just created it (reuse it if it's this org's), or a private channel we can't list holds the name.”
    Reuse owned channel, and call the result raced channel ID:
      • client
      • channel: the first channel in list public channels (client) where channel's name is name
      • name
      • purpose
    If raced channel ID is set, give back raced channel ID.
    Fail with a slack channel name taken error: "#{name} is already taken".
  If channel ID is missing, fail with an error: "Slack returned no channel id".
  Try the following:
    Set client's slack's conversations purpose (channel: channel ID and purpose).
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Release unstamped channel (client and channel ID).
    Fail with error.
  If client's team user IDs is not empty:
    Run client's slack's conversations' invite (channel: channel ID and users: client's team user IDs joined with ",").
  Give back channel ID.

“Creates (or reuses) the org's channel and sends a Slack Connect invite to `email`. Slack delivers the invite by email.”
Invite → org slack channel — given client, org ID, requested name, and email; gives back an object with channel name (async):
  Let channel name be a to slack channel name (name: requested name).
  Get or create channel (client, name: channel name, and org ID), and call the result channel ID.
  “Slack defaults invitees to external limited members, who can't invite anyone else. Full external members can bring in their own teammates.”
  Invite client's slack's conversations shared (channel: channel ID, emails: a list of email, and no external limited).
  Give back an object with channel name.

##### server/src/internal/misc/rollouts/rolloutConfigStore.ts
“An S3 read error must not send every routed customer back to the old path with no handoff.”

  • schema: rollout config schema

“The store handle, for runtimes that poll a chosen few configs (see startEdgeConfigPolling).”
Let rollout edge config be store.

To set rollout config for testing — given config:
