“No Redis view outlives its TTL, so a decrease or removal older than that cannot mark one stale.”
Let staleness retention ms be full subject cache TTL seconds times 1000.

Empty rollout entry — gives back a RolloutEntry:
  Give back an object with:
    • percent: 0
    • previous percent: 0
    • changed at: 0
    • decreases: an empty list
    • orgs: an empty object
    • customers: an empty object

“A scheduled change starts from what routes right now; a new org override inherits that from the global entry.”
To schedule rollout percent — given current, percent, and now; gives back a RolloutPercent:
  Let routing be the routing percent at current and now.
  Let decreases be current's decreases, keeping only those whose at is after now minus staleness retention ms.
  If percent is less than routing, add an object with from: routing, to: percent, and at: now to decreases.
  Give back an object with:
    • previous percent: routing
    • percent
    • changed at: now
    • decreases

“Update a rollout percentage (global or per-org). Auto-manages previousPercent and changedAt.”
To update rollout percent — given rollout ID, org ID, percent, and now (default the current time) (async):
  Read store from source, and call the result config.
  Let entry be config's rollouts' entry for rollout ID, or an empty rollout entry if that's missing.
  If org ID is set:
    “An org with no override has been following the global entry.”
    Schedule rollout percent, and put the result in entry's orgs' entry for org ID:
      • current: entry's orgs' entry for org ID, or entry if that's missing
      • percent
      • now
  Otherwise:
    Copy everything from schedule rollout percent (current: entry, percent, and now) into entry.
  Set config's rollouts' entry for rollout ID to entry.
  Write store to source (config).
  Give back config.

“Remove an org override: the org follows the global entry again from the next config poll.”
To remove rollout org — given rollout ID and org ID (async):
  Read store from source, and call the result config.
  Let entry be config's rollouts' entry for rollout ID.
  If entry is missing, give back config.
  Delete entry.orgs[orgId].
  Write store to source (config).
  Give back config.

“Every org override above 0 is scheduled down to 0; one already there keeps its change time.”
To schedule orgs to zero — given orgs and now; gives back RolloutEntry["orgs"]:
  Give back an object built from the key/value pairs of orgs, with each item turned into a list of:
    • org ID
    • depending on whether current's percent is 0:
      • if so: current
      • if not: schedule rollout percent (current, percent: 0, and now)

“Send every org override back to the legacy path in one write; the overrides stay, at 0.”
To reset rollout orgs — given rollout ID and now (default the current time) (async):
  Read store from source, and call the result config.
  Let entry be config's rollouts' entry for rollout ID.
  If entry is missing, give back config.
  Schedule orgs to zero (orgs: entry's orgs and now), and put the result in entry's orgs.
  Write store to source (config).
  Give back config.

“Re-adding a customer before its removal lands cancels the removal, so it never dips back to the fallback.”
To schedule customer add — given current and now; gives back a RolloutCustomer:
  If current is missing, give back an object with added at: now.
  If current's removed at is missing, give back current.
  Let removal landed mean now is at or after the rollout effective at current's removed at.
  If removal landed is true:
    Give back an object with added at: now.
  Otherwise:
    Give back an object with added at: current's added at.

“A second removal keeps the first one's time, which is when the customer actually leaves the worker.”
To schedule customer removal — given current and now; gives back a RolloutCustomer:
  If current's removed at is missing:
    Give back current, but with removed at set to now.
  Otherwise:
    Give back current.

Removal expired — given customer and now; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether all of these are true:
    • customer's removed at is set
    • now is at or after the rollout effective at customer's removed at plus staleness retention ms

“Drops removed customers once no pre-removal Redis view can remain, and orgs left with none.”
To prune expired customer removals — given customers and now; gives back RolloutEntry["customers"]:
  Let pruned be an empty object.
  For each key org ID and value org customers in customers:
    Let kept be the key/value pairs of org customers, keeping only those where there is no removal expired (customer and now).
    If kept is not empty, set pruned's entry for org ID to an object built from kept.
  Give back pruned.

To write rollout customers — given rollout ID, org ID, customer IDs, now, and schedule (async):
  Read store from source, and call the result config.
  Let entry be config's rollouts' entry for rollout ID, or an empty rollout entry if that's missing.
  Let org customers be an object with everything in entry's customers' entry for org ID.
  For each customer ID in customer IDs:
    Schedule (org customers' entry for customer ID), and call the result scheduled.
    If scheduled is set, set org customers' entry for customer ID to scheduled.
  Prune expired customer removals, and put the result in entry's customers:
    • customers: entry's customers, but with [org ID] set to org customers
    • now
  Set config's rollouts' entry for rollout ID to entry.
  Write store to source (config).
  Give back config.

“Pin customers of one org to the worker, one settle window from now.”
To add rollout customers — given rollout ID, org ID, customer IDs, and now (default the current time) (async):
  Write rollout customers, and give back the result:
    • rollout ID
    • org ID
    • customer IDs
    • now
    • schedule: a function of current giving back schedule customer add (current and now)

“Unpin customers of one org: they follow the org or global percent again one settle window from now.”
To remove rollout customers — given rollout ID, org ID, customer IDs, and now (default the current time) (async):
  Write rollout customers, and give back the result:
    • rollout ID
    • org ID
    • customer IDs
    • now
    • schedule: a function of current giving back schedule customer removal (current and now) if current is set (otherwise nothing)

“Deleting an entry skips the handoff, so a live rollout is rolled back to 0 first, then deleted.”
To assert rollout inactive — given rollout ID and entry:
  If entry is missing, stop here.
  Let percent active mean a list of entry and everything in the values in entry's orgs has an item whose percent is positive.
  Let customer pinned mean the values in entry's customers has a org customers where the values in org customers has an item whose removed at is missing.
  If percent active is false and customer pinned is false, stop here.
  Fail with an error: "Rollout {rollout ID} is still active; set every percent to 0 and remove every customer before deleting it" [error code's invalid request] (status 400).

“Delete a rollout entry entirely. Use this instead of setting percent to 0 when you want to reset the staleness window (previousPercent/changedAt).”
To delete rollout — given rollout ID (async):
  Read store from source, and call the result config.
  Assert rollout inactive (rollout ID and entry: config's rollouts' entry for rollout ID).
  Delete config.rollouts[rolloutId].
  Write store to source (config).
  Give back config.

  Let lane be matched's lane, or "default" if that's missing.
  If matched's use replica for body is missing, give back lane.
  Start with no body yet.
  Try the following:
    Read body, and put the result in body.
  If anything fails:
    “An unreadable body can't be proven unscoped, so keep the primary.”
    Give back nothing.
  Give back lane if use matched replica for body (body) gives back something, otherwise nothing.

“============ SYSTEM PROMPT ============”
Let system prompt be "You are a helpful pricing configuration assistant for Autumn, a billing and entitlements platform.

Your job is to help users set up their pricing model through natural conversation. You should:
1. Ask clarifying questions to understand their needs
2. Generate and update the pricing configuration as you learn more
3. Read through these instructions carefully for every single message, and follow them exactly.

**IMPORTANT**: Call the build_pricing tool EVERY time the user provides any information at all about their pricing, features, or products. This updates the live preview they see. Even partial information should trigger a tool call with your best interpretation.


## Feature Types
- **single_use**: Consumable resources (API calls, tokens, messages, credits, generations)
- **continuous_use**: Non-consumable resources (seats, workspaces, projects, team members)
- **boolean**: On/off features (advanced analytics, priority support, SSO)
- **credit_system**: A unified credit pool that maps to multiple single_use features



## Item Types
Products contain an array of items. There are THREE distinct item patterns:

1. **Flat Fee** (standalone price, no feature):
   `{ feature_id: null, price: 13, interval: "month" }`
   → Customer pays $13/month as a base subscription fee

2. **Free Feature Allocation** (feature grant, no price):
   `{ feature_id: "credits", included_usage: 10000 }`
   → Customer gets 10,000 credits included

3. **Metered/Usage-Based Pricing**:
   `{ feature_id: "credits", included_usage: 10000, price: 0.01, usage_model: "pay_per_use", interval: "month" }`
   → Customer can use 10,000 credits per month, and then pays $0.01 per credit used after that.

4. **Prepaid Credit Purchase** (one-time or recurring):
   `{ feature_id: "credits", price: 10, usage_model: "prepaid", billing_units: 10000 } `,
   → Customer pays $10 for 10,000 credits. Add `interval: "month" ` to make it a recurring subscription with selectable quantity.


5. **Tiered Pricing**:
   `{ feature_id: "api_calls", included_usage: 1000, tiers: [{ to: 5000, amount: 0.02 }, { to: "inf", amount: 0.01 }], usage_model: "pay_per_use", interval: "month" }`
   → Customer gets 1,000 API calls free, then pays $0.02/call up to 5,000, then $0.01/call after that.

6. **Per-Unit Pricing Structure**:
For any "per-X" pricing (like "$Y per seat", "$Y per project", "$Y per website"), ALWAYS use this pattern:
- Base subscription fee: `{ feature_id: null, price: 10, interval: "month" }`
- Unit allocation: `{ feature_id: "seats", included_usage: 1, price: 10, usage_model: "pay_per_use", billing_units: 1 }`
This creates: $Y/month base price that includes 1 unit, then $Y per additional unit purchased.
**ALWAYS** use this two-item pattern for any per-unit pricing - never use pure per-unit without a base fee.




## Guidelines when building the config

- Refer to the Item Types section above to see examples of how to build the config.

- **Features vs Items**: Features define WHAT can be tracked (e.g., "credits"). Items define HOW that feature is granted in a product (recurring, one-time, free, paid). NEVER create duplicate features for the same underlying resource. For example, "monthly tokens" and "one-time tokens" should be the SAME feature ("tokens"), referenced by different items and intervals.

- If you identify more than 3 features from user input, build the 3 most important (prioritizing metered features) and ask the user to confirm if they want to add more. Inform them clearly that you kept it simple to start with, but they can add more later.

- Product and Feature IDs should be lowercase with underscores (e.g., "pro_plan", "chat_messages")

- **NEVER** allow is_default: true for plans with prices. All prices MUST be null or undefined.

- Ignore reference to "Enterprise" plans with custom pricing. They do not need to be generated here. Instead, inform the user that custom plans can be created for any customer within the Autumn dashboard.

- For annual variants of plans, create another separate plan but with the annual price interval. Name it <plan_name> - Annual




## Guidelines when responding to the user

- Do NOT tell the user what pricing you have built or describe the pricing in any way, as it is a waste to read (they can see it on the right).

- If the user asks about changing currency, let them know they can do so in the Autumn dashboard, under Developer > Stripe.

- If the user has a price for a feature, ask them whether it should be a usage-based (pay_per_use) or prepaid (prepaid) pricing

- If the user asks about pricing or functionality that you are not sure whether is possible, DO NOT make up information or assume it can be done. They can reach us on discord here: https://discord.gg/atmn (we're very responsive)

- Keep responses very concise and friendly.".

##### server/src/internal/misc/pricingAgent/handlers/handleSetupPreviewOrg.ts
“Sets up a preview sandbox organization for the current user. - Creates a new preview org if one doesn't exist - Reuses existing preview org if found No API key is ever returned to the client. Preview operations (syncing pricing, creating a checkout) run server-side against this org, keyed off the caller's session.     If user ID is missing, fail with an error: "User not authenticated" ["unauthenticated"] (status 401).
    “Fetch user from database”
    Find the query's user first (where: user table's ID is user ID), and call the result user.
    If user is missing, fail with an error: "User not found".
    Build preview org slug (user ID and master org ID: master org's ID), and call the result preview slug.
    “Check if preview org already exists”
    Get by slug [OrgService] (slug: preview slug), and call the result existing org.
    Start with no preview org yet.
    If existing org is set:
      Set preview org to existing org.
      Log "[Preview] Found existing preview org: {preview org's ID} ({preview slug})".
      “Revoke any keys previously handed out for this preview org. The org is fully machine-managed and has no members, so every key on it was minted by the old setup flow.”
      Delete API key repo by org (org ID: preview org's ID), and call the result revoked.
      If revoked is not empty:

    Otherwise:

      Log "[Preview] Creating new preview org: {org ID} ({preview slug})".
      Create [OrgService], and put the result in preview org:
        • ID: org ID
        • slug: preview slug
        • name: "Preview - {user's name, or user's email if that's empty}"
        • created by: master org's ID
      “Initialize org (creates Stripe test account, svix apps, etc.)”
      After org created (org: preview org and user).
      Log "[Preview] Created preview org: {preview org's ID} ({preview slug})".
    Give back c's JSON (org slug: preview slug and org ID: preview org's ID).

##### server/src/internal/misc/idempotency/withIdempotencyKey.ts
Should release idempotency key for status? — given status:
  Give back whether status is at least 400 and status is not 409.

“Releases on failures a client should be able to retry: unknown errors (no statusCode — the request never completed) and non-409 4xx/5xx. Never releases duplicates — that would defeat the key.”
Should release idempotency key for error? — given error:
  Let status code be error's status code as a number if error is an object, error is set, and error has a "statusCode" key (otherwise nothing).
  Let code be error's code as text if error is an object, error is set, and error has a "code" key (otherwise nothing).
  If code is error code's duplicate idempotency key or status code is 409, give back whether false.
  Give back whether status code is missing or status code should release idempotency key for status.

“Wraps `run` in an idempotency-key claim: duplicate → 409 before running, retryable failure → key released so the client can retry. Shared by the Idempotency-Key header middleware and track's body-level key.”
With idempotency key — given idempotency key, route group (default nothing), run, and release on success; gives back a T (async):
  If idempotency key is missing, Run, and give back the result.
  Check idempotency key (idempotency key and TTL ms: resolve idempotency TTL ms (route group)).
  To release:
    Release idempotency key (idempotency key), and give back the result.
  Try the following:
    Run, and call the result result.
    If release on success (result) gives back something, Release.
    Give back result.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    If error should release idempotency key for, Release.
    Fail with error.

##### server/src/internal/misc/idempotency/actions/checkIdempotencyKey.ts
“Claims the key in DynamoDB: a duplicate 409s, an unavailable store fails open so an outage can't reject live traffic.”
To check idempotency key — given idempotency key and TTL ms (async):
  Build idempotency storage key (org ID: the org's ID, env: the env, and idempotency key), and take its hashed key and storage key.
  Log "[checkIdempotencyKey] claiming idempotency key {idempotency key}, hash: {hashed key}".
  Claim dynamo idempotency key (storage key and TTL ms), and call the result result.
  If result is "duplicate":
    Fail with an error: "Another request with idempotency key {idempotency key} has already been received" [error code's duplicate idempotency key] (status 409).

##### server/src/internal/misc/idempotency/actions/releaseIdempotencyKey.ts
“Frees the key so the client can retry. Swallows its own errors — a failed release only costs the caller a retry window, never the request.”
To release idempotency key — given idempotency key (async):
  Build idempotency storage key (org ID: the org's ID, env: the env, and idempotency key), and take its storage key.
  Release dynamo idempotency key (storage key).

##### server/src/internal/misc/consent/handlers/handleRevokeConsent.ts

    “Delete legacy main-org tokens and sandbox-bound consent tokens.”

    “5. Delete refresh tokens for this client + org”
    Delete OAuth refresh token repo by client and reference (client ID and reference ID).
    “6. Delete the consent”
    Delete OAuth consent repo by ID (consent ID).
    Give back c's JSON:
      • success
      • deleted API keys: the number of linked keys
      • deleted key prefixes

##### server/src/internal/misc/cacheV2Ramp/cacheV2RampClient.ts
Type CachedClient: an object.
Let cached start as nothing.
Let last decrypt failure key start as nothing.

“Returns the Redis client for the ramp destination configured in the edge config. Lazy: creates the client on first call after the destination is set. Hot-swappable: when the admin changes the URL OR rotates the encrypted connection string (e.g. credential rotation on the same host), the next call disconnects the old client and creates a new one. Returns null when no destination is configured (ramp is dormant).”
To get ramp destination Redis — gives back a Redis (or nothing):
  Get cache v2 ramp config → config.
  If config is missing:
    Close ramp destination client.
    Give back nothing.
  From config, take connection string and URL.
  If cached is set, cached's URL is URL, and cached's connection string is connection string, give back cached's instance.
  If cached is set:
    Let reason be "URL changed ({cached's URL} -> {URL})" if cached's URL is not URL, otherwise "credentials rotated".
    Log "[cacheV2Ramp] destination {reason}; disconnecting old client".
    Try the following:
      Disconnect cached's instance.
    If anything fails (call the problem error):
      Warn "[cacheV2Ramp] failed to disconnect old destination client: {error}".
    Set cached to nothing.
  Start with no decrypted yet.
  Try the following:
    Set decrypted to a decrypt data (connection string).
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Let failure key be "{URL}|{connection string}".
    If last decrypt failure key is not failure key:
      Set last decrypt failure key to failure key.
      Log an error "[cacheV2Ramp] failed to decrypt destination connectionString for {URL}: {error}. Ramp will route to primary until fixed.".
    Give back nothing.
  Set last decrypt failure key to nothing.
  Get reachable dragonfly URL (decrypted), and call the result reachable.
  Create Redis connection, and call the result instance:
    • cache URL: reachable
    • region: "{current region}:v2:ramp"
    • Redis type: "subject-secondary"
    • command timeout: Redis v2 command timeout ms
  Trigger instance's on:
    • "error"
    • a function of error that:
      Log an error "[cacheV2Ramp] destination={URL}: {error's message}".
  Trigger instance's on:
    • "ready"
    • a function that:
      Log "[cacheV2Ramp] destination={URL}: connected".
  Set cached to an object with URL, connection string, and instance.
  Give back instance.

“Tear down the cached destination client. Safe to call multiple times.”
To close ramp destination client:
  If cached is missing, stop here.
  Try the following:
    Disconnect cached's instance.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Warn "[cacheV2Ramp] failed to disconnect destination client during close: {error}".
  Set cached to nothing.

##### server/src/internal/migrations/MigrationService.ts
“Generate a stable numeric hash from a string for use with pg_advisory_lock.”
String → lock ID — given string; gives back a number:
  Give back the result of big int (hash [Bun] (string)) bitwise-and the result of big int (2,147,483,647) as a number.

Class Migration service:
  To create job — given data (async):
    Let result be insert into migration jobs:
      • the values: data
      • giving back the affected rows
    If result is empty, fail with an error: "Failed to create migration job" [error code's insert migration job failed].
    Give back the first of result.
  “Atomically check for existing migration and create a new one if none exists. Uses PostgreSQL advisory lock to prevent race conditions between concurrent requests.”
  To create job if no existing — given org ID, env, from product, and data (async):
    “Create a unique lock key based on org, env, and product”
    Let lock key be "migration:{org ID}:{env}:{from product's internal ID}".
    Let lock ID be the lock ID of lock key.
    Give back transaction:
      • a function that:
        Let tx DB be tx.
        “Try to acquire advisory lock - returns false immediately if lock is held This prevents connection pool exhaustion from concurrent requests”
        Execute tx DB (the SQL SELECT pg_try_advisory_xact_lock({…}) as acquired), and call the result lock result.
        Let lock acquired be the first of lock result's acquired.
        If lock acquired is missing:
          Fail with an error: "Another migration is ongoing for customers on the {from product's name} product, please try again" [error code's migration already in progress] (status 409).
        “Now check for existing in-progress migrations (safe since we hold the lock)”
        Find tx DB's query's migration jobs many, and call the result existing jobs:
          • where: all of these are true:
            • migration jobs' org ID is org ID
            • migration jobs' env is env
            • migration jobs' from internal product ID is from product's internal ID
            • migration jobs' current step is not migration job step's failed
            • migration jobs' current step is not migration job step's finished
        If existing jobs is not empty:
          Fail with an error: "Another migration is ongoing for customers on the {from product's name} product, cannot create a new migration. Migration ID: {the first of existing jobs' ID}" [error code's migration already in progress] (status 409).
        “Insert the new job”
        Let result be insert into migration jobs:
          • the values: data
          • giving back the affected rows
        If result is empty, fail with an error: "Failed to create migration job" [error code's insert migration job failed].
        Give back the first of result.
  To update job — given migration job ID and updates (async):
    Let results be update migration jobs:
      • setting updates, but with updated at set to the current time
      • where migration jobs' ID is migration job ID
      • giving back the affected rows
    If results is empty, give back nothing.
    Give back the first of results.
  To get job — given ID (async):
    Find the query's migration jobs first (where: migration jobs' ID is ID), and call the result job.
    If job is missing, fail with an error: "Migration job {ID} not found" [error code's migration job not found].
    Give back job.
  To get existing jobs — given org ID and env (async):
    Find the query's migration jobs many, and call the result jobs:
      • where: all of these are true:
        • migration jobs' org ID is org ID
        • migration jobs' env is env
        • migration jobs' current step is not migration job step's failed
        • migration jobs' current step is not migration job step's finished
    Give back jobs.
  To insert error — given data (async):
    Let result be insert into migration errors:
      • the values: data
      • giving back the affected rows
    If result is empty, fail with an error: "Failed to insert migration error" [error code's insert migration error failed].
    Give back the first of result.
  To get errors — given migration job ID (async):
    Find the query's migration errors many, and call the result errors:
      • where: migration errors' migration job ID is migration job ID
      • with: an object with customer: true
    Give back errors.

##### server/src/internal/migrations/runRewardMigrationTask.ts
“Match fixed prices by amount”
To find matching fixed price — given old price and candidates; gives back a Price (or nothing):
  Let old config be old price's config.
  Let possible candidate be the first candidate in candidates that passes this check:
    Let new config be candidate's config.
    Give back whether new config's amount is old config's amount.
  Give back possible candidate, or the first of candidates if that's empty.

“Match usage prices by feature and billing characteristics”
To find matching usage price — given old price and candidates; gives back a Price (or nothing):
  Let old config be old price's config.
  Give back the first candidate in candidates that passes this check, or nothing if that's empty:
    Let new config be candidate's config.
    “Match by feature”
    If new config's internal feature ID is not old config's internal feature ID, give back whether false.
    “Match by billing behavior”
    Get billing type (new config), and call the result new billing type.
    Get billing type (old config), and call the result old billing type.
    If new billing type is not old billing type, give back whether false.
    “Optionally match by tier structure if (!tiersMatch(oldConfig.usage_tiers, newConfig.usage_tiers))”
    If there is no tiers are same (old config's usage tiers and new config's usage tiers), give back whether false.
    Give back whether true.

“Main matching function with type-specific logic”
To find best match — given old price and new prices; gives back a Price (or nothing):
  “First, filter by basic characteristics”
  Let candidates be new prices, keeping only the new prices that pass this check:
    If new price's ID is old price's ID, give back whether true.
    Let old config be old price's config.
    Let new config be new price's config.
    Give back depending on whether old config's type is price type's usage (only if all of these are true):
      • get billing type (new price's config) is get billing type (old price's config)
      • new price's config's interval is old price's config's interval
      • new price's config's interval count is old price's config's interval count
      • if so: whether old config's internal feature ID is new config's internal feature ID
      • if not: true
  If candidates is empty, give back nothing.
  If the number of candidates is 1, give back the first of candidates.
  “If multiple candidates, use type-specific matching”
  If old price is fixed price:
    Find matching fixed price (old price and candidates), and give back the result.
  Otherwise, if old price is usage:
    Find matching usage price (old price and candidates), and give back the result.
  “Fallback to first candidate”
  Give back the first of candidates.

To run reward migration task — given payload (async):
  Try the following:
    From payload, take old prices, product ID, org ID, and env.
    Get full [ProductService] (ID or internal ID: product ID, org ID, and env), and call the result full product.
    Let new prices be full product's prices.
    “Get organization for Stripe operations”
    Let org be org service's entry for an object with DB and org ID.
    List reward repo, and call the result rewards:
      • org ID
      • env
      • in types: a list of:
        • reward type's percentage discount
        • reward type's fixed discount
        • reward type's invoice credits
    Let filtered rewards be rewards, keeping only those where all of these are true:
      • x's org ID is org ID
      • x's env is env
      • x's type is not reward type's free product
      • x's discount config is set
      • x's discount config's price IDs has a p where p is in the IDs of old prices
    Let should update reward mean false.
    For each reward in filtered rewards:
      Let new price IDs be an empty list.
      Let unmatched prices be an empty list.
      If reward's discount config's price IDs is set:
        For each price ID in reward's discount config's price IDs:
          Let old price be the first p in old prices where p's ID is price ID.
          If old price is missing:
            Add price ID to new price IDs.
            Move on to the next one.
          Find best match (old price and new prices), and call the result matching new price.
          If matching new price is set:
            Add matching new price's ID to new price IDs.
            Let should update mean any of these is true:
              • matching new price's config's Stripe price ID is not old price's config's Stripe price ID
              • matching new price's config's Stripe product ID is not old price's config's Stripe product ID
            If should update, set should update reward to true.
          Otherwise:
            Add old price's ID to unmatched prices.
      “Update the reward with new price IDs”
      If should update reward:
        Try the following:
          Log "Updating {reward's ID}, updating reward and Stripe coupon...".
          Update reward repo, and call the result updated reward:
            • internal ID: reward's internal ID
            • env
            • org ID
            • update: an object with:
              • discount config: reward's discount config, but with price IDs set to new price IDs
          Get in IDs [PriceService] (IDs: new price IDs), and call the result prices.
          Create Stripe coupon:
            • reward: updated reward
            • org
            • env
            • prices
          Log "Successfully updated Stripe coupon for reward {reward's ID} with new product restrictions".
        If anything fails (call the problem error):
          Log an error "Failed to update reward {reward's ID}:" (with error).
      If unmatched prices is not empty, warn "Unmatched prices for reward {reward's ID}:" (with unmatched prices).
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Log an error "Error running reward migration task" (with error).
    Fail with error.

##### server/src/internal/migrations/v2/webhookDelivery/utils/migrationWebhookDeliveryQueue.ts
“Delivery gets its OWN queue: it outlives the migration's DB work and must never contend with the chunk lanes for fleet capacity. Trigger.dev copies the queue per `concurrencyKey` value, each copy getting the full limit — so keying by migrationRunId with a limit of 1 means one batch in flight per run (deliveries in flight = the run's webhook_concurrency, nothing more), while separate runs never queue behind each other.”
Let migration webhook delivery queue name be "migration-webhook-delivery".

Let migration webhook delivery queue concurrency be 1.
Let migration webhook delivery max duration seconds be 15 times 60.

“Deliveries are at-least-once by design; a retry re-sends the batch, so a transient failure doesn't permanently drop its records.”
Let migration webhook delivery retry be an object with max attempts: 2.

“Records per queue message — keeps payloads small while still batching.”
Let migration webhook records per message be 50.

Queue, and call the result migration webhook delivery queue:
  • name: migration webhook delivery queue name
  • concurrency limit: migration webhook delivery queue concurrency

##### server/src/internal/migrations/v2/webhookDelivery/utils/queueMigrationWebhooks.ts

##### server/src/internal/migrations/v2/webhookDelivery/utils/resolveMigrationWebhookControls.ts

  • webhook concurrency: 0
  • event types: an empty list

“Resolves how a run delivers webhooks — once at run start, inside the run task. Never the request path: sizing the scope and reading the org's Svix endpoints are both too slow to sit in front of the API response. 1. an explicit `sendWebhooks` wins; 2. otherwise bulk runs (> threshold customers) default off; 3. either way, the org must actually subscribe to at least one event.”

      • filter
      • skip sizing: whether lazy run is true or params' send webhooks is set
  If resolved's send webhooks is false, give back delivery off.
  Let event types mean the org is subscribed to events (given env: the env and event types: migration webhook event types).
  If event types is empty, give back delivery off.
  Give back resolved, but with event types set to event types.

“Stops counting once the threshold is exceeded — the exact size past that point can't change the decision.”
To resolve scope size — given filter and skip sizing; gives back a number (async):
  If skip sizing is true, give back 0.
  Let customer filter be filter's customer.
  If customer filter is missing, give back migration webhook auto disable threshold plus 1.
  Count customers, and give back the result:
    • filter: customer filter
    • limit: migration webhook auto disable threshold plus 1

##### server/src/internal/migrations/v2/run/orchestrators/iterateScope.ts

    If anything fails (call the problem raw):

        If should stop, Summarize ("stopped"), and give back the result.
    Summarize ("exhausted"), and give back the result.
  Let inflight be an empty set.
  To schedule — given item:
    Let p be run item (item)'s finally:
      • a function that:
        Remove p from inflight.
    Add p to inflight.
  To drain — given completion (async):
    Wait for all of inflight.
    Summarize (completion), and give back the result.
  For each batch in iterate (as they arrive):
    For each item in batch:
      If should stop, Drain ("stopped"), and give back the result.
      If scheduled slice is complete, Drain ("slice_complete"), and give back the result.
      Schedule (item).
      If inflight's size is at least max parallel:
        Run race [Promise] (inflight).
        If should stop, Drain ("stopped"), and give back the result.
        If scheduled slice is complete, Drain ("slice_complete"), and give back the result.
  Wait for all of inflight.
  Summarize ("stopped" if should stop, otherwise "exhausted"), and give back the result.

##### server/src/internal/migrations/v2/run/migrateCustomer/processOperations.ts
“Fold ordered customer operations onto one AutumnBillingPlan. Operations are sorted by execution order (add_plan → update_plan), preserving original array order within the same type. Each op sees the projected customer state from all previous ops.”

    • plan
    • projected full customer: context's full customer
    • matched customer products: 0
    • unchanged customer products: 0
    • billing contexts: an empty list
  Let operations be context's migration's operations' customer.
  Let sorted be operations, after these steps:
    1. Turn each op into an object with op and original index
    2. ␀them, sorted by this rule:
      • compare a and b by an execution priority (a's op) minus an execution priority (b's op)
  For each op and original index in sorted:
    Get processor (op) → processor.
    Let result be a processor:
      • context
      • op
      • op index: original index
      • plan: state's plan
      • projected full customer: state's projected full customer
    Set state to an object with:
      • plan: result's plan
      • projected full customer: apply Autumn billing plan to full customer:
        • full customer: context's full customer
        • Autumn billing plan: result's plan
      • matched customer products: state's matched customer products plus result's matched customer products
      • unchanged customer products: state's unchanged customer products plus result's unchanged customer products
      • billing contexts: state's billing contexts, plus result's billing contexts
  Give back state.

##### server/src/internal/migrations/v2/run/chunks/iterateMigrationChunks.ts

    Set cursor to chunk's cursor.
  Give back an object with processed, chunks, and canceled: false.

“Anchors Stripe resource reuse to the LATEST version of the BASE plan (`product.base_variant_id ?? product.id` — so a yearly variant like `pro_yearly` reuses `pro`'s price, not its own separate history) — not "whichever sibling this run happens to prepare first". ##### server/src/internal/migrations/v2/operations/updatePlan/compute/resolveFeatureQuantityStrategy.ts
Is finite tier? — given tier; gives back tier is UsageTier & { to: number }:
  Give back whether tier's to is a number.

“Resolves the customer's current monthly amount for `featureId` on this cusProduct, using the same pure amount calculator real invoice line items are built from (`usagePriceToLineItem` calls `priceToLineAmount`) — so "current spend" is computed identically to how it'd actually be invoiced.”
To resolve current amount — given feature ID and customer product; gives back a number (or nothing):
  Let old customer price be the first customer price in customer product's customer prices where all of these are true:
    • customer price's price is set
    • customer price's price is prepaid price
    • customer price's price's config's feature ID is feature ID
  If old customer price's price is missing, give back nothing.
  Let entitlement ID be old customer price's price's entitlement ID.
  Let old customer entitlement be the first customer entitlement in customer product's customer entitlements where customer entitlement's entitlement ID is entitlement ID if entitlement ID is set (otherwise nothing).
  If old customer entitlement is missing, give back nothing.
  Add customer product to customer entitlement (customer entitlement: old customer entitlement and customer product), and call the result customer entitlement with product.
  Let overage be the prepaid invoice overage of customer entitlement with product.
  Let allowance be the allowance of a list of customer entitlement with product.
  Give back the line amount of old customer price's price (given overage and allowance).

“Picks the total-inclusive quantity boundary (allowance + purchased) for the highest new tier whose flat_amount is at-or-below the given amount. If the customer's current spend doesn't clear even the cheapest paid tier, they land on the new item's included amount only — no purchase, matching "round to the lowest price" floor semantics — rather than throwing.”
To pick lowest price tier — given new item and amount; gives back a number:
  Let tiers be the new item's price's tiers that pass is finite tier.
  Let eligible be tiers, after these steps:
    1. Keep only those where tier's flat amount, or tier's amount if that's missing, or 0 if that's missing is at most amount
    2. ␀them, sorted by to (smallest first)
  Let chosen be the last of eligible.
  Give back chosen's to if chosen is set, otherwise new item's included, or 0 if that's missing.

“Resolves `op.feature_quantities_strategy` entries into concrete `FeatureQuantityParamsV0[]`, one per matched cusProduct. Skips entries with no existing prepaid price on this cusProduct (nothing to round down from).”
To resolve feature quantity strategy — given strategies, customer product, and add items; gives back a list of FeatureQuantityParamsV0:
  Let resolved be an empty list.
  For each feature ID and strategy in strategies:
    Skip it if strategy is not "round_to_lowest_price".
    Resolve current amount (feature ID and customer product) → amount.
    Skip it if amount is missing.
    Let new item be the first item in add items where item's feature ID is feature ID.
    Skip it if new item is missing.
    Pick lowest price tier (new item and amount), and call the result quantity.
    “`quantity` is total-inclusive (allowance + purchased) per volume-tier semantics; feed it unchanged into feature_quantities — downstream `paramsToFeatureOptions` subtracts the new entitlement's allowance itself before storing to FeatureOptions.quantity. Do not subtract here.”
    Add an object with feature ID: feature ID and quantity to resolved.
  Give back resolved.

##### server/src/internal/migrations/v2/lazy/checkPendingMigrationsForCustomer.ts
“For each pending lazy migration on `ctx.org`, decide whether this customer needs migrating and enqueue a per-customer Trigger.dev task if so. Reads `migration_item_runs` from the already-loaded `fullCustomer` (embedded by the FullSubject / FullCustomer query) — no extra DB roundtrip.   If the inside Trigger task is set, stop here.
  Let pending be the org's pending migrations.
  If pending is empty, stop here.
  Let item runs by migration internal ID be an empty lookup table.
  For each item run in full customer's migration item runs:
    Let existing be item runs by migration internal ID's entry for item run's migration internal ID.
    If any of these is true:
      • existing is missing
      • item run's updated at, or 0 if that's missing is more than existing's updated at, or 0 if that's missing
      • all of these are true:
        • item run's updated at is existing's updated at
        • item run's created at is after existing's created at
    then:
      Record item run under item run's migration internal ID in item runs by migration internal ID.
  For each pending migration in pending:
    From pending migration, take internal ID (as migration run ID) and migration.
    Let matches be a customer filter matches full customer:
      • filter: migration's filter's customer, or an empty object if that's missing
      • full customer
    Skip it if matches is missing.
    Let item run be item runs by migration internal ID's entry for migration's internal ID.
    If any of these is true:
      • item run's status is "succeeded"
      • item run's status is "skipped"
      • item run's status is "running"
    then:
      Move on to the next one.
    Let payload be an object with:
      • org ID: the org's ID
      • env: the env
      • migration internal ID: migration's internal ID
      • migration run ID
      • customer internal ID: full customer's internal ID
      • customer ID: full customer's ID, or nothing if that's missing
    If should run migration inline:
      Let inline context be context, but with inside Trigger task set to true.
      Nothing.
      Move on to the next one.
    Trigger run migration customer task (payload and priority: migration lazy task priority seconds).

##### server/src/internal/migrations/v2/handlers/handleCancelMigrationRun.ts
Let cancel migration run body be a schema for an object with ID.

“POST /migrations.cancel_run — request cancellation of the active migration_run for a migration, if any. Sets a cache token so in-flight items finish but no new items start. Lazy runs are marked `canceled` immediately (and the org cache cleared) so no further per-customer tasks are enqueued; batch runs settle to `canceled` once their runner drains. Errors if no active run exists.”
Create route, and call the result handle cancel migration run:
  • scopes: a list of scopes' migrations' write
  • body: cancel migration run body
  • handler: a function of c that:
    Let context be c's entry for "ctx".
    From c's request's valid ("json"), take ID.
    Find migration repo (ID), and call the result migration.
    List migration run repo (migration internal ID: migration's internal ID and active), and call the result active runs.
    Let active run be the first of active runs.
    If active run is missing:
      Fail with an error: "No active migration run for {ID}" [error code's invalid request] (status 404).
    Set migration cancel requested (migration run ID: active run's internal ID).
    “Trigger-dispatched runs: kill the task, then settle the row — but only once the platform confirms it stopped (a settled row releases the run claim, so a still-live task must never be left behind it). Runs with no trigger handle keep the cooperative flag-only behavior.”

##### server/src/internal/migrations/v2/batchOperations/scope/utils/expandPlanFilterDisjuncts.ts

##### server/src/internal/migrations/v2/batchOperations/scope/utils/scalarConstraint.ts
“`true`/`false` narrow the scope; `null` means "no constraint"; anything the batch lane cannot prove is `unsupported` → per-customer lane.”
Type ScalarConstraint: true/false or "unsupported" (or nothing).

“Boolean matcher → scalar. `{ $eq }` is handled defensively even though BooleanMatcherSchema is currently a bare boolean.”
To lower boolean matcher — given raw; gives back a ScalarConstraint:
  If raw is missing, give back nothing.
  If raw is true/false, give back raw.
  If raw is an object, raw is set, and raw has a "$eq" key:
    Let value be raw's eq.
    If value is true/false, give back value.
  Give back "unsupported".

“Null-existence matcher (`price`) → scalar: `null` / `{ $eq: null }` mean "absent" (false), `{ $ne: null }` means "present" (true).”
To lower null existence matcher — given raw; gives back a ScalarConstraint:
  If raw is missing, give back nothing.
  If raw is missing, give back whether false.
  If raw is an object:
    Let matcher be raw.
    If matcher has a "$ne" key and matcher's ne is missing, give back whether true.
    If matcher has a "$eq" key and matcher's eq is missing, give back whether false.
  Give back "unsupported".

“Both filter levels describe the same rows: null defers to the other level, both-set must agree, disagreement is unprovable.”
To reconcile constraints — given from op and from migration; gives back a ScalarConstraint:
  If from op is "unsupported" or from migration is "unsupported", give back "unsupported".
  If from op is missing, give back from migration.
  If from migration is missing, give back from op.
  Give back from op if from op is from migration, otherwise "unsupported".

##### server/src/internal/migrations/v2/batchOperations/execute/executeBatchMigrationPage.ts
“Executes one claimed page: every patch's ops (scoped by the patch's OperationScope), then the set-based status marks. Succeeded = customers a patch actually changed (≥1 inserted row); everyone else — out-of-scope OR already converged — is skipped. The unit of atomicity is one candidate BATCH, not the page: ops commit per bounded batch (see runCandidateBatches) and the marks commit in their own transaction. Safe because mutations are dedup-idempotent and the page's claims stay `running` until the marks land — a mid-page failure keeps committed batches and a replay converges the rest.”

      Set progress's last page finished at to the current time.

      Add 1 to summary's pages.
      Add the number of outcome's page result's succeeded to summary's succeeded.
      Add the number of outcome's page result's skipped to summary's skipped.

        Set chunk phases' entry for phase to chunk phases' entry for phase, or 0 if that's missing plus ms.
      Log "batch-migration: page executed" (with data).
  “The bounded drain runs on every exit path: an orphaned cache invalidation is silent, unrecoverable staleness.”
  Let loop be run pages, then (with the result as result) an object with ok: true and result.
  Clear interval (stall watchdog).
  Do these at the same time:
    • drain caches → caches drained
    • drain events
  If loop's ok is missing, fail with loop's error.
  If caches drained's failures is not empty:
    Let timed out be the number of caches drained's failures where failure's timed out is set.
    Fail with a batch migration cache invalidation error: "batch-migration: cache invalidation did not complete for {the number of caches drained's failures} page(s) ({timed out} timed out; {caches drained's failures, after these steps}); checkpoints revoked for retry where the revoke succeeded (see per-page logs)".
  “"finished" means every page's side effects landed, not just the loop.”
  Log "batch-migration: chunk finished" (with data).
  Give back loop's result.

“The statement timeout only starts once a connection answers; a dead socket needs the client-side race too, or recovery re-creates the stall.”

##### server/src/internal/migrations/v2/batchOperations/execute/utils/batchMigrationExecutionConstants.ts
“Customers claimed + mutated + finalized per loop iteration. Max ~7280: the claim binds ~9 params per row against Postgres' 65535 cap.”
Let batch migration page size be 5000.

“Timeout for each bounded page transaction (one candidate batch, or the final marks).”
Let batch migration page statement timeout ms be 60,000.

“Candidate rows read + mutated per batch TRANSACTION. Pages are sized in CUSTOMERS, so a page's row count is unbounded (a customer can hold many customer products); committing per cp.id-keyset batch keeps every transaction, statement and JS buffer bounded no matter how row-heavy the page is.”
Let batch migration candidate row batch be 10,000.

“Refuse a page with more candidate rows than this — grinding through more is never intended; fail loudly instead.”
Let batch migration max candidate rows per page be 1,000,000.

“Distinct live entitlement definitions for one feature on one page. One unique id per customer is the pathological ceiling; over this, refuse.”
Let batch migration max distinct entitlements be 5000.

“Runaway backstop: 2000 pages × 5000 customers = 10M per run.”
Let batch migration max pages be 2000.

“Pages per trigger chunk task invocation (~100k customers per task).”
Let batch migration pages per chunk be 20.

“Concurrent feature ops within one op type (removes, replaces, adds). Different features touch disjoint customer_entitlements rows. Env-overridable so a run can be ramped (or dropped to 1) without a deploy.”
Let batch migration feature op concurrency be the BATCH_MIGRATION_FEATURE_OP_CONCURRENCY environment variable, or 3 if that's missing as a number.

“Concurrent applyReplacePatches groups (distinct grant deltas) on one page.”
Let batch migration patch group concurrency be the BATCH_MIGRATION_PATCH_GROUP_CONCURRENCY environment variable, or 50 if that's missing as a number.

“Concurrent Redis full-customer cache invalidations during finalize.”
Let batch migration cache bust concurrency be 20.

“Pages whose post-commit side effects may be in flight at once.”
Let batch migration deferred inflight be 3.

“Ceiling for one page's deferred side effect (cache invalidation or item events); a hung call otherwise parks settle/drain until trigger kills the chunk.”
Let batch migration deferred operation timeout ms be 5 times 60,000.

“Budget for one page. Pages run in ~15s; anything past this is a stall, not a big page.”
Let batch migration page timeout ms be 5 times 60,000.

“How often a chunk with no page progress logs where it is stuck.”
Let batch migration stall log interval ms be 30,000.

“Kept free at the end of a chunk's deadline: one deferred-op drain, two bounded recovery writes (failed-page cache bust + claim release), and slack.”
Let batch migration chunk finalize reserve ms be batch migration deferred operation timeout ms plus 2 times batch migration page statement timeout ms plus 30,000.

“Attempts per page transaction when Postgres drops or times out before COMMIT.”
Let batch migration transient DB attempts be 5.

“First pause between those attempts; doubles each retry (1+2+4+8s).”
Let batch migration transient DB retry delay ms be 1000.

“Below this much remaining budget a chunk yields `slice_complete` instead of starting a page that could only stall.”
Let batch migration min page budget ms be 60,000.

      • batch migration page statement timeout ms

##### server/src/internal/migrations/v2/batchOperations/compute/computeBatchMigration.ts
“One unit of batch work to compute: an op applied to one catalog product a plan_filter disjunct matched, carrying that disjunct's conjunct filters.”
Type UpdatePlanTarget: an object.

“Lowers a migration's ordered customer operations into uniform, set-based batch patches. Pure — callers load the full catalog (every version, via ProductService.listFull returnAll) and features up front. Conservative by construction: any op whose per-customer outcome cannot be proven identical for every matched customer produces a rejection, and one rejection anywhere routes the WHOLE migration to the per-customer lane (all-or-nothing; no lane mixing). Rejections are collected exhaustively so the fallback reason is fully auditable. `computable: true` with zero patches means every op is a provable no-op.”
To compute batch migration — given migration, products, and features; gives back a BatchMigrationComputeResult:
  “1. Migration-level gate: no_billing_changes, supported op types.”
  Check migration eligibility (migration), and take its rejections and update plan ops.
  Let products by plan version be an empty lookup table.
  For each product in products:
    Record product under the string of the product key of product in products by plan version.
  “2. Resolve ops to flat (op, fromProduct) targets: op-level guards, then plan_filter matched against the catalog.”
  Let targets be an empty list.
  For each op and op index in update plan ops:
    Check update plan op eligibility (op and op index), and call the result op rejections.
    If op rejections is not empty:
      Add everything in op rejections to rejections.
      Move on to the next one.
    “$or expands into disjuncts; a product matches a disjunct when EVERY conjunct's catalog part matches it.”
    Let op targets be all results, combined, of turning each plan filters in expand plan filter disjuncts (op's plan filter) into products, after these steps:
      1. Keep only those where every plan filter in plan filters satisfies: plan filter matches product (given a to catalog plan filter (plan filter) and product)
      2. Turn each from product into an object with:
        • op
        • op index
        • from product
        • plan filters
    If op targets is empty:
      Add an object with to rejections:
        • code: "no_matched_products"
        • op index
        • message: "plan_filter matches no catalog product; nothing for this operation to target."
      Move on to the next one.
    Add everything in op targets to targets.
  “3. Compute one patch per target.”
  Let patches be an empty list.
  For each target in targets:
    Compute update plan patch, and call the result computed:
      • migration
      • features
      • products by plan version
      • everything in target
    Add everything in computed's rejections to rejections.
    If computed's patch is set, add computed's patch to patches.
  “4. Ordered ops project state — two ops touching the same product is not modeled.”
  Add everything in check overlapping patches (patches) to rejections.
  If rejections is not empty, give back an object with computable: false and rejections.
  Give back an object with computable: true and plan: an object with patches.

“Two-phase claim for a migration run. 1. Insert with `status='queued'` — the partial unique index (one live run per migration) blocks concurrent claims of the same migration. 2. Run `claimed` (e.g. `prepare`, or trigger.dev dispatch). 3. On success the row stays `queued` — dispatch ≠ execution, and `withMigrationRunTracking` flips it to `running` when the task starts. Lazy runs are live as soon as prepare completes, so they flip here. On failure, flip to `failed` so the constraint releases. 4. `claimed` may return `{ triggerRunId }` to persist a handle. The SDK mints that id locally, so a handle alone does not prove the task was enqueued; `verifyDispatch` reads it back and a run that never reached the platform fails here instead of sitting `queued` forever.”

  Start with no result yet.
  Try the following:
    Set result to a claimed (migration run's internal ID).
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Fail run:
      • migration run ID: migration run's internal ID

      • error code: a classify migration run error (error)

        • migration run ID: migration run's internal ID

##### server/src/internal/logs/parser/restrictedApl.ts
Type RestrictedAplField: an object or an object.
Type LiteralValue: text, a number, or true/false (or nothing).
Type CompareOperator: one of "==", "!=", ">", ">=", "<", or "<=".
Type RestrictedAplExpr: an object, an object, an object, or an object.

Type SummarizeAggregation: an object.

Text decoder — given value:
  Give back value with /\\(['"\\])/g replaced by "$1".

To assert no dangerous text — given query:
  For each pattern and message in restricted apl dangerous text patterns:
    If query matches pattern, fail with an error: message.

Tokenize — given query; gives back a list of Token:
  Assert no dangerous text (query).
  Let tokens be an empty list.
  Let i start as 0.
  Keep repeating while i is less than the number of query:
    Let char be query's entry for i.
    If char matches /\s/:
      Increase i by 1.
      Move on to the next one.
    Let two be query from position i up to i plus 2.
    “Agents habitually write C-style logical operators.”
    If two is "&&" or two is "||":
      Add an object with kind: "identifier" and value: "and" if two is "&&", otherwise "or" to tokens:
      Add 2 to i.
      Move on to the next one.
    If char is "|":
      Add an object with kind: "symbol" and value: "|" to tokens.
      Increase i by 1.
      Move on to the next one.
    If char is "(", char is ")", or char is ",":
      Add an object with kind: "symbol" and value: char to tokens.
      Increase i by 1.
      Move on to the next one.
    If any of these is true:
      • two is "=="
      • two is "!="
      • two is ">="
      • two is "<="
    then:
      Add an object with kind: "symbol" and value: two to tokens.
      Add 2 to i.
      Move on to the next one.
    If char is ">" or char is "<":
      Add an object with kind: "symbol" and value: char to tokens.
      Increase i by 1.
      Move on to the next one.
    If char is "=":
      Add an object with kind: "symbol" and value: "=" to tokens.
      Increase i by 1.
      Move on to the next one.
    If char is "'" or char is """:
      Let quote be char.
      Let j start as i plus 1.
      Let raw start as "".
      Keep repeating while j is less than the number of query:
        Let current be query's entry for j.
        If current is "\":
          Let next be query's entry for j plus 1.
          If next is not "\" and next is not quote, fail with an error: "Only escaped quotes and backslashes are supported".
          Add current plus next to raw.
          Add 2 to j.
          Move on to the next one.
        Stop the loop if current is quote.
        Add current to raw.
        Increase j by 1.
      If j is at least the number of query or query's entry for j is not quote, fail with an error: "Unterminated string literal".
      Add an object with kind: "string" and value: a text decoder (raw) to tokens.
      Set i to j plus 1.
      Move on to the next one.
    If char matches /[0-9-]/:
      Match query from position i onward (/^-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?/) → match.
      If match is missing, fail with an error: "Invalid number literal".
      Add an object with kind: "number" and value: the first of match as a number to tokens.
      Add the number of the first of match to i.
      Move on to the next one.
    If char matches /[A-Za-z_]/:
      Match query from position i onward (/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_.]*/) → match.
      If match is missing, fail with an error: "Invalid identifier".
      Add an object with kind: "identifier" and value: the first of match to tokens.
      Add the number of the first of match to i.
      Move on to the next one.
    Fail with an error: "Unsupported query character: {char}".
  Give back tokens.

Let nested root names be the keys of restricted apl nested roots.

Is nested root? — given value; gives back value is RestrictedAplNestedRoot:
  Give back whether value is in nested root names.

  Split raw split on "." into root and any other path.
  If root is not nested, give back nothing.

    Fail with an error: "Nested query field must have 1-{restricted apl max nested path depth} path segments: {raw}".

Class Parser:
  Field index starts as 0.

Field → apl — given field; gives back text:
  Give back the apl of field's name if field's kind is "topLevel", otherwise the apl of field.

Nested field alias — given field:
  Give back a list of field's root and everything in field's path joined with "_".

Field → string apl — given field; gives back text:
  If field's kind is "nested", give back "tostring({the apl of field})".
  If field's name is "request_body" or field's name is "response_body", give back "dynamic_to_json({the apl of field})".
  Give back the apl of field.

Field → comparison apl — given field and value; gives back text:
  If field's kind is not "nested", give back the apl of field.
  If value is text, give back "tostring({the apl of field})".
  If value is a number, give back "todouble({the apl of field})".
  If value is true/false, give back "tobool({the apl of field})".
  Give back the apl of field.

Field → in apl — given field and values; gives back text:
  If field's kind is not "nested", give back the apl of field.
  Let non null values be values, keeping only those where value is set.
  If every value in non null values satisfies: value is text, give back "tostring({the apl of field})".
  If every value in non null values satisfies: value is a number, give back "todouble({the apl of field})".
  If every value in non null values satisfies: value is true/false, give back "tobool({the apl of field})".
  Give back the apl of field.

Field → summarize by apl — given field; gives back text:
  If field's kind is "topLevel", give back the apl of field.
  Give back "{nested field alias (field)} = tostring({the apl of field})".

“Aliased back to `timestamp` so later order/project stages keep working.”
To summarize by column to apl — given column; gives back text:
  If column's kind is "bin":
    Give back "timestamp = bin(timestamp, {column's interval})".
  Otherwise:
    Give back the summarize by apl of column's field.

Field → numeric aggregate apl — given field; gives back text:
  Give back "todouble({the apl of field})" if field's kind is "nested", otherwise the apl of field.

Reference → apl — given reference; gives back text:
  If reference's kind is "identifier", give back reference's name.
  From reference, take field.
  If field's kind is "nested", give back "tostring({the apl of field})".
  Give back the apl of field.

Reference → project apl — given alias and source; gives back text:
  If alias is set, give back "{alias} = {the apl of source}".
  If source's kind is "field" and source's field's kind is "nested":
    Give back "{nested field alias (source's field)} = {the apl of source}".
  Give back the apl of source.

Class Restricted apl stage not allowed error (extends error):
  When created — given stage:
    Set up the parent class ("Unsupported query stage: {stage}").

To parse restricted apl — given query and allowed stages; gives back a RestrictedAplAst:
  Let trimmed be query without surrounding spaces.
  If trimmed is missing, give back an object with stages: an empty list.
  Parse a new parser (a tokenize (trimmed)), and call the result ast.
  Let allowed be allowed stages, or default restricted apl stages if that's missing.
  For each stage in ast's stages:
    If stage's kind is not in allowed, fail with a restricted apl stage not allowed error: stage's kind.
  Give back ast.

Escape apl string — given value; gives back text:
  Give back value with /\\/g replaced by "\\" with /'/g replaced by "\'".

Literal → apl — given value; gives back text:
  If value is text, give back "'{an escape apl string (value)}'".
  If value is missing, give back "null".
  Give back value as text.

Expr → apl — given expr; gives back text:
  Depending on expr's kind:
    • If it is "comparison":
      Give back "{the comparison apl of expr's field (given expr's value)} {expr's op} {the apl of expr's value}".
    • If it is "stringMatch":
      Give back "{the string apl of expr's field} {expr's op} '{an escape apl string (expr's value)}'".
    • If it is "in":
      Give back "{the in apl of expr's field (given expr's values)} in ({expr's values, after these steps})".
    • If it is "and" or "or":
      Give back "({the apl of expr's left} {expr's kind} {the apl of expr's right})".

To summarize function to apl — given function; gives back text:
  Depending on function's kind:
    • If it is "count":
      Give back "count()".
    • If it is "countif":
      Give back "countif({the apl of function's expr})".
    • If it is "numeric":
      Give back "{function's name}({the numeric aggregate apl of function's field})".
    • If it is "percentile":
      Give back "percentile({the numeric aggregate apl of function's field}, {function's percentile})".

Restricted apl → apl — given ast; gives back a list of text:
  Give back ast's stages, with each stage turned into the result of:
    Depending on stage's kind:
      • If it is "where":
        Give back "| where {the apl of stage's expr}".
      • If it is "orderBy":
        Give back "| order by {the apl of stage's target} {stage's direction}".
      • If it is "limit":
        Give back "| limit {stage's value}".
      • If it is "summarize":
        Let aggregations be stage's aggregations, after these steps:
          1. Turn each item (alias and function) into "{alias} = {summarize function to apl (function)}"
          2. Join them with ", "
        Let by be " by {stage's by, after these steps}" if stage's by is not empty, otherwise "".
        Give back "| summarize {aggregations}{by}".
      • If it is "project":
        Give back "| project {stage's columns, after these steps}".
    Fail with an error: "Unsupported restricted APL stage".

##### server/src/internal/logs/actions/searchRequestLogs/projectRequestLog.ts
Type RequestLogSource: one of "api_request" or "stripe_webhook".
Type ApiRequestLogEntry: an object.
Type AxiomMatch: an object.

To pick string — given data and keys; gives back text (or nothing):
  For each key in keys:
    Let value be data's entry for key.
    If value is text and value is not empty, give back value.
  Give back nothing.

To pick number — given data and keys; gives back a number (or nothing):
  For each key in keys:
    Let value be data's entry for key.
    If value is a number and value is a real number, give back value.
  Give back nothing.

To pick unknown — given data and keys; gives back anything (or nothing):

  Give back nothing.

  Try the following:
    Give back a new URL (URL)'s pathname.
  If anything fails:

  If path starts with "/v1", give back "api_request".

    • source
    • status code: pick number (data and a list of "status_code" and "statusCode"), or 0 if that's missing

      • URL
      • path
    • context: an object with:
      • org ID: pick string (data and a list of "org_id" and "context.org_id")

        • data

“Rows stranded by a parent transition: parent expired with ended_at inside the live parents' phase-adjacency window (a switch ends the old parent the moment a live one starts). The time bound is what keeps this read bounded — long-dead rows are never fetched; set-based sweeps handle them without reads. Returned oldest-first so slot contention resolves deterministically.”
To list adoptable stranded customer licenses — given internal customer ID and live parent start times; gives back a list of StrandedCustomerLicense (async):
  If live parent start times is empty, give back an empty list.
  Let ended at min ms be the smaller of all of live parent start times minus phase boundary tolerance ms.
  Let ended at max ms be the larger of all of live parent start times plus phase boundary tolerance ms.
  Let parent product be alias (products and "parent_product").
  Let license product be alias (products and "license_product").
  Let rows be look up fields from customer licenses:
    • picking an object with:
      • customer license: customer licenses
      • parent ended at: customer products' ended at
      • parent group: parent product's group
      • license plan ID: license product's ID
    • joined with customer products on customer licenses' parent customer product ID is customer products' ID
    • joined with parent product on customer products' internal product ID is parent product's internal ID
    • joined with license product on customer licenses' license internal product ID is license product's internal ID
    • where all of these are true:
      • customer licenses' internal customer ID is internal customer ID
      • customer products' status is customer product status's expired
      • customer products' ended at is at least ended at min ms
      • customer products' ended at is at most ended at max ms
  Give back rows, after these steps:
    1. Turn each row into depending on whether row's parent ended at is missing, and flatten the results into one list:
      • if so: an empty list
      • if not: a list of row, but with parent ended at set to row's parent ended at
    2. ␀them, sorted by this rule:
      • compare a and b by a's customer license's created at minus b's customer license's created at, or how a's customer license's ID compares alphabetically to b's customer license's ID if that's empty

Create route, and call the result handle mint key:
  • scopes: a list of scopes' API keys' write
  • body: mint key params schema
  • handler: a function of c that:
    Let context be c's entry for "ctx".
    From c's request's valid ("json"), take customer ID and indefinite.
    Let customer be customer service's entry for an object with:
      • DB: the context
      • ID or internal ID: customer ID
      • org ID: the org's ID
      • env: the env
    If customer is missing:
      Fail with an error: "Customer {customer ID} not found" [error code's customer not found] (status 404).
    Read family (internal customer ID: customer's internal ID) → family.
    Let epoch be family's epoch, or 0 if that's missing.
    Let refresh kid be family's refresh kid, or 0 if that's missing plus 1.
    Set family:
      • internal customer ID: customer's internal ID
      • org ID: the org's ID
      • env: the env
      • epoch
      • refresh kid
      • indefinite: indefinite, or false if that's missing
    Mint token pair → pair:
      • customer ID: customer's ID, or customer's internal ID if that's missing
      • internal customer ID: customer's internal ID
      • env: the env
      • epoch
      • refresh kid
      • indefinite: indefinite, or false if that's missing
    Give back c's JSON:

      • refresh token: pair's refresh token
      • expires at: pair's expires at
      • refresh expires at: pair's refresh expires at

##### server/src/internal/keys/handleRefreshKey.ts
“Tenant self-service: exchange a refresh token (verified + scoped by customerJwtMiddleware) for a fresh access + refresh pair. Rotating with a 1-generation grace window so retries / multi-node don't false-positive into a reuse lockout.”
Create route, and call the result handle refresh key:
  • scopes: a list of scopes' public
  • handler: a function of c that:
    Let context be c's entry for "ctx".
    Let claim be the customer JWT.
    If claim is missing, fail with an error: "Missing customer token" [error code's invalid request] (status 401).
    Read family (internal customer ID: claim's internal customer ID) → family.
    Let epoch be family's epoch, or 0 if that's missing.
    Let current be family's refresh kid, or 0 if that's missing.
    Let presented be claim's refresh kid.
    Let write key be an object with:
      • internal customer ID: claim's internal customer ID
      • org ID: the org's ID
      • env: the env
    Start with no refresh kid yet.
    If presented is current:
      Set refresh kid to current plus 1.
      “rotate”
      Set family (everything in write key, epoch, and refresh kid).
    Otherwise, if presented is current minus 1:
      Set refresh kid to current.
      “grace: re-issue at current generation”
      Set family (everything in write key, epoch, and refresh kid).
    Otherwise:
      “Older than the grace window ⇒ reuse ⇒ revoke the whole family.”
      Bump epoch (write key).
      Fail with an error: "Refresh token reuse detected" [error code's invalid request] (status 401).
    Mint token pair → pair:
      • customer ID: claim's customer ID
      • internal customer ID: claim's internal customer ID
      • env: the env
      • epoch
      • refresh kid
    Give back c's JSON:
      • access token: pair's access token
      • refresh token: pair's refresh token
      • expires at: pair's expires at
      • refresh expires at: pair's refresh expires at

##### server/src/internal/keys/handleRevokeKey.ts

    Let context be c's entry for "ctx".

      • DB: the context
      • ID or internal ID: customer ID
      • org ID: the org's ID
      • env: the env
    If customer is missing:
      Fail with an error: "Customer {customer ID} not found" [error code's customer not found] (status 404).
    Bump epoch:
      • internal customer ID: customer's internal ID
      • org ID: the org's ID
      • env: the env
    Give back c's JSON (revoked).
