##### server/src/internal/invoices/lineItems/actions/storeLineItems.ts
“Mirrors a Stripe invoice's lines into Autumn, enriched with Autumn billing context.”
To store line items — given Stripe invoice ID, Autumn invoice ID, billing line items, and reconcile only (async):
  From context, take org and env.
  Create Stripe client (org and env) → Stripe client.
  “1. Fetch line items from Stripe.”
  Get Stripe invoice line items (Stripe client and invoice ID: Stripe invoice ID), and call the result Stripe line items.
  “Subscription discounts appear in discount_amounts on each line, but their expanded coupon is only available through invoice.discounts.”
  Let Stripe discounts be depending on whether Stripe line items has a line item where the number of line item's discount amounts, or 0 if that's missing is positive:
    • if so: get Stripe invoice's discounts:
      • Stripe client
      • invoice ID: Stripe invoice ID
      • expand: a list of "discounts.source.coupon"
    • if not: an empty list
  If Stripe line items is empty:
    Debug log "[storeInvoiceLineItems] No line items found for {Stripe invoice ID}".
    “Still need to delete any stale items (invoice might have been emptied)”
    Delete invoice line item repo stale by Stripe invoice ID (Stripe invoice ID and active Stripe IDs: an empty list).
    Stop here.
  “2. Fetch subscription item info (metadata + isMetered flag)”
  Fetch subscription items info (Stripe client and Stripe line items), and call the result subscription item info.
  “3. Filter out $0 placeholder line items Stripe creates these for usage-based prices with zero usage, and for empty price placeholders (stripe_empty_price_id) used on entity subscriptions”
  Let filtered Stripe line items be Stripe line items, keeping only the lis that pass this check:
    If li's amount is not 0, give back whether true.
    If li's quantity, or 0 if that's missing is not 0, give back whether true.
    Let subscription item ID be li's parent's subscription item details' subscription item.
    If subscription item ID is not text, give back whether true.
    Let info be subscription item info's entry for subscription item ID.
    If info is metered, give back whether false.
    If li's pricing's unit amount decimal is "0", give back whether false.
    Give back whether true.
  “4. Update deferred line items that were stored at billing time When ProrateNextCycle creates pending invoice items, they're stored with invoice_id=null. Now that they appear on a real invoice, update them.”
  Update deferred line items, and call the result remaining Stripe line items:
    • Stripe line items: filtered Stripe line items
    • Autumn invoice ID
    • Stripe invoice ID
  “5. Parse billing line items if provided”
  Start with no Autumn line items yet.
  If billing line items is set and billing line items is not empty:
    Set Autumn line items to billing line items, after these steps:
      1. Turn each item into the result of these steps:
        Let result be a safe parse [LineItemSchema] (item).
        If result's success is missing:
          Warn "[storeInvoiceLineItems] Dropping unparseable billing line item for {Stripe invoice ID}: {result's error's issues, after these steps}".
          Give back nothing.
        Give back result's data.
      2. Keep only those where item is set
  “6. Convert to DB format (extract metadata for matching)”
  Let subscription item metadata be a lookup table built from subscription item info's entries as a list, each turned into a list of ID and info's metadata.
  Let DB line items be the DB line items of remaining Stripe line items:
    • Stripe discounts
    • invoice ID: Autumn invoice ID
    • Stripe invoice ID
    • Autumn line items
    • subscription item metadata
  “7. Write to DB”
  If DB line items is not empty:
    If reconcile only is true:
      “Reconcile mode: only update Stripe-authoritative fields, preserve Autumn metadata”
      Reconcile invoice line item repo many (line items: DB line items).
    Otherwise:
      “Full upsert: update all columns (used when we have full Autumn context)”
      Upsert invoice line item repo many (line items: DB line items).
    Log "{"Reconciled" if reconcile only is true, otherwise "Stored"} invoice line items" (with data2).
  “8. Delete stale line items (removed between invoice.created and invoice.finalized) Use filtered list so we also delete $0 metered placeholders from DB”
  Let active Stripe IDs be filtered Stripe line items, after these steps:
    1. Take each one's ID
    2. Keep only those where ID is set
  Delete invoice line item repo stale by Stripe invoice ID (Stripe invoice ID and active Stripe IDs).

“Finds Stripe line items that originated from pending invoice items (deferred charges), checks if we have pre-stored deferred DB rows for them, and updates those rows with the real invoice info + new Stripe line item ID. Returns the Stripe line items that were NOT matched to deferred rows (i.e., the ones that still need normal processing).”
To update deferred line items — given Stripe line items, Autumn invoice ID, and Stripe invoice ID; gives back a list of ExpandedStripeInvoiceLineItem (async):
  “Collect invoice_item IDs from Stripe line items with invoice_item_details parent”
  Let invoice item map be an empty lookup table.
  For each li in Stripe line items:
    Let invoice item ID be li's parent's invoice item details' invoice item.
    If invoice item ID is text, record li under invoice item ID in invoice item map.
  If invoice item map's size is 0, give back Stripe line items.
  “Query DB for existing deferred rows”
  Start with no deferred rows yet.
  Try the following:
    Get invoice line item repo deferred by invoice item IDs (Stripe invoice item IDs: invoice item map's keys as a list), and put the result in deferred rows.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Log an error "[storeInvoiceLineItems] Failed loading deferred rows for {Stripe invoice ID}: {error's message if error is an error, otherwise "Unknown error"}".
    Give back Stripe line items.
  If deferred rows is empty, give back Stripe line items.
  “Update each matched deferred row with invoice info”
  Let matched invoice item IDs be an empty set.
  For each row in deferred rows:
    Try the following:
      Skip it if row's Stripe invoice item ID is missing.
      Let Stripe line item be invoice item map's entry for row's Stripe invoice item ID.
      Skip it if Stripe line item is missing.
      Let amount be the Autumn amount of Stripe:
        • amount: Stripe line item's amount
        • currency: Stripe line item's currency
      Let discount total be the total amount across Stripe line item's discount amounts.
      Let amount after discounts be the Autumn amount of Stripe:
        • amount: Stripe line item's amount minus discount total
        • currency: Stripe line item's currency
      Update invoice line item repo deferred line item:
        • ID: row's ID

“Creates and finalizes the replacement, then retires the original: an open invoice is voided and its deferred pointers move across, while a paid one keeps its money and gets a credit note instead.”

    Delete draft (Stripe client and draft ID: draft's ID).

    Give back a credit and issue:
      • Stripe client
      • Stripe invoice
      • draft
      • issue method
  “Automatic collection is what makes Stripe treat the replacement as the subscription's receivable (overdue → past_due, paid → active). Parked before the replacement is issued so Stripe's scheduled finalization can't race it; a draft Stripe finalized meanwhile comes back open and is voided like any other.”
  Let original is draft mean all of these are true:

    Delete draft (Stripe client and draft ID: draft's ID).
    Fail with error.

    Repoint deferred references:
      • from Stripe invoice ID: Stripe invoice's ID
      • to Stripe invoice ID: issued's ID
    If original is draft is false, Void invoice (invoice ID).
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    “The original keeps standing; retire the replacement instead.”
    Repoint deferred references (and if that fails, nothing instead):
      • from Stripe invoice ID: issued's ID
      • to Stripe invoice ID: Stripe invoice's ID

      An unpark draft original (Stripe client and Stripe invoice) (and if that fails, nothing instead).

    “Stripe may have collected the original between our read and the void.”

      Fail with an error: "Invoice {invoice ID} was paid while being reissued; nothing was changed" [error code's invalid request] (status 409).
    Fail with error.

  Give back an object with:
    • issued: collect remainder now (Stripe client and finalized: issued)

    Stop here.

  Let invoice be retrieve Stripe client's invoices (Stripe invoice ID) (and if that fails, nothing instead).

“Returns a paid invoice's money to the customer's Stripe balance and issues the replacement, which that balance settles once finalized. No refund is issued: the cash never moves. The credit must exist before finalization or Stripe bills the replacement in full, so a finalization failure has to hand the credit back — a credit note on a paid invoice cannot be voided, which leaves a reversing balance entry.”
Credit and issue — given Stripe client, Stripe invoice, draft, and issue method; gives back an object with issued and credit note ID (async):
  Let amount be Stripe invoice's amount paid.

    • amount
    • credit amount: amount
    • reason: "order_change"

  Start with no issued yet.
  Try the following:
    Issue Stripe invoice (Stripe client, draft, and issue method), and put the result in issued.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Try the following:
      Reverse credit:
        • Stripe client
        • Stripe invoice
        • credit note
        • amount
    Either way, finally:
      Delete draft (Stripe client and draft ID: draft's ID).
    Fail with error.
  Give back an object with:
    • issued: collect remainder now (Stripe client and finalized: issued)
    • credit note ID: credit note's ID

“Stripe waits about an hour before first attempting a card invoice created through the API, so a card replacement is charged now instead. A declined card leaves it open for Stripe's retries, like any other invoice.”

##### server/src/internal/features/utils/updateFeatureUtils/detectFeatureUpdateBlockers.ts

    • from is not feature type's credit system and to is feature type's credit system

“Whether a change touches the dimensions (type/id/usage_type) that can block.”

  Let is changing type mean updates' type is set and feature's type is not updates' type.
  Let is changing ID mean updates' ID is set and feature's ID is not updates' ID.
  Let is changing usage type mean all of these are true:
    • feature's type is not feature type's boolean
    • updates' type is not feature type's boolean
    • feature's config's usage type is not updates' config's usage type
  Give back whether is changing type, is changing ID, or is changing usage type.

“Read-only detection of every condition that would make `updateFeature` reject the change, in the same priority order it throws. Shared by the live update path and `catalog.preview_update` so the two never drift.”
To detect feature update blockers — given feature, updates, objects using feature, and all features; gives back a list of FeatureUpdateBlocker:
  From objects using feature, take entitlements, prices, credit systems, linked entitlements, and customer entitlements.
  Let blockers be an empty list.
  Let is changing type mean updates' type is set and feature's type is not updates' type.
  Let is changing ID mean updates' ID is set and feature's ID is not updates' ID.
  Let is changing usage type mean all of these are true:
    • feature's type is not feature type's boolean
    • updates' type is not feature type's boolean
    • feature's config's usage type is not updates' config's usage type
  If is changing type and updates' type is set:
    Let new type be updates' type.
    If feature's type is credit system switch (given new type):
      Add an object with to blockers:
        • field: "type"
        • code: "type_switch_credit_system"
        • message: "Cannot change type of feature {feature's ID} from {feature's type} to {new type}"
    If customer entitlements is not empty:
      Add an object with to blockers:
        • field: "type"
        • code: "attached_to_customer"
        • message: "Cannot change type of feature {feature's ID} because it has been attached to a customer before"
    If linked entitlements is not empty:
      Add an object with to blockers:
        • field: "type"
        • code: "used_as_entity_feature"
        • message: "Cannot change type of feature {feature's ID} because it is used in an entity feature by {the first of linked entitlements' feature's name}"
    If prices is not empty:
      Add an object with to blockers:
        • field: "type"
        • code: "has_usage_price"
        • message: "Cannot change type of feature {feature's ID} because it has a usage price set"
    If credit systems is not empty:
      Add an object with to blockers:
        • field: "type"
        • code: "used_in_credit_system"
        • message: "Cannot change type of feature {feature's ID} because it is used in a credit system"
    If all of these are true:
      • entitlements is not empty
      • feature's type is feature type's credit system or new type is feature type's credit system
    then:
      Add an object with to blockers:
        • field: "type"
        • code: "used_in_product_credit_system"
        • message: "Cannot change type from {feature's type} to {new type} because the feature is used in a product"
  If is changing ID and updates' ID is set:
    Let new ID be updates' ID.
    If all features has a other where other's ID is new ID:
      Add an object with to blockers:
        • field: "id"
        • code: "id_already_exists"
        • message: "Feature {new ID} already exists"
    If customer entitlements is not empty:
      Add an object with to blockers:
        • field: "id"
        • code: "attached_to_customer"
        • message: "Cannot change id of feature {feature's ID} because a customer is using it or has used it before"
  If is changing usage type and updates' config's usage type is set:
    Let usage type title be the title of updates' config's usage type in lowercase.
    If credit systems is not empty:
      Add an object with to blockers:
        • field: "usage_type"
        • code: "used_in_credit_system"
        • message: "Cannot set to {usage type title} because it is used in credit system {the first of credit systems' ID}"
    If linked entitlements is not empty:
      Add an object with to blockers:
        • field: "usage_type"
        • code: "used_as_entity_feature"
        • message: "Cannot set to {usage type title} because it is used as an entity by {the first of linked entitlements' feature's name}"
    If customer entitlements is not empty:
      Add an object with to blockers:
        • field: "usage_type"
        • code: "attached_to_customer"
        • message: "Cannot set to {usage type title} because it is / was used by customers"
  Give back blockers.

##### server/src/internal/features/featureActions/updateFeature.ts
Type UpdateFeatureParams: context, feature ID, and updates.

“Generic keyed-record equality check with a caller-supplied per-entry comparison.”
Are markup records equal? — given a, b, and entries equal; gives back true/false:
  Let a is absent mean a is missing.
  Let b is absent mean b is missing.
  If a is absent is true and b is absent is true, give back whether true.
  If a is absent is true or b is absent is true, give back whether false.
  Let a keys be the keys of a.
  Let b keys be the keys of b.
  If the number of a keys is not the number of b keys, give back whether false.
  For each key in a keys:
    Let a entry be a's entry for key.
    Let b entry be b's entry for key.
    If b entry is missing, give back whether false.
    If there is no entries equal (a entry and b entry), give back whether false.
  Give back whether true.

Are model markups equal? — given a and b; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether a are markup records equal (given b and a function of a entry and b entry giving back whether all of these are true):
    • a entry's markup is b entry's markup
    • a entry's input cost is b entry's input cost
    • a entry's output cost is b entry's output cost

Are provider markups equal? — given a and b; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether a are markup records equal (given b and a function of a entry and b entry giving back whether a entry's markup is b entry's markup).

Has ai markup config changed? — given old config and new config; gives back true/false:
  If old config's default markup, or nothing if that's missing is not new config's default markup, or nothing if that's missing:
    Give back whether true.
  Give back whether old config's provider markups are not provider markups equal (given b: new config's provider markups).

“Reproduce the exact error `updateFeature` historically threw for a blocker.”
To throw feature update blocker — given blocker and new ID:
  If blocker's code is "id_already_exists" and new ID is set, fail with a feature already exists error.
  Fail with an error: blocker's message [nothing if blocker's code is "type_switch_credit_system"; otherwise error code's invalid feature] (status 400).

“Updates an existing feature with full validation logic”
To update feature — given feature ID and updates; gives back a Feature (or nothing) (async):
  “1. Get all features and find the one to update”
  List [FeatureService] (org ID: the org's ID and env: the env), and call the result all features.
  Let feature be the first f in all features where f's ID is feature ID.
  If feature is missing, fail with an error: "Feature {feature ID} not found" [error code's invalid feature] (status 404).
  “Check if changing type, id, or usage type”
  Let is changing type mean updates' type is set and feature's type is not updates' type.
  Let is changing ID mean updates' ID is set and feature's ID is not updates' ID.
  Let is changing usage type mean all of these are true:
    • feature's type is not feature type's boolean
    • updates' type is not feature type's boolean
    • feature's config's usage type is not updates' config's usage type
  Let is changing name mean updates' name is set and feature's name is not updates' name.
  If is changing type, is changing ID, or is changing usage type:
    Get objects using feature (feature) → objects using feature.
    “Validate the whole change before any mutation so it stays atomic.”
    Split detect feature update blockers into blocker:
      • feature
      • updates
      • objects using feature
      • all features
    If blocker is set, Throw feature update blocker (blocker and new ID: updates' ID).
    “Handle type change”
    If is changing type and updates' type is set:
      Handle feature type changed (objects using feature, feature, and new type: updates' type).
    From objects using feature, take linked entitlements, entitlements, prices, and credit systems.
    “Handle ID change”
    If is changing ID and updates' ID is set:
      Handle feature ID changed:
        • feature
        • linked entitlements
        • entitlements
        • prices
        • credit systems
        • new ID: updates' ID
    “Handle usage type change”
    If is changing usage type and updates' config's usage type is set:
      Handle feature usage type changed:
        • feature
        • linked entitlements
        • entitlements
        • prices
        • credit systems
        • new usage type: updates' config's usage type
  Let effective type be updates' type, or feature's type if that's missing.
  Let new config be the result of a function that:
    If updates' config is missing, give back feature's config.
    Depending on effective type:
      • If it is feature type's ai credit system or feature type's credit system:
        Validate credit system (updates' config and effective type), and call the result validated config.
        If effective type is feature type's credit system:
          Validate credit system schema references:
            • config: validated config
            • all features
            • self feature ID: updates' ID, or feature's ID if that's missing
        Give back validated config.
      • If it is feature type's metered:
        Validate metered config (updates' config), and give back the result.
      • For anything else:
        Give back updates' config.
  Let is credit system mean feature's type is any credit system.
  Let rate card changed mean all of these are true:
    • is credit system
    • updates' config is set
    • feature's config has credit rate card changed (given new config)
  Let markups changed mean all of these are true:
    • is credit system
    • updates' model markups is set
    • updates' model markups are not model markups equal (given b: feature's model markups)
  Let ai markup config changed mean all of these are true:
    • feature's type is ai credit system
    • updates' config is set
    • feature's config has ai markup config changed (given new config)
  Let should clear credit system customer cache mean rate card changed is true, markups changed is true, or ai markup config changed is true.
  “Update the feature”
  Update [FeatureService], and call the result updated feature:
    • ID: feature ID
    • org ID: the org's ID
    • env: the env
    • updates: an object with:

      • event names: updates' event names
      • config: new config
      • model markups: updates' model markups
      • display: updates' display

  If is changing name and updated feature is set:
    Trigger workflows generate feature display:
      • feature ID: updated feature's ID
      • org ID: the org's ID
      • env: the env
  If should clear credit system customer cache and updated feature is set:
    Add task to queue:

    Give back whether left's credit amount is right's credit amount.

##### server/src/internal/features/featureActions/runClearCreditSystemCacheTask.ts
Type ClearCreditSystemCachePayload: org ID, env, and internal feature ID.

“Clears the cache for all customers who have an entitlement to a credit system feature. This is used when the credit schema is updated to ensure customers get the new deduction rates.”
To run clear credit system cache task — given payload (async):
  From payload, take org ID, env, and internal feature ID.
  “TEMP 2026-04-24: skip credit-system cache clears for 1h to let the poison-message loop (SQS msg 2e30616f-7622-454a-91a2-e67d1fd0698a, redelivering every ~34s and hammering Redis with ~40k UNLINKs/sec) drain. Remove this guard after 2026-04-24 15:50 UTC.”
  Let skip until ms be the result of UTC [Date]:
    • 2026
    • 3
    • 24
    • 15
    • 50
    • 0
  If the current time is before skip until ms:
    Warn "Skipping credit-system cache clear (org={org ID} feature={internal feature ID}) — temporary guard active until 2026-04-24 15:50 UTC".
    Stop here.
  Get with features [OrgService] (org ID and env), and call the result org with features.
  If org with features is missing:
    Log an error "Organization {org ID} not found while clearing customer cache".
    Stop here.
  Let features by org env be the features by org env of org with features' org (given env and features: org with features' features).
  Log "Clearing cache for customers with credit system feature: {internal feature ID}".
  “First get the total count to check if we should proceed”
  Let max customers be 300,000.
  Split look up fields from customer entitlements into count result:
    • picking an object with count: count
    • joined with customer products on customer entitlements' customer product ID is customer products' ID
    • joined with customers on customer products' internal customer ID is customers' internal ID
    • where all of these are true:
      • the SQL {…} COLLATE "C" = {…} is set
      • customer products' status is in relevant statuses
      • customers' org ID is org ID
      • customers' env is env
  Let total count be count result's count, or 0 if that's missing.
  Log "Total customers to clear cache for: {total count}".
  If total count is more than max customers:
    Log an error "Cannot clear cache for {total count} customers. Maximum allowed is {max customers}. Skipping cache clear.".
    Stop here.
  Let page size be 50,000.
  Let cursor start as nothing.
  Let page start as 0.
  Let all affected customers be an empty list.
  Keep repeating (until something stops it):
    Let batch be look up fields from customer entitlements:
      • picking an object with:
        • customer ID: customers' ID
        • internal customer ID: customers' internal ID
      • joined with customer products on customer entitlements' customer product ID is customer products' ID
      • joined with customers on customer products' internal customer ID is customers' internal ID
      • where all of these are true:
        • the SQL {…} COLLATE "C" = {…} is set
        • customer products' status is in relevant statuses
        • customers' org ID is org ID
        • customers' env is env
        • customers' internal ID is more than cursor if cursor is set (otherwise nothing) is set
      • sorted by the result of asc (customers' internal ID)
      • at most page size row(s)
    Let filtered batch be batch, keeping only those where c's customer ID is set.
    Add everything in filtered batch to all affected customers.
    Increase page by 1.
    Log "Fetched page {page}: {the number of batch} customers".
    Stop the loop if the number of batch is less than page size.
    Set cursor to batch's entry for the number of batch minus 1's internal customer ID.
  Log "Total affected customers: {the number of all affected customers}".
  “Process in batches of BATCH_SIZE”
  Let cache batch size be 1000.
  Let total deleted start as 0.
  Start with let i = 0, repeat while i is less than the number of all affected customers, then add cache batch size to i each time:
    Let batch be all affected customers from position i up to i plus cache batch size.
    Let customers to delete be batch, after these steps:
      1. Keep only those where c's customer ID is set
      2. Turn each c into an object with org ID, env, and customer ID: c's customer ID
    If customers to delete is not empty:
      Batch invalidate cached full subjects, and call the result deleted:
        • customers: customers to delete
        • features by org env
        • get Redis targets for customer: a function giving back get Redis targets for customer (org: org with features' org)
      Add deleted to total deleted.
  Log "Cleared {total deleted} cache entries for {the number of all affected customers} customers".

##### server/src/internal/features/creditDimensions/validateCreditDimensionRules.ts

##### server/src/internal/features/creditDimensions/validateCreditMultipliers.ts
To validate multiplier shape — given name, multiplier, and invalid credit system:
  Let has factor mean multiplier's factor is set.
  Let has add mean multiplier's add is set.
  If has no factor and has no add, Invalid credit system ("Multiplier "{name}" needs a factor or an add.").
  Let factor be multiplier's factor as a number.
  If all of these are true:
    • has factor
    • factor is not a real number or factor is zero or less
  then:
    Invalid credit system ("Multiplier "{name}" factor must be greater than zero.").
  Let add be multiplier's add as a number.
  If has add and add is not a real number, Invalid credit system ("Multiplier "{name}" add must be a number.").
  “Coerce in place: a string would concatenate rather than add downstream.”
  If has factor, set multiplier's factor to factor.
  If has add, set multiplier's add to add.

“A set of multipliers can apply together only if every pair can coexist, so the worst case is the deepest discount over any such set. Grown greedily from each multiplier: enough to catch a genuinely negative rate without enumerating the power set.”
Worst case rate — given multipliers and cheapest rate; gives back a Decimal:
  Give back multipliers combined into one value, starting from cheapest rate; for each seed (with the running total worst):
    Let stacked be an empty list.
    For each candidate in multipliers:
      Let discounts mean any of these is true:
        • candidate's factor is set and candidate's factor is less than 1
        • candidate's add is set and candidate's add is negative
      Let fits with all mean every chosen in stacked satisfies: chosen's match matches can coexist (given candidate's match).
      If all of these are true:
        • discounts is true or candidate is seed
        • seed's match matches can coexist (given candidate's match)
        • fits with all is true
      then:
        Add candidate to stacked.
    Let rate be stacked combined into one value, starting from cheapest rate; for each multiplier (with the running total amount):
      • the running total becomes add multiplier's add if multiplier's add is set and multiplier's add is negative, otherwise 0 to amount times depending on whether multiplier's factor is set and multiplier's factor is less than 1
    Give back the result of min [Decimal] (worst and rate).

To validate multipliers keep rates non negative — given schema item and invalid credit system:
  Let multipliers be the values in schema item's multipliers, or an empty object if that's missing.
  Let rates be a list of:
    • schema item
    • everything in the values in schema item's dimensions, or an empty object if that's missing
  Let cheapest rate be the smaller of all of rates, each passed through minimum credit rate amount.
  If a worst case rate (multipliers and cheapest rate) is less than 0:
    Invalid credit system:
      • "Multipliers on {schema item's metered feature ID} can take a rate below zero."

To validate credit multipliers — given schema item and invalid credit system:
  For each key name and value multiplier in schema item's multipliers, or an empty object if that's missing:
    Validate multiplier shape (name, multiplier, and invalid credit system).
  Validate multipliers keep rates non negative (schema item and invalid credit system).

##### server/src/internal/features/creditDimensions/validateDimensionsAreSeparable.ts
“Two dimensions that could match one event with nothing to break the tie are rejected at save.”
To validate dimensions are separable — given dimensions and invalid credit system:
  Split find ambiguous credit dimensions (dimensions) into ambiguous.
  If ambiguous is missing, stop here.
  Split ambiguous's names into left name and right name.
  Invalid credit system:
    • "Dimensions "{left name}" and "{right name}" can both match the same event ({format credit match (ambiguous's example)}). Give one more match keys or a priority."

##### server/src/internal/events/eventUtils.ts
“Epoch ms of a pipe's "%F %T" bucket start. Hour buckets are always UTC; day/week/month buckets are wall-clock times in `timezone`.”
Period → epoch — given period, timezone, and bin size; gives back a number:
  If timezone is missing, timezone is "UTC", or bin size is "hour", give back a new UTC date (period) as a timestamp.
  Split period split on " " into date part and time part (default "00:00:00").
  Split date part split on "-", each passed through number into year, month, and day.
  Split time part split on ":", each passed through number into hours, minutes, and seconds.
  Give back a new tz date as a timestamp.

“Convert event periods from pipe strings to epoch timestamps, in place.”
To convert periods to epoch — given events, timezone, and bin size:
  For each event in events:
    Set event's period to the epoch of event's period (given timezone and bin size).

“Normalize a group value to a string. For `plan_id`, an empty string is a meaningful bucket ("no plan") and is preserved; for other fields, empty is treated as missing.”
To normalize group value — given value and group by field; gives back text (or nothing):
  If value is missing, give back nothing.
  If value is "" and group by field is not "plan_id", give back nothing.
  Give back value as text.

“Collect grouping metadata from a list of rows.”
To collect grouping metadata — given rows and group by field; gives back an object with group values and feature names:
  Let group values be an empty set.
  Let feature names be an empty set.
  For each row in rows:
    From row, take group by field (as group value), period, and the rest as metrics.
    Normalize group value (group value and group by field), and call the result normalized.
    If normalized is set, add normalized to group values.
    For each feature name in the keys of metrics:
      Add feature name to feature names.

##### server/src/internal/entities/repos/planFilterScope.ts
“Resolving the plan filter as a correlated EXISTS re-probes customer_products for every entity in the org — 197M buffer reads / 176s to return 20 rows on mintlify, because the LIMIT can't push through the per-row subquery. Instead resolve which (customer, entity-scope) pairs match the plan ONCE, then drive the entity scan from that (much smaller) set. Scopes are built so each entity matches at most one row — a customer-level match covers all of that customer's entities, so its entity-level rows are redundant and are dropped. That keeps the join 1:1 and avoids a DISTINCT that would force materialising every match before ORDER BY / LIMIT.”
To build plan scope cte — given org ID, env, plans, and in statuses; gives back a SQL:
  Let plan conditions be plans, with each plan turned into depending on whether plan's versions is set and plan's versions is not empty:
    • if so: the SQL (p.id = {…} AND p.version IN ({…}))
    • if not: the SQL p.id = {…}
  Give back the SQL plan_matched_products AS ( SELECT cp.internal_customer_id….

“Drives the entity scan from plan_scopes rather than probing per entity.”
Let plan scope join SQL be the SQL JOIN plan_scopes ps ON ps.internal_customer_id = e.intern….

##### server/src/internal/entities/actions/createEntitiesV2/errors/handleCreateEntitiesErrors.ts
Refuse consumable features — given entities by feature:
  For each feature in entities by feature:
    Skip it if feature utils is not consumable (feature).
    Fail with an error: "Feature '{feature's ID}' is consumable (e.g. credits, API calls). Entities can only be created for non-consumable features (e.g. seats)." (status 400).

Refuse second idless entity — given existing entities and requested entities:
  Let existing idless be existing entities, keeping only those where entity's ID is missing.
  Let requested idless be requested entities, keeping only those where entity's ID is missing.
  If the number of existing idless plus the number of requested idless is at most 1, stop here.
  Fail with an error: "Each entity must have a unique id; only one entity per customer may omit an id." [error code's entity ID required] (status 400).

Refuse existing entity IDs — given existing entities:
  For each entity in existing entities:
    Skip it if entity's ID is missing.
    Fail with an entity already exists error.

Refuse entities for feature — given context, entities by feature, and params:
  From entities by feature, take feature and inserted.
  Let feature customer entitlements be context's customer entitlements, keeping only those where customer entitlement matches feature (given feature).
  For each customer entitlement in feature customer entitlements:
    Let has price mean there is a customer price of customer entitlement.
    If has price and params does not allow paid features:
      Fail with an error: "Failed to auto create entity for feature {feature's name} because it is a paid feature." [error code's invalid inputs] (status 400).
    Let usage limit be customer entitlement's entitlement's usage limit.
    “New seats reuse paid-for replaceables first; each gives its seat back.”
    Let reused seats be the number of the first the number of inserted of customer entitlement's replaceables.
    Let balance after be customer entitlement's balance, or 0 if that's missing minus the number of inserted plus reused seats.
    If usage limit is set and balance after is less than negative usage limit:
      Fail with an error: "Cannot create {the number of inserted} entities for feature {feature's name} as it would exceed the usage limit." [error code's feature limit reached] (status 400).

Refuse several invoiced features — given invoiced customer entitlements:
  If invoiced customer entitlements has at most 1 item, stop here.
  Fail with an error: "Entities for more than one paid feature must be created in separate requests." [error code's invalid inputs] (status 400).

To handle create entities errors — given context and params:
  Refuse consumable features (context).
  Refuse second idless entity (context).
  Refuse existing entity IDs (context).
  For each entities by feature in context's entities by feature:
    Refuse entities for feature (context, entities by feature, and params).
  Refuse several invoiced features (context).

##### server/src/internal/customers/repos/getFullSubject/getFullSubjectRowsQuery.ts
Let customer product limit be 200.
Let extra customer entitlement limit be 200.

“Every aggregate and `distinct_*` CTE below is declared `AS MATERIALIZED`. Postgres inlines a CTE referenced once, which is normally the better plan. But the row estimate for the subject set collapses to 1 — the planner multiplies org_id/internal_customer_id/env as independent conditions and clamps — while a multi-subject page (entities.list) really returns up to 1,000. So each `LEFT JOIN xxx_agg ON subject_key` was planned as a nested loop and the inlined aggregate re-ran once per output row, re-sorting its whole input each time to keep one group. Measured on mintlify's 12,212-entity customer: 28,450ms, of which cus_products_agg alone was 18,025ms across 1,001 loops. MATERIALIZED forces one evaluation into a tuplestore, so the estimate stops mattering. Same customer: 839ms. There is nothing to push down into these (they are already scoped by subject_records), so the usual cost of blocking predicate pushdown does not apply, and the single-subject getFullSubject path measured neutral — 585ms vs 570ms, byte-identical output. Per-subject aggregate CTE → key in the subject object. Each exposes (subject_key, items).”
Let subject aggregates be a list of:
  • an object with cte: "cus_products_agg" and column: "customer_products"
  • an object with cte: "cus_entitlements_agg" and column: "customer_entitlements"
  • an object with cte: "cus_prices_agg" and column: "customer_prices"
  • an object with cte: "customer_licenses_agg" and column: "customer_licenses"
  • an object with:
    • cte: "extra_cus_entitlements_agg"
    • column: "extra_customer_entitlements"
  • an object with cte: "replaceables_agg" and column: "replaceables"
  • an object with cte: "rollovers_agg" and column: "rollovers"
  • an object with cte: "usage_windows_agg" and column: "usage_windows"
  • an object with cte: "subscriptions_agg" and column: "subscriptions"

“Org catalog. Identical for every subject, so these are built once per page and returned once alongside the subject array, never per subject.”

##### server/src/internal/customers/handlers/handleRefundInvoice/invoiceRefundUtils.ts
“Resolve the Stripe charge from an invoice's payments list”
To resolve charge from invoice — given Stripe client and Stripe invoice; gives back a Stripe.Charge (or nothing) (async):
  Let payments be Stripe invoice's payments' data.
  Let paid payments be payments, keeping only those where p's status is "paid".
  If paid payments is empty, give back nothing.
  If paid payments has more than 1 item:
    Fail with an error: "This invoice has multiple payments and cannot be refunded via Autumn, please visit the Stripe dashboard to perform this action." [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
  From the first of paid payments, take payment.
  If payment's type is "charge" and payment's charge is set:
    If payment's charge is text, Retrieve Stripe client's charges (payment's charge), and give back the result.
    Give back payment's charge.
  If payment's type is "payment_intent" and payment's payment intent is set:
    Let payment intent ID be depending on whether payment's payment intent is text:
      • if so: payment's payment intent
      • if not: payment's payment intent's ID
    Retrieve Stripe client's payment intents (payment intent ID and expand: a list of "latest_charge"), and call the result payment intent.
    Let latest charge be payment intent's latest charge.
    If latest charge is missing or latest charge is text, give back nothing.
    Give back latest charge.
  Give back nothing.

“Validate that the charge is refundable and return the refundable amount in cents”
To validate charge refundable — given charge; gives back a number:
  If charge's paid is missing or charge's status is not "succeeded":
    Fail with an error: "This charge is not eligible for a refund" [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
  Let refundable amount in cents be charge's amount minus charge's amount refunded.
  If refundable amount in cents is zero or less:
    Fail with an error: "This charge has already been fully refunded" [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
  Give back refundable amount in cents.

“Calculate the refund amount in cents based on mode and optional user-provided amount”
To calculate refund amount in cents — given mode, amount, refundable amount in cents, and currency; gives back a number:
  If mode is "full", give back refundable amount in cents.
  If amount is missing:
    Fail with an error: "Amount is required for partial refunds" [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
  Let refund amount in cents be the Stripe amount of Autumn (amount and currency).
  If refund amount in cents is zero or less:
    Fail with an error: "Refund amount is too small" [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
  If refund amount in cents is more than refundable amount in cents:
    Let refundable display be the Autumn amount of Stripe (amount: refundable amount in cents and currency).
    Fail with an error: "Refund amount exceeds the refundable balance of {refundable display} {currency in uppercase}" [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
  Give back refund amount in cents.

“Issue a Stripe refund and atomically increment refunded_amount on the Autumn invoice”
To create refund and update invoice — given Stripe client, charge ID, Stripe invoice ID, and amount in cents; gives back a Stripe.Refund (async):
  Create Stripe client's refunds, and call the result Stripe refund:
    • charge: charge ID
    • amount: amount in cents
    • Autumn Stripe request options (source: "refund")
  Let refunded amount be the Autumn amount of Stripe (amount: Stripe refund's amount and currency: Stripe refund's currency).
  Add refunded amount [InvoiceService] (Stripe ID: Stripe invoice ID and amount: refunded amount), and call the result updated.
  If updated is missing:
    Warn "[createRefundAndUpdateInvoice] No Autumn invoice found for stripe_id {Stripe invoice ID} — refunded_amount not tracked".
  Give back Stripe refund.

##### server/src/internal/customers/handlers/handleRefundInvoice/refundVercelInvoice.ts
Let default vercel refund reason be "Refund issued from Autumn".

  Give back amount rounded to 2 decimal places.

  Give back cent amount.

“Requests a refund through Vercel's Invoice Actions API (`POST /v1/installations/{id}/billing/invoices/{invoiceId}/actions`). Vercel returns 204 and settles asynchronously; `refunded_amount` is only written when the `marketplace.invoice.refunded` webhook confirms it. Vercel itself rejects a second request while one is `refund_requested`.”

    • bearer token: access token
    • server URL: get vercel SDK server URL (test options)
  Update marketplace invoice:
    • integration configuration ID: installation ID
    • invoice ID: vercel invoice ID
    • request body: an object with:
      • action: "refund"
      • reason
      • total: a to vercel amount string (amount)
  Give back an object with vercel invoice ID and installation ID.

##### server/src/internal/customers/exports/workflows/upload/mapStreamWithConcurrency.ts
Type BatchSettled: a function.
Type PendingBatch: an object.
Let default max pending batches be 8.

“One pool spanning every batch: a slow item holds a single slot rather than stalling its whole batch, and slots stay full while batches are sparse.”
To map stream with concurrency — given batches, concurrency, max pending batches (default default max pending batches), run, and on batch settled; gives back an AsyncGenerator (async):
  Let slots be the larger of 1 and concurrency.
  Let in flight be an empty lookup table.
  Let pending be an empty list.
  Let order be an empty list.
  Let next token start as 0.
  Start with no failure yet.
  To start — given item and owner:
    Let token be increase next token by 1.
    Record run (item)'s then, and if that fails' finally under token in in flight:
      • a function of result that:
        Add an object with token and result to pending.
        Add result to owner's settled.
        Give back token.
      If failure is missing, set it to error.
      Give back token.
      • a function that:
        Decrease owner's remaining by 1.
  To settle reportable batches (async):
    Keep repeating while order is not empty:
      Let head be the first of order.
      Stop the loop if head's remaining is positive or head's reported is true.
      Set head's reported to true.
      Take the first item off order.
      Trigger on batch settled (batch: head's batch and results: head's settled).
  To drain one (async):
    Let token be a race [Promise] (in flight's values).
    Remove token from in flight.
  For each batch in batches (as they arrive):
    Stop the loop if failure is set.
    Keep repeating while the number of order is at least the larger of 1 and max pending batches and failure is missing:
      Stop the loop if in flight's size is 0.
      Drain one.
      Everything yielded by the results of pending's splice (0).
      Settle reportable batches.
    Stop the loop if failure is set.
    Let owner be an object with:
      • batch
      • settled: an empty list
      • remaining: the number of batch
      • reported: false
    Add owner to order.
    If batch is empty:
      Settle reportable batches.
      Move on to the next one.
    For each item in batch:
      Stop the loop if failure is set.
      Start (item and owner).
      Keep repeating while in flight's size is at least slots and failure is missing:
        Drain one.
        Everything yielded by the results of pending's splice (0).
        Settle reportable batches.
  Keep repeating while in flight's size is positive:
    Drain one.
    Everything yielded by the results of pending's splice (0).
    Settle reportable batches.
  Everything yielded by the results of pending's splice (0).
  Settle reportable batches.
  If failure is set, fail with failure.

##### server/src/internal/customers/customerLsns/isCustomerRecentlyUpdated.ts
“Derived from REPLICA_LAG_MAX_MS so the ledger window and the replica lag bound cannot drift apart — the ledger only covers lag inside this window.”
Let customer freshness window s be replica lag max ms divided by 1000.

Let negative TTL ms be 2000.
Let negative cache max entries be 5000.

“Negatives only: worst case a write lands mid-window and one read goes replica — stale by ≤ NEGATIVE_TTL_MS + replica lag, well inside the 60s ledger window.”
Let negative cache be a new lru cache (max: negative cache max entries and TTL: negative TTL ms).

To reset recently updated negative cache for testing:
  Empty out negative cache.

  Give back "{org ID}:{env}:{customer ID}".

“Read-your-writes in-process: marks drop their cached negative so the next check queries; other processes stay stale for at most NEGATIVE_TTL_MS.”
To invalidate recently updated negative cache — given org ID, env, and customer ID:
  Remove build negative cache key (org ID, env, and customer ID) from negative cache.

Recently updated negative cache size for testing — gives back a number:
  Give back negative cache's size.

“True when the customer had a structural write inside the freshness window (DB clock only) — such reads must be routed to the primary.”
Is customer recently updated? — given org ID, env, and customer ID; gives back true/false (async):
  Build negative cache key (org ID, env, and customer ID) → cache key.
  If negative cache's entry for cache key gives back something, give back whether false.

  If rows is not empty, give back whether true.
  Record true under cache key in negative cache.
  Give back whether false.

##### server/src/internal/customers/cusUtils/cusResponseUtils/getCusAutoTopupPurchaseLimits.ts
“When `expand=billing_controls.auto_topups.purchase_limit` is requested, return a replacement `auto_topups` array where each entry's `purchase_limit` is augmented with runtime tracking (`count`, `next_reset_at`) from the `auto_topup_limit_states` table. Behavior: - Returns `undefined` when the expand path is not requested. - Returns `undefined` when there are no configured auto_topups. - For each configured auto_topup with a matching DB row, the `purchase_limit` object is rebuilt with `count` + `next_reset_at` from the row. If the stored window has elapsed, `count` is projected to 0 and `next_reset_at` is advanced from the stored boundary by the configured interval. If the config had no `purchase_limit`, `interval` / `interval_count` / `limit` are returned as `null`. - For configured auto_topups WITHOUT a matching DB row (no top-up has ever fired), the entry is passed through unchanged from config.”
To get customer auto topup purchase limits — given internal customer ID, auto topups config, and expand; gives back a list of AutoTopupResponse (or nothing) (async):
  If customer expand's auto topups purchase limit is not in expand, give back nothing.
  If auto topups config is missing or auto topups config is empty, give back nothing.
  Find auto topup limit repo all by customer (internal customer ID), and call the result rows.
  Let rows by feature ID be a lookup table built from rows, each turned into a list of row's feature ID and row.
  Give back auto topups config, with each config turned into the result of:
    Let row be rows by feature ID's entry for config's feature ID.
    If row is missing, give back config.
    Let configured limit be config's purchase limit if config's purchase limit is set and config's purchase limit has no "count" key (otherwise nothing).
    Normalize window counter, and call the result normalized:
      • now: the current time
      • window ends at: row's purchase window ends at
      • count: row's purchase count
      • window config: configured limit
      • from: row's purchase window ends at
    Give back config, but with:
      • purchase limit set to an object with:
        • interval: configured limit's interval, or nothing if that's missing
        • interval count: configured limit's interval count, or nothing if that's missing
        • limit: configured limit's limit, or nothing if that's missing
        • count: normalized's count, or row's purchase count if that's missing
        • next reset at: normalized's window ends at, or row's purchase window ends at if that's missing

##### server/src/internal/customers/cusProducts/cusProductUtils/getUpcomingSchedules.ts
“Return unique transition points for customer products: 1. Scheduled products (will start in the future) 2. Active products scheduled for cancellation (will end at ended_at) Results are sorted ascending, truncated to second precision.”
To get unique upcoming schedule pairs — given customer products, now, and include past (default false); gives back a list of number:
  Let current time be now, or the current time if that's missing.
  “Deduplicate by timestamp only (not timestamp+status) A scheduled product starting at T and a canceled product ending at T represent the same transition point”
  Let unique timestamps be an empty set.
  For each customer product in customer products:
    Let prices be the prices of customer product.
    Let free mean prices is free product.
    Let one off mean prices is one off.
    “Case 1: Scheduled products (will start)”
    If customer product's status is customer product status's scheduled:
      Skip it if customer product's starts at is not a number.
      Skip it if include past is false and customer product's starts at is at or before current time.
      Add truncate ms to second precision (customer product's starts at) to unique timestamps.
    “Case 2: Active products scheduled for cancellation (will end)”
    If all of these are true:
      • customer product's status is customer product status's active

To get feature balance — given customer entitlements, internal feature ID, and entity ID:
  Let balance start as 0.
  Get unlimited and usage allowed (customer entitlements and internal feature ID), and take its unlimited.
  If unlimited is true, give back nothing.

  Give back paid allowance.

  Give back whether customer entitlements has a customer entitlement where customer entitlement's internal feature ID is feature's internal ID.

To get total negative balance — given customer entitlement, balance, entities, and billing units:
  Let entity feature ID be customer entitlement's entitlement's entity feature ID.
  If entity feature ID is missing, give back balance.
  Let total negative start as 0.
  For each key group in entities:
    If entities' entry for group's balance is negative:
      Let balance start as entities' entry for group's balance.
      If billing units is set, set balance to round balance divided by billing units times billing units.
      Add balance to total negative.
  If total negative is 0:
    If the values in entities is not empty:
      Let entity balances be each e's balance, or 0 if that's empty, for each e in the values in entities.
      Give back the smaller of all of entity balances.
    Otherwise:
      Give back customer entitlement's entitlement's allowance, or 0 if that's empty.
  Give back total negative.

##### server/src/internal/customers/cusProducts/actions/cleanupOneOff/getOneOffToCleanup.ts
“Fetches one-off customer products eligible for cleanup. A customer product is eligible when: 1. Status is Active or PastDue 2. All its prices are one_off interval 3. All its entitlements are either: - Boolean features, OR - Single-use consumables with balance=0 and usage_allowed=false 4. A newer active customer product exists for the same product”
To get one off customer products to cleanup — gives back a list of OneOffCustomerProductResult (async):
  Execute, and call the result result:
    • "
		WITH 
		-- CTE 1: Active customer products (with at least one price) on products that
		-- have a one_off price. Driving from the catalog side keeps this off the
		-- full customer_products table.
		active_cus_products_with_prices AS (
			SELECT DISTINCT cp.id
			FROM customer_products cp
			WHERE cp.status IN ('{customer product status's active}', '{customer product status's past due}')
			  AND cp.internal_product_id IN (
				SELECT DISTINCT p.internal_product_id
				FROM prices p
				WHERE COALESCE(p.config->>'interval', '') = '{billing interval's one off}'
			)
			  AND EXISTS (
				SELECT 1 FROM customer_prices cpr WHERE cpr.customer_product_id = cp.id
			)
		),
		
		-- CTE 2: Exclude customer products that have ANY price that is NOT one_off
		cus_products_with_non_one_off_prices AS (
			SELECT DISTINCT cpr.customer_product_id
			FROM customer_prices cpr
			INNER JOIN prices p ON p.id = cpr.price_id
			WHERE cpr.customer_product_id IN (SELECT id FROM active_cus_products_with_prices)
			  AND COALESCE(p.config->>'interval', '') != '{billing interval's one off}'
		),
		
		-- CTE 3: One-off customer products (has prices AND all prices are one_off)
		one_off_cus_products AS (
			SELECT id FROM active_cus_products_with_prices
			WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT customer_product_id FROM cus_products_with_non_one_off_prices)
		),
		
		-- CTE 4: From one-off products, filter to those with at least one entitlement
		cus_products_with_entitlements AS (
			SELECT DISTINCT cp.id
			FROM customer_products cp
			WHERE cp.id IN (SELECT id FROM one_off_cus_products)
			  AND EXISTS (
				SELECT 1 FROM customer_entitlements ce WHERE ce.customer_product_id = cp.id
			)
		),
		
		-- CTE 5: Valid one-off customer products where ALL entitlements meet criteria
		-- Every entitlement must be either:
		--   A. Boolean feature, OR
		--   B. Single-use consumable (usage_type = single_use AND allowance_type = fixed AND balance = 0 AND usage_allowed = false)
		valid_one_off_cus_products AS (
			SELECT cp.id, cp.internal_customer_id, cp.internal_entity_id, cp.created_at, cp.internal_product_id
			FROM customer_products cp
			WHERE cp.id IN (SELECT id FROM cus_products_with_entitlements)
			  -- Exclude if ANY entitlement does NOT match criteria A or B
			  AND NOT EXISTS (
			  	SELECT 1
			  	FROM customer_entitlements ce
			  	INNER JOIN entitlements e ON e.id = ce.entitlement_id
			  	INNER JOIN features f ON f.internal_id = e.internal_feature_id
			  	WHERE ce.customer_product_id = cp.id
			  	  -- Entitlement does NOT satisfy A (boolean) AND does NOT satisfy B (single_use consumable)
			  	  AND f.type != '{feature type's boolean}'
			  	  AND NOT (
			  	  	-- B: Single-use consumable with all conditions met
			  	  	COALESCE(f.config->>'usage_type', '') = '{feature usage type's single}'
			  	  	AND COALESCE(e.allowance_type, '') = '{allowance type's fixed}'
			  	  	AND COALESCE(ce.balance, 0) = 0
			  	  	AND ce.usage_allowed = false
			  	  )
			  )
		),
		
		-- CTE 6: Customer products that have a valid corresponding newer active product
		cus_products_with_newer_active_product AS (
			SELECT DISTINCT oo.id
			FROM valid_one_off_cus_products oo
			INNER JOIN products prod1 ON prod1.internal_id = oo.internal_product_id
			WHERE EXISTS (
				SELECT 1 
				FROM customer_products cp2
				INNER JOIN products prod2 ON prod2.internal_id = cp2.internal_product_id
				WHERE cp2.internal_customer_id = oo.internal_customer_id
				  AND (
				  	(cp2.internal_entity_id IS NULL AND oo.internal_entity_id IS NULL)
				  	OR cp2.internal_entity_id = oo.internal_entity_id
				  )
				  AND prod2.id = prod1.id
				  AND cp2.created_at > oo.created_at
				  AND cp2.status IN ('{customer product status's active}', '{customer product status's past due}')
				  AND cp2.id != oo.id
				  -- Ensure all boolean features from original exist in newer product
				  AND NOT EXISTS (
				  	-- Find boolean features in original that don't exist in newer
				  	SELECT 1
				  	FROM customer_entitlements ce1
				  	INNER JOIN entitlements e1 ON e1.id = ce1.entitlement_id
				  	INNER JOIN features f1 ON f1.internal_id = e1.internal_feature_id
				  	WHERE ce1.customer_product_id = oo.id
				  	  AND f1.type = '{feature type's boolean}'
				  	  AND NOT EXISTS (
				  	  	-- Check if newer product has this boolean feature
				  	  	SELECT 1
				  	  	FROM customer_entitlements ce2
				  	  	INNER JOIN entitlements e2 ON e2.id = ce2.entitlement_id
				  	  	INNER JOIN features f2 ON f2.internal_id = e2.internal_feature_id
				  	  	WHERE ce2.customer_product_id = cp2.id
				  	  	  AND f2.id = f1.id
				  	  	  AND f2.type = '{feature type's boolean}'
				  	  )
				  )
			)
		)
		
		-- Final query: Get full data for customer products meeting all criteria
		SELECT 
			row_to_json(cp.*) as customer_product,
			row_to_json(cpr.*) as customer_price,
			row_to_json(p.*) as price,
			row_to_json(c.*) as customer,
			row_to_json(prod.*) as product,
			row_to_json(o.*) as org
		FROM customer_products cp
		INNER JOIN customer_prices cpr ON cpr.customer_product_id = cp.id
		INNER JOIN prices p ON p.id = cpr.price_id
		INNER JOIN customers c ON c.internal_id = cp.internal_customer_id
		INNER JOIN products prod ON prod.internal_id = cp.internal_product_id
		INNER JOIN organizations o ON o.id = c.org_id
		WHERE cp.id IN (
			SELECT id FROM cus_products_with_newer_active_product
		)
	"
  Give back result.

##### server/src/internal/customers/cache/fullSubject/sanitize/normalizeFromSchema.ts
“Normalize cached JSON against a Zod schema to repair Upstash cjson quirks. Upstash's Lua cjson (Go-backed) differs from standard Redis Lua: - JSON `null` decodes to Lua `nil` (dropped on re-encode). - Empty JS objects/arrays both become `{}` after a Lua round-trip. Walks the schema and fills holes at nullable positions, and swaps empty-object/empty-array when the schema says otherwise. Never throws, never re-validates — this is a cleanup pass, not a `.parse()`.”
Type ZodSchema: a z.core.$ZodType.

Is plain object? — given value; gives back value is Record<string, unknown>:
  Give back whether value is set, value is an object, and value is not a list.

Is empty object? — given value; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether value is plain object and the keys of value is empty.

Is empty array? — given value; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether value is a list and value is empty.

“True if the schema's wrapper chain contains `ZodNullable`. Walks through `ZodOptional` / `ZodDefault` / `ZodPipe` so `.nullish()` (optional→nullable) and `.nullable().default(x)` both report as nullable.”
Is nullable? — given schema; gives back true/false:
  If schema is a z.zod nullable, give back whether true.
  If schema is a z.zod optional, give back whether schema's def's inner type is nullable.
  If schema is a z.zod default, give back whether schema's def's inner type is nullable.
  If schema is a z.zod pipe, give back whether schema's def's in is nullable or schema's def's out is nullable.
  Give back whether false.

“Strip wrapper layers to reveal the payload-shaping schema (`ZodObject` / `ZodArray` / `ZodRecord` / leaf).”
To unwrap schema — given schema; gives back a ZodSchema:
  If schema is a z.zod nullable, Unwrap schema (schema's def's inner type), and give back the result.
  If schema is a z.zod optional, Unwrap schema (schema's def's inner type), and give back the result.
  If schema is a z.zod default, Unwrap schema (schema's def's inner type), and give back the result.
  If schema is a z.zod pipe, Unwrap schema (schema's def's in), and give back the result.
  Give back schema.

“If `undefined` hits a `ZodDefault` anywhere in the wrapper chain, return its default value. v4 exposes `defaultValue` as a direct value, not a thunk.”
To apply default if undefined — given schema and value; gives back an object or an object:
  If value is set, give back an object with applied: false.
  If schema is a z.zod default, give back an object with applied: true and value: schema's def's default value.
  If schema is a z.zod optional, Apply default if undefined (schema's def's inner type and value), and give back the result.
  If schema is a z.zod nullable, Apply default if undefined (schema's def's inner type and value), and give back the result.
  If schema is a z.zod pipe, Apply default if undefined (schema's def's in and value), and give back the result.
  Give back an object with applied: false.

To normalize — given schema and data; gives back anything:
  If data is missing:
    Apply default if undefined (schema and data), and call the result default result.
    If default result's applied is set, Normalize (unwrap schema (schema) and default result's value), and give back the result.
    If schema is nullable, give back nothing.
    Give back data.
  Unwrap schema (schema), and call the result unwrapped.
  If unwrapped is a z.zod object:
    “Upstash Lua cjson collapses empty `{}` to `[]`; treat as empty object so nested defaults (e.g. ProductConfigSchema) still get applied.”
    Let object data be an empty object if data is empty array, otherwise data.
    If object data is not plain object, give back data.
    Let shape be unwrapped's def's shape.
    Let normalized be an object with everything in object data.
    For each key in the keys of shape:
      Normalize (shape's entry for key and normalized's entry for key), and put the result in normalized's entry for key.
    Give back normalized.
  If unwrapped is a z.zod array:
    If data is empty object, give back an empty list.
    If data is not a list, give back data.
    Let element be unwrapped's def's element.
    Give back normalize (element and each item), for each item in data.
  If unwrapped is a z.zod record:
    If data is empty array, give back an empty object.
    If data is not plain object, give back data.
    Let value type be unwrapped's def's value type.
    Let normalized be an empty object.
    For each key in the keys of data:
      Normalize (value type and data's entry for key), and put the result in normalized's entry for key.
    Give back normalized.
  Give back data.

To normalize from schema — given schema and data; gives back a T:
  Normalize (schema and data), and give back the result.

##### server/src/internal/customers/cache/fullSubject/actions/rehydrateWithLiveBalances.ts
“After we write a subject via `setCachedFullSubject`, the balance hashes are written with HSETNX — so any concurrent Lua deduction that landed between our Lua script starting and finishing will have left its patched balance in place. To reflect those patches we need to re-read the balance hashes. We don't need to re-read the subject blob itself because we just wrote it ourselves. This helper does a single balance hmget batch (one RTT) and merges the live values into the already-known normalized subject. Returns undefined if the balance batch is incomplete — callers should fall back to the DB-derived fullSubject in that case.”
Rehydrate with live balances — given normalized; gives back a FullSubject (or nothing) (async):
  From normalized, take customer ID and entity ID.
  Let customer entitlement IDs by feature ID be an empty object.
  For each ce in normalized's customer entitlements:
    Let list be customer entitlement IDs by feature ID's entry for ce's feature ID.
    Add ce's ID to list.
    Set customer entitlement IDs by feature ID's entry for ce's feature ID to list.
  Let usage window feature IDs be the unique values of the usage window feature IDs of normalized.
  Let feature IDs be one list combining without duplicates:
    • the keys of customer entitlement IDs by feature ID
    • usage window feature IDs
  Let is customer subject mean entity ID is missing.
  Get cached feature balances batch, and call the result outcome:
    • customer ID
    • feature IDs
    • customer entitlement IDs by feature ID
    • include aggregated: is customer subject
    • usage window feature IDs
  If outcome's kind is not "ok", give back nothing.
  Set normalized's customer entitlements to all the balances across outcome's value.
  If is customer subject, Apply live aggregated balances (normalized and feature balances: outcome's value).
  Apply live usage windows (normalized and feature balances: outcome's value).
  Give back the full subject of normalized.

##### server/src/internal/customers/attach/mergeUtils/phaseUtils/mergeSimilarPhases.ts
“Normalize items for comparison (order-agnostic, price id as string)”
To normalize phase items — given items:
  Give back items, after these steps:
    1. Turn each item into an object with:
      • price: item's price
      • quantity: item's quantity, or 0 if that's empty
    2. ␀them, sorted by this rule:
      If a's price is b's price, give back a's quantity, or 0 if that's empty minus b's quantity, or 0 if that's empty.
      Give back how a's price compares alphabetically to b's price.

“Compare two item lists for equality (same length, same price+quantity pairs)”
Have same items? — given a and b:
  If the number of a is not the number of b, give back whether false.
  Normalize phase items (a), and call the result na.
  Normalize phase items (b), and call the result nb.
  For each position i in na:
    If na's entry for i's price is not nb's entry for i's price, give back whether false.
    If na's entry for i's quantity, or 0 if that's empty is not nb's entry for i's quantity, or 0 if that's empty:
      Give back whether false.
  Give back whether true.

“Check if a phase has no items”
Has no items? — given phase:
  Let items be phase's items, or an empty list if that's empty.
  Give back whether items is empty.

“Remove empty phases and adjust dates to maintain timeline continuity”
To remove empty phases and adjust dates — given phases; gives back a list of Stripe.SubscriptionScheduleUpdateParams.Phase:
  If phases is missing or phases has at most 1 item, give back phases.
  Let result be an empty list.
  For each position i in phases:
    Let phase be phases' entry for i.
    If phase has no no items:
      Let cloned phase be a deep copy of phase.
      “If this is not the first non-empty phase, we need to check if there were empty phases before it and extend the previous non-empty phase to cover the gap”
      If result is not empty:
        Let previous phase be the last of result.
        “Find if there are empty phases between the previous non-empty phase and current”
        Let has empty phases between mean false.
        Start with let j = i - 1, repeat while j is zero or more, then decrease j by 1 each time:
          Let check phase be phases' entry for j.
          Stop the loop if check phase has no no items.
          Set has empty phases between to true.
        “If there were empty phases, extend the previous phase's end_date to current phase's start_date”
        If has empty phases between and cloned phase's start date is set:
          Set previous phase's end date to cloned phase's start date.
      Add cloned phase to result.
  Give back result.

“Merge adjacent phases that have identical items”
To merge adjacent phases with same items — given phases; gives back a list of Stripe.SubscriptionScheduleUpdateParams.Phase:
  If phases is missing or phases has at most 1 item, give back phases.
  “First, remove empty phases and adjust dates to maintain continuity”
  Remove empty phases and adjust dates (phases), and call the result non empty phases.
  If non empty phases has at most 1 item, give back non empty phases.
  “Then, merge adjacent phases with same items”
  Let merged be an empty list.
  Let current start as a deep copy of the first of non empty phases.
  Count i from 1 while i is less than the number of non empty phases:
    Let next be non empty phases' entry for i.
    Let same mean current's items, or an empty list if that's empty have same items (given next's items, or an empty list if that's empty).
    If same is true:
      “Keep earliest start_date”
      Let current start be current's start date.
      Let next start be next's start date.
      If current start is a number, next start is a number, and next start is less than current start:
        Set current's start date to next start.
      “Extend end_date to the later one”
      Let current end be current's end date.
      Let next end be next's end date.
      If current end is a number, next end is a number, and next end is more than current end:
        Set current's end date to next end.
      Otherwise, if current end is not a number:
        “If current has no end_date but next does, adopt it”
        Set current's end date to next's end date.
    Otherwise:
      Add current to merged.
      Set current to a deep copy of next.
  Add current to merged.
  Give back merged.

##### server/src/internal/customers/attach/attachUtils/handleAttachErrors.ts

##### server/src/internal/customers/actions/resetUsageWindows/lazyResetSubjectUsageWindows.ts
“Lazily ROLLS the subject's usage-window counters on every subject read: zero counts whose stored window closed, and re-align bounds/anchor to the current derivation (this is where a plan change lands in the DB). The decision table lives in usageWindowsToRolls. Best-effort, like lazyResetSubjectEntitlements: reads and the deduction script both derive a closed count as 0 and stamp fresh bounds on write, so a failed roll only delays persistence. Rolls are idempotent (same target state), so concurrent reads converge. Returns true if any rows rolled.”

      • feature IDs: the feature IDs of usage windows without duplicates
      • features: the features
      • now
      • in statuses: the in statuses of the org
    Let rolls be the rolls of usage windows (given limits and now).
    If rolls is empty, give back whether false.
    Roll usage window repo windows, and call the result did roll:
      • rolls
      • now
      • org ID: the org's ID
      • env: the env
      • customer ID: full subject's customer ID
    If did not roll, give back whether false.
    Log "[lazyResetSubjectUsageWindows] customer: {full subject's customer ID}, rolling: {the number of rolls}".
    Roll usage windows cache (customer ID: full subject's customer ID, rolls, and now).
    Apply usage window rolls to subject:
      • full subject
      • normalized
      • rolls
      • now
    Give back whether true.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Log an error "[lazyResetSubjectUsageWindows] customer: {full subject's customer ID}, failed: {error}" (with error).
    Give back whether false.

“Two orderings pull against each other. A promo code is owned by exactly one reward, so replacing a reward while keeping its code needs the old row gone BEFORE the new one is written. A referral program cannot point at a reward that does not exist, so a repoint needs the new row written BEFORE the old one goes. Splitting the deletes satisfies both: everything unlinked leaves first and frees its codes, and only the rows a surviving program still holds wait until after the repoint.”

“Every check that can still reject the request, run before the first write. The phase below is a straight sequence of independent, non-transactional writes, and it cannot be wrapped in a transaction because it calls Stripe. So a 400 thrown mid-sequence leaves whatever already committed — a rename that survives a rejected RevenueCat collision, say. Worse for adopted prices: `newlyAdoptedPrices` diffs against the CURRENT row, so once a failed attempt has persisted a bad Stripe price id, the retry reads it as already-known, skips the lookup and succeeds on an id that does not exist. Validating first closes both.”
To validate catalog before writes — given update catalog plan (async):
  Assert revenue cat IDs unclaimed (update catalog plan).
  “The same set Stripe init walks, so a stated id is checked against exactly the rows that would have consumed it.”
  Validate adopted Stripe prices (upsert products: Stripe init targets (update catalog plan)).

##### server/src/internal/catalogV2/actions/updateCatalog/utils/productStateUtils/projectProductStatesContext.ts
“Pure projection: product state after `upsertProducts` apply (projectCatalog analogue). Rows group by their PROJECTED id, so an id patch re-keys the plan and subsequent intents/derives see the rename.”
To project product states context — given original and upsert products; gives back a ProductStatesContext:
  Let next row by internal ID be a lookup table built from all results, combined, of turning each upsert in upsert products into.
  Let created rows be upsert products, after these steps:
    1. Keep only those where upsert's row's op is "create"
    2. Turn each upsert into upsert's row's next full product
  Let versions by plan ID be an empty lookup table.
  To push row — given row:
    Let rows be versions by plan ID's entry for row's ID.
    Add row to rows.
    Record rows under row's ID in versions by plan ID.
  For each rows in the values in original's versions by plan ID:
    For each row in rows:
      Push row:
        • next row by internal ID's entry for row's internal ID, or row if that's missing
  For each row in created rows:
    Push row (row).
  For each rows in versions by plan ID's values:
    Rows, sorted by version (largest first).
  “Keep original keys alive even when renamed/absent — lookups expect them.”
  For each plan ID in the keys of original's versions by plan ID:
    If plan ID is not in versions by plan ID, record an empty list under plan ID in versions by plan ID.
  Let usage by internal ID be a lookup table built from the values in original's states by plan version, each turned into a list of state's current full product's internal ID and state's customer usage.
  “Reward programs follow the plan's projected id.”
  Let reward programs by plan ID be an empty lookup table.
  For each key plan ID and value programs in original's reward programs by plan ID:
    Let latest be an active full product for plan (plan ID and product states context: original).
    Let projected ID be depending on whether latest is set:
      • if so: next row by internal ID's entry for latest's internal ID's ID, or latest's ID if that's missing
      • if not: plan ID
    Record reward programs by plan ID's entry for projected ID, plus programs under projected ID in reward programs by plan ID.
  Build product states context, and give back the result:
    • plan IDs: a copy of versions by plan ID's keys
    • versions by plan ID
    • usage by internal ID
    • reward programs by plan ID
    • max version by plan ID: original's max version by plan ID
