##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/utils/handleOneOffPrepaidCarryOvers/applyOneOffPrepaidCarryOvers.ts
“billing.update variant: merges preserved balance into the new cusProduct's matching one-off slot when one exists; lifetime fallback otherwise. MUTATES `newCustomerProduct.customer_entitlements` in place.”
To apply one off prepaid carry overs — given old customer product, new customer product, and full customer; gives back an object with entitlements and customer entitlements:
  Let lifetime carry overs be the one off prepaid carry overs of customer products:
    • current customer products: a list of old customer product
    • full customer
  Let new slot by feature ID be a one off prepaid customer entitlements by feature ID (new customer product).
  Let merged entitlement IDs be an empty set.
  Let remaining customer entitlements be an empty list.
  For each carry over row in lifetime carry overs' customer entitlements:
    Let feature ID be carry over row's feature ID.
    Let new slot be new slot by feature ID's entry for feature ID if feature ID is set (otherwise nothing).
    If new slot is missing:
      Add carry over row to remaining customer entitlements.
      Move on to the next one.
    Let added balance be carry over row's balance, or 0 if that's missing.
    “Bump `adjustment` in lockstep with `balance` — grantedBalance picks up the preserved amount so usage stays at 0 instead of going negative.”
    Set new slot's balance to new slot's balance, or 0 if that's missing plus added balance.
    Set new slot's adjustment to new slot's adjustment, or 0 if that's missing plus added balance.
    If new slot's external ID is missing, set it to carry over row's external ID, or nothing if that's missing.
    Add carry over row's entitlement ID to merged entitlement IDs.
  Let remaining entitlements be lifetime carry overs' entitlements, keeping only those where entitlement's ID is not in merged entitlement IDs.
  Give back an object with:
    • entitlements: remaining entitlements
    • customer entitlements: remaining customer entitlements

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/utils/handleOneOffPrepaidCarryOvers/cusProductToOneOffPrepaidCarryOvers.ts
Let one off prepaid carryover prefix be "one_off_prepaid_carryover_".

One off prepaid carryover external ID — given originating customer entitlement ID; gives back text:
  Give back "{one off prepaid carryover prefix}{the first 10 of update create hash ("sha256") (originating customer entitlement ID)'s digest ("hex")}".

“Single source of truth for "which cusEnts on this cusProduct are paid by a one-off prepaid price and are consumable" — keyed by feature_id so both the "old → preserve" and "new → merge target" lookups share one classifier.”
One off prepaid customer entitlements by feature ID — given customer product; gives back a map of text to FullCustomerEntitlement:
  Let one off prepaid entitlement IDs be the unique values of customer product's customer prices, after these steps.
  Let result be an empty lookup table.
  If one off prepaid entitlement IDs' size is 0, give back result.
  For each customer entitlement in customer product's customer entitlements:
    Skip it if customer entitlement is boolean.
    Skip it if customer entitlement is unlimited.
    Skip it if customer entitlement's entitlement's ID is not in one off prepaid entitlement IDs.
    “For now, restrict to consumable features (single-use messages, credits). Allocated features (continuous-use seats) need different semantics.”
    Skip it if feature utils is allocated (customer entitlement's entitlement's feature).
    Let feature ID be customer entitlement's entitlement's feature's ID.
    Skip it if feature ID is missing.
    Record customer entitlement under feature ID in result.
  Give back result.

“Builds a "lifetime" Entitlement + InsertCustomerEntitlement pair preserving `balance` units of the originating cusEnt: `customer_product_id: null`, `interval: null`, `expires_at: null`, with a deterministic carryover external_id stamped on the cusEnt for audit.”
To build lifetime carry over — given customer entitlement, balance, full customer, and current customer product; gives back an object with entitlement and customer entitlement:
  Init carry over entitlement → entitlement:
    • customer entitlement
    • org ID: full customer's org ID
    • allowance: balance
  Let customer entitlement be init carry over customer entitlement, but with:
    • customer entitlement
    • entitlement ID: entitlement's ID
    • internal customer ID: full customer's internal ID
    • customer ID: full customer's ID
    • internal entity ID: current customer product's internal entity ID, or nothing if that's missing
    • balance
    • expires at: nothing
    • external ID set to a one off prepaid carryover external ID (customer entitlement's ID)
  Give back an object with entitlement and customer entitlement.

“Auto-preserve any one-off prepaid cusEnt balances on the outgoing customer product as a lifetime cusEnt. Lifetime here means `interval: null`, `next_reset_at: null`, `expires_at: null`, and `customer_product_id: null` (loose) — the credits remain spendable regardless of which product the customer is on after the transition. Pure transform: callers decide when the outgoing product is actually being expired. Used by paths that always preserve as a separate row (attach, multiAttach, createSchedule, migrations-v2, schedule-webhook). For the billing.update / UpdatePlan path that can merge into the new cusProduct's own slot, use `applyOneOffPrepaidCarryOvers`.”
Customer product → one off prepaid carry overs — given current customer product and full customer; gives back an object with entitlements and customer entitlements:
  Let entitlements be an empty list.
  Let customer entitlements be an empty list.
  If current customer product is missing, give back an object with entitlements and customer entitlements.
  For each customer entitlement in a one off prepaid customer entitlements by feature ID (current customer product)'s values:
    Let balance be customer entitlement's balance, or 0 if that's missing.
    Skip it if balance is zero or less.
    Build lifetime carry over, and take its entitlement and customer entitlement:
      • customer entitlement
      • balance
      • full customer
      • current customer product
    Add entitlement to entitlements.
    Add customer entitlement to customer entitlements.
  Give back an object with entitlements and customer entitlements.

“Multi-product variant: runs the single-product helper over each input and concatenates the results. Use this from compute paths that may expire more than one cusProduct in a single transition (e.g. createSchedule with a multi-plan immediate phase).”
Customer products → one off prepaid carry overs — given current customer products and full customer; gives back an object with entitlements and customer entitlements:
  Let entitlements be an empty list.
  Let customer entitlements be an empty list.
  For each current customer product in current customer products:
    Let next be the one off prepaid carry overs of customer product (current customer product and full customer).
    Add everything in next's entitlements to entitlements.
    Add everything in next's customer entitlements to customer entitlements.
  Give back an object with entitlements and customer entitlements.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/utils/handleExistingUsages/applyExistingUsages.ts
To log existing usages — given existing usages:
  Let existin usages logs be the key/value pairs of existing usages, with each item turned into the result of:
    Let entity usages be the key/value pairs of existing usage's entity usages, with each item turned into an object with entity ID and entity usage.
    Give back an object with:
      • feature ID: the first f in the features where f's internal ID is internal feature ID's ID
      • usage: existing usage's usage
      • accrued overage: existing usage's accrued overage
      • entity usages: entity usages if entity usages is not empty (otherwise nothing)
  Add to extra logs (extras: an object with existing usages: existin usages logs).

To apply existing usages — given customer product, existing usages, and entities:
  “1. Merge entities with existing usages”
  Merge entities with existing usages (entities and existing usages), and call the result merged existing usages.
  Log existing usages (existing usages: merged existing usages).
  For each key internal feature ID and value existing usage in merged existing usages:
    Let customer entitlements be the customer entitlements of a list of customer product (given internal feature IDs: a list of internal feature ID).
    Let attribution owner ID be the first customer entitlement in customer entitlements where customer entitlement is invoice credit's ID, or the first of customer entitlements' ID if that's missing if existing usage's usage attribution is set (otherwise nothing).
    “An unlimited grant absorbs the usage its allowance covers, so carried usage must not reach a priced sibling and become billable overage.”
    Let unlimited customer entitlements be the customer entitlements that pass is unlimited customer entitlement.
    Let has unlimited grant mean unlimited customer entitlements is not empty.
    Let carry targets be unlimited customer entitlements if has unlimited grant, otherwise customer entitlements.
    “Overage already exceeded its allowance on the source, so it was owed before this transition and survives it even when the grant grows.”
    Let accrued overage be depending on whether has unlimited grant:
      • if so: existing usage's accrued overage, or 0 if that's missing
      • if not: 0
    Let absorbed usage be existing usage's usage minus accrued overage.
    “1. Deduct entity usages”
    For each key entity ID and value entity usage in existing usage's entity usages:
      Deduct from customer entitlements typescript:
        • customer entitlements: carry targets
        • amount to deduct: entity usage
        • target entity ID: entity ID
        • allow overage
    “2. Deduct top level usages”
    Deduct from customer entitlements typescript:
      • customer entitlements: carry targets
      • amount to deduct: absorbed usage
      • allow overage
    “3. Re-apply overage the source had already accrued to the priced rows”
    If accrued overage is positive:
      Deduct from customer entitlements typescript:
        • customer entitlements: customer entitlements, keeping only those where customer entitlement is not unlimited
        • amount to deduct: accrued overage
        • allow overage
    For each new customer entitlement in customer entitlements:
      Let original be the first ce in customer product's customer entitlements where ce's ID is new customer entitlement's ID.
      If original is set:
        Set original's balance to new customer entitlement's balance.
        Set original's entities to new customer entitlement's entities.
        Set original's adjustment to new customer entitlement's adjustment.
        If new customer entitlement's ID is attribution owner ID:
          Set original's usage attribution to a deep copy of existing usage's usage attribution, or an empty object if that's missing.
        Debug log "Deduction for feature {new customer entitlement's feature ID}:" (with balance, entities, and adjustment).

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/utils/handleExistingUsages/cusProductToExistingUsages.ts
Customer product → existing usages — given customer product, entity ID, carry all consumable features, consumable feature IDs to carry (default an empty list), and carry unlimited usage (default false); gives back an ExistingUsages:
  If customer product is missing, give back an empty object.
  Let customer entitlements be customer product's customer entitlements.
  Let existing usages be an empty object.
  For each customer entitlement in customer entitlements:
    Skip it if customer entitlement is boolean.
    Let is unlimited mean customer entitlement is unlimited.
    Skip it if is unlimited and carry unlimited usage is false.
    Add customer product to customer entitlement (customer entitlement and customer product), and call the result customer entitlement with customer product.
    Skip it if customer entitlement with customer product is one off prepaid consumable customer entitlement.
    Let is allocated mean feature utils is allocated (customer entitlement's entitlement's feature).
    “By default, don't carry any consumable feature, unless carryAll is true, OR consumableFeatureIdsToCarry includes the feature id”
    Let carry consumable feature mean any of these is true:
      • carry all consumable features is true
      • customer entitlement's entitlement's feature's ID is in consumable feature IDs to carry
    Let should carry mean is allocated or carry consumable feature is true.
    Skip it if should not carry.
    Let internal feature ID be customer entitlement's entitlement's internal feature ID.
    If existing usages' entry for internal feature ID is missing:
      Set existing usages' entry for internal feature ID to an object with usage: 0, accrued overage: 0, and entity usages: an empty object.
    Let current existing usage be existing usages' entry for internal feature ID.
    If all of these are true:
      • carry consumable feature is true
      • the keys of customer entitlement's usage attribution, or an empty object if that's missing is not empty
    then:
      Let merged usage attribution be current existing usage's usage attribution, or an empty object if that's missing.
      For each key source internal feature ID and value attribution in customer entitlement's usage attribution, or an empty object if that's missing:
        Let current attribution be merged usage attribution's entry for source internal feature ID.
        If current attribution is set:
          Fail with an error: "carry_over_usages cannot merge multiple attribution positions for credit feature '{customer entitlement's entitlement's feature's ID}'." [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
        Set merged usage attribution's entry for source internal feature ID to an object with units: attribution's units and credits: attribution's credits.
      Set current existing usage's usage attribution to merged usage attribution.
    “1. If it's entity scoped”
    If customer entitlement is entity scoped:
      Let starting balance be the starting balance of customer entitlement with customer product.
      For each key entity ID and value entity balance in customer entitlement's entities:
        “Usage = startingBalance + adjustment - currentBalance”
        Let entity usage be starting balance plus entity balance's adjustment, or 0 if that's missing minus entity balance's balance.
        Set current existing usage's entity usages' entry for entity ID to current existing usage's entity usages' entry for entity ID, or 0 if that's missing plus entity usage.
      Move on to the next one.
    “Unlimited rows track usage as a raw negative balance that the granted balance helpers zero out, so read it directly. Never owed, so no overage.”
    If is unlimited:
      Set existing usages' entry for internal feature ID's usage to existing usages' entry for internal feature ID's usage plus the unlimited usage of a list of customer entitlement with customer product (given entity ID).
      Move on to the next one.
    “2. If it's not entity scoped”
    Let usage be the usage of a list of customer entitlement with customer product (given entity ID).
    Set existing usages' entry for internal feature ID's usage to existing usages' entry for internal feature ID's usage plus usage.
    “A negative balance is usage that already exceeded its allowance, so it was billable before this transition regardless of what replaces it.”
    Let row balance be the balance of customer entitlement with customer product (given entity ID).
    If row balance is negative:
      Set current existing usage's accrued overage to current existing usage's accrued overage, or 0 if that's missing minus row balance.
  Give back existing usages.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/utils/handleExistingUsages/mergeEntitiesWithExistingUsages.ts
To merge entities with existing usages — given entities and existing usages; gives back an ExistingUsages:
  “Count entities per feature (for continuous-use features like seats)”
  Let internal feature ID to entity count be an empty lookup table.
  For each entity in entities:
    Record internal feature ID to entity count's entry for entity's internal feature ID, or 0 if that's empty plus 1 under entity's internal feature ID in internal feature ID to entity count.
  “Add entity counts as top-level usage for features that track entities Entity count takes priority over existing usage data”
  For each entity count (at position internal feature ID) in internal feature ID to entity count:
    If existing usages' entry for internal feature ID is missing:
      Set existing usages' entry for internal feature ID to an object with usage: entity count and entity usages: an empty object.
    Otherwise:
      “Entity count takes priority - override existing usage”
      Set existing usages' entry for internal feature ID's usage to entity count.
  Give back existing usages.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/utils/handleExistingRollovers/applyExistingRollovers.ts
Let kind match score be 4.
Let interval match score be 2.
Let capacity score be 1.

“Ranks same-feature candidates by item identity (billing kind, then reset interval — the same dimensions as item keys/filters), then by whether the bucket's effective max can actually hold a carried balance.”
To score rollover candidate — given customer product, customer entitlement, and existing rollover; gives back a number:
  Let score start as 0.
  Let billing type be the billing type of customer entitlement, but with customer product set to customer product.
  If billing type, or nothing if that's missing is existing rollover's source billing type, or nothing if that's missing:
    Add kind match score to score.
  Let interval matches mean all of these are true:
    • customer entitlement's entitlement's interval, or nothing if that's missing is existing rollover's source interval, or nothing if that's missing
    • customer entitlement's entitlement's interval count, or 1 if that's missing is existing rollover's source interval count, or 1 if that's missing
  If interval matches is true, add interval match score to score.
  Let effective max be the effective rollover max of customer entitlement, but with customer product set to customer product.
  If effective max is missing or effective max is positive, add capacity score to score.
  Give back score.

To apply existing rollovers — given customer product and existing rollovers:
  To get applicable rollovers — gives back a list of ExistingRollover:
    Give back existing rollovers, keeping only those where any of these is true:
      • rollover's balance is positive
      • the values in rollover's entities has a entity where entity's balance is positive
  For each existing rollover in get applicable rollovers:
    Let candidates be customer product's customer entitlements, keeping only those where all of these are true:
      • customer entitlement's entitlement's internal feature ID is existing rollover's internal feature ID
      • customer entitlement allows rollovers
    Start with no target customer entitlement yet.
    Let best score start as negative 1.
    For each customer entitlement in candidates:
      Score rollover candidate (customer product, customer entitlement, and existing rollover), and call the result score.
      If score is more than best score:
        Set target customer entitlement to customer entitlement.
        Set best score to score.
    Skip it if target customer entitlement is missing.
    From existing rollover, take internal feature ID, source billing type, source interval, source interval count, and the rest as rollover.
    Add rollover, but with to target customer entitlement's rollovers:
      • ID set to generate ID ("roll")
      • customer entitlement ID set to target customer entitlement's ID

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/utils/handleCarryOvers/cusProductToExistingBalanceCarryOvers.ts
“A carried-over balance would have expired at the old plan's next reset. If the item rolls over, a positive leftover would instead have become a rollover at that reset, so give it the rollover's expiry (null = forever). Negative balances (debt) never roll over, so they keep the reset expiry.”
To get carry over expires at — given customer entitlement, balance, and end of cycle ms; gives back a number (or nothing):
  Let reset at be customer entitlement's next reset at, or end of cycle ms if that's missing, or nothing if that's missing.
  Let rollover config be customer entitlement's entitlement's rollover.
  If reset at is missing, rollover config is missing, or balance is zero or less, give back reset at.
  Calculate next expiry (reset at and rollover config), and give back the result.

“Pays carried debt down from the new plan's own grant for the feature, so the incoming allowance is reduced instead of a separate negative row being kept (which API balances clamp to 0 and which expires unpaid). Mutates the new product's cusEnts in place. Returns false when the new plan has no finite, customer-level grant for the feature to absorb the debt.”
To pay down debt from new customer product — given new customer product, internal feature ID, and debt; gives back true/false:
  Let targets be the customer entitlements of a list of new customer product (given internal feature IDs: a list of internal feature ID), keeping only those where customer entitlement is not unlimited and customer entitlement is not entity scoped.
  If targets is empty, give back whether false.
  Deduct from customer entitlements typescript:
    • customer entitlements: targets
    • amount to deduct: debt
    • allow overage
  “cusProductsToCusEnts returns copies, so write the paid-down balances back.”
  For each target in targets:
    Let original be the first customer entitlement in new customer product's customer entitlements where customer entitlement's ID is target's ID.
    Skip it if original is missing.
    Set original's balance to target's balance.
    Set original's adjustment to target's adjustment.
  Give back whether true.

Customer product → existing balance carry overs — given attach billing context, params, and new customer product; gives back an object with entitlements and customer entitlements:
  From attach billing context, take carry over source customer product, plan timing, end of cycle ms, and full customer.
  Let carry over params be params' carry over balances.
  If plan timing is not "immediate":
    Give back an object with entitlements: an empty list and customer entitlements: an empty list.
  If carry over source customer product is missing:
    Give back an object with entitlements: an empty list and customer entitlements: an empty list.
  If carry over params' enabled is missing:
    Give back an object with entitlements: an empty list and customer entitlements: an empty list.
  Let feature IDs be carry over params' feature IDs.
  Let customer be full customer.
  Let org ID be customer's org ID.
  Let entitlements be an empty list.
  Let customer entitlements be an empty list.
  For each customer entitlement in carry over source customer product's customer entitlements:
    Skip it if customer entitlement is boolean.
    Skip it if customer entitlement is unlimited.
    Skip it if feature utils is allocated (customer entitlement's entitlement's feature).
    “One-off prepaid consumable cusEnts are already auto-preserved as a lifetime cusEnt by cusProductToOneOffPrepaidCarryOvers — skip here to avoid minting a second carry-over row for the same balance.”
    Add customer product to customer entitlement, and call the result customer entitlement with customer product:
      • customer entitlement
      • customer product: carry over source customer product
    Skip it if customer entitlement with customer product is one off prepaid consumable customer entitlement.
    Skip it if feature IDs is set and customer entitlement's entitlement's feature's ID is not in feature IDs.
    If customer entitlement is entity scoped:
      Let entity pairs be the key/value pairs of customer entitlement's entities, after these steps:
        1. Keep only those where entity balance's balance is not 0

          Let entity be the first e in full customer's entities where e's ID is entity ID.

          Init carry over entitlement (customer entitlement, org ID, and allowance: entity balance's balance), and call the result entitlement.
          Init carry over customer entitlement, and call the result customer entitlement row:
            • customer entitlement
            • entitlement ID: entitlement's ID
            • internal customer ID: customer's internal ID
            • customer ID: customer's ID
            • internal entity ID: entity's internal ID
            • balance: entity balance's balance
            • expires at: get carry over expires at:
              • customer entitlement
              • balance: entity balance's balance
              • end of cycle ms

      Add everything in the entitlements of entity pairs to entitlements.
      Add everything in the customer entitlement rows of entity pairs to customer entitlements.
      Move on to the next one.
    Let balance be customer entitlement's balance, or 0 if that's missing.

    “Pay-per-use overage is invoiced in arrears on the outgoing plan, so only unbilled debt (free or prepaid) is paid down from the new grant.”

    Let is unbilled debt mean all of these are true:

      • is unbilled debt
      • pay down debt from new customer product gives back something:
        • new customer product
        • internal feature ID: customer entitlement's entitlement's internal feature ID
        • debt: negative balance
    then:
      Move on to the next one.
    Init carry over entitlement (customer entitlement, org ID, and allowance: balance), and call the result entitlement.
    Init carry over customer entitlement, and call the result customer entitlement row:
      • customer entitlement
      • entitlement ID: entitlement's ID
      • internal customer ID: customer's internal ID
      • customer ID: customer's ID
      • internal entity ID: carry over source customer product's internal entity ID, or nothing if that's missing

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/utils/handleCarryOvers/shouldCarryOverUsage.ts

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/utils/billingPlan/toNextCyclePreview/computeScheduledAnchorResetPreview.ts
“Compute the next cycle start, billing context override, and proration ratio for a scheduled billing cycle anchor reset. When it resets at or after the period end, the next invoice is the normal renewal at the original period end with full amount.”

  Get cycle end, and call the result original period end:
    • anchor: original anchor ms
    • interval
    • interval count
    • now: billing context's current epoch ms
  Truncate ms to second precision (scheduled anchor), and call the result normalized scheduled anchor.
  Truncate ms to second precision (original period end), and call the result normalized original period end.
  If normalized scheduled anchor is before normalized original period end:
    Get cycle end, and call the result new cycle end:
      • anchor: scheduled anchor
      • interval
      • interval count
      • now: scheduled anchor
    Truncate ms to second precision (new cycle end), and call the result normalized new cycle end.
    Let extra window be normalized new cycle end minus normalized original period end.
    Let full new cycle be normalized new cycle end minus normalized scheduled anchor.
    Give back an object with:
      • next cycle start: scheduled anchor
      • proration ratio: nothing if full new cycle is zero; otherwise extra window divided by full new cycle
      • line items billing context: billing context
  Give back an object with:
    • next cycle start: original period end
    • proration ratio: nothing
    • line items billing context: billing context, but with billing cycle anchor ms set to original anchor ms

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/utils/billingPlan/preview/tax/computeAttachTaxPreview.ts
“Build-stage helper that computes a tax preview for an attach via Stripe Tax. Read-only: calls `stripe.tax.calculations.create` (a non-mutating "what would tax be" lookup). Output is consumed by the formatter, not the executor — only ever populated when attach is invoked with `preview: true`. Skip-conditions (return undefined): - org has `automatic_tax: false` - flow is `stripe_checkout` (Stripe Checkout collects the address itself and computes tax during the buyer-facing form, so any pre-checkout preview here would diverge from what Stripe ultimately charges) - no `chargeImmediately` line items at all When the net taxable subtotal is negative, Stripe Tax is called with the absolute amount and the result is negated to preview tax-credit invoices. Net-subtotal collapsing: we sum positive and negative `chargeImmediately` line items into a single Stripe Tax line. Stripe Tax requires positive line amounts (so we can't pass a -$10 unused-credit line directly), and Stripe charges tax on the net invoice subtotal — not on positive lines alone. Collapsing to one combined line yields the same total tax that Stripe will actually invoice. If we ever need per-line `tax_code` overrides we'll have to switch to proportional credit redistribution across positive lines. Note: `autumn_checkout` is intentionally NOT skipped. It's a confirmation-only flow — no address or payment method collection — so the customer's existing Stripe address (and the resulting tax) is exactly what gets charged on confirmation. On Stripe error → returns `{ status: "incomplete", ...zeros }` so the merchant sees an explicit "tax not computed" signal in the preview rather than a silently missing field.”
To compute attach tax preview — given billing context and Autumn billing plan; gives back a PreviewTax (or nothing) (async):
  Let all line items be Autumn billing plan's line items.
  If all line items is empty, give back nothing.
  Let immediate lines be all line items, keeping only those where line's charge immediately is set.
  If immediate lines is empty, give back nothing.
  “Stripe charges tax on the net invoice subtotal — positives plus negative proration credits — not on positive lines alone. Sum across ALL chargeImmediately lines so the preview matches what Stripe actually invoices.”
  Let net subtotal be the total of each line's amount after discounts, or each line's amount if that's missing across immediate lines.
  Compute Stripe tax preview for net subtotal (billing context and net subtotal), and give back the result.

“Core Stripe Tax lookup for a net post-discount subtotal.”
To compute Stripe tax preview for net subtotal — given billing context and net subtotal; gives back a PreviewTax (or nothing) (async):
  If billing context does not want Stripe automatic tax, give back nothing.
  If billing context's checkout mode is "stripe_checkout", give back nothing.
  Let currency be the currency of billing context (given org: the org).
  Create Stripe client (org: the org and env: the env) → Stripe client.
  Zero tax — given status; gives back a PreviewTax:
    Give back an object with:
      • total: 0
      • amount inclusive: 0
      • amount exclusive: 0
      • currency
      • status
  If net subtotal is 0, give back a zero tax ("complete").
  Let customer details be the tax calculation customer details of billing context.
  Let has tax location mean any of these is true:
    • customer details is set
    • customer has usable tax location for Stripe tax (given billing context's Stripe customer)
  If has no tax location:
    Give back a zero tax:
      • "complete" if billing context is tax exempt customer, otherwise "requires_location"
  Let Stripe customer ID be billing context's Stripe customer's ID.
  Let tax sign be negative 1 if net subtotal is negative, otherwise 1.
  Let taxable subtotal be the absolute value of net subtotal.
  Try the following:
    Create Stripe client's tax's calculations, and call the result calc:
      • currency
      • everything in depending on whether customer details is set:
        • if so: an object with customer details: customer details
        • if not: an object with customer: Stripe customer ID
      • line items: a list of:
        • an object with:
          • amount: the Stripe amount of Autumn (amount: taxable subtotal and currency)
          • reference: "preview_net_subtotal"
          • quantity: 1
    Give back an object with:
      • total: the Autumn amount of Stripe times tax sign:
        • amount: calc's tax amount exclusive, or 0 if that's missing plus calc's tax amount inclusive, or 0 if that's missing
        • currency
      • amount inclusive: the Autumn amount of Stripe times tax sign:
        • amount: calc's tax amount inclusive, or 0 if that's missing
        • currency
      • amount exclusive: the Autumn amount of Stripe times tax sign:
        • amount: calc's tax amount exclusive, or 0 if that's missing
        • currency
      • currency
      • status: "complete"
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Let error message be error's message, or error as text if that's missing.
    Warn "[computeAttachTaxPreview] Stripe Tax calculation failed; returning incomplete status: {error message}".
    Give back a zero tax ("incomplete").

Let billing lock wait ms be billing lock TTL ms plus 5000.

“Background-only (early-acked webhooks — HTTP routes 423 instantly instead of waiting). Waits (bounded) for every key, runs fn, then releases only locks this call still owns.”
With billing lock — given lock keys and function; gives back a T (async):
  Let token be crypto's random UUID.
  “Sorted so concurrent multi-key holders acquire in the same order (no deadlock).”
  Let sorted keys be lock keys, after these steps:
    1. Remove duplicates
    2. ␀them, sorted
  “One deadline across ALL keys — it outlives any legitimately-held lease, so a waiter can only time out under continuous reacquisition by others.”
  Let deadline be the current time plus billing lock wait ms.
  Let held keys be an empty list.
  Try the following:
    For each lock key in sorted keys:
      Acquire lock with wait:
        • lock key
        • TTL ms: billing lock TTL ms
        • token
        • max wait ms: deadline minus the current time
        • retry ms: billing lock retry ms
      Add lock key to held keys.
    “Earlier keys' leases burned down while waiting for later ones — re-arm once so every lease covers the full critical section.”
    For each lock key in held keys:
      Refresh lock lease (lock key, token, and TTL ms: billing lock TTL ms).
    Give back a function.
  Either way, finally:
    For each lock key in held keys:
      Clear lock (lock key and token).

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/publish/publishBillingTransition.ts
To publish billing transition — given billing context, billing plan, and execution deferred (async):
  “The worker holds the live balances and the plan carries usage itself: nothing to rebase in Redis.”
  Let external customer ID be billing context's full customer's ID.
  If external customer ID is set and external customer ID is balance worker rollout enabled, stop here.
  “1. Decide whether this plan has a supported runtime transition”

    If decision's unsupported reason is set:
      Log "[publishBillingTransition] Skipped unsupported balance transition" (with unsupported reason).
    Stop here.
  Let customer ID be billing context's full customer's ID, or billing context's full customer's internal ID if that's missing.
  Try the following:
    “2. Load the final Postgres subject written by the billing plan”
    Get full subject normalized, and call the result final subject:
      • customer ID
      • entity ID: billing context's full customer's entity's ID, or nothing if that's missing
      • no run lazy resets
      • read from: "primary"
      • route source: "publishBillingTransition"
    If final subject is missing:
      Warn "[publishBillingTransition] Final subject was unavailable after execution".
      Stop here.
    “3. Atomically rebase live A usage onto B and publish the new view”
    Publish cached full subject, and call the result publish result:
      • normalized: final subject's normalized
      • balance transition plan: decision's balance transition plan
    If publish result's status is "UNSUPPORTED":
      Log "[publishBillingTransition] Skipped unsupported balance transition" (with unsupported reason).
      Stop here.
    If publish result's status is not "OK", stop here.
    “4. Preserve the atomically published subject view”
    Preserve subject cache.
    “5. Persist its exact balance to Postgres or queue a guarded retry”
    Persist or queue published balance transitions:
      • customer ID
      • balance transitions: publish result's balance transitions
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Warn "[publishBillingTransition] Failed to complete balance transition" (with error).

To resolve price match — given item, candidate, and org; gives back a ProductLevelPriceMatch (or nothing):
  Find keyed price (item and candidate) → keyed price.
  If keyed price is set:
    Give back an object with:
      • price: keyed price

        • type: "stripe_product_id"
        • Stripe product ID: item's Stripe product ID

    • currency: item's currency

  If base price is set:

      • price: base price
      • matched on: an object with type: "stripe_base_price_shape" and everything in shape matched on
  Let prepaid price be find matching prepaid price (item, candidate, and org) if org is set (otherwise nothing).

To find product level match for Stripe item — given item, candidates, org, and linked internal product IDs; gives back a ProductLevelMatch (or nothing):
  If candidates is empty, give back nothing.
  Let resolved be candidates, each turned into candidate, but with price match set to resolve price match (item, candidate, and org).
  “A claim-less single candidate is only a plausible custom base under the same gate multi-candidate fallback uses — a metered item must not silently become a custom base with its price stripped.”
  If the number of resolved is 1:
    Let only be the first of resolved.
    If only is missing, give back nothing.
    If only's price match is set, give back only.
    Give back a base plan fallback (item, resolved, and linked internal product IDs).
  “Ambiguous candidates resolve only via price claims, strongest kind first — a unique claim of that kind wins, a tie is unresolvable.”
  Let claim priority be a list of:
    • "stripe_product_id"
    • "stripe_base_price_shape"
    • "stripe_prepaid_price_shape"

    If the number of claims is 1, give back the first of claims, or nothing if that's missing.
    If claims has more than 1 item, give back nothing.
  Give back a base plan fallback (item, resolved, and linked internal product IDs).

“No price claims at all: a plausible custom base stays on the plan already linked to the subscription (a custom amount is a price change, not a plan swap); otherwise it falls back to the base plan (variants defer to their base), first base plan winning if several.”
Base plan fallback — given item, resolved, and linked internal product IDs; gives back a ProductLevelMatch (or nothing):
  “Mirrors stripeItemToBasePrice's gate — metered/tiered items are never a custom base and must stay unmatched so the anchored rematch can claim them.”
  If item's recurring usage type is "metered", give back nothing.
  If item's unit amount is missing or item's recurring interval is missing, give back nothing.
  Let linked plans be resolved, keeping only those where match's product's internal ID is in linked internal product IDs.
  If the number of linked plans is 1, give back the first of linked plans, or nothing if that's missing.
  Let base plans be resolved, keeping only those where match's product's base variant ID is missing.
  Give back the first of base plans, or nothing if that's missing.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/providers/stripe/utils/subscriptions/getRequiredActionFromSubscriptionInvoice.ts
“Fetches invoice with expanded payments and determines the required action code. When payment_behavior is "default_incomplete", Stripe doesn't throw an error - instead it returns an invoice with a payment intent in a specific status. Payment intent statuses map to: - requires_payment_method → payment_method_required - requires_action → 3ds_required (needs customer authentication) - requires_confirmation → 3ds_required (needs confirmation, typically 3DS) - requires_capture → already authorized, should not reach here - canceled/processing/succeeded → should not reach here for open invoices Falls back to payment_method_required for cases where we can't determine the status.”
To get required action from subscription invoice — given Stripe client, invoice ID, has payment method, invoice mode, and enable plan immediately; gives back a BillingResponseRequiredAction (or nothing) (async):
  “Should enable product immediately, can pay later”
  If invoice mode's enable product immediately is set, give back nothing.
  If enable plan immediately is true, give back nothing.
  “Fetch invoice with expanded payments to get payment intent status”
  Get Stripe invoice → invoice:
    • Stripe client
    • invoice ID
    • expand: a list of "payments.data.payment.payment_intent"
  “If invoice is paid, no action required”
  If invoice's status is "paid", give back nothing.
  “If invoice isn't open, no action required (could be draft, void, etc.)”
  If invoice's status is not "open", give back nothing.
  “If no payment method on customer, that's the issue”
  If has no payment method, give back an object with code: "payment_method_required" and reason: "No payment method found".
  “Get payment intent from expanded payments (properly typed from getStripeInvoice)”
  Let first payment be the first of invoice's payments' data.
  Let payment intent be first payment's payment's payment intent.
  “No payment intent info available - default to payment_method_required This happens with default_incomplete before payment is attempted”
  If payment intent is missing or payment intent is text:
    Give back an object with code: "payment_method_required" and reason: "Payment required".
  “Map payment intent status to required action code”
  Depending on payment intent's status:
    • If it is "requires_payment_method":
      “If there's a last_payment_error, a payment was attempted and failed (e.g., card declined). Otherwise, no payment method was attached.”
      If payment intent's last payment error is set:
        Give back an object with:
          • code: "payment_failed"
          • reason: payment intent's last payment error's message, or "Payment failed" if that's missing
      Give back an object with code: "payment_method_required" and reason: "Payment method required".
    • If it is "requires_action" or "requires_confirmation":
      Give back an object with:
        • code: "3ds_required"
        • reason: payment intent's last payment error's message, or "Additional authentication required" if that's missing
    • If it is "canceled":
      Give back an object with:
        • code: "payment_failed"
        • reason: payment intent's last payment error's message, or "Payment was canceled" if that's missing
    • If it is "processing":
      “Payment is processing - not a failure, but not complete either”
      Give back nothing.
    • If it is "requires_capture" or "succeeded":
      “These statuses shouldn't occur for open invoices”
      Give back nothing.
    • For anything else:
      “Unknown status - treat as payment failed”
      Give back an object with:
        • code: "payment_failed"
        • reason: "Unexpected payment intent status: {payment intent's status}"

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/providers/stripe/utils/subscriptionItems/buildStripeSubscriptionItemsUpdate.ts

  Let subscription items update be an empty list.

            • everything in an object with metadata: spec's metadata (only if spec's metadata is set)
      Otherwise:
        Add the subscription item of spec to subscription items update.
      Move on to the next one.
    “Stored price — check for existing subscription item”
    Skip it if spec's Stripe price ID is missing.
    Find Stripe subscription item by Stripe price ID, and call the result existing item:
      • Stripe price ID: spec's Stripe price ID
      • Stripe subscription items: current subscription items
    Let should update item mean existing item is set and existing item's quantity is not spec's quantity.
    Let should create item mean existing item is missing.
    If should update item:
      Add an object with to subscription items update:
        • ID: existing item's ID
        • everything in an object with quantity: spec's quantity (only if spec's quantity is set)
        • everything in an object with metadata: spec's metadata (only if spec's metadata is set)
    If should create item:
      Add an object with to subscription items update:
        • price: spec's Stripe price ID
        • everything in an object with quantity: spec's quantity (only if spec's quantity is set)
        • everything in an object with metadata: spec's metadata (only if spec's metadata is set)
  “Remove subscription items that are no longer in the desired specs”

    Skip it if subscription item's ID is in matched subscription item IDs.

      • Stripe price ID: the Stripe price ID of subscription item
      • Stripe item specs

  Give back subscription items update.

    • Stripe subscription ID: billing context's Stripe subscription's ID
  “2. Drop customer products managed by a non-Stripe processor (e.g. RevenueCat). `filterCustomerProductsByStripeSubscriptionId` with `undefined` returns every customer product whose `subscription_ids` is empty — and RC-managed cus products have empty `subscription_ids`. Without this step, an RC product's Stripe price would leak into a brand-new Stripe subscription created for an add-on attach.”
  Filter customer products by processor type, and call the result Stripe managed customer products:
    • customer products: related customer products
    • processor type: processor type's Stripe
  “2a. Exclude orphan paid-recurring cusProducts (no sub link, not freshly inserted) — their recurring prices would otherwise leak into a new sub on the next attach.”
  Let mutated customer product IDs be the unique values of one list combining.
  Let non orphan customer products be Stripe managed customer products, keeping only the customer products that pass this check:
    If customer product's ID is in mutated customer product IDs, give back whether true.
    Let is paid recurring orphan mean all of these are true:
      • a customer product (customer product)'s paid's recurring's valid is set
      • whether a customer product (customer product) has subscription's valid is missing
    Give back whether is not paid recurring orphan.
  “3. Filter customer products by active statuses”
  Filter customer products by active statuses (customer products: non orphan customer products), and call the result active customer products.
  “4. Get recurring subscription item array (doesn't include one-off items)”
  Let recurring Stripe item specs be the recurring Stripe item specs of active customer products (given billing context).

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/providers/stripe/utils/stripeItemSpec/customerProductsToRecurringStripeItemSpecs.ts

        Add item to inline specs.

          Do nothing.

      Otherwise:
        Record item under price ID in stored price specs.
  Give back stored price specs' values as a list, plus inline specs.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/providers/stripe/utils/stripeItemSpec/cusPriceToStripeItemSpec/cusPriceToStripeItemSpec.ts

    • if so: the currency of billing context (given org: the org)

  To build spec — given mode; gives back a StripeItemSpec (or nothing):
    “1. Fixed / one-off price (no entitlement needed)”

      Let config be price's config.
      If config's amount, or 0 if that's missing is zero or less, give back nothing.

        • customer price
        • customer product
        • currency
        • org default

      • customer product
      • customer entitlements: customer product's customer entitlements
    If customer entitlement with customer product is missing, give back nothing.
    “2. Prepaid (usage-in-advance)”

      Give back the Stripe item spec of prepaid:
        • customer entitlement with customer product
        • currency
        • org default

      Give back the Stripe item spec of allocated (customer entitlement with customer product, currency, and org default).
    Give back nothing.
  Start with no spec yet.
  Try the following:
    Build spec, and put the result in spec.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    “Read-only rendering (verify): a fixed/prepaid price that can't render its stored Stripe id is re-rendered in inline mode instead of failing.”

      • billing context's action source is "verify"
      • price is fixed or price is prepaid
    If can retry inline:
      Build spec ("inline"), and put the result in spec.
    Otherwise, if all of these are true:
      • billing context's action source is "verify"
      • error is an internal error
      • error's code is error code's Stripe price not linked
    then:
      “Usage prices have no inline render; their Stripe prices are created lazily at attach, so an unlinked one is expected state, not drift.”
      Give back nothing.
    Otherwise:
      Fail with error.
  If spec is missing, give back nothing.
  “Correlate Stripe-generated invoice lines back to Autumn billing context.”
  Set spec's metadata to an object with:
    • Autumn product ID: customer product's product's ID

  Give back spec.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/providers/stripe/utils/invoices/handleInvoicePaymentFailure.ts

  Let auth codes be a list of:

    • "authentication_not_handled"

    • "authentication" is in message
    • "3d secure" is in message
  then:
    Give back "3ds_required".
  Give back "payment_failed".

“Builds a failed PayInvoiceResult from an invoice and error. Handles "no_payment_method" and Stripe errors - throws non-Stripe errors.”

    Give back an object with:

  Let is Stripe error mean Stripe error's type is set.
  If is not Stripe error, fail with error.
  “3. Handle Stripe errors”
  Give back an object with:
    • paid: false
    • invoice

      • reason: Stripe error's message, or "Failed to pay invoice" if that's missing
    • Stripe error

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/providers/stripe/utils/invoiceLines/convertToDbLineItem/groupStripeLineItems.ts
Type StripeLineItemGroup: an object.

  Let groups be an empty lookup table.
  For each line item in Stripe line items:
    Let parent be line item's parent.

    Start with no group type yet.
    If parent's subscription item details' subscription item is set:
      Set group key to parent's subscription item details' subscription item.
      Set group type to "subscription_item".
    Otherwise, if parent's invoice item details' invoice item is set:
      Set group key to parent's invoice item details' invoice item.
      Set group type to "invoice_item".

      Set group key to line item's ID.
      Set group type to "ungrouped".
    Let existing be groups' entry for group key.
    If existing is set:
      Add line item to existing's line items.
    Otherwise:
      Record an object with group key, group type, and line items: a list of line item under group key in groups.
  Give back groups' values as a list.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/providers/stripe/utils/invoiceLines/convertToDbLineItem/stripeLineItemGroupToDbLineItems.ts
“Map of subscription_item_id -> metadata”
Type SubscriptionItemMetadataMap: a map of text to Stripe.Metadata.

“Converts a group of Stripe line items to Autumn DB invoice line items. For single-item groups: matches to Autumn LineItem(s), creates one DB row. For multi-item groups (tiered): matches first item to Autumn LineItem(s), applies context to all items in group. Multi-entity support: One Stripe line item can match multiple Autumn line items (e.g., when 2 entities each have a $20 base price merged into one $40 Stripe item). All matched customer_product_ids and customer_entitlement_ids are collected into arrays.”
Stripe line item group → DB line items — given group, Stripe discounts, invoice ID, Stripe invoice ID, Autumn line items, and subscription item metadata; gives back an object with DB line items and matched Autumn line items:

  Let representative line item be the first of group's line items.
  “Get subscription item metadata if available”
  Let subscription item ID be representative line item's parent's subscription item details' subscription item.
  Let subscription item metadata be subscription item metadata's entry for subscription item ID if subscription item ID is text (otherwise nothing).
  “Find ALL matching Autumn LineItems (multi-entity support)”
  Filter billing line items by Stripe line item, and call the result matched line items:
    • Stripe line item: representative line item
    • Autumn line items
    • subscription item metadata
  “Determine stripe_subscription_item_id for grouping”
  Let Stripe subscription item ID be group's group key if group's group type is "subscription_item" (otherwise nothing).
  “Check if this is a multi-item group (tiered pricing)”
  Let is multi item group mean group's line items has more than 1 item.
  “Convert each Stripe line item to DB row”
  Let DB line items be group's line items, with each Stripe line item turned into the result of:
    If matched line items is not empty:
      Merge Stripe and billing line items, and give back the result:
        • Stripe line item
        • Stripe discounts
        • billing line items: matched line items
        • invoice ID
        • Stripe invoice ID
        • Stripe subscription item ID
        • is multi item group
    Create DB line item from Stripe only, and give back the result:
      • Stripe line item
      • Stripe discounts
      • invoice ID
      • Stripe invoice ID
      • Stripe subscription item ID
      • subscription item metadata
  Give back an object with DB line items and matched Autumn line items: matched line items.

“Creates DB line item by merging Stripe line item data with Autumn billing line item context. Stripe fields: stripe identifiers, amounts, quantities, discounts Autumn fields: entity relationships, billing timing, direction, prorated For multi-item groups (tiered pricing), we use Stripe's description (includes tier info) and mark description_source as "stripe". Multi-entity support: Accepts array of billing line items and collects all customer_product_ids and customer_entitlement_ids into arrays.”
To merge Stripe and billing line items — given Stripe line item, Stripe discounts, billing line items, invoice ID, Stripe invoice ID, Stripe subscription item ID, and is multi item group; gives back an InsertDbInvoiceLineItem:
  “Use first billing line item as primary context source”
  Let primary line item be the first of billing line items.
  From primary line item, take context.
  Let price details be Stripe line item's pricing's price details.
  Let Stripe proration be Stripe line item's proration, or primary line item's prorated if that's missing.
  “Determine discount data source based on discountable flag When discountable === false, Autumn pre-calculates discounts and sends the post-discount amount to Stripe. So stripeLineItem.amount is already discounted and discount_amounts is empty. In this case, use Autumn's original pre-discount amount and discount breakdown.”
  Let Autumn discountable be context's discountable, or true if that's missing.
  Let is backdated aggregate mean context's backdate is set.
  Let has Autumn discounts mean all of these are true:
    • is not backdated aggregate
    • Autumn discountable is missing
    • primary line item's discounts is not empty
  Start with no amount yet.
  Start with no amount after discounts yet.
  Start with no discounts yet.
  If has Autumn discounts:
    “Non-discountable: Autumn pre-calculated discounts Stripe amount is already post-discount, use Autumn's original values”
    Set amount to the total amount across billing line items.
    Set amount after discounts to the total amount after discounts across billing line items.
    Set discounts to primary line item's discounts, with each d turned into an object with:
      • amount off: d's amount off
      • percent off: d's percent off
      • Stripe coupon ID: d's Stripe coupon ID
  Otherwise:
    “Discountable (or no Autumn discounts): Stripe handles discounts Use Stripe's discount_amounts”
    Set amount to the Autumn amount of Stripe:
      • amount: Stripe line item's amount
      • currency: Stripe line item's currency
    Let discount total be the total amount across Stripe line item's discount amounts.
    Set amount after discounts to the Autumn amount of Stripe:
      • amount: Stripe line item's amount minus discount total
      • currency: Stripe line item's currency
    Set discounts to the DB discounts of Stripe discounts, plus Stripe line item's discounts:
      • discount amounts: Stripe line item's discount amounts
      • currency: Stripe line item's currency
  “Stripe quantity (for reference)”
  Let Stripe quantity be Stripe line item's quantity, or nothing if that's missing.
  “Determine quantities based on scenario”
  Let total quantity start as nothing.
  Let paid quantity start as nothing.
  If is multi item group:
    “Multi-item group (tiered pricing): use Stripe quantities per tier Each tier has its own quantity from Stripe”
    If Stripe quantity is set:
      Let price config be context's price's config.
      Let billing units be price config's billing units, or 1 if that's missing.
      Set total quantity to Stripe quantity times billing units.
      Set paid quantity to total quantity.
  Otherwise:
    “Single item: use Autumn quantities (handles 1:1 and multi-entity)”
    Let Autumn total quantity be the total of each li's total quantity, or 0 if that's missing across billing line items.
    Let Autumn paid quantity be the total of each li's paid quantity, or 0 if that's missing across billing line items.
    Set total quantity to Autumn total quantity, or nothing if that's empty.
    Set paid quantity to Autumn paid quantity, or nothing if that's empty.
    “Fall back to Stripe calculation if no Autumn quantities”
    If total quantity is missing and Stripe quantity is set:
      Let price config be context's price's config.
      Let billing units be price config's billing units, or 1 if that's missing.
      Set total quantity to Stripe quantity times billing units.
      Set paid quantity to total quantity.
  “For multi-item groups, use Stripe description (has tier info); otherwise use Autumn”
  Let use Stripe description mean all of these are true:
    • is multi item group or is backdated aggregate
    • Stripe line item's description is set
  Let description be depending on whether use Stripe description is true:
    • if so: Stripe line item's description
    • if not: primary line item's description, or "" if that's missing
  Let description source be "stripe" if use Stripe description is true, otherwise "autumn".
  “Collect customer_product_ids, customer_price_ids, and customer_entitlement_ids from ALL matched line items”
  Let customer product IDs be billing line items, after these steps:
    1. Turn each li into li's context's customer product's ID
    2. Keep only those where ID is set and ID is set
  Let customer price IDs be billing line items, after these steps:
    1. Turn each li into li's context's customer price's ID
    2. Keep only those where ID is set and ID is set
  Let customer entitlement IDs be billing line items, after these steps:
    1. Turn each li into li's context's customer entitlement's ID
    2. Keep only those where ID is set and ID is set
  “Tiered groups split by Stripe tier, not by entity, so there is no per-entity fact to store”
  Let entities be an empty list if is multi item group, otherwise the DB entities of billing line items.
  Give back an object with:
    • ID: generate ksuid (prefix: "invoice_li_")
    • invoice ID: invoice ID
    • Stripe ID: Stripe line item's ID
    • Stripe invoice ID: Stripe invoice ID
    • Stripe invoice item ID: Stripe line item's parent's invoice item details' invoice item, or nothing if that's missing
    • Stripe subscription item ID: Stripe subscription item ID
    • Stripe product ID: price details' product, or nothing if that's missing
    • Stripe price ID: price details' price, or nothing if that's missing

    • amount
    • amount after discounts: amount after discounts
    • currency: Stripe line item's currency
    • Stripe quantity: Stripe quantity
    • total quantity: total quantity
    • paid quantity: paid quantity

    • description

    • price ID: context's price's ID

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/providers/stripe/utils/invoiceLines/convertToDbLineItem/stripeLineItemToDbLineItem.ts
“Map of subscription_item_id -> metadata”
Type SubscriptionItemMetadataMap: a map of text to Stripe.Metadata.

“Converts multiple Stripe invoice line items to Autumn DB invoice line items. Groups Stripe line items by subscription_item/invoice_item first to handle tiered pricing (where Stripe creates multiple line items per tier). Matching order: 1. Match by autumn_line_item_id in metadata (best match) 2. Match by autumn_customer_price_id in metadata 3. Match by stripe_price_id (config.stripe_price_id or config.stripe_prepaid_price_v2_id) 4. Match by stripe_product_id (product.processor?.id) Multi-entity support: One Stripe line item can match multiple Autumn line items. All matched Autumn line items are removed from candidates to prevent double-matching.”
Stripe line items → DB line items — given Stripe line items, Stripe discounts, invoice ID, Stripe invoice ID, Autumn line items, and subscription item metadata; gives back a list of InsertDbInvoiceLineItem:
  “Track which autumn line items have been matched”
  Let remaining Autumn line items be a copy of Autumn line items.
  Let all DB line items be an empty list.
  “Group Stripe line items by subscription_item/invoice_item”
  Group Stripe line items (Stripe line items), and call the result groups.
  For each group in groups:
    From the DB line items of group, take DB line items and matched Autumn line items:
      • Stripe discounts
      • invoice ID
      • Stripe invoice ID
      • Autumn line items: remaining Autumn line items
      • subscription item metadata
    “Remove ALL matched Autumn LineItems from candidates (multi-entity support)”
    For each matched item in matched Autumn line items:
      Let match index be the position of the first li in remaining Autumn line items where li's ID is matched item's ID (or -1).
      If match index is not negative 1, run remaining Autumn line items' splice (match index and 1).
    Add everything in DB line items to all DB line items.
  Give back all DB line items.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/providers/stripe/utils/discounts/applyAmountOffDiscountToLineItems.ts
To allocate amount off discounts — given line items, amount off minor units, and currency:
  Let weighted items be line items, after these steps:
    1. Turn each item into an object with:
      • item
      • index
      • weight: the Stripe amount of Autumn (amount: the absolute value of item's amount and currency)
    2. Keep only those where item's weight is positive
  Let total weight be the total weight across weighted items.
  If total weight is 0, give back an empty lookup table.
  Let allocations be weighted items, with each item turned into the result of:
    Let exact be amount off minor units times weight divided by total weight.
    Let minor units be exact's floor.
    Give back an object with:
      • item
      • index
      • minor units
      • remainder: exact minus minor units
  Let remaining start as amount off minor units minus the total minor units across allocations.
  Let by remainder be a copy of allocations, sorted by this rule:
    Let diff be b's remainder's compared to (a's remainder).
    Give back a's index minus b's index if diff is 0, otherwise diff.
  For each index in by remainder:
    Stop the loop if remaining is zero or less.
    Add 1 to allocations' entry for index's minor units.
    Subtract 1 from remaining.
  Give back a lookup table built from allocations, with each item turned into a list of.

“Applies an amount_off discount to line items. Only applies to charge items (not refunds) - distributes proportionally across charges.”
To apply amount off discount to line items — given line items, discount, and options; gives back a list of LineItem:
  Let coupon be discount's source's coupon.
  Let amount off cents be coupon's amount off.
  If amount off cents is missing or amount off cents is 0, give back line items.
  Let currency be coupon's currency, or "usd" if that's missing.
  “Filter to applicable CHARGE line items only Discounts reduce what the customer pays, so only apply to charges”
  Let applicable charge items be line items, keeping only those where there is a line item of discount applies (discount and line item: item).
  If applicable charge items is empty, give back line items.
  Let eligible cycle count be the larger of all of get backdated discount cycle count (line item: each item and coupon), for each item in applicable charge items.
  If eligible cycle count is zero or less, give back line items.
  “Build a map of line item -> discount amount”
  Allocate amount off discounts, and call the result discount map:
    • line items: applicable charge items
    • amount off minor units: amount off cents
    • currency
  “Apply discounts to line items”
  Give back line items, with each item turned into the result of:
    Let item discount be discount map's entry for item.
    If item discount is missing or item discount is 0, give back item.
    Let new discount be an object with:
      • amount off: item discount
      • Stripe coupon ID: coupon's ID
      • coupon name: coupon's name, or coupon's ID if that's empty
    Let existing discounts be item's discounts.
    Let total discount be the total amount off across existing discounts plus item discount.
    Let is proration credit mean item's context's direction is "refund".
    Let amount after discounts be depending on whether is proration credit:
      • if so: the smaller of item's amount plus total discount and 0
      • if not: the larger of item's amount minus total discount and 0
    Let description be depending on whether item's context's discountable is set:
      • if so: item's description
      • if not: add discount tag to description (description: item's description)
    Give back item, but with:
      • description set to description
      • discounts set to a list of everything in existing discounts and new discount
      • amount after discounts set to amount after discounts

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/providers/stripe/utils/discounts/applyPercentOffDiscountToLineItems.ts

      • if so: item's description
      • if not: add discount tag to description (description: item's description)

      • amount after discounts set to amount after discounts

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/providers/stripe/utils/discounts/getBackdatedDiscountCycleCount.ts

  If backdate is missing, give back 1.
  From backdate, take starts at and cycle count.
  If coupon's duration is "forever", give back cycle count.
  If coupon's duration is "once", give back 1.
  If coupon's duration is not "repeating", give back 1.
  Let duration in months be coupon's duration in months, or 0 if that's missing.
  If duration in months is zero or less, give back 0.
  Add interval, and call the result discount ends at:
    • from: starts at
    • interval: billing interval's month
    • interval count: duration in months
  Let eligible cycles start as 0.
  Let cycle start mean starts at is true.
  Keep repeating while eligible cycles is less than cycle count and cycle start is before discount ends at:
    Add 1 to eligible cycles.
    Add interval, and call the result next cycle start:
      • from: cycle start
      • interval: the interval of line item's context's price's config
      • interval count: the interval count of line item's context's price's config, or 1 if that's missing
    Stop the loop if next cycle start is at most cycle start.
    Set cycle start to next cycle start.
  Give back the smaller of eligible cycles and cycle count.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/providers/stripe/actionBuilders/buildStripeRefundAction.ts
“Build a Stripe refund action from the computed refund plan. Retrieves the invoice/charge, validates refundability, and computes the final cents amount so execute only needs to issue the refund.”
To build Stripe refund action — given Autumn billing plan; gives back a StripeRefundAction (or nothing) (async):
  From Autumn billing plan, take refund plan.
  If refund plan is missing, give back nothing.
  If refund plan's amount is zero or less, give back nothing.
  Create Stripe client (org: the org and env: the env) → Stripe client.
  Retrieve Stripe client's invoices, and call the result Stripe invoice:
    • refund plan's invoice's Stripe ID
    • expand: a list of "payments.data.payment.payment_intent"
  Resolve charge from invoice (Stripe client and Stripe invoice), and call the result charge.
  If charge is missing:
    Fail with an error: "Could not resolve a charge from the invoice to refund" [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
  If charge's paid is missing or charge's status is not "succeeded":
    Fail with an error: "This charge is not eligible for a refund" [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
  Let refundable amount in cents be charge's amount minus charge's amount refunded.
  If refundable amount in cents is zero or less, give back nothing.
  Let amount in cents be the smaller of the Stripe amount of Autumn and refundable amount in cents.
  If amount in cents is zero or less, give back nothing.
  Give back an object with:
    • type: "refund_last_invoice"
    • Stripe invoice ID: refund plan's invoice's Stripe ID
    • charge ID: charge's ID
    • amount in cents

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/providers/stripe/actionBuilders/buildStripeSubscriptionScheduleAction.ts
“═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ TYPES ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════”
Type StripeSubscriptionScheduleResult: an object.

“The 4 possible scenarios for subscription schedule actions: - no_phases: No phases with items, nothing to do - single_indefinite: 1 phase with no end_date (e.g., uncancel) - simple_cancel: 1 phase + trailing empty (cancel at end of cycle) - future_standalone: A standalone schedule that starts in the future - multi_phase: Multiple phases requiring a schedule”

“═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════ HELPER FUNCTIONS ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════”

  Give back whether phase's items is set and phase's items is not empty.

Is free phase placeholder only? — given phase; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether phase has items and all of phase's items pass is free phase placeholder item.

“Filters out empty phases from both ends. Stripe requires items in every phase.”
To filter empty phases — given phases; gives back a list of Stripe.SubscriptionScheduleUpdateParams.Phase:
  Find phases index (phase has items), and call the result first non empty index.
  If first non empty index is negative 1, give back an empty list.
  Let last non empty index start as the number of phases minus 1.
  Keep repeating while all of this holds:
    • last non empty index is zero or more
    • phase has no items (given phases' entry for last non empty index)
    Decrease last non empty index by 1.
  Give back phases from position first non empty index up to last non empty index plus 1.

“Determines which scenario we're in based on phases.”
To get schedule scenario — given scheduled phases, ends with empty phase, should create future schedule, has subscription, and is create schedule; gives back a ScheduleScenario:
  If scheduled phases is empty, give back "no_phases".
  If should create future schedule, give back "future_standalone".
  If the number of scheduled phases is 1:
    “A lone $0 placeholder has no subscription items to create a subscription from.”
    Let needs standalone schedule mean all of these are true:
      • is create schedule
      • has no subscription
      • the first of scheduled phases is free phase placeholder only
    If ends with empty phase is true and does not need standalone schedule, give back "simple_cancel".
    If the first of scheduled phases' end date is missing, give back "single_indefinite".
  Give back "multi_phase".

“An existing schedule is released onto its subscription, or cancelled when it has none.”

“A recreate unlinks its rows from the old subscription and schedule before relinking them.”

  Give back whether customer product's subscription IDs is empty and customer product's scheduled IDs is empty.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/pooledBalances/execute/promoteDuePooledContributions.ts

License-keyed granted is purchased × G — this statement only promotes due rows, it does not rewrite granted from Σ. Contribution-less subscription pools are left untouched. DB + memory only — cache propagation is the caller's job, AFTER its own cache writes (the lazy path patches the subject cache post-reset).”

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/pooledBalances/compute/applyIncomingPooledBalanceSources/computePooledBalanceLifecycle.ts

  If customer product's customer license link ID is set, give back pooled balance reset mode's lazy.

    • pooled balance's customer license link ID is customer license link ID

      • customer license link ID: nothing
  Give back an object with Stripe subscription ID: nothing and customer license link ID: nothing.
