##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/pooledBalances/compute/applyIncomingPooledBalanceSources/upsertPooledBalance.ts
To upsert pooled balance — given compute context, contribution customer entitlement, customer product, identity, contribution amounts, next reset at, and now; gives back a MutablePooledCustomerEntitlement:
  Let existing pooled customer entitlement be compute context's pooled customer entitlement by identity's entry for the key of identity.
  Let tracks balance mean all of these are true:
    • identity's unlimited is missing
    • contribution customer entitlement's entitlement is not boolean
  “A source that was already pooled carries balance 0 — its grant lives in the pool it is leaving. Seed from the contribution instead, whether the grant lands back on the same pool or on a newly inserted one.”
  Let replaces removed contribution mean compute context's pooled balance IDs with removed contributions as a list has a pool ID where compute context's pooled customer entitlement by pool ID's entry for pool ID's pooled balance's internal feature ID is identity's internal feature ID.
  Let balance delta start as depending on whether tracks balance is true:
    • if so: contribution customer entitlement's balance, or 0 if that's missing
    • if not: 0
  If tracks balance is true and replaces removed contribution is true:
    Set balance delta to contribution amounts' current contribution.
  “Re-admitting a source that still contributes to this very pool would count its grant twice: the pool already includes it, and nothing removed it. Only the difference is owed, so re-running a transition is a no-op.”
  Let existing contribution be contribution customer entitlement's pooled balance contribution.
  Let already counted by pool be whether all of these are true:
    • existing contribution is set
    • existing pooled customer entitlement is set
    • existing contribution's pooled balance ID is existing pooled customer entitlement's pooled balance's ID
    • existing contribution's pooled balance ID is not in compute context's pooled balance IDs with removed contributions
  Let is license keyed mean identity's customer license link ID is set.
  Let granted delta be depending on whether is license keyed:
    • if so: 0
    • if not: depending on whether already counted by pool is set:
      • if so: contribution amounts' current contribution minus existing contribution's current contribution, or 0 if that's missing
      • if not: contribution amounts' current contribution
  If already counted by pool is set or is license keyed, set balance delta to 0.
  If existing pooled customer entitlement is missing:
    Init pooled balance graph, and call the result inserted pooled customer entitlement:
      • contribution customer entitlement
      • customer product
      • identity
      • balance delta
      • granted: 0 if is license keyed, otherwise contribution amounts' current contribution
      • next reset at
      • now
    Add inserted pooled balance to compute context:
      • compute context
      • pooled customer entitlement: inserted pooled customer entitlement
    If tracks balance is true:
      Carry source rollovers to pool:
        • pooled balance plan: compute context's plan
        • contribution customer entitlement
        • pooled customer entitlement: inserted pooled customer entitlement
    Give back inserted pooled customer entitlement.
  Let should update existing pooled balance mean balance delta is not 0 or granted delta is not 0.
  If should update existing pooled balance:
    Add to update pool balances:
      • pooled balance plan: compute context's plan
      • pooled customer entitlement: existing pooled customer entitlement
      • balance: add safe:
        • left: existing pooled customer entitlement's balance
        • right: balance delta
      • granted: add safe:
        • left: existing pooled customer entitlement's pooled balance's granted
        • right: granted delta
  If tracks balance is true:
    Carry source rollovers to pool:
      • pooled balance plan: compute context's plan
      • contribution customer entitlement
      • pooled customer entitlement: existing pooled customer entitlement
  Give back existing pooled customer entitlement.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/pooledBalances/attribution/attributePooledBalances.ts
Type AttributedBalance: an ApiBalanceV1.
Type PoolTotals: an ApiBalanceV1.

“What one scope feeds into one pool; `poolId` is null until billing links the source.”
Type PooledContribution: an object.

“Billing's recorded contribution, else what billing records when it links the source.”
Contribution of — given customer entitlement and customer product:
  Give back customer entitlement's pooled balance contribution's current contribution, or compute pooled balance contribution amounts' current contribution if that's missing:
    • contribution customer entitlement: customer entitlement
    • customer product

Earliest reset at — given first and second:
  If first is missing, give back second.
  If second is missing, give back first.
  Give back the smaller of first and second.

To merge contribution — given existing and added; gives back a PooledContribution:
  Give back an object with:
    • pool ID: added's pool ID
    • contribution: existing's contribution, or 0 if that's missing plus added's contribution
    • next reset at: the earliest reset at existing's next reset at, or nothing if that's missing and added's next reset at

“What the given plans pool into the customer's shared balances, per feature and pool.”
Customer products → pooled contributions — given customer products and in statuses; gives back a lookup of text to list of PooledContribution:
  Let contributions be an empty object.
  For each customer product in customer products:
    Skip it if customer product's status is not in in statuses.
    For each customer entitlement in customer product's customer entitlements:
      Skip it if customer entitlement is not pooled balance source.
      Let feature ID be customer entitlement's entitlement's feature's ID.
      Let by pool be contributions' entry for feature ID, or an empty lookup table if that's missing.
      Let pool ID be customer entitlement's pooled balance contribution's pooled balance ID, or nothing if that's missing.
      Record merge contribution under pool ID in by pool:
        • existing: by pool's entry for pool ID
        • added: an object with:
          • pool ID
          • contribution: the contribution of customer entitlement and customer product
          • next reset at: customer entitlement's next reset at, or nothing if that's missing
      Set contributions' entry for feature ID to by pool.
  Give back an object built from the key/value pairs of contributions, each turned into a list of feature ID and a copy of by pool's values.

“A contributor's slice of a pool: its contribution as granted, with the pool's remaining and usage split by its share of all contributions, so rollovers in the pool are shared out too.”
Attribute pooled balance — given own, contribution, pool, and pool contributions; gives back an AttributedBalance:
  Let base be own, or an object with if that's missing:
    • granted: 0
    • remaining: 0
    • usage: 0
    • unlimited: false
    • next reset at: contribution's next reset at
    • overage allowed: false
  Let share be depending on whether pool contributions is positive:
    • if so: contribution's contribution divided by pool contributions
    • if not: 0
  Give back base, but with:
    • granted set to base's granted plus contribution's contribution
    • remaining set to base's remaining plus pool's remaining, or 0 if that's missing times share
    • usage set to base's usage plus pool's usage, or 0 if that's missing times share
    • unlimited set to base's unlimited, or pool's unlimited, or false if that's missing if that's empty
    • overage allowed set to base's overage allowed, or pool's overage allowed, or false if that's missing if that's empty

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/execute/applyDerivedCustomerProductIsCustom.ts
“A customer product to derive for, and where the result has to land.”
Type DerivationTarget: an object.

“A patch entry carries the PRE-patch customer product, with the changes in its insert/delete arrays, so the post-patch item set has to be reconstructed before diffing. Known gap: one-off prepaid carry-overs land on the patched row via the plan's own `insertCustomerEntitlements`, in DB-insert shape with no hydrated entitlement, so they are not reconstructed here. A patch that carries credits can read non-custom now and custom on the next write. The drift is towards custom — the safe direction — and it self-corrects the next time the row is touched.”
To collect derivation targets — given Autumn billing plan; gives back a list of DerivationTarget:
  Give back one list combining:
    • Autumn billing plan's insert customer products, with each customer product turned into an object with customer product, target: customer product, and via: "insert"
    • get patch customer products (Autumn billing plan), with each patch turned into an object with:
      • customer product: apply customer product items patch:
        • customer product: patch's customer product
        • insert customer prices: patch's insert customer prices
        • insert customer entitlements: patch's insert customer entitlements
        • delete customer prices: patch's delete customer prices
        • delete customer entitlements: patch's delete customer entitlements
      • target: patch's customer product
      • via: "update"

“Every distinct catalog version the plan touches, fetched in one pass so the derivation itself runs with no further IO. An unresolved product resolves to null, which the derivation reads as custom — the safe direction — rather than failing the billing write.”
To load base products — given targets; gives back a map of text to FullProduct (or nothing) (async):
  Let internal product IDs be all results, combined, of turning each item in targets into depending on whether customer product's internal product ID is set without duplicates:
    • if so: a list of customer product's internal product ID
    • if not: an empty list
  Let loaded be for every internal product ID in internal product IDs, all at the same time, collecting the results:
    Try the following:
      Get full [ProductService], and call the result product:
        • ID or internal ID: internal product ID
        • org ID: the org's ID
        • env: the env
        • allow not found
      Give back a list of internal product ID and product.
    If anything fails (call the problem error):
      Warn "[isCustom] could not load base product {internal product ID}" (with error).
      Give back a list of internal product ID and nothing.
  Give back a lookup table built from loaded.

“Stamps the derived `is_custom` onto every customer product this plan creates or whose items it rewrites. Runs here rather than in each action's compute step because every v2 write funnels through the billing plan: one hook covers attach, update, schedules, sync, restore, imports and the lifecycle actions alike, and no caller can reintroduce a hand-picked value. Plain update entries are left alone — they only move status, dates and subscription ids, so the customer's item set (and therefore the flag) is unchanged.”
To apply derived customer product is custom — given Autumn billing plan (async):
  Collect derivation targets (Autumn billing plan) → targets.
  If targets is empty, stop here.
  Load base products (targets) → base products.
  “Every load is done, so the rest is pure — no IO inside the loop.”
  Get update customer products (Autumn billing plan), and call the result update entries.
  For each customer product, target, and via in targets:
    Derive customer product is custom → is custom:
      • customer product
      • base product: base products' entry for customer product's internal product ID if customer product's internal product ID is set (otherwise nothing)
      • features: the features
    If via is "insert":
      Set target's is custom to is custom.
      Move on to the next one.
    Skip it if is custom is target's is custom.
    Let update entry be the first entry in update entries where entry's customer product's ID is target's ID.
    If update entry is set:
      Set update entry's updates' is custom to is custom.
      Move on to the next one.
    “The patch plan always registers an update entry for the patched row, so this is a guard against a future caller that doesn't — without it the derived value would be silently dropped.”
    Set Autumn billing plan's update customer products to a list of:
      • everything in Autumn billing plan's update customer products
      • an object with:
        • customer product: target
        • updates: an object with is custom: is custom

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/execute/deriveCustomerProductIsCustom.ts
“Which keys of a plan diff mean "this customer's plan is custom". `diffPlanV1` can also emit `free_trial`, deliberately left out: a longer trial for one customer is not a custom plan, and trials are inherited rather than re-read from catalog across version changes, so those customers stay intact without the flag. Everything else `diffPlanV1` reports counts — base price, item adds and removes, and the license lane (`upsert_licenses` / `remove_licenses`).”
Let custom diff keys be a list of:
  • "price"
  • "add_items"
  • "remove_items"
  • "upsert_licenses"
  • "remove_licenses"

“Best-effort: a reporting failure must never change the derived flag.”
To report derivation failure — given customer product and error:
  Try the following:
    Let IDs be an object with:
      • customer product ID: customer product's ID
      • internal product ID: customer product's internal product ID
    Report error:
      • context: an object with logger: child (context: IDs)
      • error: an error: "is_custom derivation failed for customer product {IDs' customer product ID} (product {IDs' internal product ID}): {error's message if error is an error, otherwise error as text}"
      • operation: "derive customer product is_custom"
  If anything fails, ignore it.

“Is this customer product a customized version of the plan it points at? Diffs the customer's own plan against the catalog version its `internal_product_id` references — never taken from request input. Reuses `diffPlanV1`, the same diff the catalog and migration-draft builders run on, so licenses, per-currency pricing and item identity are compared exactly once in the codebase. Notably `pricesEqual` treats an added or removed catalog currency as compatible and only flags a shared currency whose amount moved — so offering a plan in a new currency never marks the customers already on it as custom. `includeAdds` is on: an item or license the customer has and the plan does not is a divergence, not a lifecycle event. Biased towards `true`. A false positive only means the customer is skipped by version migrations; a false negative lets a migration overwrite genuinely customized prices, entitlements and license terms.”
To derive customer product is custom — given customer product, base product, and features; gives back true/false:
  “RevenueCat purchases carry no params and can't be customised, so any diff is catalog drift.”
  If the processor type of customer product is processor type's revenue cat, give back whether false.
  “Cannot prove it matches the catalog, so assume it does not.”
  If base product is missing, give back whether true.
  Try the following:
    Diff plan v1, and call the result diff:
      • from: the API plan v1 sync of base product (given features)
      • to: the API plan v1 sync of the product of customer product (given features)
      • include adds
    Give back whether custom diff keys has a key where diff's entry for key is set.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Report derivation failure (customer product and error).
    Give back whether true.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/compute/computeSchedulePhaseReplacements.ts
“Two customer products share a schedule slot when one can stand in for the other on the customer: same entity scope, same group, add-ons keyed on their own product so they never absorb a main plan's slot. Timing is part of the slot — a plan starting now never stands in for one a future phase is waiting on, so retiring that future plan drops its phase instead of rewriting it.”
To schedule slot key — given customer product:
  Give back a list of joined with ":":
    • customer product's internal entity ID, or "customer" if that's missing
    • customer product's product's group, or "" if that's missing

      • if not: "main"
    • "scheduled" if customer product's status is customer product status's scheduled, otherwise "current"

  Let successors by slot be an empty lookup table.
  For each inserted in Autumn billing plan's insert customer products:
    Schedule slot key (inserted), and call the result slot.
    If slot is not in successors by slot, record inserted under slot in successors by slot.
  Give back successors by slot.

“Schedule phases store raw customer product ids, so any plan that replaces a product has to hand its phases the successor. Expiring without a successor is left alone — the row still resolves, so the phase keeps its history; a deleted row leaves nothing to point at and is dropped from the phase.”
To compute schedule phase replacements — given Autumn billing plan; gives back a NonNullable:
  Get expired updated customer products (Autumn billing plan), and call the result expired customer products.
  Get delete customer products (Autumn billing plan), and call the result deleted customer products.
  If the number of expired customer products plus the number of deleted customer products is 0, give back an empty list.
  Find successors by slot (Autumn billing plan) → successors by slot.
  Let seen customer product IDs be an empty set.
  Let replacements be an empty list.
  To add replacement — given retired and drop without successor:
    If retired's ID is in seen customer product IDs, stop here.
    Let successor be successors by slot's entry for schedule slot key (retired).
    If successor is missing and drop without successor is false, stop here.
    Add retired's ID to seen customer product IDs.
    Add an object with to replacements:
      • old customer product ID: retired's ID
      • new customer product ID: successor's ID, or nothing if that's missing
      • internal customer ID: retired's internal customer ID
      • internal entity ID: retired's internal entity ID
  For each deleted in deleted customer products:
    Add replacement (retired: deleted and drop without successor).
  For each expired in expired customer products:
    Add replacement (retired: expired and no drop without successor).
  Give back replacements.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/compute/finalize/computeRefundPlan.ts

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/compute/finalize/finalizeLineItems.ts
“Finalizes line items for a billing plan by: 1. If custom line items are provided, overrides computed line items entirely 2. Filtering line items based on trial state transitions 3. Filtering out unchanged prices (refund + charge pairs that cancel out) 4. Adding line items for sibling products affected by trial state changes 5. Applying Stripe discounts to line items”
To finalize line items — given line items, billing context, Autumn billing plan, custom line items, and resets like Stripe under none (default false); gives back a list of LineItem:
  If billing context skip billing changes, give back an empty list.
  “"none" skips prorated charges: mid-cycle changes on a subscription, the stub before a new subscription's anchor, or a new subscription's backdated cycles.”
  Let has prorated period mean any of these is true:
    • billing context's Stripe subscription is set
    • the new subscription anchor ms of billing context is set
    • billing context is new subscription backdate
  Let skips proration mean billing context's requested proration behavior is "none" and has prorated period.
  Let resets cycle now be depending on whether resets like Stripe under none is true:
    • if so: whether billing context's requested billing cycle anchor is "now"
    • if not: billing context's anchor reset refund's no partial refund
  If skips proration is true and resets cycle now is false:
    “set_plans only: usage of a plan no subscription billed is still owed under none.”
    Let unbilled usage be depending on whether billing context is set plans:
      • if so: the line items that pass is usage no subscription billed
      • if not: an empty list
    If unbilled usage is empty, give back an empty list.
    Set line items to unbilled usage.
  Let billed line items be depending on whether skips proration is true and resets like Stripe under none is true:
    • if so: drop unchanged subscription item charges:
      • billing context
      • line items: line items, keeping only those whose context's direction is "charge" or context's billing timing is "in_arrear"
    • if not: line items
  “0. If custom line items provided, override computed line items entirely”
  If custom line items is not empty:
    Set Autumn billing plan's custom line items to custom line items.
    Give back an empty list.
  “1. Filter line items based on trial state transitions”
  Filter line items for trial transition (line items: billed line items and billing context), and call the result finalized line items.
  “2. Filter out unchanged prices (refund + charge pairs that cancel out)”
  Filter unchanged prices from line items (line items: finalized line items), and put the result in finalized line items.
  Set finalized line items to prorate bill difference credits (line items: finalized line items and billing context).
  “3. Add line items for sibling products affected by trial state changes”
  Build shared subscription trial line items (billing context and Autumn billing plan), and call the result shared trial line items.
  Set finalized line items to finalized line items, plus shared trial line items.
  “4. Apply Stripe discounts if present”
  If billing context's Stripe discounts is not empty:
    Apply Stripe discounts to line items, and put the result in finalized line items:
      • line items: finalized line items
      • discounts: billing context's Stripe discounts
      • options: an object with disable discountable for fresh discounts: true
  Give back finalized line items.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/compute/finalize/prorateBillDifferenceCredits.ts
To sum by — given line items and value:
  Give back line items combined into one value, starting from 0; for each line item (with the running total total):
    • the running total becomes total plus a value (line item), or 0 if that's missing

Line quantity — given line item:
  Give back line item's paid quantity, or line item's total quantity if that's missing.

By direction — given line items:
  Give back an object with:
    • refunds: line items, keeping only those where li's context's direction is "refund"
    • charges: line items, keeping only those where li's context's direction is "charge"

Has quantities? — given line items:
  Give back whether every line item in line items satisfies: a line quantity (line item) is set.

“Removal is judged by quantity, since stored credits may already be discounted.”
Price is removal — given line items:
  From a by direction (line items), take refunds and charges.
  If refunds is empty, give back whether false.
  If charges is empty, give back whether true.
  If line items has no quantities:
    Give back whether sum by (line items and value: a function of li giving back li's amount) is negative.
  Give back sum by (line items: charges and value: line quantity)'s less than (sum by (line items: refunds and value: line quantity)).

Customer product ID — given line item:
  Give back line item's context's customer product's ID.

“A changed quantity on a new customer product replaces the old quantity whole, so only the old product's credit is prorated; an in-place change bills just the difference.”
Price quantity is replaced — given line items:
  From a by direction (line items), take refunds and charges.
  If refunds is empty or charges is empty, give back whether false.
  If line items has no quantities, give back whether false.
  Let charged product IDs be the unique values of charges, each passed through customer product ID.
  Let moved product mean every refund in refunds satisfies: a customer product ID (refund) is not in charged product IDs.
  Let quantity changed mean sum by (line items: charges and value: line quantity) is not sum by (line items: refunds and value: line quantity).
  Give back whether moved product is true and quantity changed is true.

Credited line items — given line items and replaces quantity on relist:
  If replaces quantity on relist is true and price quantity is replaced (given line items):
    Give back a by direction (line items)'s refunds.
  Give back line items if price is removal (given line items), otherwise an empty list.

Prorate → now — given line item and now; gives back a LineItem:
  Let period be line item's context's billing period.
  If period is missing or period's end is at most period's start, give back line item.
  Let fraction be the larger of period's end minus now and 0 divided by period's end minus period's start.
  To scale — given amount:
    Give back fraction times amount.
  Give back line item, but with:
    • amount set to scale (line item's amount)
    • amount after discounts set to scale (line item's amount after discounts)

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/common/errors/handleExternalPSPErrors.ts
“Validates that we're not trying to modify (or attach alongside) a customer product managed by an external PSP like RevenueCat. For `update`: validates the specific cusProduct being modified. For `attach`: scans the customer's existing products. Throws if any RECURRING product is managed by a non-Stripe processor — UNLESS the product being attached is itself a true one-off (no recurring prices). One-off cross-processor purchases (in either direction) are safe: they create a parallel cus_product, never spin up or reuse a recurring Stripe subscription, and so cannot conflict with the existing external subscription. Concretely: - external recurring + attaching anything → throw (would create / mutate a Stripe sub that coexists or collides with the external sub). - external recurring + attaching one-off  → bypass (parallel one-off only). - external one-off only + attaching anything → bypass (no external sub exists to conflict with).”
To handle external psp errors — given customer product, customer products, attach product, action, cancel action, no billing changes, intent, and has field updates:
  If action is "update":
    If customer product is missing, stop here.
    “Autumn-only cancel: no Stripe write happens, so it cannot conflict with the external subscription. Intent must be CancelAction and no other mutation may ride along; uncancel is excluded because RC would remain canceled while Autumn reactivates.”
    Let is Autumn only cancel mean all of these are true:
      • intent is update subscription intent's cancel action
      • cancel action is set
      • cancel action is not "uncancel"
      • no billing changes is true
      • has no field updates
    If is Autumn only cancel, stop here.
    Let processor type be the processor type of customer product.
    If processor type is processor type's revenue cat:
      Fail with an error: "Subscription for '{customer product's product's name}' is managed by RevenueCat and cannot be updated directly" (status 409).
    Stop here.
  “action === "attach"”
  If customer products is missing or customer products is empty, stop here.
  “Safe path: a true one-off attach (no recurring prices) can mix across processors. One-offs create a parallel cus_product and never spin up a recurring Stripe subscription, so a customer with an active RC sub can still buy a Stripe-billed top-up. Recurring add-ons take the strict path.”
  If attach product is set and attach product is one off, stop here.
  “Only block on EXTERNAL RECURRING products. External one-off-only products (e.g. a previously-purchased RC one-off pack) don't have a recurring subscription and so can't conflict with the new Stripe attach.”
  Let conflicting external customer product be the first customer product in customer products that passes this check:
    Let is external mean the processor type of customer product is not processor type's Stripe.
    If is not external, give back whether false.
    Give back whether customer product is not customer product one off.
  If conflicting external customer product is set:
    Fail with an error: "Cannot attach because the customer's current product '{conflicting external customer product's product's name}' is managed by RevenueCat." (status 409).

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/actions/verify/evaluate/evaluateCancelState.ts

    • schedule's status is "completed"
    • schedule's status is "canceled"
  then:
    Give back inactive.

    Let last phase be the last of schedule's phases.
    Let current phase be schedule's current phase.
    If current phase is set and current phase's start date is last phase's start date, give back inactive.

      2. Keep only those where start date is after now seconds
    • end behavior: schedule's end behavior
    • ends at seconds: schedule's phases' entry for the number of schedule's phases minus 1's end date
    • quantity only: whether schedule is quantity only

“Evaluates cancel/schedule state on a subscription against the classified scenario.”

  Let ignores quantity only be an org ignores verify rule (org ID and rule: ignored verify rules' quantity only schedule).

      Give back nothing.
    • If it is "simple_cancel":

        • schedule state's end behavior is "cancel"
        • schedule state's upcoming phase starts is empty
        • any of these is true:
          • cancel at seconds is missing
          • all of these are true:
            • schedule state's ends at seconds is set
            • schedule state's ends at seconds cancels at same time (given expected seconds: cancel at seconds)
      If schedule implements cancel is set, give back nothing.
      Let cancel at implements cancel mean all of these are true:
        • schedule state's upcoming phase starts is empty
        • subscription's cancel at is set
        • cancel at seconds is set
        • subscription's cancel at cancels at same time (given expected seconds: cancel at seconds)
      If cancel at implements cancel is true, give back nothing.
      If schedule state's schedule active is true:
        If all of these are true:
          • schedule state's upcoming phase starts is not empty
          • schedule state's quantity only is false or ignores quantity only is false
        then:
          Give back an object with:
            • type: "schedule_mismatch"
            • reason: "unexpected_schedule"

        Give back an object with:
          • type: "cancel_state_mismatch"
          • expected canceling: true
          • actual canceling: actual canceling
      If subscription's cancel at is missing:
        Give back an object with:
          • type: "cancel_state_mismatch"
          • expected canceling: true
          • actual canceling: actual canceling
      If all of these are true:
        • cancel at seconds is set
        • subscription's cancel at does not cancel at same time (given expected seconds: cancel at seconds)
      then:
        Give back an object with:
          • type: "cancel_state_mismatch"
          • expected canceling: true
          • actual canceling: true
      Give back nothing.
    • If it is "multi_phase":
      “Schedule presence for multi_phase is evaluated by evaluateSchedulePhases, which reports a schedule_mismatch rather than a cancel-state mismatch.”
      Give back nothing.

“Finds the actual candidate that corresponds to an expected phase item, without reusing a candidate another expected item already claimed. Tier 1 (both kinds): exact `autumn_customer_price_id` metadata match — no shape/amount check, since a mismatched amount is a real discrepancy we want to report, not a reason to fail to find the item in the first place. Tier 2 (fallback, only when metadata identity is absent or stale): - Inline: match by `autumn_price_id` metadata + price-shape equality (`stripeInlinePriceMatchesStripePrice`). A candidate already tagged with some OTHER currently-valid inline cusPriceId is excluded — but a stale tag (pointing at a cusPrice that no longer exists on this customer) does not block the match. - Stored: every known Stripe price id for the Autumn price (`findSubscriptionItemForAutumnPrice`/`findPhaseItemForAutumnPrice`, via `getStripePriceIdsForAutumnPrice`) — covers a V1/V2 companion id swap. Tier 3 (stored fixed/prepaid, non-strict only): same-shape licensed item under one of the plan's Stripe product ids (`findShapeFallbackIndex`) — covers imported subs billing their own historical price ids.”

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/actions/verify/evaluate/evaluateRewards.ts

    Otherwise:
      Give back nothing.

  If missing reward IDs is empty and unexpected reward IDs is empty, give back nothing.
  Give back an object with:
    • type: "reward_mismatch"
    • missing reward IDs: missing reward IDs
    • unexpected reward IDs: unexpected reward IDs

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/actions/verify/evaluate/evaluateSchedulePhases.ts

    • if not: subscription's schedule's ID

  Let mismatches be an empty list.

  “One expected phase claims one actual phase, so a genuine extra phase can't hide behind a sibling that already matched within the day tolerance.”

        • if not: a similar unix:
          • unix1: expected start seconds times 1000
          • unix2: phase's start date times 1000

        • reason: "billing_cycle_anchor_mismatch"

  Give back mismatches.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/actions/verify/compute/buildStoredPriceCatalog.ts

Type CusPriceCatalog: a map of text to object.

“Maps every known Stripe price id for a customer's prices (a price can have both a V1 `stripe_price_id` and a V2 `stripe_prepaid_price_v2_id` companion) back to the originating Autumn price + product + customer_price id(s), so a stored item whose id has drifted from whichever id `buildStripePhasesUpdate` picked can still be resolved — either by its `autumn_customer_price_id` metadata (if present) or by checking every known id for that price.”

        • customer product
        • customer entitlements: customer product's customer entitlements

        Let existing be catalog's entry for Stripe price ID.
        If existing is set:
          Add customer price's ID to existing's customer price IDs.
          Move on to the next one.
        Record an object with under Stripe price ID in catalog:
          • price: customer price's price
          • product: customer product's product
          • customer price IDs: the unique values of a list of customer price's ID
          • entitlement: customer entitlement's entitlement
          • customer entitlement: customer entitlement, or nothing if that's missing
  Give back catalog.

  Give back catalog.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/actions/updateSubscription/setup/setupUpdateSubscriptionTrialContext.ts
“Sets up trial context for update subscription operations. Logic: 1. If a free_trial param passed (customize.free_trial or the shorthand) → Use it (null removes trial, value sets fresh trial) 2. If revert trial → Inherit from customer product (its subscription belongs to the paused plan) 3. If Autumn-managed no-card trial (on_trial_end "bill", no Stripe sub) → keep it Autumn-managed 4. If paid product with trialing subscription → Inherit from subscription 5. If customer product is trialing (free product case) → Inherit from customer product 6. Otherwise → No trial context”
To setup update subscription trial context — given Stripe subscription, customer product, current epoch ms, params, and full product; gives back a TrialContext (or nothing):
  Let is revert trial mean customer product is customer product reverting trial.
  Let is Autumn managed trial mean customer product is customer product Autumn managed trial.
  “Handle explicit free_trial param (null or value), in either shape”
  Resolve free trial param (params) → free trial param.
  If free trial param is set:
    Handle free trial param, and call the result trial context:
      • free trial params: free trial param
      • Stripe subscription
      • customer product
      • full product
      • current epoch ms
    If trial context is set and is revert trial:
      Give back trial context, but with on end set to trial context's on end, or "revert" if that's missing.
    “A changed no-card trial stays Autumn's; removing it or requiring a card moves it to Stripe.”
    Let stays Autumn managed mean all of these are true:
      • is Autumn managed trial
      • trial context's card required is missing
      • trial context's trial ends at is set
    If trial context is set and stays Autumn managed is true, give back trial context, but with Autumn managed set to true.
    Give back trial context.
  If customer product is set and is revert trial:
    Give back an inherit trial from customer product (customer product and current epoch ms).
  If all of these are true:
    • customer product is set
    • is Autumn managed trial
    • customer product is customer product trialing (given now ms: current epoch ms)
  then:
    Give back an object with:
      • free trial: customer product's free trial
      • trial ends at: customer product's trial ends at, or nothing if that's missing
      • applies to billing: true
      • card required: false
      • on end: customer product's on trial end, or nothing if that's missing
      • Autumn managed: true
  “Inherit from stripe subscription (paid product case)”
  If full product is product paid and recurring:
    If Stripe subscription is set and Stripe subscription is Stripe subscription trialing:
      Give back an inherit trial from subscription (Stripe subscription).
    Give back nothing.
  “Inherit from customer product (free product case)”
  If customer product is set, give back an inherit trial from customer product (customer product and current epoch ms).
  Give back nothing.

          • if not: "none"

          • if so: "noPartialRefund: {billing context's anchor reset refund's no partial refund} | refundCycle: {depending on whether billing context's anchor reset refund's refund cycle is set}"
          • if not: "none"

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/actions/updateSubscription/errors/handleOneOffErrors.ts
“Block non-ManualTopUp paths from mutating an existing one-off prepaid item's quantity. First-time set-balance (no existing options entry) and carry-through (quantity unchanged) are both allowed; only true quantity changes are rejected.”
To block one off quantity change outside manual top up — given billing context and params:
  From billing context, take customer product.
  Let feature quantities be params' feature quantities.
  If feature quantities is empty, stop here.
  For each fq in feature quantities:
    “Tie-break aware: only guard features whose prepaid quantity actually resolves to a one-off price — a recurring prepaid sibling wins instead.”
    Find prepaid quantity target price → target price:
      • prices: the prices of customer product's customer prices
      • feature ID: fq's feature ID
    Skip it if target price is missing or target price is not one off price.
    Let one off prepaid price be target price.
    Let current option be the first o in customer product's options where o's feature ID is fq's feature ID.
    Skip it if current option is missing.
    Let matching customer entitlement be the first ce in customer product's customer entitlements where ce's entitlement's feature's ID is fq's feature ID.
    Let allowance be matching customer entitlement's entitlement's allowance, or 0 if that's missing.
    Let billing units be one off prepaid price's config's billing units, or 1 if that's missing.
    Let requested units be fq's quantity, or 0 if that's missing.
    Let units excluding allowance be the larger of 0 and requested units minus allowance.
    Round usage to nearest billing unit (usage: units excluding allowance and billing units), and call the result rounded units.
    Let requested packs be rounded units divided by billing units.
    Let current packs be current option's quantity, or 0 if that's missing.
    If requested packs is not current packs:
      Fail with an error: complex update error [error code's invalid request] (status 400).

To handle one off errors — given billing context, Autumn billing plan, and params:
  From billing context, take customer product.
  “ManualTopUp is a legit one-off mutation; its own strict-shape gate (handleManualTopUpErrors) owns rejecting non-conforming requests.”
  If billing context's intent is update subscription intent's manual top up, stop here.
  “UpdatePlan combined with a one-off feature_quantity change is allowed: the custom-plan flow creates a new cusProduct billed for the requested quantity, and the one-off carryover helper preserves the existing balance.”
  If billing context's intent is not update subscription intent's update plan:
    Block one off quantity change outside manual top up (billing context and params).
  “Only apply these checks to one-off products”
  If customer product is not customer product one off, stop here.
  “1. Check that free trial param isn't passed in”
  Resolve free trial param (params), and call the result free trial.
  If free trial is set, fail with an error: "Free trials are not available for one-off products" (status 400).
  Let new customer product be the first of Autumn billing plan's insert customer products.
  If new customer product is missing, stop here.
  Let current full product be the product of customer product.
  Let new full product be the product of new customer product.
  From a products are same, take only entitlements changed:
    • current product v1: current full product
    • new product v1: new full product
    • features: the features
  If only entitlements changed is missing:
    Fail with an error: "For one-off products, only entitlement changes are allowed; price and billing changes are not supported" (status 400).

“Don't allow removing a trial from a paid recurring product when adding one-off items”
To check trial removal with one off items — given billing context and Autumn billing plan:
  Let is paid recurring mean billing context's customer product is customer product paid recurring.
  If is not paid recurring, stop here.
  Get trial state transition (billing context), and take its is trialing and will be trialing.
  If is not trialing or will be trialing, stop here.
  Let new customer products be Autumn billing plan's insert customer products.
  Let new prices be the prices of each customer product in new customer products, combined into one list.
  Let new has one off prices mean at least one of new prices passes is one off price.
  If new has one off prices is true:
    Fail with an error: "Cannot remove the free trial while adding one-off items to a paid recurring subscription" (status 400).

Let complex update error be "Cannot update a one-off prepaid quantity alongside other subscription changes. Update the plan first, then adjust the quantity separately.".

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/actions/updateSubscription/errors/handleUpdateSubscriptionLicenseErrors.ts
To throw invalid request — given message:
  Fail with an error: message [error code's invalid request] (status 400).

“Pool-in-place quantity moves: every entry must target an existing pool and may not shrink it below its live assignments.”
To handle license quantity errors — given billing context and params:
  Let pools be billing context's customer product's customer licenses.
  For each license quantity in params' license quantities:
    Let pool be the first candidate in pools where candidate's plan license's product's ID is license quantity's license plan ID.
    If pool is missing:
      Throw invalid request, and give back the result:
        • "Customer has no license pool for {license quantity's license plan ID} on this plan."
    Let used be the usage of pool.
    If license quantity's quantity is less than used:
      Throw invalid request:
        • "license_quantities for {license quantity's license plan ID} is below its {used} active assignments. Release licenses first."

“Plan restructures replace the customer product; until license transitions execute on updates, pools may only ride when nothing would strand.”
To handle update plan license errors — given billing context and params:
  From billing context, take customer product, patch context, and full products.
  Let pools be customer product's customer licenses.
  Let offered license plan IDs be the unique values of each link's product's ID, for each link in the first of full products' licenses.
  For each license quantity in params' license quantities:
    If license quantity's license plan ID is not in offered license plan IDs:
      Throw invalid request ("Plan does not offer license {license quantity's license plan ID}.").
  If pools is empty, stop here.
  If patch context's mode is "new":
    Throw invalid request:
      • "Version-changing item customize is not supported on license-backed plans yet."
  “Expire+insert transitions carry pools across rows, but only for licenses the incoming plan still offers — a dropped license with assigned seats would strand them.”
  If patch context is missing:
    For each pool in pools:
      Let license plan ID be pool's plan license's product's ID.
      Let used be the usage of pool.
      Skip it if used is 0 or license plan ID is missing.
      Skip it if license plan ID is in offered license plan IDs.
      Throw invalid request:
        • "License changes conflict with active license assignments: {used} assigned for {license plan ID}, but the incoming plan drops the license. Release licenses first."

To handle update subscription license errors — given billing context and params:
  Let touches license params mean params' license quantities is set or params' customize's upsert licenses is set.
  If all of these are true:
    • touches license params is true
    • billing context's customer product's status is customer product status's scheduled
  then:
    Throw invalid request ("License changes are not supported on scheduled plans.").
  If all of these are true:
    • billing context's intent is update subscription intent's update quantity
    • params' license quantities is not empty
  then:
    Handle license quantity errors (billing context and params).
  If billing context's intent is update subscription intent's update plan:
    Handle update plan license errors (billing context and params).

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/actions/sync/sync.ts
To sync — given params (async):
  From context, take org and env.
  “1. Load full customer”
  Get full [CusService], and call the result full customer:
    • ID or internal ID: params' customer ID
    • with subscriptions
    • with entities
  Let Stripe customer ID be full customer's processor's ID.
  If Stripe customer ID is missing:
    Fail with an error: "This customer has no linked Stripe customer ID. Set the customer's Stripe ID, then resync." [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
  Create Stripe client (org and env) → Stripe client.
  Let results be an empty list.
  “2. Process each mapping”
  For each mapping in params' mappings:
    Try the following:
      “Refresh full customer after each mapping so subsequent mappings see updates”
      Get full [CusService], and put the result in full customer:
        • ID or internal ID: params' customer ID
        • with subscriptions
        • with entities
      Process sync mapping (Stripe client, full customer, and mapping).
      Add an object with plan ID: mapping's plan ID and success: true to results.
    If anything fails (call the problem error):
      Let message be error's message if error is an error, otherwise "Unknown error".
      Log an error "billing.sync mapping failed for {mapping's plan ID}: {error}".
      Add an object with plan ID: mapping's plan ID, success: false, and error: message to results.
  “3. Clear customer cache”
  Delete cached full customer (customer ID: params' customer ID and source: "billing.sync").
  Give back an object with results.

To process sync mapping — given Stripe client, full customer, and mapping (async):
  From context, take org and env.
  “1. Retrieve the Stripe subscription”
  Retrieve Stripe client's subscriptions (mapping's Stripe subscription ID and expand: a list of "items.data"), and call the result Stripe subscription.
  “2. Load the target Autumn product”
  Get full [ProductService] (ID or internal ID: mapping's plan ID, org ID: org's ID, and env), and call the result full product.
  “3. Apply custom items if provided”
  Start with no customize plan yet.
  If mapping's items is set and mapping's items is not empty, set customize plan to the customize plan v1 of mapping's items.
  Setup custom full product (current full product: full product and customize plan), and take its full product (as final product), custom prices, and custom entitlements.
  “3.5 Skip if this subscription is already linked to an active instance of this product — avoids double-attaching when auto-sync got there first. expire_previous: true means the caller intends to expire-and-replace it (the V0 repair flow), so only the no-op dedup case skips here.”
  Let already linked be the first customer product in filter customer products by Stripe subscription ID where all of these are true:
    • customer products: full customer's customer products
    • Stripe subscription ID: mapping's Stripe subscription ID
    • customer product's product ID is final product's ID
    • customer product's status is in active statuses
  If already linked is set and mapping's expire previous is missing, stop here.
  “4. Find transition context (current cusProduct to expire)”
  Setup attach transition context (full customer and attach product: final product), and take its current customer product.
  “5. Build init context from Stripe subscription state”
  Let current epoch ms be the current time.
  Get trial ends at from Stripe (Stripe subscription), and call the result trial ends at.
  Get cancel fields from Stripe (Stripe subscription), and take its canceled at and ended at.
  Let reset cycle anchor ms be the ms of Stripe subscription's billing cycle anchor.
  “Init prepaid feature quantities”
  Let feature quantities be an empty list.
  For each price in final product's prices:
    Skip it if price is not prepaid.
    Find feature by ID or internal ID, and call the result feature:
      • features: the features
      • feature ID or internal ID: price's config's feature ID
    Skip it if feature is missing.
    Let prepaid feature option be the first feature option in mapping's prepaid feature options where any of these is true:
      • feature option's feature ID is feature's ID
      • feature option's internal feature ID is feature's internal ID
    Add an object with to feature quantities:
      • feature ID: feature's ID
      • internal feature ID: feature's internal ID
      • quantity: prepaid feature option's quantity, or 0 if that's missing
      • upcoming quantity: prepaid feature option's upcoming quantity
      • adjustable quantity: prepaid feature option's adjustable quantity
  “6. Init the new customer product”
  Init full customer product, and call the result new customer product:
    • init context: an object with:
      • full customer
      • full product: final product
      • feature quantities
      • reset cycle anchor: reset cycle anchor ms
      • now: current epoch ms
      • free trial: nothing
      • trial ends at
    • init options: an object with:
      • subscription ID: Stripe subscription's ID
      • canceled at
      • ended at
      • starts at: the ms of Stripe subscription's start date if Stripe subscription's start date is set (otherwise nothing)
      • keep subscription IDs: true
      • status: the Autumn status of Stripe subscription's status
  “7. Build the Autumn billing plan”
  Let Autumn billing plan be an object with:
    • customer ID: full customer's ID
    • insert customer products: a list of new customer product
    • custom prices: custom prices if custom prices is not empty (otherwise nothing)
    • custom entitlements: custom entitlements if custom entitlements is not empty (otherwise nothing)
    • update customer product: (only if mapping's expire previous is set and current customer product is set) an object with:
      • customer product: current customer product
      • updates: an object with:
        • status: customer product status's expired
        • ended at: current epoch ms
        • canceled: true
        • canceled at: current epoch ms
    • upsert subscriptions: a list of init subscription from Stripe (Stripe subscription)
  “8. Execute (DB only — no Stripe changes)”
  Execute Autumn billing plan (Autumn billing plan).

    Clear lock (lock key).

  Give back result.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/actions/sync/scope/buildIncrementalSyncParams.ts
Type IncrementalSyncSkipReason: one of "no_current_phase", "unsupported_phase_shape", "unsupported_target", "ambiguous_linked_targets", or "no_changed_targets".
Type IncrementalSyncParamsResult: an object or an object.

Current phase — given match:
  Give back the first phase in match's phase matches where phase is current, or nothing if that's missing.

  Give back linked customer products, keeping only the linked products that pass this check:
    If linked product is not customer product add on, give back whether false.
    If linked product's product's ID is not sync plan's plan ID, give back whether false.
    If sync plan's entity ID is set:
      Give back whether linked product's internal entity ID is sync plan's entity ID.
    Otherwise:
      Give back whether linked product's internal entity ID is missing.

“Current API-side prepaid totals (packs × billing_units + allowance).”
Linked prepaid feature totals — given linked product and matched plan; gives back a map of text to number:
  Let totals be an empty lookup table.
  For each price in matched plan's product's prices:
    Skip it if price is not prepaid.
    Let entitlement be the entitlement of price (given entitlements: matched plan's product's entitlements).
    Skip it if entitlement is missing.
    Let option be the first o in linked product's options where o's feature ID is entitlement's feature's ID.
    Let packs be option's quantity, or 0 if that's missing.
    Let billing units be price's config's billing units, or 1 if that's missing.
    Let allowance be entitlement's allowance, or 0 if that's missing.
    Record packs times billing units plus allowance under entitlement's feature's ID in totals.
  Give back totals.

Prepaid quantities drifted — given linked product, matched plan, and sync plan; gives back true/false:
  Let current totals be linked prepaid feature totals (linked product and matched plan).
  If current totals' size is 0, give back whether false.
  For each feature ID and current total in current totals:
    Let desired be the first fq in sync plan's feature quantities where fq's feature ID is feature ID.
    If desired's quantity, or 0 if that's missing is not current total, give back whether true.
  Give back whether false.

To build incremental sync params — given match, params, and linked customer products; gives back an IncrementalSyncParamsResult:
  Let phase match be a current phase (match).
  If phase match is missing, give back an object with should sync: false and reason: "no_current_phase".
  Let phases be params' phases.
  Let phase be the first phase in phases where phase's starts at is "now", or the first of phases if the number of phases is 1 (otherwise nothing) if that's missing.
  If phase is missing or the number of phase's plans is not the number of phase match's plans:
    Give back an object with should sync: false and reason: "unsupported_phase_shape".
  Let linked targets be the target group map of linked customer products.
  If linked targets' ok is missing, give back an object with should sync: false and reason: "ambiguous_linked_targets".
  Let matched plan map be a matched plans by product ID (matched plans: phase match's plans).
  If matched plan map's ok is missing, give back an object with should sync: false and reason: "unsupported_target".
  Let changed plans be an empty list.
  For each sync plan in phase's plans:
    Let matched plan be matched plan map's plans by product ID's entry for sync plan's plan ID.
    If matched plan is missing, give back an object with should sync: false and reason: "unsupported_target".
    “Add-ons: syncPlan.quantity is the plan-INSTANCE count (rollup derives it from the base item's Stripe quantity, never from prepaid items — prepaid pack counts live in syncPlan.feature_quantities instead).”
    If matched plan's product is add on:
      Let linked instances be linked add on instances (linked customer products and sync plan).
      Let desired quantity be sync plan's quantity, or 1 if that's missing.
      If the number of linked instances is less than desired quantity:
        “Fewer instances linked than Stripe shows — attach only the missing ones; expire_previous: false so existing instances survive.”
        Add sync plan, but with to changed plans:
          • quantity set to desired quantity minus the number of linked instances
          • expire previous set to false
        Move on to the next one.
      “Same instance count but prepaid packs drifted — push the syncPlan unmodified (expire_previous: true) so syncV2 expire+replaces with usage carry.”
      Let drifted instance be the first linked product in linked instances where there is a prepaid quantities drifted (linked product, matched plan, and sync plan).
      If drifted instance is set, add an object with everything in sync plan to changed plans.
      Move on to the next one.
    “Main plans re-sync only when the linked target's product id changed (upgrade/downgrade); prepaid drift is not checked for them here.”
    Let target be the target group link of matched plan (given sync plan).
    If target is missing, give back an object with should sync: false and reason: "unsupported_target".
    Let linked product be linked targets' targets' entry for target's key.
    Let version changed mean sync plan's version is set and linked product's product's version is not sync plan's version.
    If any of these is true:
      • linked product is missing
      • linked product's product's ID is not target's product ID
      • version changed is true
    then:
      Add sync plan to changed plans.
      Move on to the next one.
    “Same product still attached — seat quantity changes converge the pool in place instead of re-attaching the parent.”
    Find license quantity drifts (linked customer product: linked product and sync plan) → license quantity drifts.
    If license quantity drifts is not empty, add sync plan to changed plans.
  “Linked add-ons whose Stripe items disappeared from the sub get expired. Removal of MAIN linked products may get the same handling in the future. An unmatched item_diff means detection failed to classify something still on the subscription (e.g. the tiered-prepaid enrichment gap) — that's a detection miss, not proof of removal, so skip expiring anything this phase to avoid dropping a live entitlement.”
  Let has unmatched items mean phase match's item diffs has a diff where diff's match's kind is "none".
  Let matched plan IDs be the unique values of each matched plan's product's ID, for each matched plan in phase match's plans.
  Let removed customer products be depending on whether has unmatched items:
    • if so: an empty list
    • if not: linked customer products, keeping only those where all of these are true:
      • linked product is customer product add on
      • linked product's product's ID is not in matched plan IDs
  If changed plans is empty and removed customer products is empty:
    Give back an object with should sync: false and reason: "no_changed_targets".
  Give back an object with:
    • should sync: true
    • params: params, but with phases set to a list of phase, but with plans set to changed plans if changed plans is not empty (otherwise nothing)
    • removed customer products

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/actions/sync/scope/stampEntityFromExistingLinks.ts
“Autumn's scheduled start is anchored, Stripe's phase start is not, so the two drift by minutes on the same phase.”
Let max phase start drift ms be 24 times 60 times 60 times 1000.

To find copies on phase — given customer products and starts at; gives back a list of FullCusProduct:
  “Past-due plans are still live, so they belong to the current phase too.”
  If starts at is "now":
    Give back customer products, keeping only those where customer product's status is in active statuses.
  Let scheduled be customer products, keeping only those where customer product's status is customer product status's scheduled.
  Let nearest start be the first of scheduled, after these steps:
    1. Take each one's starts at
    2. Keep only those where the absolute value of start minus starts at is at or before max phase start drift ms
    3. ␀them, sorted by this rule:
      • compare a and b by the absolute value of a minus starts at minus the absolute value of b minus starts at
  If nearest start is missing:
    Give back an empty list.
  Otherwise:
    Give back scheduled, keeping only those where customer product's starts at is nearest start.

“The entity every existing copy of this plan agrees on for this phase, or undefined when they disagree — a customer-level copy must never be dragged onto the entity of a differently scoped copy of the same plan.”
To find agreed entity ID — given customer products, plan ID, and starts at; gives back text (or nothing):
  Split find copies on phase into first and any other rest:
    • customer products: customer products, keeping only those where customer product's product's ID is plan ID
    • starts at
  If first's internal entity ID is missing, give back nothing.
  If every customer product in rest satisfies: customer product's internal entity ID is first's internal entity ID:
    Give back first's internal entity ID.
  Otherwise:
    Give back nothing.

“Detection is scope-blind: it matches Stripe prices to catalog products with no knowledge of the customer's existing customer products. When a product is already linked to this Stripe subscription via an entity-scoped customer product, re-syncing it without that binding would insert a duplicate at the customer level (and `expire_previous` would miss the entity-scoped original). Stamp the existing entity binding onto each matched plan so the sync re-attaches the product on the same entity and matches/expires the original.”
To stamp entity from existing links — given phases, subscription, and customer products; gives back a list of SyncPhase:
  If subscription is missing, give back phases.
  Filter customer products by Stripe subscription ID (customer products and Stripe subscription ID: subscription's ID), and call the result linked customer products.
  If linked customer products is empty, give back phases.
  Give back phases, with each phase turned into phase, but with:
    • plans set to phase's plans, with each plan turned into the result of:
      If plan's entity ID is set, give back plan.
      Find agreed entity ID → entity ID:
        • customer products: linked customer products
        • plan ID: plan's plan ID
        • starts at: phase's starts at
      Give back plan, but with entity ID set to entity ID if entity ID is set, otherwise plan.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/actions/sync/buildSyncParams/buildFeatureQuantities.ts
“Build feature_quantities for a MatchedPlan by walking the product's prepaid prices. Stripe stores the same Autumn prepaid price under TWO Stripe price ids with different quantity semantics: - `price.config.stripe_price_id` (V1): Stripe quantity counts EXTRAS only — allowance is implicit, not billed. We add `allowance` back so `paramsToFeatureOptions`'s allowance subtraction resolves to extras. - `price.config.stripe_prepaid_price_v2_id` (V2): Stripe quantity is TOTAL packs (allowance included). Pass through unchanged. Either way the emitted `quantity` is in feature units, which is what `paramsToFeatureOptions` expects. If a prepaid price is defined in Autumn but absent from Stripe, the helper emits `{ quantity: 0 }` so the synced cusProduct surfaces the feature with zero allowance.”
To build feature quantities — given matched plan and item diffs; gives back a list of FeatureQuantityParamsV0:
  Let result be an empty list.
  For each price in matched plan's product's prices:
    Skip it if price is not prepaid.
    Let entitlement be the entitlement of price (given entitlements: matched plan's product's entitlements).
    Skip it if entitlement is missing.
    Let matched feature be the first f in matched plan's features where f's Autumn price ID is price's ID.
    If matched feature is missing:
      Add an object with feature ID: entitlement's feature's ID and quantity: 0 to result.
      Move on to the next one.
    Let item diff be the first d in item diffs where d's Stripe's ID is matched feature's Stripe item ID.
    If item diff is missing:
      Add an object with feature ID: entitlement's feature's ID and quantity: 0 to result.
      Move on to the next one.
    Let billing units be price's config's billing units, or 1 if that's missing.
    Let allowance be entitlement's allowance, or 0 if that's missing.
    Let Stripe price ID on subscription be item diff's Stripe's Stripe price ID.
    “Stripe quantity counts EXTRAS only for the explicit V1 prepaid price id, where the allowance is implicit/unbilled and must be added back. For the V2 id — or any imported / Stripe-native price id on the sub — the quantity is the TOTAL (allowance-inclusive), so it passes through. Defaulting non-V1 ids to the "extras" branch folded Stripe's default `quantity: 1` into a phantom +1 credit on top of the allowance.”
    Let is v1 extras only mean all of these are true:
      • price's config's Stripe price ID is set
      • Stripe price ID on subscription is price's config's Stripe price ID
    Let Stripe quantity in units be item diff's Stripe's quantity times billing units.
    Let feature units be depending on whether is v1 extras only:
      • if so: Stripe quantity in units plus allowance
      • if not: Stripe quantity in units
    Add an object with to result:
      • feature ID: entitlement's feature's ID
      • quantity: feature units
      • Stripe price ID: Stripe price ID on subscription
  Give back result.

    Give back a requested matches granted (quantities: second's quantities and licenses: first's licenses).
  If first's type is "requested" and second's type is "granted":
    Give back a licenses match (first: second, second: first, and plan licenses).
  If first's type is "granted" and second's type is "includedOnly":
    Give back whether every one of first's licenses has paid quantity is 0.
  If first's type is "includedOnly" and second's type is "granted":
    Give back a licenses match (first: second, second: first, and plan licenses).
  If first's type is "requested" and second's type is "requested":
    Give back whether sorted quantities (first's quantities) is sorted quantities (second's quantities).
  If first's type is "requested" and second's type is "includedOnly":
    Give back a requested is included only (quantities: first's quantities and plan licenses).
  If first's type is "includedOnly" and second's type is "requested":
    Give back a licenses match (first: second, second: first, and plan licenses).
  Give back whether first's type is "includedOnly" and second's type is "includedOnly".

“The one equality set_plans uses: same plan version, quantities, licenses and items.”
Instance configs match — given features, first, and second:
  Let same plan version mean first's full product's internal ID is second's full product's internal ID.
  If same plan version is false, give back whether false.
  Let same scheduling shape mean all of these are true:
    • first's plan quantity is second's plan quantity
    • first's resets billing cycle is second's resets billing cycle
  Let same feature quantities be a feature options are same:
    • current feature options: first's feature quantities
    • new feature options: second's feature quantities
  If same scheduling shape is false or same feature quantities is missing, give back whether false.
  Let plan licenses be second's full product's licenses, or first's full product's licenses if that's missing.
  If there is no licenses match (first: first's licenses, second: second's licenses, and plan licenses):
    Give back whether false.
  From a products are same, take items same:
    • new product v1: second's full product
    • current product v1: first's full product
    • features
  Give back items same.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/actions/setPlans/setup/setupSetPlansPolicies.ts
“Live rows carry, with a requested trial patched onto them, unless the cycle resets now. A replacement for a paid-up subscription keeps plans' cycle unless a new paid plan or anchor restarts billing; a backdate keeps it unless it restarts the cycle.”
Live rows policy — given billing context; gives back SetPlansPolicies["liveRows"]:
  From billing context, take replaced Stripe subscription and requested billing cycle anchor.
  “Resetting the cycle now restarts every renewing plan's period, so kept plans are re-billed like changed ones.”
  If requested billing cycle anchor is "now", give back "recreateRenewing".
  If replaced Stripe subscription is missing, give back "carry".
  If billing context is backdate recreate:
    If there is a restarts cycle at backdated start (billing context):
      Give back "recreate".
    Otherwise:
      Give back "carry".
  Let continues paid up cycle mean all of these are true:
    • replaced Stripe subscription's status is "canceled"
    • requested billing cycle anchor is missing
  Give back "recreateWhenPaidRecurringStarts" if continues paid up cycle is true, otherwise "recreate".

To setup set plans policies — given billing context and params; gives back a SetPlansPolicies:
  Give back an object with:
    • undeclared: depending on whether there is a first phase starts in future (billing context):
      • if so: "end"
      • if not: params' undeclared plans, or "end" if that's missing
    • canceling: "keepCancellation"
    • past due: "continue"
    • live rows: a live rows policy (billing context)
    • unbilled rows: "carry" if billing context skip billing changes, otherwise "recreate"

  If preview is true, give back an object with source: an object with coupon: carried coupon.
  Give back an object with:
    • source: an object with:
      • coupon: create coupon copy (coupon: carried coupon and replaced Stripe subscription)

“A subscription's own discounts can't be reused on another one, so each moves as its coupon: forever as is, repeating for its remaining months; a once discount was already spent.”

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/actions/setPlans/setup/carryReplacedSubscription/remainingDiscountMonths.ts

  • week: "weeks"
  • month: "months"
  • year: "years"

  Give back add (billing cycle anchor ms and renewal's interval count times count) as a timestamp.

“The last renewal, from the period end on, inside the discount; each steps from the anchor so month ends don't drift.”

  Start with no last renewal yet.
  Start with let count = 0, then increase count by 1 each time:
    Let renewal ms be the renewal at billing cycle anchor ms, renewal, and count.
    If renewal ms is at least discount end ms, give back last renewal.
    If renewal ms is at least period end ms, set last renewal to renewal ms.

“Months a discount starting now must run to reach exactly the renewals the old one would have. Zero when the old discount ends before the next renewal.”

  Let last renewal be a last discounted renewal:
    • billing cycle anchor ms
    • period end ms
    • renewal
    • discount end ms
  If last renewal is missing, give back 0.
  Let months start as 1.
  Keep repeating while add months (current epoch ms and months) as a timestamp is at or before last renewal:
    Increase months by 1.
  Give back months.

##### server/src/internal/billing/v2/actions/setPlans/preview/diffPhaseBalances.ts
Type PhaseBalances: a lookup of text to AttributedBalance.

“One feature's change within a single scope; the caller adds the scope.”
Type PhaseBalanceDiff: a SetPlansPreviewBalanceChange.

Type BalanceBehavior: SetPlansPreviewBalanceChange["behavior"].
Type BalanceTransition: an object.

Let tracked fields be a list of:
  • "granted"
  • "remaining"
  • "usage"
  • "unlimited"
  • "next_reset_at"
  • "overage_allowed"

“A feature missing from a phase reads as an empty balance, so gaining or losing it diffs like any other change.”
To preview balance — given balance; gives back a SetPlansPreviewBalance:
  Give back an object with:
    • granted: balance's granted, or 0 if that's missing
    • remaining: balance's remaining, or 0 if that's missing
    • usage: balance's usage, or 0 if that's missing
    • unlimited: balance's unlimited, or false if that's missing
    • next reset at: balance's next reset at, or nothing if that's missing
    • overage allowed: balance's overage allowed, or false if that's missing

“Pay-per-use grants access with nothing granted: its usage is billed instead.”
Grants access? — given balance:
  Give back balance's unlimited, or whether balance's granted is positive if that's empty, or balance's overage allowed if that's empty.

“Nothing granted and nothing used on either side: there is no balance to report.”
Holds nothing? — given before and after:
  Give back whether all of these are true:
    • before does not grant access
    • after does not grant access
    • before's usage is 0
    • after's usage is 0

Gains access — given before and after:
  Give back whether before does not grant access and after grants access.

Loses access — given before and after:
  Give back whether before grants access and after does not grant access.

Clears usage? — given before and after:
  Give back whether before's usage is positive and after's usage is 0.

Keeps usage? — given before and after:
  Give back whether after's usage is positive and after's usage is before's usage.

Keeps allowance? — given before and after:
  Give back whether before's granted is after's granted and before's unlimited is after's unlimited.

“The same allowance starts over; a changed allowance is an update even when usage clears.”
Resets allowance? — given transition:
  Give back whether transition clears usage and transition keeps allowance.

“What was left survives as a fresh grant, as a one-off prepaid carry-over does.”
Keeps remaining? — given before and after:
  Give back whether all of these are true:
    • before clears usage (given after)
    • after's unlimited is missing
    • after's remaining is before's remaining

“First matching row wins: access changes outrank usage changes, which outrank a plain update.”
Let behavior table be a list of:
  • a list of "added" and gains access
  • a list of "removed" and loses access
  • a list of "carried" and keeps remaining
  • a list of "reset" and resets allowance

        • internal entity ID: context's entity's internal ID
    2. Pass each one through charged plan label
  If rebilled labels is empty, give back an empty list.
  Give back a list of:
    • an object with:
      • type: "cycle_reset_rebills_plans"
      • everything in a warning text:
