##### server/src/internal/analytics/actions/propertyRollupCompleteness.ts
“events_property_mv's insert-time gate drops high-entropy values (UUIDs, long hex, 32+ char opaque ids) so per-event-unique keys can't explode the rollup.”
Type EventTotals: a lookup of text to object.

“Sums are Float64 through two different aggregation paths, so exact equality would report phantom shortfalls on large values.”
Let relative tolerance be 1e-9.

Let absolute tolerance be 0.000001.

Is materially less than? — given value and reference; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether reference minus value is more than the larger of absolute tolerance and the absolute value of reference times relative tolerance.

To sum grouped rows by event name — given rows; gives back a lookup of text to number:
  Let sums be an empty object.
  For each row in rows:
    Set sums' entry for row's event name to sums' entry for row's event name, or 0 if that's missing plus row's total value.
  Give back sums.

To sum all rows — given rows; gives back a number:
  Give back the total total value across rows.

“Event counts can't cancel the way signed values can, but older deployments of the pipe don't return them, so every count check stays opt-in.”
To count rows by event name — given rows; gives back a lookup of text to number (or nothing):
  Let counts be an empty object.
  For each row in rows:
    If row's event count is missing, give back nothing.
    Set counts' entry for row's event name to counts' entry for row's event name, or 0 if that's missing plus row's event count.
  Give back counts.

“The gated rollup carries small historical seams (backfill boundaries) that exact coverage exposes. Recovering them means a raw-events scan over the whole window, which times out on long windows. A shortfall a reader could notice retries outright; a smaller one is judged by the value-aware totals check, which shares the rollup's seams and only fires on real loss.”
Let retry shortfall ratio be 0.005.

Let retry shortfall floor be 10,000.

“Events ingested between the grouped and coverage queries can put a few more events in the groups than in coverage; that is lag, not an empty coverage rollup.”
Let ingestion lag ratio be 0.0001.

Is within ingestion lag? — given difference and reference; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether difference is at most reference times ingestion lag ratio.

Type CoverageShortfall: one of "none", "minor", or "major".

Property rollup coverage shortfall — given rows and coverage; gives back a CoverageShortfall:
  Count rows by event name (rows), and call the result grouped counts.
  If grouped counts is missing, give back "none".
  Let worst start as "none".
  For each key event name and value property event count in coverage:
    Let shortfall be property event count minus grouped counts' entry for event name, or 0 if that's missing.
    Skip it if shortfall is zero or less.
    If any of these is true:
      • property event count is less than retry shortfall floor
      • shortfall divided by property event count is at least retry shortfall ratio
    then:
      Give back "major".
    Set worst to "minor".
  Give back worst.

“Value-only judgement for a minor count shortfall. When some events lack the key, the all-events value gap is theirs too and can't attribute loss to the gate.”
Grouped value is materially short — given rows, totals, and coverage; gives back true/false:
  Sum grouped rows by event name (rows), and call the result grouped sums.
  Give back whether at least one item in the key/value pairs of totals passes this check:
    If total's sum is zero or less, give back whether false.
    If total's count is more than coverage's entry for event name, or 0 if that's missing, give back whether false.
    Let missing be total's sum minus grouped sums' entry for event name, or 0 if that's missing.
    Give back whether missing divided by total's sum is at least retry shortfall ratio.

Property rollup coverage is incomplete — given rows and coverage; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether a property rollup coverage shortfall (rows and coverage) is "major".

“Every grouped event carries the key, so populated coverage can never report fewer events than the grouped result. Seeing that means the coverage rollup is empty or mid-backfill, and trusting it would hide real gate loss.”
Property rollup coverage under reports — given rows and coverage; gives back true/false:
  Count rows by event name (rows), and call the result grouped counts.
  If grouped counts is missing, give back whether false.
  Give back whether at least one item in the key/value pairs of grouped counts passes this check:
    Let coverage count be coverage's entry for event name, or 0 if that's missing.
    If grouped count is at most coverage count, give back whether false.
    Give back whether grouped count minus coverage count is not within ingestion lag (given reference: coverage count).

Total event count — given rows; gives back a number (or nothing):
  Let total start as 0.
  For each row in rows:
    If row's event count is missing, give back nothing.
    Add row's event count to total.
  Give back total.

“Whether the retry recovered anything. Prefers event counts, since a recovered group whose values cancel to zero moves the count but not the sum.”
Reports more than? — given candidate and current; gives back true/false:
  Let candidate count be a total event count (rows: candidate).
  Let current count be a total event count (rows: current).
  If candidate count is set and current count is set:
    If candidate count is not current count, give back whether candidate count is more than current count.
  Give back whether sum all rows (rows: candidate) is more than sum all rows (rows: current).

“Whether the gated property rollup under-reports against the ungated totals. A key with both gate-surviving and gate-dropped values comes back non-empty yet short, so emptiness alone never detects it.”
Grouped result is incomplete — given rows and totals; gives back true/false:
  Sum grouped rows by event name (rows), and call the result grouped sums.
  Count rows by event name (rows), and call the result grouped counts.
  Give back whether at least one item in the key/value pairs of totals passes this check:
    If total's count is zero or less, give back whether false.
    “Signed values can cancel, so a matching sum does not prove the groups are all present; the count catches what the sum hides.”
    If all of these are true:
      • grouped counts is set
      • grouped counts' entry for event name, or 0 if that's missing is less than total's count
    then:
      Give back whether true.
    Give back whether grouped sums' entry for event name, or 0 if that's missing is materially less than (given reference: total's sum).

##### server/src/internal/analytics/actions/revenueAnalytics.ts

“── 1. Revenue by product over time ─────────────────────────────────”
To get revenue by product — given granularity (async):
  Get ClickHouse client, and call the result ch.
  From context, take org.
  Let date format be granularity format's entry for granularity.
  Let target currency be org's default currency, or "usd" if that's empty.
  Get conversion rates JSON (base currency: target currency), and call the result rates.
  Let date cutoff map be an object with:
    • day: "AND i.created_at >= toInt64(toUnixTimestamp(now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY)) * 1000"
    • month: "AND i.created_at >= toInt64(toUnixTimestamp(now() - INTERVAL 24 MONTH)) * 1000"
    • year: "AND i.created_at >= toInt64(toUnixTimestamp(now() - INTERVAL 10 YEAR)) * 1000"
  Let date cutoff be date cutoff map's entry for granularity, or "" if that's missing.
  Let query be "
		SELECT
			formatDateTime(toDateTime(i.created_at / 1000), {date_format:String}) AS period_label,
			p.name AS product_name,
			SUM({converted total split}) AS volume,
			{target_currency:String} AS currency
		FROM invoices AS i FINAL
		ARRAY JOIN i.internal_product_ids AS ipid
		INNER JOIN (
			SELECT internal_id, org_id, name
			FROM products FINAL
		) AS p ON p.internal_id = ipid AND p.org_id = {org_id:String}
		INNER JOIN (
			SELECT internal_id, org_id, env
			FROM customers FINAL
		) AS cus ON cus.internal_id = i.internal_customer_id AND cus.org_id = {org_id:String}
		WHERE cus.env = 'live'
			AND i.hosted_invoice_url LIKE '%live%'
			AND i.status = 'paid'
			AND i.__action != 'delete'
			{date cutoff}
		GROUP BY period_label, product_name
		ORDER BY period_label ASC, product_name ASC
	".
  Query ch, and call the result result:
    • query
    • query params: an object with:
      • org ID: org's ID
      • date format: date format
      • rates
      • target currency: target currency
    • format: "JSON"
  Let result JSON be result's JSON.
  Give back result JSON's data, with each row turned into an object with:
    • period label: row's period label
    • product name: row's product name
    • volume: row's volume as a number
    • currency: row's currency

##### server/src/internal/admin/handleAdminCacheV2Ramp.ts

  Give back the user's email, or the user ID if that's missing, or "unknown" if that's missing.

“GET /admin/cache-v2-ramp Returns the current ramp config in frontend-safe shape (host + percent only). Never echoes the encrypted connectionString.”

“PATCH /admin/cache-v2-ramp  body: { connectionString } Upsert the destination. Accepts a PLAINTEXT redis:// or rediss:// URI; server validates the scheme, extracts host:port for logging, encrypts the connection string, and persists. Refuses while migrationPercent > 0.”
Create route, and call the result handle upsert admin cache v2 ramp:
  • scopes: a list of scopes' superuser
  • body: a schema for an object with connection string
  • handler: a function of c that:
    Let context be c's entry for "ctx".
    From c's request's valid ("json"), take connection string (as raw).
    Let connection string be raw without surrounding spaces.
    Start with no Redis URL yet.
    Try the following:
      Set Redis URL to a new URL (connection string).
    If anything fails:
      Fail with an error: "Invalid connection string: could not parse URL" [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
    If Redis URL's protocol is not in Redis protocols:
      Fail with an error: "Invalid connection string: expected redis:// or rediss://" [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
    If Redis URL's host is missing:
      Fail with an error: "Invalid connection string: missing host" [error code's invalid request] (status 400).
    “Store enforces "refuse while migrationPercent > 0" atomically against fresh S3 state — no separate handler-level guard against the polled snapshot (which can lag in multi-instance deployments).”
    Let was configured mean get cache v2 ramp config gives back something.
    Upsert cache v2 ramp connection:
      • connection string: encrypt data (connection string)
      • URL: Redis URL's host
    Log "[admin/handleUpsertAdminCacheV2Ramp] {"updated" if was configured, otherwise "created"}, url={Redis URL's host}, actor={an actor string}".
    Give back c's JSON (success).

“PATCH /admin/cache-v2-ramp/migration  body: { migrationPercent } Updates the percent. Stores previous value + timestamp.”
Create route, and call the result handle update admin cache v2 ramp migration:
  • scopes: a list of scopes' superuser
  • body: a schema for an object with migration percent
  • handler: a function of c that:
    Let context be c's entry for "ctx".
    From c's request's valid ("json"), take migration percent.
    “Snapshot the previous percent for logging only; the store enforces "config must exist" atomically against fresh S3 state.”
    Get cache v2 ramp config, and call the result previous snapshot.
    Update cache v2 ramp migration percent (migration percent).
    “Warm the destination client on first ramp-up so the first ramped requests don't pay the connect-handshake latency.”
    If all of these are true:
      • migration percent is positive
      • previous snapshot's migration percent, or 0 if that's missing is 0
    then:
      Get ramp destination Redis.
    Log "[admin/handleUpdateAdminCacheV2RampMigration] {previous snapshot's migration percent, or 0 if that's missing}% -> {migration percent}%, actor={an actor string}".
    Give back c's JSON (success).

“DELETE /admin/cache-v2-ramp Removes the cache V2 ramp config entirely. Refuses while migrationPercent > 0.”

          From org, take Redis config (as raw Redis config), claim token hash, and the rest as rest.

##### server/src/internal/account/deleteAccount.ts
Is owner role? — given role:
  Give back whether "owner" is in role split on ",".

“Works out which orgs go away with the user. Orgs where the user is the only member are deleted (deleteOrg also removes their sandboxes). Orgs with other members are left alone, but the user can't be their last owner.”
To get orgs to delete — given user ID; gives back a list of Organization (async):
  Find the query's member many (where: member's user ID is user ID), and call the result user memberships.
  If user memberships is empty, give back an empty list.
  Let org IDs be the organization IDs of user memberships.
  Find the query's member many (where: member's organization ID is in org IDs), and call the result org members.
  Find the query's organizations many (where: organizations' ID is in org IDs), and call the result orgs.
  Let orgs to delete be an empty list.
  For each org in orgs:
    Let other members be org members, keeping only those where org member's organization ID is org's ID and org member's user ID is not user ID.
    If other members is empty:
      Add org to orgs to delete.
      Move on to the next one.
    Let user membership be the first membership in user memberships where membership's organization ID is org's ID.
    Let user is owner be whether user membership is set and user membership's role is owner role.
    Let has other owner mean other members has a org member where org member's role is owner role.
    If user is owner is set and has no other owner:
      Fail with an error: "You're the only owner of {org's name}. Make another member an owner, or remove them, before deleting your account." ["LAST_OWNER"] (status 400).
  Give back orgs to delete.

“Permanently deletes a user, every org they solely belong to (plus sandboxes), and their marketing contacts (via the better-auth user.delete hook).”
To delete account — given user ID (async):
  Get orgs to delete (user ID) → orgs to delete.
  “Check every org (and sandbox) up front so we never leave the account half-deleted.”
  If orgs to delete is not empty:
    List org sandboxes (org IDs: the IDs of orgs to delete) → sandboxes.
    Let orgs to check be orgs to delete, plus sandboxes.
    Find the query's customers first, and call the result live customer:
      • where: all of these are true:
        • customers' org ID is in the IDs of orgs to check
        • customers' env is app env's live
    If live customer is set:
      Let org be the first o in orgs to check where o's ID is live customer's org ID.
      Fail with an error: "{org's name, or "One of your organizations" if that's missing} has production mode customers. Contact support to delete your account." [error code's org has customers] (status 400).
  “Each org is re-validated right before deletion (membership here, live customers inside deleteOrg). If one fails midway, only orgs the user solely owned are gone and the account survives, so a retry picks up.”
  For each org in orgs to delete:
    Find the query's member first, and call the result other member:
      • where: all of these are true:
        • member's organization ID is org's ID
        • member's user ID is not user ID
    If other member is set:
      Fail with an error: "Someone just joined {org's name}. Please try again." ["MEMBERSHIP_CHANGED"] (status 409).
    Log "Deleting org {org's ID} ({org's slug}) for account deletion".
    Delete org (org and delete org from DB).
  “Goes through better-auth so sessions/accounts are cleared and the user.delete hooks (Loops/Resend cleanup) run.”
  Let auth context be auth's context.
  Delete auth context's internal adapter user (user ID).

##### server/src/honoUtils/handleHealthCheck.ts

    • elapsed ms: the current time minus started at
  If ready is missing, stop here.
  Set startup ready to true.
  Log "[health-check] startup gate latched ({reason})" (with Redis status, Redis v2 status, and has Redis v2 config).

If has Redis v2 config, run Redis v2's once ("ready" and try latch startup ready).
Try latch startup ready.

  If startup ready is false:
    Try latch startup ready.
    If startup ready is false, give back c's text ("Redis not ready" and 503).

##### server/src/honoUtils/startupGate.ts
“After this long without Redis becoming ready, latch the gate anyway and fall back to the runtime fail-open path. Bounds the worst case to a brief startup delay instead of an indefinite crash-loop — e.g. when the active V2 instance has been failed over to an alternate while the Dragonfly client the gate watches never connects. Kept well under the ECS health-check grace period so the timeout latch always beats ECS's task-kill timer.”
Let startup gate max wait ms be 20,000.

“Pure decision for the startup gate. `redisReady`/`redisV2Ready` already fold in "not configured" as ready. Once `elapsedMs` reaches the max wait we serve regardless, leaving degradation to the runtime fail-open path.     Give back an object with:
      • ready: true
      • reason: "max wait elapsed; serving via runtime fail-open"
  Give back an object with ready: false and reason: nothing.

“Create a type-safe route with validation that preserves full type inference! ##### server/src/honoMiddlewares/versionResolver.ts

      If hit is set, give back hit.
  Give back map's latest.

  Let missing from a be a copy of keys b, keeping only those where k is not in keys a.

##### server/src/external/vercel/misc/vercelAuth.ts
Create remote jwk set (a new URL ("https://marketplace.vercel.com/.well-known/jwks")), and call the result jwks.

“Vercel OIDC Claims schema”
Let oidc claims schema be a schema for an object with subscription, aud, iss, exp, iat, and account ID (+5 more).

Type OidcClaims: a z.infer.
Type VercelOidcTestOptions: an object.
Let test oidc prefix be "test_oidc:".

Synthesize test claims — given token, org, env, and test options; gives back an OidcClaims (or nothing):
  If the NODE_ENV environment variable is "production", give back nothing.
  If test options does not allow vercel test oidc, give back nothing.
  If token does not start with test oidc prefix, give back nothing.
  Let installation ID be token from position the number of test oidc prefix onward, or nothing if that's empty.
  Let audience be depending on whether env is app env's live:
    • if so: org's processor configs' vercel's client integration ID, or "test_client_id" if that's missing
    • if not: org's processor configs' vercel's sandbox client ID, or "test_client_id" if that's missing
  Let now seconds be the current time divided by 1000, rounded down.
  Give back an object with:
    • subscription: "test:{installation ID, or "no_install" if that's missing}"
    • aud: audience
    • iss: "https://marketplace.vercel.com"
    • exp: now seconds plus 60 times 60
    • iat: now seconds
    • account ID: "acc_test_{installation ID, or "no_install" if that's missing}"
    • installation ID: installation ID

To verify token — given token, org, env, and test options; gives back an OidcClaims (async):
  Let test claims be synthesize test claims:
    • token
    • org
    • env
    • test options
  If test claims is set, give back test claims.
  Try the following:
    From a JWT verify (token, jwks, and clock tolerance: 5), take payload (as claims).
    “Get the correct client_integration_id based on env”
    Let client integration ID be depending on whether env is app env's live:
      • if so: org's processor configs' vercel's client integration ID
      • if not: org's processor configs' vercel's sandbox client ID
    If claims' aud is not client integration ID:
      “Dump both sides so an audience mismatch is debuggable end-to-end. Common causes: org config has the wrong env's client_id, or the integration was re-installed and the org's `sandbox_client_id` hasn't been refreshed. Claim values are intentionally redacted — `aud` is the only one relevant here; surface present keys for schema-drift debugging without leaking user_email/etc.”
      Warn "[vercel/oidc] Invalid audience" (with env, token.aud (from vercel), configured (from org.processor configs.vercel), and token claim keys).
      Fail with an auth error: "Invalid audience".
    If claims' iss is not "https://marketplace.vercel.com":
      Warn "[vercel/oidc] Invalid issuer" (with "
  token.iss:", claims' iss, and "
  expected: https://marketplace.vercel.com").
      Fail with an auth error: "Invalid issuer".
    Give back claims.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    “Don't log here — the caller (vercelOidcAuthMiddleware) already runs logCaughtError on the re-thrown error with the request-scoped logger.”
    If error is a JWT expired, fail with an auth error: "Auth expired".
    If error is a JWT invalid, fail with an auth error: "Auth invalid".
    Fail with error.

To get authorization token — given auth header; gives back text:
  If auth header does not start with "Bearer ", fail with an auth error: "Invalid Authorization header".
  Give back item #2 of auth header split on " ".

To verify claims — given claims, org, env, and metadata:
  “Get the correct client_integration_id based on env”
  Let client integration ID be depending on whether env is app env's live:
    • if so: org's processor configs' vercel's client integration ID
    • if not: org's processor configs' vercel's sandbox client ID
  If claims' aud is not client integration ID, fail with an auth error: "Invalid audience".
  If claims' installation ID is not metadata's integration configuration ID, fail with an error: "Invalid installation ID".
  If claims' iss is not "https://marketplace.vercel.com", fail with an auth error: "Invalid issuer".
  Give back claims.

Class Auth error (extends error):

“OIDC authentication middleware for Vercel integration routes Validates both user and system authentication via OIDC tokens Flow: 1. Extract Authorization Bearer token and X-Vercel-Auth header (user|system) 2. Verify JWT using JWKS 3. For user auth: validate installation_id matches URL param 4. For system auth: validate installation_id if not null 5. Store validated claims in context”
Vercel oidc auth middleware — given c and next (async):
  From c's entry for "ctx", take org, env, and test options.
  Let auth header be c's request's header ("authorization").
  Let auth type be c's request's header ("x-vercel-auth").
  Let path be c's request's path.
  Let method be c's request's method.
  “Helper so every 401/403 here screams to console before the response is returned. The 401/403 body's `code` is useful but doesn't show up in dev server logs unless you tail responses, so we dump the reason here.”
  To reject — given code, status, and reason:
    Warn (with message, method, path, reason, auth type, and auth header present).
    Let error be "Unauthorized" if status is 401, otherwise "Forbidden".
    Give back c's JSON (error, code, and status).
  “Validate required headers”
  If auth header is missing, Reject ("missing_auth_header" and 401), and give back the result.
  If auth type is missing, Reject ("missing_auth_type_header" and 401), and give back the result.
  If auth type is none of "user" or "system":
    Reject ("invalid_auth_type", 401, and "got "{auth type}""), and give back the result.
  “Extract and verify token”
  Start with no token yet.
  Try the following:
    Get authorization token (auth header), and put the result in token.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Log caught error:
      • message: "[vercel/oidc] Invalid authorization header"
      • error
      • data: an object with method and path
      • level: "warn"
    Reject, and give back the result:
      • "invalid_auth_header_format"
      • 401
      • error's message, or error as text if that's missing
  “Verify JWT using JWKS”

##### server/src/external/vercel/misc/vercelProvisioning.ts
“Provisions a Vercel customer product via V2 attach. Idempotency-checks via existing Stripe subscription metadata, then calls V2 `attach()` in invoice mode (`send_invoice`). Vercel marketplace moves the money; Stripe is the ledger. The legacy custom-payment-method path is no longer required for provisioning.”
To provision vercel customer product — given customer, Stripe customer, Stripe client, integration configuration ID, billing plan ID, resource ID, and metadata; gives back an object with subscription, customer product, and product (async):
  From context, take org and env.
  “1. Look up product (hoisted — reused by idempotency branch and free path)”
  Get full [ProductService] (org ID: org's ID, env, and ID or internal ID: billing plan ID), and call the result product.
  If product is missing:
    Fail with an error: "Product not found for billing plan {billing plan ID}" [error code's product not found] (status status codes' not found).
  “2. Idempotency check via existing subscription”
  Let existing subscription be the first s in Stripe customer's subscriptions' data where all of these are true:
    • s' metadata's vercel installation ID is integration configuration ID
    • s' status is not "incomplete_expired"
    • s' status is not "canceled"
  If existing subscription is set:
    Get customer product repo by Stripe subscription ID, and call the result existing customer products:
      • Stripe subscription ID: existing subscription's ID
      • org ID: org's ID
      • env
    “Lazily migrate existing Vercel subs to invoice mode before short-circuit. Idempotent — no-op if already `send_invoice`.”
    Ensure vercel invoice mode subscription (Stripe client and subscription: existing subscription), and call the result migrated subscription.
    If existing customer products is not empty:
      Give back an object with:
        • subscription: migrated subscription
        • customer product: the first of existing customer products
        • product
    “A subscription exists for this installation but no cus_product yet. This is almost always a concurrent in-flight provision: the marketplace safety-net webhooks (invoice.created / invoice.paid) can fire BEFORE the original POST /resources call has run executeAutumnBillingPlan. We must NOT cancel that subscription — Vercel is already processing payment against it. Skip provisioning and let the in-flight call finish. The next webhook retry (Vercel re-delivers paid events) will see the cus_product and short-circuit on the early-return above.”
    Log "[provisionVercelCusProduct] Existing sub without cus_product — skipping (likely in-flight provision elsewhere)" (with data).
    Fail with an error: "Vercel subscription is still being provisioned. Retry shortly." ["vercel_provisioning_in_flight"] (status status codes' conflict).
  “3. Parse prepaid options”
  Let options list be depending on whether metadata is set and the keys of metadata is not empty:
    • if so: parse vercel prepaid quantities (metadata, product, and prices: product's prices)
    • if not: an empty list
  “4. Call V2 attach in invoice mode”
  Let feature quantities be options list, with each opt turned into an object with feature ID: opt's feature ID and quantity: opt's quantity.
  “Note: we intentionally do NOT override `fullCustomer` here. V2's `setupFullCustomerContext` reloads it with `withEntities: true, withSubs: true`, which downstream usage merging requires. Overriding would skip that load and cause `mergeEntitiesWithExistingUsages` to throw on `undefined` entities. We pass a stripeBillingContext WITHOUT a payment method. Vercel handles money movement out of band; Stripe is just the ledger. Invoice mode (`send_invoice`) auto-activates the subscription regardless of first invoice status, so we don't need default_incomplete + custom-PM gymnastics.”
  Let context override be an object with:
    • product context: an object with full product: product
    • Stripe billing context: an object with Stripe customer and Stripe discounts: an empty list
    • skip custom payment method guard: true
  Attach, and call the result result:
    • params: an object with:
      • customer ID: customer's ID, or customer's internal ID if that's empty
      • plan ID: billing plan ID
      • redirect mode: "if_required"
      • feature quantities: feature quantities
      • enable plan immediately: true
      • invoice mode: an object with enabled: true, finalize: true, and enable plan immediately: true
      • metadata: an object with:
        • vercel installation ID: integration configuration ID
        • vercel billing plan ID: billing plan ID
        • vercel product ID: product's ID
        • vercel resource ID: resource ID, or integration configuration ID if that's empty
    • context override
    • skip Autumn checkout
  “5. Extract subscription and cus_product”
  Let subscription be result's billing result's Stripe's Stripe subscription, or nothing if that's missing.
  If subscription is set:
    Get customer product repo by Stripe subscription ID (Stripe subscription ID: subscription's ID, org ID: org's ID, and env), and call the result new customer products.
    If new customer products is not empty:
      Give back an object with:
        • subscription
        • customer product: the first of new customer products
        • product
  “Free product path: look up cus_product by customer + product”
  Get customer product repo by customer and product, and call the result free customer products:
    • internal customer ID: customer's internal ID
    • internal product ID: product's internal ID
    • org ID: org's ID
    • env
    • in statuses: a list of "active" and "trialing"
  If free customer products is not empty:
    Give back an object with:
      • subscription: nothing
      • customer product: the first of free customer products
      • product
  “Should not reach here if attach succeeded”
  Fail with an error: "Failed to find created customer product after attach" ["cus_product_not_found"] (status status codes' internal server error).

##### server/src/external/vercel/misc/vercelSignatureMiddleware.ts
“Webhook signature validation middleware for Vercel marketplace webhooks Validates the X-Vercel-Signature header using HMAC-SHA1. This ensures that webhook requests are genuinely from Vercel. Flow: 1. Extract X-Vercel-Signature header 2. Get raw request body from context (captured by rawBodyMiddleware) 3. Get appropriate client_secret based on environment 4. Compute HMAC-SHA1 signature 5. Perform constant-time comparison 6. Reject request if signature doesn't match”
Vercel signature middleware — given c and next (async):
  From c's entry for "ctx", take org and env.
  Let signature be c's request's header ("x-vercel-signature").
  Let path be c's request's path.
  Let method be c's request's method.
  “Validate signature header presence”
  If signature is missing:
    Warn "[vercel/sig] REJECT 401 missing_signature" (with "
  method:", method, "
  path:", and path).
    Warn "Missing X-Vercel-Signature header".
    Give back c's JSON (error: "Unauthorized", code: "missing_signature", and 401).
  “Get raw body from context (captured by rawBodyMiddleware)”
  Let raw body be c's entry for "rawBody".
  If raw body is missing:
    Log an error "[vercel/sig] REJECT 500 missing_raw_body — captureRawBody middleware did not run before signature middleware" (with "
  method:", method, "
  path:", and path).
    Log an error "Raw body not found in context".
    Give back c's JSON (error: "Internal Server Error", code: "missing_raw_body", and 500).
  “Get appropriate client secret based on environment”
  Let client secret be depending on whether env is app env's live:
    • if so: org's processor configs' vercel's client secret
    • if not: org's processor configs' vercel's sandbox client secret
  If client secret is missing:
    Log an error "[vercel/sig] REJECT 500 missing_client_secret" (with "
  method:", method, "
  path:", path, "
  env:", env, "
  org_id:", and org's ID).
    Log an error "Vercel client secret not configured" (with env).
    Give back c's JSON (error: "Internal Server Error", code: "missing_client_secret", and 500).
  “Compute HMAC-SHA1 signature”
  Let raw body buffer be the from raw body and "utf-8" [Buffer].
  Let computed signature be update create crypto hmac ("sha1" and client secret) (raw body buffer)'s digest ("hex").
  “Perform constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks (timingSafeEqual throws if buffers differ in length, so guard first)”
  Let sig buf be the from signature and "utf-8" [Buffer].
  Let comp buf be the from computed signature and "utf-8" [Buffer].
  Let is valid mean all of these are true:
    • the number of sig buf is the number of comp buf
    • crypto's timing safe equal (sig buf and comp buf) gives back something
  If is not valid:
    Warn "[vercel/sig] REJECT 401 invalid_signature" (with "
  method:", method, "
  path:", path, "
  env:", env, "
  signature_received:", "{the first 12 of signature}...", "
  signature_computed:", "{the first 12 of computed signature}...", "
  raw_body_length:", and the number of raw body buffer).
    Warn "Webhook signature validation failed" (with env and has signature).
    Give back c's JSON (error: "Unauthorized", code: "invalid_signature", and 401).
  Run next.

##### server/src/external/vercel/misc/vercelStripeInvoiceMode.ts

“Ensure a Vercel-owned Stripe subscription is in invoice mode (`send_invoice` + `days_until_due: 30`). - No-op if already `send_invoice`. - Best-effort clears `default_payment_method` (`default_payment_method` is not typed as nullable on `SubscriptionUpdateParams`, so we cast to `unknown` and treat any rejection as non-fatal). - Skips silently if the subscription is canceled.”

      • data: an object with subscription ID: subscription's ID
      • level: "warn"

    Try the following:
      Update Stripe client's subscriptions, and call the result updated:
        • subscription's ID
        • collection method: "send_invoice"
        • days until due: 30
      Warn "[vercelInvoiceMode] migrated subscription to send_invoice; could not clear default_payment_method" (with data).
      Give back updated.
    If anything fails (call the problem retry error):
      Log caught error:
        • message: "[vercelInvoiceMode] failed to migrate subscription to send_invoice"
        • error: retry error
        • data: an object with subscription ID: subscription's ID
      Give back subscription.

“Strip a Vercel-owned Stripe customer's default payment method when it points at a Custom Payment Method. Required before `invoices.pay` — Stripe rejects the call with "Custom payment methods are not supported on invoices.pay" if the customer's default is a CPM. Clears `invoice_settings.default_payment_method` only; the CPM stays attached so historical invoices/payment records that reference it keep resolving. Idempotent + best-effort: a real card stays untouched, a non-CPM default is left alone, and Stripe failures log a warning without throwing.”
To ensure vercel invoice mode customer — given Stripe client and Stripe customer ID (async):

      • Stripe customer ID

“Mark a Stripe invoice paid out of band (Vercel handled the money movement). Idempotent: - Skips if the invoice is already `paid`. - Skips if the invoice is `void`/`voided`/`uncollectible`/`deleted`. - Logs and continues for known race/already-paid states.”
To mark vercel invoice paid out of band — given Stripe client and invoice; gives back a Stripe.Invoice (async):
  If invoice's ID is missing, give back invoice.
  If invoice's status is "paid":
    Log "[vercelInvoiceMode] invoice already paid, skipping" (with data).
    Give back invoice.
  If invoice's status is "void" or invoice's status is "uncollectible":
    Log "[vercelInvoiceMode] invoice not payable, skipping" (with data).
    Give back invoice.
  If invoice's status is "draft":
    “`invoices.pay` requires a finalized invoice. The finalize webhook is what triggers Vercel submission; by the time `marketplace.invoice.paid` lands, the invoice should be `open`. If it's still `draft`, log and skip — finalization will happen in a separate webhook.”
    Warn "[vercelInvoiceMode] invoice still draft when paid webhook arrived" (with data).
    Give back invoice.
  Try the following:
    Pay Stripe client's invoices (invoice's ID and paid out of band), and give back the result.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Let message be error's message, or "" if that's missing.
    If "already paid" is in message or "This invoice is already paid" is in message:
      Log caught error:
        • message: "[vercelInvoiceMode] invoice already paid (race)"
        • error
        • data: an object with invoice ID: invoice's ID
        • level: "warn"
      Give back invoice.
    If "voided" is in message, "uncollectible" is in message, or "Cannot pay invoice" is in message:
      Log caught error:
        • message: "[vercelInvoiceMode] invoice transitioned to non-payable state"
        • error
        • data: an object with invoice ID: invoice's ID
        • level: "warn"
      Give back invoice.
    Log caught error:
      • message: "[vercelInvoiceMode] failed to mark invoice paid out of band"
      • error
      • data: an object with invoice ID: invoice's ID
    Fail with error.

##### server/src/external/vercel/handlers/handleListBillingPlans.ts
“Calculate total cost of prepaid quantities from metadata”
To calculate prepaid costs — given metadata and product; gives back a number:
  If metadata is missing or the keys of metadata is empty, give back 0.
  Let total prepaid cost start as 0.
  “Parse prepaid quantities using existing validation logic”
  Parse vercel prepaid quantities (metadata, product, and prices: product's prices), and call the result options list.
  “Calculate cost for each prepaid feature”
  For each options in options list:
    Find prepaid price → prepaid price:
      • prices: product's prices
      • internal feature ID: options' internal feature ID, or "" if that's missing
    If prepaid price is set:
      Let config be prepaid price's config.
      Let billing units be config's billing units, or 1 if that's empty.
      “Calculate quantity in subscription items (metadata quantity / billing_units, rounded up)”
      Let subscription item quantity be options' quantity divided by billing units, rounded up.
      “Get unit price from first usage tier”
      Let unit amount be config's first usage tier's amount, or 0 if that's empty.
      “Calculate total cost for this feature”
      Let feature cost be subscription item quantity times unit amount.
      Add feature cost to total prepaid cost.
  Give back total prepaid cost.

Product → billing plan — given product, org currency, and metadata; gives back a VercelBillingPlan:
  “const paymentMethodRequired = false;”
  Map to product v2 (product) → product v2.
  Let base price be the base price of product v2.
  “Calculate prepaid costs from metadata”
  Let prepaid costs start as 0.
  If metadata is set and the keys of metadata is not empty:
    Calculate prepaid costs (metadata and product), and put the result in prepaid costs.
  “Total cost = base recurring + prepaid quantities”
  Let total amount be base price's price, or 0 if that's empty plus prepaid costs.
  Let highlighted details be product v2's items, after these steps:
    1. Keep only those where x is not price item
    2. Turn each x into the result of these steps:
      Get product item display (item: x and features: the features of product's entitlements), and call the result d.
      Give back an object with:
        • label: d's primary text
        • value: d's secondary text without surrounding spaces if d's secondary text without surrounding spaces is not "" (otherwise nothing)
  Let bp be an object with:
    • cost: "{format amount}/{base price's interval}" if base price's interval is set and total amount is positive (otherwise nothing)
    • ID: product's ID
    • type: "subscription"
    • name: product's name
    • scope: "installation"
    • description: ""
    • highlighted details
    • payment method required: whether total amount is positive
    • everything in an object with preauthorization amount: total amount (only if total amount is positive)
    • disabled: whether product's archived is set
  Give back bp.

To get vercel plan filter reason — given product:
  If product's prices has a price where price is not fixed and price is not prepaid, give back "Has usage prices".
  If product is add on, give back "Is add-on".
  If product's prices is one off and product's prices is not free product, give back "Is paid one-off".
  If product's archived is set, give back "Is archived".
  If product's entitlements is empty and product is not default, give back "Has no entitlements and is not default".
  Give back nothing.

    • if not: org's processor configs' vercel's allowed product IDs sandbox

    • org ID: org's ID
    • env
    • no archived
    • in IDs: allowed IDs if allowed IDs is not empty (otherwise nothing)
  Sort products by price (products).
  Log "Products before filtering" (with the names of products).
  “1. Get rid of products that have usage prices 2. Get rid of products that are archived 3. Get rid of products that are one off, only if they are not free”
  Let filtered products be products, keeping only those where get vercel plan filter reason (product) gives back nothing.
  Log "Products after filtering" (with the names of filtered products).
  Log "For each product, here is the reason it was filtered out" (with products, after these steps).
  Give back a copy of filtered products, with each product turned into the billing plan of each product:
    • org currency: org's default currency, or "usd" if that's missing
    • metadata

##### server/src/external/vercel/handlers/marketplace/handleMarketplaceInvoiceNotPaid.ts
“Handles Vercel's `marketplace.invoice.notpaid` webhook. Replaces the legacy Custom Payment Method + Payment Records "report failed payment" flow. Vercel marketplace already failed to collect; we just clean up Autumn-side and cancel the Stripe subscription so the customer loses access. The invoice itself is left in its current Stripe status (not paid) — the Stripe ledger reflects the failure naturally. - Does NOT call `stripeCli.paymentRecords.reportPayment`. - Does NOT call `stripeCli.invoices.attachPayment`. - Sets the Vercel resource to `suspended`. - Expires the Autumn customer product and activates the default fallback. - Cancels the Stripe subscription.”
To handle marketplace invoice not paid — given payload (async):
  From context, take org and env.
  From payload, take installation ID and external invoice ID.
  Create Stripe client (org and env) → Stripe client.
  Retrieve Stripe client's invoices (external invoice ID and expand: a list of "subscription"), and call the result invoice.
  “If the paid webhook already won the race, do nothing destructive.”
  If invoice's status is "paid":
    Log "Invoice already marked as paid; skipping notpaid cleanup" (with data).
    Stop here.
  Get invoice subscription ID (invoice) → subscription ID.
  If subscription ID is missing:
    Warn "[handleMarketplaceInvoiceNotPaid] No subscription on invoice; nothing to cancel" (with data).
    Stop here.
  Retrieve Stripe client's subscriptions (subscription ID), and call the result subscription.
  “Lazy migration before destructive ops — keeps state consistent for any downstream observers that read collection_method.”
  Ensure vercel invoice mode subscription (Stripe client and subscription).
  “Resolve customer for cus_product cleanup. Failure is logged but doesn't block the destructive cleanup below (we still want the resource suspended + sub canceled even if our DB lookup misfires).”
  Start with no customer internal ID yet.
  Try the following:
    Get by Stripe ID [CusService] (Stripe ID: invoice's customer), and call the result partial customer.
    If partial customer is set:
      Set customer internal ID to partial customer's internal ID.
    Otherwise:
      Warn "[handleMarketplaceInvoiceNotPaid] Customer not found" (with data).
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Log caught error:
      • message: "[vercel/marketplace.invoice.notpaid] Customer lookup failed"
      • error
      • data: an object with Stripe customer ID: invoice's customer
  “Suspend the Vercel resource so the end user loses access in Vercel's UI.”
  Let vercel resource ID be subscription's metadata's vercel resource ID.
  If vercel resource ID starts with "vre_":
    Try the following:
      Update [VercelResourceService]:
        • resource ID: vercel resource ID
        • installation ID
        • org ID: org's ID
        • env
        • updates: an object with status: "suspended"
    If anything fails (call the problem error):
      Log caught error:
        • message: "[vercel/marketplace.invoice.notpaid] Could not suspend resource"
        • error
        • data: an object with resource ID: vercel resource ID
        • level: "warn"
  “Expire the Autumn cus_product and activate the default fallback. This mirrors the legacy first-invoice failure path but runs for renewals too — payment failed at any point means the customer should lose paid access.”
  If customer internal ID is set:
    Try the following:
      Get full [CusService] (ID or internal ID: customer internal ID), and call the result full customer.
      If full customer is set:
        Get customer product repo by Stripe subscription ID (Stripe subscription ID: subscription's ID, org ID: org's ID, and env), and call the result existing customer products.
        If existing customer products is not empty:
          Expire customer product actions and activate default:
            • customer product: the first of existing customer products
            • full customer
        Otherwise:
          Log "[handleMarketplaceInvoiceNotPaid] No cus_product to expire" (with data).
    If anything fails (call the problem error):
      Log caught error:
        • message: "[vercel/marketplace.invoice.notpaid] Failed to expire cus_product"
        • error
        • data: an object with customer internal ID and subscription ID: subscription's ID
  “Cancel the Stripe subscription. We deliberately do NOT mark the invoice paid — Vercel reported it as unpaid, so the Stripe ledger should keep reflecting that.”
  Try the following:
    Cancel Stripe client's subscriptions (subscription's ID).
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    “`resource_missing` means the sub is already gone — fine, idempotent.”
    If error's code is "resource_missing":
      Log "[handleMarketplaceInvoiceNotPaid] Subscription already canceled" (with data).
      Stop here.
    Log caught error:
      • message: "[vercel/marketplace.invoice.notpaid] Failed to cancel subscription"
      • error
      • data: an object with subscription ID: subscription's ID
    Fail with error.

##### server/src/external/vercel/handlers/marketplace/handleMarketplaceInvoiceRefunded.ts
“Handles Vercel's `marketplace.invoice.refunded` webhook — the only confirmation that money actually moved back. Vercel retries webhook deliveries, so the payload's `amount` can't be accumulated (a retried $20 refund would record $40). Instead we fetch the invoice from Vercel and set `refunded_amount` to its `refundTotal`, which is idempotent across retries while still counting multiple partial refunds. If Vercel can't be reached or returns no total, `refunded_amount` is left untouched rather than guessed.”
To handle marketplace invoice refunded — given payload (async):
  From context, take org and env.
  From payload, take installation ID, invoice ID (as vercel invoice ID), and external invoice ID.
  If external invoice ID is missing or vercel invoice ID is missing:
    Warn "[vercel/marketplace.invoice.refunded] unusable payload" (with data).
    Stop here.
  Let customer be the full customer, or get by vercel ID [CusService] (vercel installation ID: installation ID) if that's missing.
  Let access token be customer's processors' vercel's access token.
  If access token is missing:
    Warn "[vercel/marketplace.invoice.refunded] no Vercel access token for installation" (with data).
    Stop here.
  Start with no refund total yet.
  Try the following:
    Let marketplace be a new marketplace:
      • bearer token: access token
      • server URL: get vercel SDK server URL (the test options)
    Get marketplace invoice, and call the result vercel invoice:
      • integration configuration ID: installation ID
      • invoice ID: vercel invoice ID
    Let parsed be vercel invoice's refund total as a number.
    If vercel invoice's refund total is missing or parsed is not a real number:
      Warn "[vercel/marketplace.invoice.refunded] Vercel invoice has no usable refundTotal" (with data).
    Otherwise:
      Set refund total to parsed.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    “Rethrow so the router answers non-2xx and Vercel redelivers; acking here would silently drop the only confirmation that money moved.”
    Log caught error:
      • message: "[vercel/marketplace.invoice.refunded] failed to fetch invoice from Vercel; not acking so Vercel retries"
      • error
      • data: an object with vercel invoice ID, external invoice ID, and installation ID
      • level: "warn"
    Fail with error.
  If refund total is set:
    Update [InvoiceService], and call the result updated:
      • query: an object with Stripe ID: external invoice ID
      • updates: an object with refunded amount: refund total
    If updated is missing:
      Warn "[vercel/marketplace.invoice.refunded] no Autumn invoice" (with data).
      Stop here.
  Get by Stripe ID [InvoiceService] (Stripe ID: external invoice ID), and call the result invoice.
  If invoice is set and customer's ID is set, Upsert invoice in cache (customer ID: customer's ID and invoice).
  “Backfill the Vercel invoice id for invoices submitted before it was stored.”
  Try the following:
    Create Stripe client (org and env) → Stripe client.
    Store vercel invoice ID:
      • Stripe client
      • Stripe invoice ID: external invoice ID
      • vercel invoice ID
      • installation ID
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Log caught error:
      • message: "[vercel/marketplace.invoice.refunded] could not stamp vercel_invoice_id"
      • error
      • data: an object with external invoice ID
      • level: "warn"

##### server/src/external/tinybird/migrations/migrationItemEventsDataSource.ts
Let Tinybird us east API URL be the TINYBIRD_US_EAST_API_URL environment variable.
Let Tinybird us east token be the TINYBIRD_US_EAST_TOKEN environment variable.
Let migration Tinybird config be an object with base URL: Tinybird us east API URL and token: Tinybird us east token if Tinybird us east API URL is set and Tinybird us east token is set (otherwise nothing).
Type MigrationItemEventStatus: one of "succeeded", "skipped", or "failed".
Type MigrationItemPreview: an object.
Type MigrationItemEventResponse: a lookup of text to anything (or nothing).

Let migration item events datasource be a define datasource:
  • "migration_item_events"
  • description: "One audit result row per migration item run."
  • schema: an object with:
    • timestamp: t's date time64 (6)
    • org ID: t's string
    • env: t's string's low cardinality
    • migration internal ID: t's string
    • migration run ID: t's string
    • dry run: t's bool
    • item kind: t's string's low cardinality
    • item ID: t's string
    • item preview: t's JSON
    • status: t's string's low cardinality
    • response: t's JSON
  • engine: merge engine tree:
    • partition key: "toYYYYMM(timestamp)"
    • sorting key: a list of:
      • "org_id"
      • "env"
      • "migration_run_id"
      • "item_kind"
      • "item_id"
      • "timestamp"

Type TinybirdMigrationItemEvent: an InferRow.

Let list migration item events endpoint be a define endpoint:
  • "list_migration_item_events"
  • description: "List audit result rows for a migration run."
  • params: an object with:
    • org ID: p's string
    • env: p's string
    • migration internal ID: p's string
    • migration run ID: p's string's optional ("")
    • item IDs: p's array (p's string)'s optional
    • limit: p's int32's optional (1000)
  • nodes: a list of:
    • a node:
      • name: "endpoint"
      • SQL: "
					SELECT
						timestamp,
						org_id,
						env,
						migration_internal_id,
						migration_run_id,
						dry_run,
						item_kind,
						item_id,
						item_preview,
						status,
						response
					FROM migration_item_events
					WHERE org_id = {{String(org_id)}}
						AND env = {{String(env)}}
						AND migration_internal_id = {{String(migration_internal_id)}}
						{% if defined(migration_run_id) and String(migration_run_id, '') != '' %}
							AND migration_run_id = {{String(migration_run_id)}}
						{% end %}
						{% if defined(item_ids) and length(item_ids) > 0 %}
							AND item_id IN {{Array(item_ids, 'String')}}
						{% end %}
					ORDER BY timestamp DESC, item_kind ASC, item_id ASC
					LIMIT {{Int32(limit, 1000)}}
				"
  • output: an object with:
    • timestamp: t's date time64 (6)
    • org ID: t's string
    • env: t's string's low cardinality
    • migration internal ID: t's string
    • migration run ID: t's string
    • dry run: t's bool
    • item kind: t's string's low cardinality
    • item ID: t's string
    • item preview: t's JSON
    • status: t's string's low cardinality
    • response: t's JSON

Let migration Tinybird be (only if migration Tinybird config is set) a new Tinybird:
  • datasources: an object with item events: migration item events datasource
  • pipes: an object with list item events: list migration item events endpoint
  • everything in migration Tinybird config
  • fetch: gzip Tinybird events fetch
  • no dev mode

##### server/src/external/stripe/handleStripeWebhookEvent.ts

  From context, take org and env.
  Try the following:
    Run Stripe webhook handlers.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    If error is a stripe.errors.stripe error:
      If "No such customer" is in error's message:
        Warn "stripe customer missing: {error's message}".
        Give back c's JSON (success and 200).

        Unset org Stripe keys (org and env).
        Give back c's JSON (success and 200).
    If all of these are true:
      • the NODE_ENV environment variable is "development"
      • error is an error
      • "No stripe account linked to organization" is in error's message
    then:
      Give back c's JSON (success and 200).
    Handle webhook error skip (error), and call the result should skip.
    If should skip, give back c's JSON (message: "Webhook received, skipped known error" and 200).
    Log an error "Stripe webhook error: {error}" (with error).
    “Rethrow so the ack middleware owns the outcome: sync events 500 (Stripe retries), early events release the idempotency lock for manual replay.”
    Fail with error.
  “Note: Cache refresh is now handled by stripeWebhookRefreshMiddleware”
  Give back c's JSON (success and 200).

  Give back the STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SQS_QUEUE_URL environment variable.

“Queues a failed early-acked webhook for replay. Never throws — the caller is a background failure path and enqueue is best-effort.”
To enqueue Stripe webhook replay — given failure reason; gives back true/false (async):
  From context, take org, env, and Stripe event.
  Get Stripe webhook replay queue URL → queue URL.
  If org is missing or Stripe event is missing, give back whether false.
  If queue URL is missing:
    Warn "[stripeWebhookReplay] STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SQS_QUEUE_URL not set, cannot queue failed event {Stripe event's ID} for replay".
    Give back whether false.
  Try catch, and take its error:
    • add task to queue:
      • job name: job name's Stripe webhook replay
      • queue URL
      • payload: an object with:
        • org ID: org's ID
        • env
        • Stripe event
        • failed at: the current time
        • failure reason
  If error is set:
    Log an error "[stripeWebhookReplay] Failed to queue event {Stripe event's ID} for replay: {error}" (with error).
    Give back whether false.
  Give back whether true.

##### server/src/external/stripe/webhookReplay/runStripeWebhookReplay.ts
Type StripeWebhookReplayPayload: an object.

“Thrown when the event lock is held elsewhere or unavailable but required; retryable via SQS.”
Class Stripe webhook replay in flight error (extends error):
  When created — given event ID:
    Set up the parent class ("Stripe webhook replay in flight for event {event ID}").
    Set this's name to "StripeWebhookReplayInFlightError".

“Worker entry: replays a failed early-acked Stripe webhook through the same pipeline the route runs (customer resolution -> handlers -> cache refresh -> sync mirror), guarded by the same Redis idempotency claim.”
To run Stripe webhook replay — given payload and receive count (default 1) (async):
  From payload, take Stripe event.
  Let webhook context be context, but with:
    • auth type set to auth type's Stripe
    • Stripe event set to Stripe event
    • Stripe client set to depending on whether Stripe event's type is "account.application.deauthorized":
      • if so: init master Stripe (env: the env)
      • if not: create Stripe client (org: the org and env: the env)
  Attach Stripe event customer (context: webhook context), and call the result routed context.
  Build Stripe webhook event key (org ID: the org's ID, env: the env, and event ID: Stripe event's ID) → event key.
  Claim Stripe webhook event (event key), and call the result claim.
  If claim is "duplicate_completed":
    Log "[stripeWebhookReplay] Event {Stripe event's ID} already completed elsewhere, skipping replay".
    Stop here.
  “Lock-required events must never run unlocked next to a Stripe redelivery.”
  Let lock unavailable mean claim is "unavailable" and Stripe event is Stripe webhook lock required.
  If claim is "in_flight" or lock unavailable is true:
    If receive count is at least Stripe webhook replay max attempts, stop here.
    Fail with a Stripe webhook replay in flight error: Stripe event's ID.
  Log "[stripeWebhookReplay] Replaying {Stripe event's type} ({Stripe event's ID}), originally failed at {payload's failed at as a date as an ISO date string}: {payload's failure reason}".
  Try the following:
    Run Stripe webhook handlers (context: routed context).
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    If claim is "claimed", Release Stripe webhook event (event key).
    If receive count is at least Stripe webhook replay max attempts, stop here.
    Fail with error.
  If claim is "claimed", Complete Stripe webhook event (event key).
  “Post-processing mirrors the route's refresh + sync middlewares (best-effort).”
  If all of these are true:
    • routed context's full customer's ID is set
    • routed context should refresh after webhook handler
  then:
    Try catch:
      • delete cached full customer:
        • customer ID: routed context's full customer's ID
        • context: routed context
        • source: "stripeWebhookReplay: {Stripe event's type}"
        • flush balances
  Sync Stripe event to sync DB (context: routed context).

##### server/src/external/stripe/webhookMiddlewares/classifyStripeWebhookAckMode.ts
Type StripeWebhookAckMode: one of "early" or "sync".

“Decides whether a Stripe webhook is acked before processing ("early") or only after processing succeeds ("sync", so a failure 500s and Stripe retries). Sync is reserved for events whose handler is load-bearing: external changes Autumn didn't cause, plus deferred-checkout / period-boundary work that runs ONLY in the webhook. Early-ack keeps Autumn-triggered events from blocking the billing actions that emitted them.”
Classify Stripe webhook ack mode — given event and now (default the current time); gives back a StripeWebhookAckMode:
  If event is missing, give back "early".
  Depending on event's type:
    • If it is "account.application.deauthorized":
      Give back "sync".
    • If it is "checkout.session.completed" or "checkout.session.expired":
      Give back "sync".
    • If it is "customer.updated":
      Give back "sync".
    • If it is "invoice.paid":
      Let invoice be event's data's object.
      Give back "sync" if invoice's metadata's Autumn metadata ID is set, otherwise "early".
    • If it is "invoice.finalized":
      Let invoice be event's data's object.
      If all of this holds:
        • invoice's metadata's vercel installation ID is set
        • invoice's metadata's Autumn metadata ID is set
        Give back "sync".
      Otherwise:
        Give back "early".
    • If it is "invoice.created":
      Let invoice be event's data's object.
      Give back "sync" if invoice's billing reason is "subscription_cycle", otherwise "early".
    • If it is "customer.subscription.created", "customer.subscription.updated", or "customer.subscription.deleted":
      If event is Autumn originated Stripe, give back "early".
      Let subscription be event's data's object.
      From whether subscription's metadata is Autumn managed subscription (given now and require recent: whether event's type is not "customer.subscription.created"), take skip.
      Give back "early" if skip is set, otherwise "sync".
    • For anything else:
      Give back "early".

“Cycle invoices write money to Stripe from this webhook, so overlapping deliveries must be impossible: without the event lock, ask Stripe to retry.”
Is Stripe webhook lock required? — given event; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether all of these are true:
    • event's type is "invoice.created"
    • event's data's object's billing reason is "subscription_cycle"

##### server/src/external/stripe/webhookMiddlewares/stripeConnectSeederMiddleware.ts
“Seeder middleware for Stripe Connect webhooks - Verifies webhook signature using master stripe - Gets org from event.account (accountId) - Sets up StripeWebhookContext (org, env, features, stripeEvent)”
Stripe connect seeder middleware — given c and next (async):
  Let context be c's entry for "ctx".
  From c's request's param, take env.
  “Step 1: Initialize master stripe client”
  Start with no master Stripe yet.
  Try the following:
    Init master Stripe (env), and put the result in master Stripe.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Log an error "Failed to initialize master stripe client {error}".
    Give back c's JSON (error: "Failed to initialize stripe client" and 500).
  “Step 2: Verify webhook signature”
  Let raw body be c's request's text.
  Let signature be c's request's header ("stripe-signature"), or "" if that's empty.
  Let skip verify mean all of these are true:
    • the STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SKIP_VERIFY environment variable is "true"
    • the NODE_ENV environment variable is not "production"
  Start with no event yet.
  If skip verify is true:
    “logger.warn( "[Stripe] SKIPPING webhook signature verification — non-prod only", );”
    Try the following:
      Set event to raw body parsed from JSON.
    If anything fails (call the problem error):
      Let message be error's message if error is an error, otherwise error as text.
      Warn "Webhook body parse error (skip-verify): {message}".
      Give back c's JSON (error: message and 400).
  Otherwise:
    Try the following:
      Get Stripe webhook secret (org ID: query c's request ("org_id") and env) → webhook secret.
      Construct master Stripe's webhooks event async (raw body, signature, and webhook secret), and put the result in event.
    If anything fails (call the problem error):
      Let message be error's message if error is an error, otherwise error as text.
      If the NODE_ENV environment variable is not "development", warn "Webhook verification error: {message}".
      Give back c's JSON (error: message and 400).
  “Step 4: Get org from account ID”
  Let account ID be event's account.
  If account ID is missing:
    Log an error "Account ID not found in webhook event".
    Give back c's JSON (error: "Account ID not found" and 200).
  Start with no org yet.
  Start with no features yet.
  Try the following:
    Get by account ID [OrgService], and call the result data:
      • account ID
      • deauthorized env: env if event's type is "account.application.deauthorized" (otherwise nothing)
    Set org to data's org.
    Set features to data's features.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    “Only ack accounts genuinely not linked to an org; any other failure (e.g. DB outage) must 500 so Stripe retries instead of dropping the event.”
    Let is org not found mean error is a recase error and error's code is error code's org not found.
    If is not org not found:
      Log an error "Failed to resolve org for Stripe account {account ID}, returning 500 for Stripe to retry: {error}" (with error).
      Give back c's JSON (error: "Failed to resolve org for Stripe webhook" and 500).
    If the NODE_ENV environment variable is not "development":
      Warn "Account ID {account ID} not linked to any org, skipping Stripe webhook".
    Give back c's JSON:
      • message: "Account ID not linked to any org, skipping Stripe webhook"
      • 200
  “Step 5: Set up context”
  Set the org to org.
  Set the features to features.
  Set the env to env.
  Set the auth type to auth type's Stripe.
  Set the Stripe event to event.
  Set the Stripe client to depending on whether event's type is "account.application.deauthorized":
    • if so: master Stripe
    • if not: create Stripe client (org and env)
  Run next.

##### server/src/external/stripe/webhookMiddlewares/stripeIdempotencyMiddleware.ts
Let processing TTL ms be 5 times 60 times 1000.
Let completed TTL ms be 24 times 60 times 60 times 1000.
Let processing be "processing".
Let completed be "completed".

To build Stripe webhook event key — given org ID, env, and event ID:
  Give back "stripe:webhook:{org ID}:{env}:{event ID}".

Type StripeWebhookClaimResult: one of "claimed", "duplicate_completed", "in_flight", or "unavailable".

“Atomically claims an event for processing. "unavailable" = Redis down (fail open).”
To claim Stripe webhook event — given event key; gives back a StripeWebhookClaimResult (async):
  Get misc Redis → misc Redis.
  If misc Redis's status is not "ready", give back "unavailable".
  Try catch, and take its data (as result) and error:
    • set misc Redis:
      • event key
      • processing
      • "PX"
      • processing TTL ms
      • "NX"
  If error is set, give back "unavailable".
  If result is set, give back "claimed".
  Try catch (misc Redis's entry for event key), and take its data (as existing).
  Give back "duplicate_completed" if existing is completed, otherwise "in_flight".

Complete Stripe webhook event — given event key (async):
  Try catch:
    • set get misc Redis:
      • event key
      • completed
      • "PX"
      • completed TTL ms

To release Stripe webhook event — given event key (async):
  Try catch (delete get misc Redis (event key)).

“Two-state webhook idempotency: a processing lock is taken before handling, but the event only counts as a duplicate once marked COMPLETED (via the ctx.webhookIdempotency hooks). A failed run deletes the lock so Stripe's retry of the same event id reprocesses instead of being dropped. If Redis is unavailable or errors, the request is allowed through (fail-open), except for events that must never run twice concurrently (see isStripeWebhookLockRequired), which are 500ed so Stripe retries later.”
Stripe idempotency middleware — given c and next (async):
  Let context be c's entry for "ctx".
  From context, take Stripe event, org, and env.
  Set the webhook ack mode to a classify Stripe webhook ack mode (event: Stripe event).
  Build Stripe webhook event key (org ID: org's ID, env, and event ID: Stripe event's ID) → event key.
  Claim Stripe webhook event (event key), and call the result claim.
  If claim is "unavailable":
    If Stripe event is Stripe webhook lock required:
      Log an error "[stripeIdempotencyMiddleware] Redis unavailable and event requires the lock, asking Stripe to retry: {Stripe event's ID}".
      Give back c's JSON (no received, lock unavailable, and 500).
    “Redis down or errored - fail open”
    Warn "[stripeIdempotencyMiddleware] Redis unavailable, allowing through: {Stripe event's ID}".
    Run next.
    Stop here.
  If any of these is true:
    • claim is "duplicate_completed"
    • claim is "in_flight" and the webhook ack mode is "early"
  then:
    Log "[stripeIdempotencyMiddleware] Duplicate webhook event detected, skipping: {Stripe event's ID}".
    Give back c's JSON (received, duplicate, and 200).
  If claim is "in_flight":
    “Sync event still in flight — 500 keeps Stripe retrying until completed.”
    Log "[stripeIdempotencyMiddleware] Sync webhook event in flight, asking Stripe to retry: {Stripe event's ID}".
    Give back c's JSON (no received, in flight, and 500).
  Set the webhook idempotency to an object with:
    • mark completed: a function giving back a complete Stripe webhook event (event key)
    • release: a function giving back release Stripe webhook event (event key)
  Run next.

        • failure reason: error's message if error is an error, otherwise error as text

      Run next.

      Stop here.

  Start tracer span ("stripe.webhook.deferred"), and call the result deferred span.

  To run webhook:

      • context with span
      • a function giving back nothing's then (next)'s then, and if that fails' finally (a function giving back end deferred span):
        • a function that:
          If c's error is set, fail with c's error.
          Mark idempotency completed, and give back the result.
        Record deferred span exception (error).

  Get wait until (c) → wait until.

    If anything fails (call the problem error):
      Log an error "Stripe webhook waitUntil failed: {error}" (with error).
      “The chain settles the claim + span itself once started; only a failure BEFORE start needs rescheduling so the event isn't lost.”
      If webhook run is missing, Set immediate (a function giving back nothing).
  Otherwise:
    Set immediate (a function giving back nothing).
  Give back c's JSON (received and 200).

##### server/src/external/stripe/webhookHandlers/handleStripeSubscriptionUpdated/tasks/syncCustomerProductStatus/getStripeOwnedFieldUpdates.ts
Type StripeOwnedFieldUpdates: an InsertCustomerProduct.

“Stripe's `subscription.updated` carries the whole subscription, but only `previous_attributes` says what actually changed. A Stripe subscription can hold Autumn products whose trial or collection method Stripe never knew about (a trial product merged onto a shared paid subscription, a trial that lives in a schedule phase), so copying `trial_end` / `collection_method` from the subscription on every event silently erases them. Only mirror those fields when Stripe itself changed them; status is always Stripe's to own. Even when Stripe did change `trial_end`, a shared subscription can carry both its own trial and an Autumn-only one, so `trial_ends_at` moves only on products whose trial was Stripe's — i.e. matched Stripe's previous value. Autumn keeps ms and Stripe keeps seconds, so the match is at second precision, as in `normalizeCustomerProductTimestamps`. Pass `current` to skip no-op writes. Omit it for a blind bulk write, where every field Stripe changed is written.”
Trial was stripes — given current trial ends at and previous Stripe trial end; gives back true/false:
  Let previous Stripe trial ends at be the ms of previous Stripe trial end if previous Stripe trial end is set (otherwise nothing).
  If current trial ends at is missing or previous Stripe trial ends at is missing:
    Give back whether current trial ends at is previous Stripe trial ends at.
  Give back whether truncate ms to second precision (current trial ends at) is previous Stripe trial ends at.

To get Stripe owned field updates — given previous attributes, current, Stripe trial ends at, and Stripe collection method; gives back a StripeOwnedFieldUpdates:
  Let updates be an empty object.
  Let trial end changed mean previous attributes has a "trial_end" key.
  If trial end changed is true:
    Let new trial ends at be Stripe trial ends at, or nothing if that's missing.
    Let current trial ends at be current's trial ends at, or nothing if that's missing.
    Let should write trial ends at be depending on whether current is set:
      • if so: trial was stripes (only if current trial ends at is not new trial ends at):
        • current trial ends at
        • previous Stripe trial end: previous attributes' trial end
      • if not: true
    If should write trial ends at, set updates' trial ends at to new trial ends at.
  Let collection method changed mean previous attributes has a "collection_method" key.
  If all of these are true:
    • collection method changed is true
    • current is missing or current's collection method is not Stripe collection method
  then:
    Set updates' collection method to Stripe collection method.
  Give back updates.

##### server/src/external/stripe/webhookHandlers/handleStripeSubscriptionScheduleUpdated/getSchedulePhaseMoves.ts

    Skip it if the absolute value of old start ms minus new start ms is less than Stripe second precision ms.
    Add an object with old start ms and new start ms to moves.
  Give back moves.

##### server/src/external/stripe/webhookHandlers/handleStripeSubscriptionDeleted/tasks/processConsumablePricesForSubscriptionDeleted.ts
“Checks if the subscription was canceled during/at trial end. When a trialing subscription is canceled at period end, `ended_at` equals `trial_end`. In this case, we should skip arrear charges since trial usage is free.”

  Let trial end be Stripe subscription's trial end.
  Let ended at be Stripe subscription's ended at.
  If trial end is missing or ended at is missing, give back whether false.
  “If ended_at equals trial_end, the subscription was canceled at trial end”
  Give back whether trial end is ended at.

“Creates a single invoice for all usage-based (arrear) prices across all customer products when a subscription is deleted. Skips creating an arrear invoice if: 1. The subscription has metered items (Stripe handles metered billing automatically) 2. The cancellation was immediate (not end-of-period) - we don't charge overage on immediate cancels 3. The subscription was canceled at trial end - trial usage is free Note: Autumn-initiated deletions are filtered out before this via the lock mechanism in setupStripeSubscriptionDeletedContext.”
To process consumable prices for subscription deleted — given event context (async):
  From event context, take Stripe subscription, full customer, and customer products.
  “Skip if subscription has metered items - Stripe handles metered billing automatically”
  If Stripe subscription has metered items, stop here.
  “Skip if this was an immediate cancellation (not end-of-period) We only bill arrear usage when the subscription naturally ends at period end This matches the behavior of customer-level consumables (metered) where Stripe also doesn't charge overage on immediate cancels”
  If Stripe subscription was immediate Stripe cancellation, stop here.
  “Skip if the subscription was canceled at trial end - trial usage is free”
  If Stripe subscription was trial cancellation:
    Log "[subscription.deleted] Subscription canceled at trial end, skipping consumable charges".
    Stop here.
  Let disable overage billing mean the org should disable overage billing (given customer ID: event context's full customer's ID and customer config: event context's full customer's config).
  “1. Generate arrear line items Use ended_at (when subscription was actually deleted) as the period end. This handles mid-cycle cancellations correctly - we bill up to when they canceled, not up to when the cycle would have ended. Falls back to nowMs if ended_at is not available.”
  From the arrear line items of event context, take line items, invoice credit line items, update customer entitlements, and billing context:
    • period end ms: the ms of Stripe subscription's ended at if Stripe subscription's ended at is set (otherwise nothing)
    • no Stripe discountable
    • invoice credits: an object with:
      • idempotency scope: Stripe subscription's ID
      • fully offset overage: disable overage billing
  If disable overage billing is true and line items is not empty:
    Add to extra logs (extras: an object with overage billing disabled by config: true).
  Let invoice line items be one list combining:
    • an empty list if disable overage billing is true, otherwise line items
    • invoice credit line items
  If invoice line items is not empty:
    “2. Create, finalize, and pay a single invoice with all line items”
    Let invoice lines be the invoice add lines params of invoice line items.
    Create invoice for billing, and take its paid and invoice:
      • billing context
      • Stripe invoice action: an object with add line params: an object with lines: invoice lines
      • options: an object with skip subscription link: true
    Upsert invoice from billing:
      • Stripe invoice: invoice
      • full products: the products of customer products
      • full customer
    If paid is missing, stop here.
  “4. Reset usage balances for all affected customer entitlements (only if payment succeeded)”
  Batch update [CusEntService] (data: update customer entitlements).
  Delete cached full customer:
    • customer ID: event context's full customer's ID, or event context's full customer's internal ID if that's missing
    • source: "subscription-deleted-consumable-reset"
