##### server/src/external/stripe/webhookHandlers/handleStripeInvoicePaid/tasks/handleStripeInvoiceDiscounts.ts
To handle Stripe invoice discounts — given invoice paid context (async):
  “Handle coupon”
  From context, take org and env.
  From invoice paid context, take Stripe invoice and Stripe subscription ID.
  Create Stripe client (org, env, and legacy version) → Stripe client.
  If Stripe invoice's discounts is empty, stop here.
  Retrieve Stripe client's customers (Stripe invoice's customer), and call the result Stripe customer.
  Retrieve Stripe client's invoices, and call the result legacy invoice:
    • Stripe invoice's ID
    • expand: a list of "total_discount_amounts" and "discounts.coupon"
  Try the following:
    Let total discount amounts be legacy invoice's total discount amounts.
    “Log coupon information for debugging”
    For each discount in legacy invoice's discounts:
      Skip it if discount is text or discount has no "coupon" key.
      Let current coupon be discount's coupon.
      Skip it if current coupon is missing, current coupon is text, or current coupon's amount off is missing.
      Let roll suffix index be the position of "_roll_" in current coupon's ID (or -1).
      Let coupon ID be depending on whether roll suffix index is not negative 1:
        • if so: current coupon's ID's substring (0 and roll suffix index)
        • if not: current coupon's ID
      Let Autumn reward be reward repo's entry for an object with:
        • DB: the context
        • ID or internal ID: coupon ID
        • org ID: org's ID
        • env
      Let should rollover mean all of these are true:
        • Autumn reward is set
        • any of these is true:
          • Autumn reward's type is reward type's invoice credits
          • Autumn reward's type is reward type's free product
      Skip it if should not rollover.
      “Get ID of coupon”
      Retrieve Stripe client's coupons (coupon ID and expand: a list of "applies_to"), and call the result original coupon.
      Let current amount be current coupon's amount off.
      Let amount used be the first item in total discount amounts where item's discount is discount's ID's amount.
      Let new amount be current amount minus amount used.
      Let current expires at be current coupon's metadata's expires at as a number if current coupon's metadata expires at (otherwise nothing).
      Let discount finished mean new amount is zero or less.
      Let now be the now ms of Stripe customer (given Stripe client).
      Let expired be whether current expires at is set and current expires at is before now.
      If discount finished is true or expired is set:
        Log "Coupon {coupon ID}, stripeCus: {Stripe customer's ID}: credits used up or expired. discountFinished: {discount finished}, expired: {expired}".
        If Stripe subscription ID is set:
          Delete coupon from customer:
            • Stripe client
            • Stripe subscription ID
            • Stripe customer ID: Stripe invoice's customer
            • discount ID: discount's ID
        Move on to the next one.
      Log "Coupon {coupon ID}, stripeCus: {Stripe customer's ID}, updating amount from {current amount} to {new amount}".
      “Set expiry date”
      Let expires at mean current coupon's metadata expires at or nothing is set.
      Let discount config be Autumn reward's discount config.
      If discount config's duration type is coupon duration type's months:
        Set expires at to add months (the current time and discount config's duration value) as a timestamp as text.
      Create Stripe client's coupons, and call the result new coupon:
        • ID: "{coupon ID}_{generate ID ("roll")}"
        • name: current coupon's name
        • amount off: new amount
        • currency: Stripe invoice's currency
        • duration: "once"
        • applies to: original coupon's applies to
        • metadata: an object with expires at: expires at
      Raw Stripe client request:
        • "POST"
        • "/v1/customers/{Stripe invoice's customer}"
        • coupon: new coupon's ID
      Delete Stripe client's coupons (new coupon's ID).
      If Stripe subscription ID is set:
        Delete coupon from subscription (Stripe client, Stripe subscription ID, and discount ID: discount's ID).
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Log an error "invoice.paid: error updating coupon".
    Log an error (with error).

##### server/src/external/stripe/webhookHandlers/handleStripeInvoiceCreated/handleStripeInvoiceCreated.ts

    • customer products: event context's customer products
    • options: an object with:
      • skip non cycle invoices: whether should not store schedule proration invoice

“The invoice is finalized, so the difference between what it billed and what the line is worth now becomes a pending invoice item for the next invoice. Percent coupons from the finalized invoice still apply to the delta, fixed-amount coupons were already consumed, and the item is not discountable again so next cycle's coupons cannot touch it. Negative deltas (a credit line that grew) are carried the same way.”

##### server/src/external/stripe/webhookHandlers/common/buildBillingContextFromWebhook.ts
“Common fields between InvoiceCreatedContext and StripeSubscriptionDeletedContext. Discounts can be accessed from: - `stripeSubscription.discounts` (subscription-level discounts) - `stripeCustomer.discount` (customer-level discount)”
Type BaseWebhookEventContext: Stripe subscription, Stripe customer, full customer, customer products, now ms, and payment method.

“Builds a BillingContext for generating arrear (usage-in-arrear) invoice line items from Stripe webhook events. This function is used by both: - `invoice.created` webhook: to add consumable usage line items to the renewal invoice - `subscription.deleted` webhook: to create a final arrear invoice for usage If not provided, falls back to `eventContext.nowMs`. - For `invoice.created`: use `secondsToMs(stripeInvoice.period_end)` - For `subscription.deleted`: use `secondsToMs(stripeSubscription.ended_at)` if available **Why we use "just before" the period end:** The billing period calculation functions (`getCycleStart`, `getCycleEnd`) determine which cycle a given timestamp falls into. If we pass exactly `periodEndMs` (e.g., Feb 1), the functions will return the NEW cycle (Feb 1 - Mar 1) instead of the OLD cycle (Jan 1 - Feb 1) that we actually want to bill for. By subtracting 30 minutes, we ensure we're still "within" the old cycle: ``` periodEndMs = Feb 1 00:00:00 justBeforePeriodEndMs = Jan 31 23:30:00 getCycleStart(now = Jan 31 23:30) → Jan 1  ✓ (old cycle) getCycleEnd(now = Jan 31 23:30)   → Feb 1  ✓ (old cycle) ```”
To build billing context for arrear invoice — given event context and period end ms; gives back a BillingContext:
  From event context, take Stripe subscription, full customer, payment method, and now ms.
  “Use periodEndMs if provided, otherwise fall back to nowMs”
  Let effective period end ms be period end ms, or now ms if that's missing.
  “Use "just before" period end so getCycleStart/getCycleEnd return the OLD cycle that just ended, not the NEW cycle that's starting. See JSDoc above for detailed explanation.”
  Let just before period end ms be effective period end ms minus ms' minutes (30).
  Give back an object with:
    • full customer
    • full products: an empty list
    • feature quantities: an empty list
    • current epoch ms: just before period end ms
    • billing cycle anchor ms: the ms of Stripe subscription's billing cycle anchor
    • reset cycle anchor ms: the ms of Stripe subscription's billing cycle anchor
    • Stripe customer: Stripe subscription's customer
    • Stripe subscription
    • payment method: payment method, or nothing if that's missing
    • billing version: billing version's v2

“Builds a BillingContext for generating in-advance (upcoming cycle) invoice line items. Unlike `buildBillingContextForArrearInvoice`, this uses `periodEndMs` directly as `currentEpochMs`. This places us at the start of the NEW cycle, so: - `getCycleStart(now = Feb 1)` → Feb 1 (new cycle start) - `getCycleEnd(now = Feb 1)` → Mar 1 (new cycle end) This is correct for in-advance line items (base prices, prepaid, allocated) which are charging for the upcoming billing period.”
To build billing context for in advance invoice — given event context and period end ms; gives back a BillingContext:
  From event context, take Stripe subscription, full customer, and payment method.
  Give back an object with:
    • full customer
    • full products: an empty list
    • feature quantities: an empty list
    • current epoch ms: period end ms
    • billing cycle anchor ms: the ms of Stripe subscription's billing cycle anchor
    • reset cycle anchor ms: the ms of Stripe subscription's billing cycle anchor
    • Stripe customer: Stripe subscription's customer
    • Stripe subscription
    • payment method: payment method, or nothing if that's missing
    • billing version: billing version's v2

“Builds a BillingContext for previewing a subscription's upcoming invoice. Unlike its two siblings this anchors at `nowMs` rather than a period boundary: the caller has no invoice to key off, so `getNextCycleEvent` locates the next boundary itself and may land on a scheduled change rather than a plain renewal.”
To build billing context for invoice preview — given full customer, Stripe subscription, Stripe customer, Stripe discounts, and now ms; gives back a BillingContext:
  Give back an object with:
    • full customer
    • full products: an empty list
    • feature quantities: an empty list
    • current epoch ms: now ms
    • billing cycle anchor ms: the ms of Stripe subscription's billing cycle anchor
    • reset cycle anchor ms: the ms of Stripe subscription's billing cycle anchor
    • Stripe customer: Stripe customer, or Stripe subscription's customer if that's missing
    • Stripe subscription
    • Stripe discounts
    • billing version: billing version's v2

##### server/src/external/stripe/webhookHandlers/common/eventContextToArrearLineItems.ts
“Generates arrear (usage-in-arrear) line items from webhook event context. Used by: - `invoice.created` webhook: adds consumable usage line items to renewal invoice - `subscription.deleted` webhook: creates final arrear invoice for usage ## Discount handling Line items are created with `discountable: true`, which tells Stripe to auto-apply subscription/customer discounts when adding these items to an invoice. We also call `applyStripeDiscountsToLineItems` locally to calculate the discounted amounts for our own records (stored in `amountAfterDiscounts`). This is purely for audit/tracking purposes - Stripe handles the actual discount application. We use `skipDescriptionTag: true` so the description doesn't include "[inc. discount]" since we're not pre-deducting the discount from the amount sent to Stripe.”
Event context → arrear line items — given event context, period end ms, customer entitlement filter, Stripe discountable (default true), idempotency scope, and invoice credits; gives back an object with line items, invoice credit line items, update customer entitlements, and billing context (async):
  Build billing context for arrear invoice (event context and period end ms), and call the result billing context.
  “Collect line items from all customer products”
  Let line items start as an empty list.
  Let invoice credit line items be an empty list.
  Let update customer entitlements be an empty list.
  For each customer product in event context's customer products:
    From the arrear line items of customer product, take line items (as product line items), invoice credit line items (as product invoice credit line items), and update customer entitlements (as product updates):
      • billing context
      • filters: an object with:
        • customer entitlement filter
        • invoice credit customer entitlement filter: invoice credits' customer entitlement filter
      • options: an object with:
        • update next reset at: true
        • discountable: Stripe discountable
        • idempotency scope
        • invoice credits: (only if invoice credits is set) an object with:
          • idempotency scope: invoice credits' idempotency scope
          • fully offset overage: invoice credits' fully offset overage
          • include line items: invoice credits' include line items
    For each update in product updates:
      Let next reset at be update's updates' next reset at.
      Skip it if next reset at is not a number.
      Set update's updates to update's updates, but with:
        • next reset at set to clamp next reset at to pending billing cycle anchor:
          • billing cycle anchor resets at: customer product's billing cycle anchor resets at
          • current epoch ms: event context's now ms
          • next reset at
    Add everything in product line items to line items.
    Add everything in product invoice credit line items to invoice credit line items.
    Add everything in product updates to update customer entitlements.
  “Apply discounts to line items (for our DB records) Note: discountable: true lets Stripe auto-apply discounts, but we still need to track discounts on our side for accurate DB storage”
  Extract Stripe discounts → discounts:
    • Stripe subscription: event context's Stripe subscription
    • Stripe customer: event context's Stripe customer
  If discounts is not empty:
    Apply Stripe discounts to line items, and put the result in line items:
      • line items
      • discounts
      • options: an object with skip description tag: true
  “Per-feature skip_overage_billing spend limits exclude items from billing”
  From partition skipped overage line items (full customer: billing context's full customer and line items), take billable line items and skipped line items.
  “Log the arrear line items and customer entitlement updates”
  Log webhook arrear line items:
    • line items: billable line items
    • skipped line items
    • update customer entitlements
  Give back an object with:
    • line items: billable line items
    • invoice credit line items
    • update customer entitlements
    • billing context

##### server/src/external/stripe/subscriptions/utils/convertStripeSubscription.ts
“Maps Stripe subscription status to Autumn CusProductStatus. Stripe subscription statuses: - trialing: Customer is in trial period. Transitions to active after first payment. - active: Subscription is in good standing. - incomplete: Customer has 23 hours to make successful payment to activate. - incomplete_expired: Initial payment failed and customer didn't pay within 23 hours. Terminal state. - past_due: Payment on latest invoice failed. Subscription continues creating invoices. - canceled: Subscription was cancelled. Terminal state. - unpaid: Latest invoice hasn't been paid but subscription remains in place. - paused: Trial ended without payment method. Invoices no longer created.”

  Depending on Stripe status:
    • If it is "trialing" or "active":
      Give back customer product status's active.

      Give back customer product status's past due.
    • If it is "incomplete_expired" or "canceled":
      Give back customer product status's expired.
    • For anything else:
      “Unknown status - return unknown status”
      Give back customer product status's unknown.

##### server/src/external/stripe/prices/utils/buildIdempotencyKey.ts

##### server/src/external/stripe/prices/utils/classifyStripePriceUtils.ts
Is positive? — given amount and amount decimal; gives back true/false:
  Give back whether amount, or amount decimal, or 0 if that's missing as a number if that's missing is positive.

“Can this price ever bill money, regardless of current quantity? Distinct from `stripePriceToAmount`, which answers what an item bills *right now* — a metered item sits at quantity 0 between usage, yet still bills. Tiers are only present when expanded; an unexpanded tiered price is treated as billable so an unknown price is surfaced rather than silently ignored.”
Stripe price can bill — given Stripe price; gives back true/false:
  If Stripe price is missing, give back whether false.
  If Stripe price's billing scheme is "tiered":
    Let tiers be Stripe price's tiers.
    If tiers is empty, give back whether true.
    Give back whether tiers has a tier where any of these is true:
      • tier's unit amount is positive (given tier's unit amount decimal)
      • tier's flat amount is positive (given tier's flat amount decimal)
  Give back whether Stripe price's unit amount is positive (given Stripe price's unit amount decimal).

##### server/src/external/stripe/prices/utils/convertStripePriceUtils.ts
Tier amount — given amount and amount decimal; gives back a Decimal:
  Give back amount decimal, or amount if that's missing, or 0 if that's missing.

“Volume: the whole quantity bills at the single tier it falls into.”
Volume tiers → amount — given tiers and quantity; gives back a Decimal:
  Let tier be the first candidate in tiers where candidate's up to is missing or quantity is at most candidate's up to, or the last of tiers if that's missing.
  Give back a tier amount (tier's flat amount and tier's flat amount decimal) plus a tier amount (tier's unit amount and tier's unit amount decimal) times quantity.

“Graduated: each tier bills the units falling inside its own band.”
Graduated tiers → amount — given tiers and quantity; gives back a Decimal:
  Let total start as 0.
  Let band start start as 0.
  For each tier in tiers:
    Stop the loop if quantity is at most band start.
    Let band end be tier's up to, or infinity if that's missing.
    Let units be the smaller of quantity and band end minus band start.
    Set total to total plus a tier amount (tier's flat amount and tier's flat amount decimal) plus a tier amount (tier's unit amount and tier's unit amount decimal) times units.
    Set band start to band end.
  Give back total.

“What a Stripe price bills for `quantity`, in the currency's smallest unit. Null when the price is tiered but its `tiers` were not expanded — the amount is unknowable rather than zero.”
Stripe price → amount — given Stripe price and quantity; gives back a number (or nothing):
  If Stripe price's billing scheme is "tiered":

##### server/src/external/stripe/customers/billingDetails/operations/applyStripeTaxIdChanges.ts

  Let deleted be an empty list.

      Delete Stripe client's customers tax ID (Stripe customer ID and tax ID's ID).

“Non-prod failure injection: an event whose Stripe object carries `test_webhook_fail` (pass it via the billing API's `metadata` param) fails EVERY delivery until the marker is removed from the live decision object — remove it and the next delivery succeeds. Deterministic outage simulation. Marker value picks the live decision object: "customer" → the Stripe customer's metadata (toggling it emits no self-healing events for the marked object); anything else → the marked object itself.”

  If the NODE_ENV environment variable is "production", stop here.
  Let event be the Stripe event.
  Let object be event's data's object.
  Let marker value be object's metadata's entry for test webhook fail metadata key.
  If marker value is missing, stop here.
  “Re-fetch failing open: a broken test helper must never wedge processing.”
  Try catch, and take its data (as live metadata) and error:
    • depending on whether marker value is "customer":
      • if so: retrieve live customer metadata (Stripe client: the Stripe client and object)
      • if not: retrieve live metadata (Stripe client: the Stripe client and object)
  If error is set, stop here.
  If live metadata's entry for test webhook fail metadata key is set:
    Fail with an error: "Simulated webhook failure for {event's type} {event's ID} — remove {test webhook fail metadata key} metadata from the live {"customer" if marker value is "customer", otherwise object's object} to let it pass".

    • internal product IDs: a list of product's internal ID

    • processor type: processor type's revenue cat

    • total

    • refunded amount: 0
    • currency

    • items: an empty list
    • created at: created at

  If customer's ID is set, Delete cached full customer (customer ID: customer's ID and source: "recordRevenueCatInvoice").

“Provisions a RevenueCat customer product via V2 attach. RC payments happen on App Store / Play Store / etc., so Autumn never reads or writes Stripe state for these flows. We funnel through V2 `attach()` so the new cus_product, entitlements, prices, line items, webhooks, and rollover carry-overs all run through the same pipeline as Stripe/Vercel, just with the Stripe and external-PSP guards disabled. Handles new / upgrade / downgrade scenarios via `computeAttachPlan`'s transition logic — the caller does not need to expire the outgoing cus_product manually. Transitions are forced immediate (`plan_schedule`) since RC is the payment source-of-truth; we don't schedule downgrades end-of-cycle the way a Stripe-billed attach would.”

    • skip external psp guard: true

    • params: an object with:

      • no billing changes: true
      • enable plan immediately: true
      • plan schedule: "immediate"
      • everything in depending on whether revenuecat metadata is set:
        • if so: an object with metadata: revenuecat metadata
        • if not: an empty object

        • if so: an object with feature quantities: feature quantities
        • if not: an empty object

    • skip Autumn checkout
  Get customer product repo by customer and product, and call the result customer products:
    • internal customer ID: customer's internal ID

    • env

##### server/src/external/revenueCat/misc/revenuecatMcp.ts

“Call a tool on RevenueCat's hosted MCP server (the only supported way to write test-store prices). Auth is the org's RC token — OAuth (`atk_`) or secret (`sk_`).”

  Fetch impl, and call the result response:
    • rc mcp URL

      • authorization: "Bearer {access token}"

      • accept: "application/json, text/event-stream"
    • body: an object with as JSON
  If response's ok is missing, fail with an error: "RevenueCat MCP error ({response's status})".
  “Streamable-HTTP MCP replies as SSE and may emit preamble frames (ping, progress) before the result — pick the frame that carries result/error.”
  Let text be response's text.
  Let candidates be text split on "
", after these steps:
    1. Turn each line into line without surrounding spaces
    2. Keep only those where line starts with "data:" or line starts with "{"
    3. Turn each line into line with /^data:\s*/ replaced by ""
  Start with no parsed yet.

    Try the following:
      Set frame to candidate parsed from JSON.
    If anything fails:
      Move on to the next one.
    If frame's result is set or frame's error is set:
      Set parsed to frame.
      Stop the loop.
  If parsed is missing, fail with an error: "RevenueCat MCP returned no result frame: {the first 200 of text}".
  If parsed's error is set:
    Fail with an error: "RevenueCat MCP tool error: {parsed's error's message, or "unknown" if that's missing}".
  If parsed's result is error:
    Fail with an error: "RevenueCat MCP tool "{name}" failed: {the first 300 of parsed's result's content as JSON}".

##### server/src/external/redis/getReachableDragonflyUrl.ts
“Map a stored dragonfly URL to one that is actually reachable from the current process. Background: orgs whose `redis_config` points at the SHARED dragonfly instance store its private VPC URL (`CACHE_V2_DRAGONFLY_URL`) in the config row. That URL is only reachable from inside our AWS Fargate tasks. Off-AWS callers (local dev, trigger.dev workers) need the public mirror `CACHE_V2_DRAGONFLY_PUBLIC_URL` instead. Heuristic: if the URL equals the private shared URL AND we're not on AWS, swap to public. Anything else (per-org dragonfly, Upstash, Redis Cloud, etc.) is returned untouched — we have no opinion about those. Returns the same input string when no swap applies, so callers can use it transparently in place of the raw URL.”
To get reachable dragonfly URL — given URL; gives back text:
  If on aws ecs gives back something, give back URL.
  Let private URL be the CACHE_V2_DRAGONFLY_URL environment variable without surrounding spaces.
  If private URL is missing or URL without surrounding spaces is not private URL, give back URL.
  Let public URL be the CACHE_V2_DRAGONFLY_PUBLIC_URL environment variable without surrounding spaces.
  If public URL is missing, give back URL.
  Give back public URL.

##### server/src/external/redis/initRedisV2.ts
Let raw dragonfly URL be the CACHE_V2_DRAGONFLY_URL environment variable without surrounding spaces.
Let dragonfly URL be get reachable dragonfly URL (raw dragonfly URL) if raw dragonfly URL is set (otherwise nothing).
Let has Redis v2 config mean dragonfly URL is set.

Let Redis v2 be depending on whether dragonfly URL is set:
  • if so: create pooled standby Redis connection:
    • cache URL: dragonfly URL
    • region: "{current region}:v2"
    • Redis type: "subject-primary"
    • command timeout: Redis v2 command timeout ms
  • if not: create Redis connection:
    • cache URL: ""
    • region: "{current region}:v2"
    • Redis type: "subject-primary"
    • command timeout: Redis v2 command timeout ms

Let alternate instance URLs be an object with:
  • Upstash: the CACHE_V2_UPSTASH_URL environment variable without surrounding spaces, or nothing if that's empty
  • Redis: the CACHE_V2_REDIS_URL environment variable without surrounding spaces, or nothing if that's empty

##### server/src/external/redis/utils/redisOpTimeouts.ts
“Opt-in per-operation Redis bounds (positive-limiting): anything absent here keeps the client's `commandTimeout` — 1s on V2, 10s on legacy. Only ops with a working non-Redis path belong here. Reads qualify by default; a write qualifies only when landing late or not at all is harmless — a TTL'd read-through cache write costs one extra miss, so `withTimeout` abandoning the promise is safe. Writes carrying state no other path can rebuild are not. Values are sized above each op's measured production p99.9. A value above the client's `commandTimeout` is inert: ioredis arms that timer per command at dispatch (offline-queued commands and pipeline members included), so on V2 the 1s ceiling ends the attempt first and the p99.9 figures below are measured against an already-truncated tail.”
Let Redis op timeout ms be an object with:
  • secret key get: 200
  • secret key set: 200
  • feature balances: 500
  • feature balances batch: 1200
  • subject pipeline: 1200

##### server/src/external/redis/utils/runRedisOp.ts
Let Redis warning interval ms be 30,000.

“Below this a retry cannot finish, so spend the budget on the fallback.”
Let min retry budget ms be 50.

Let standby retry reserve ratio be 0.25.
Let max standby retry reserve ms be 250.
Let last Redis warning at by source be an empty lookup table.

To get preferred attempt budget ms — given timeout ms; gives back a number (or nothing):
  If timeout ms is missing, give back nothing.
  Let retry reserve ms be the smaller of timeout ms times standby retry reserve ratio, rounded down and max standby retry reserve ms.
  If retry reserve ms is at least min retry budget ms:
    Give back timeout ms minus retry reserve ms.
  Otherwise:
    Give back timeout ms.

Classify error reason — given target Redis and error; gives back an UnavailableReason (or nothing):
  If target Redis's status is not "ready", give back "not_ready".
  Let message be error's message if error is an error, otherwise error as text.
  If message matches /ETIMEDOUT|timeout/i, give back "timeout".
  If message matches /ECONN|closed|writeable|max retries/i, give back "connection".
  Give back nothing.

Warn Redis unavailable — given source, reason, and error:
  Let key be "{source}:{reason}".
  Let now be the current time.
  Let last warning at be last Redis warning at by source's entry for key, or 0 if that's missing.
  If now minus last warning at is before Redis warning interval ms, stop here.
  Record now under key in last Redis warning at by source.
  Warn "[redis] operation unavailable" (with source, reason, and error).

“Runs a Redis operation. Returns the operation's value on success; throws `RedisUnavailableError` on timeout/connection/not-ready failures. Callers that want to fail open catch at the request boundary (see `withRedisFallback`). Callers distinguishing "null value" from "missing" still inspect the return value — this helper does not interpret nullish. When the client is not ready this throws immediately rather than letting the command sit in ioredis's offline queue until `commandTimeout` (10s in prod on the primary client) stalls the request. `queueIfNotReady` opts back into the offline queue: the command waits out a reconnect (bounded by `commandTimeout`) instead of failing instantly. For ops with no fallback — invalidations, where a dropped command means silent cache staleness — riding out a sub-second blip beats dropping the op.”
To run Redis op — given operation, source, Redis instance, queue if not ready (default false), retry on standby (default false), use read pool (default false), and timeout ms; gives back a T (async):
  Let read lane lease be acquire Redis read lane (Redis instance) if retry on standby is true and use read pool is true (otherwise nothing).
  Let target Redis be read lane lease's Redis, or Redis instance if that's missing.
  Let Redis attempts be an empty list.
  Try the following:
    If queue if not ready is false and target Redis's status is not "ready":
      Let reason be "not_ready".
      Warn Redis unavailable (source and reason).
      Fail with a Redis unavailable error.
    “Plan one budget for the whole op, not one per attempt: a retry must not double the ceiling the caller sized against its non-Redis fallback.”
    Let deadline at be the current time plus timeout ms if timeout ms is set (otherwise nothing).
    To run attempt — given Redis and budget ms:
      Let attempt be an operation (Redis).
      Add attempt to Redis attempts.
      If budget ms is set:
        Give back a with timeout:
          • timeout ms: budget ms
          • function: a function giving back attempt
          • timeout message: "[redis] {source} timeout after {budget ms}ms"
      Otherwise:
        Give back attempt.
    Try the following:
      Let router be get standby Redis router (target Redis) if retry on standby is true (otherwise nothing).
      If router is missing, Run attempt (target Redis and timeout ms), and give back the result.
      Split router's ordered into preferred and alternate.
      “Only shorten the preferred attempt for an alternate worth retrying on. A penalized alternate still beats the non-Redis fallback after failure.”
      Let preferred attempt budget ms be depending on whether router is usable (alternate):
        • if so: get preferred attempt budget ms (timeout ms)
        • if not: timeout ms
      Let reserved retry budget ms be depending on whether timeout ms is set and preferred attempt budget ms is set:
        • if so: timeout ms minus preferred attempt budget ms
        • if not: 0
      Try the following:
        Run attempt (preferred and preferred attempt budget ms), and call the result value.
        Record router outcome (connection: preferred).
        Give back value.
      If anything fails (call the problem first error):
        Record router outcome (connection: preferred and error: first error).
        Let remaining ms be deadline at minus the current time if deadline at is set (otherwise nothing).
        “A delayed timeout callback must not consume the budget deliberately reserved for the alternate connection.”
        Let retry budget ms be nothing if remaining ms is missing; otherwise the larger of remaining ms and reserved retry budget ms.
        Let can retry mean all of these are true:
          • alternate's status is "ready"
          • first error is connection level Redis
          • retry budget ms is missing or retry budget ms is at least min retry budget ms
        If cannot retry, fail with first error.
        Try the following:
          Run attempt (alternate and retry budget ms), and call the result value.
          Record router outcome (connection: alternate).
          Log "[redis] standby served a read the preferred connection failed" (with source and type).
          Give back value.
        If anything fails (call the problem retry error):
          Record router outcome (connection: alternate and error: retry error).
          Fail with retry error.
    If anything fails (call the problem error):
      Let classified be a classify error reason (target Redis and error).
      Let reason be classified, or "other" if that's missing.
      Warn Redis unavailable (source, reason, and error).
      Fail with a Redis unavailable error.
  Either way, finally:
    If read lane lease is set and Redis attempts is empty, Release read lane lease.
    If read lane lease is set and Redis attempts is not empty:
      Nothing.

“Fail-open variant of `runRedisOp`. On failure: runs `onError`, returns `undefined`. Use this from mutation/invalidation paths where a Redis outage shouldn't propagate — the cache goes stale, not the request.”
To try Redis op — given operation, source, Redis instance, queue if not ready, retry on standby, use read pool, timeout ms, and on error; gives back a T (or nothing) (async):
  Try the following:
    Run Redis op, and give back the result:
      • operation
      • source
      • Redis instance
      • queue if not ready
      • retry on standby
      • use read pool
      • timeout ms
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    Trigger on error (error).
    Give back nothing.

##### server/src/external/redis/initUtils/registerRedisCommands.ts
Let Redis error log cooldown ms be 30,000.

“Build a per-instance deduping logger for ioredis "error" events so an unreachable Redis doesn't spam the log tens of times a second. This is what otherwise floods `bun tw` µVM boot with `[Redis] Connection error: ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:6379` while Dragonfly is still starting (ioredis reconnects ~every 50ms). Logs the first occurrence of a message, then suppresses repeats of the SAME message within the cooldown. Prod-safe: a real, persistent error is still surfaced (once per cooldown). The dedup state is closed over PER instance (not module-level), so one connection's error is never swallowed just because another logged the same string recently — each connection dedupes independently.”
To make Redis error logger — gives back a function:
  Start with no last message yet.
  Let last logged at start as 0.
  Give back a function of message that:
    Let now be the current time.
    If message is last message and now minus last logged at is before Redis error log cooldown ms, stop here.
    Set last message to message.
    Set last logged at to now.
    Log an error "[Redis] Connection error:" (with message).

“Configure a Redis instance with the FullSubject (V2 cache) custom commands.”

  Define Redis instance command ("publishCachedFullSubject" and lua: publish cached full subject script).
  Define Redis instance command:
    • "updateFullSubjectCustomerDataV2"

  Define Redis instance command:

“Wraps the `exec()` of an ioredis Pipeline or Multi so the batched round trip shows up as a single parent span (`redis.pipeline` / `redis.multi`) in Axiom. Individual command spans continue to fire for each queued command; this span gives us total batch latency and a command-count attribute so we can tell at a glance whether a request was pipelined.”
To wrap pipeline exec — given pipeline, tracer, region, Redis type, and kind:
  Let original exec be pipeline's exec.
  If original exec is not a function, stop here.
  Set pipeline's exec to a function of this and any other exec args that:
    Start with no span context yet.
    Try the following:
      Start tracer span ("redis.{kind}" and kind: span kind's client) → span.
      Set span attribute ("db.system" and "redis").
      Set span attribute ("db.operation" and kind in uppercase).
      If region is set, Set span attribute ("db.redis.region" and region).
      Set span attribute ("db.redis.type" and Redis type).
      Let queue be pipeline's queue.
      Let command count be depending on whether queue is a list:
        • if so: the number of queue
        • if not: the number of pipeline if the number of pipeline is a number (otherwise nothing)
      If command count is a number, Set span attribute ("db.redis.pipeline.command_count" and command count).
      If queue is a list:
        Let names be queue, after these steps:
          1. Take each one's name
          2. Keep only those where n is text
          3. The first 20 of ␀them
          4. Join them with ","
        If names is set, Set span attribute ("db.redis.pipeline.commands" and names).

##### server/src/external/redis/otel/parseRedisKeyContext.ts
“Parses business context (org_id, customer_id, entity_id) out of the Redis key patterns used by the app. Supported patterns: - `{orgId}:env:customer:version:customerId` - `{orgId}:env:customer:version:customerId:entity:entityId` - `{orgId}:env:customer:version:customerId:balances:featureId[...]` - `{orgId}:env:customer_guard:customerId` - `{orgId}:env:test_cache_delete_guard:customerId` - `{orgId}:env:fullcustomer:version:customerId` - `{orgId}:env:fullcustomer:guard:customerId` - `{orgId}:env:fullcustomer:pathidx:customerId` - `{customerId}:orgId:env:full_subject[:...]` (FullSubject V2 — hash-tagged on customerId, orgId is the first unbraced segment; covers base, shared-balances, and view-epoch shapes) - `{customerId}:orgId:env:entity:entityId:full_subject` (FullSubject V2 entity variant) Any parsing failure is swallowed — callers get `{}` back.”
Type RedisCacheGeneration: one of "v1" or "v2".

Type RedisKeyContext: an object.

To strip hash tag — given segment; gives back text:
  If segment starts with "{" and segment ends with "}", give back segment from position 1 up to negative 1.
  Give back segment.

To parse Redis key context — given key; gives back a RedisKeyContext:
  If key is missing, give back an empty object.
  Try the following:
    Let parts be key split on ":".
    If parts has fewer than 3 items, give back an empty object.
    Let first be the first of parts.
    “FullSubject V2 keys — hash-tagged on customerId, orgId is the first unbraced segment. Shapes: {customerId}:orgId:env:full_subject[:...] {customerId}:orgId:env:entity:entityId:full_subject”
    If first starts with "{", first ends with "}", and "full_subject" is in parts:
      Strip hash tag (first), and call the result customer ID.
      Let org ID be item #2 of parts.
      Let entity ID be item #5 of parts if item #4 of parts is "entity", item #5 of parts is set, and item #6 of parts is "full_subject" (otherwise nothing).
      Give back an object with:
        • customer ID
        • org ID
        • entity ID
        • generation: "v2"
    “{orgId}:env:<kind>:...”
    If first starts with "{" and first ends with "}":
      Strip hash tag (first), and call the result org ID.
      Let kind be item #3 of parts.
      If kind is "fullcustomer":
        “{orgId}:env:fullcustomer:(version|guard|pathidx):customerId”
        Let customer ID be item #5 of parts.
        Give back an object with org ID, customer ID, and generation: "v1".
      If kind is "customer":
        “{orgId}:env:customer:version:customerId[:entity:entityId][...]”
        Let customer ID be item #5 of parts.
        Start with no entity ID yet.
        Let entity index be the position of "entity" in parts (or -1).
        If entity index is not negative 1 and parts' entry for entity index plus 1 is set:
          Set entity ID to parts' entry for entity index plus 1.
        Give back an object with:
          • org ID
          • customer ID
          • entity ID
          • generation: "v1"
      If kind is "customer_guard" or kind is "test_cache_delete_guard":
        Give back an object with org ID, customer ID: item #4 of parts, and generation: "v1".
      “Unknown kind, but orgId is still useful.”
      Give back an object with org ID and generation: "v1".
    Give back an empty object.
  If anything fails:
    Give back an empty object.

##### server/src/external/redis/otel/redisSlowlogConfig.ts
“Redis slowlog thresholds (per-operation SLOs). Scope: the V2 FullSubject cache surface only. Commands outside this set fall through to `DEFAULT_THRESHOLD`, which is intentionally lax so it doesn't flap on untuned ops. Two independent lookups compose into an effective threshold: 1. Per-operation base threshold ("how long should this command take once it gets there?" — service time + same-region network) 2. Per-region additive baseline ("how much extra network cost do I expect when hitting Redis in this region?") effective slowMs = base.slowMs + regionBaselineMs See `redis-slow-command-investigation.md` for the Axiom query templates used to tune these numbers.”

Let default region baseline ms be 0.

  • a threshold (operation: "expire", slow ms: 15, and severe ms: 100)
  • a threshold (operation: "setCachedFullSubject", slow ms: 50, and severe ms: 300)
  • a threshold (operation: "adjustSubjectBalance", slow ms: 50, and severe ms: 300)
  • a threshold:
    • operation: "updateFullSubjectCustomerDataV2"
    • slow ms: 50
    • severe ms: 300
  • a threshold:
    • operation: "updateFullSubjectEntityDataV2"

##### server/src/external/redis/actions/oauthRefreshReplay/oauthRefreshReplay.ts
Let refresh replay TTL seconds be 30.
Let refresh replay pending be "pending".
Let claim max attempts be 200.
Let claim poll ms be 25.

“Keyed on a fingerprint of the whole refresh request (resource + authorization header + normalized body), not on the refresh token: two different requests carrying the same token are different grants and must not share a response.”
To build o auth refresh replay key — given request fingerprint:
  Give back "oauth:refresh-replay:{request fingerprint}".

Type OAuthRefreshReplayClaim: an object.

“Nothing to replay and no key to hand back: the caller mints unguarded.”
Let no key held be an object with body: nothing and holds key: false.

“Single-flight guard for OAuth refresh-token replays: the first caller claims the key (SET NX) and mints tokens; concurrent replays of the same refresh request spin until the winner stores its response, then return that body. Dedupe is an optimisation, never a dependency: if Redis cannot answer, the claim comes back holding no key and the token endpoint carries on unguarded. Only a genuine spin-out — the winner held the key past its polling budget — returns null, because minting alongside it would race the token rotation.”
To claim o auth refresh replay — given key; gives back an OAuthRefreshReplayClaim (or nothing) (async):
  Try the following:
    Get misc Redis → misc Redis.
    Count attempt from 0 while attempt is less than claim max attempts:
      Try Redis op, and call the result value:
        • operation: a function giving back misc Redis's entry for key
        • source: "oauth-refresh-replay:read"
        • Redis instance: misc Redis
      “undefined = Redis unavailable (vs null = key missing) — bail out.”
      If value is missing, give back no key held.
      If value is set and value is not refresh replay pending:
        Give back an object with body: a decrypt data (value) parsed from JSON and holds key: false.
      If value is missing:
        Try Redis op, and call the result claimed:
          • operation: a function giving back set misc Redis:
            • key
            • refresh replay pending
            • "EX"
            • refresh replay TTL seconds
            • "NX"
          • source: "oauth-refresh-replay:claim"
          • Redis instance: misc Redis
        If claimed is missing, give back no key held.
        If claimed is set, give back an object with body: nothing and holds key: true.
      Run timeout (claim poll ms).
    Give back nothing.
  If anything fails:
    “Redis missing, or a stored response we cannot decrypt/parse. Either way there is nothing to replay, so mint instead of failing the refresh.”
    Give back no key held.

“Drops a claim the winner never stored a response for, so a retry of the same refresh request re-races immediately instead of spinning out the claim's TTL.”
To release o auth refresh replay — given key (async):
  Try the following:
    Get misc Redis → misc Redis.
    Try Redis op:
      • operation: a function giving back delete misc Redis (key)
      • source: "oauth-refresh-replay:release"
      • Redis instance: misc Redis
  If anything fails, ignore it.

“Winner stores its (encrypted) token response for spinning replayers.”
To store o auth refresh replay — given body and key (async):
  Try the following:
    Get misc Redis → misc Redis.
    Try Redis op:
      • operation: a function giving back set misc Redis:
        • key
        • encrypt data (body as JSON)
        • "EX"
        • refresh replay TTL seconds
      • source: "oauth-refresh-replay:store"
      • Redis instance: misc Redis
  If anything fails, ignore it.

##### server/src/external/motherduck/initMotherDuck.ts
Let md schema be an object with ce balances cache.
Type MotherDuckDb: a DuckDBDatabase.

“v2 is a TRANSIENT database (no historical snapshots, 1-day failsafe): CREATE OR REPLACE churn on the old lake_cache parked every prior version in a 7-day failsafe window and billed it. This is a cache rebuilt from Iceberg; nothing in it ever needs recovery.”
Let default database be "lake_cache_v2".

“Shed to the caller's unavailable-path instead of queueing behind a saturated pool — a lesson from the PgBouncer era.”

  Give back parsed if parsed is a whole number and parsed is positive, otherwise default pool size.

“MotherDuck meters concurrent queries account-wide; DuckDB runs one query per pooled connection, so fleet ceiling = processes x pool size.”

  Give back "[initMotherDuck] potential fleet concurrency ({fleet connections}) exceeds MOTHERDUCK_MAX_CONCURRENT ({md account concurrency ceiling}) — pools are lazy so this only bites if every process serves balance sorts; lower MOTHERDUCK_POOL_MAX or raise the ceiling to match the MotherDuck plan.".

##### server/src/external/motherduck/mdPoolMonitor.ts

##### server/src/external/motherduck/refreshCeBalancesCache.ts
Let glue region be the LAKE_GLUE_REGION environment variable, or "us-east-2" if that's missing.
Let glue database be "internal".

“metadata_location is interpolated into SQL (DDL can't take bind params), so it must match the lake's exact shape before we trust it.”
Metadata location pattern — given table:
  Give back a new reg exp:
    • "^s3://autumn-lake-prod-us-east-2/internal/{table}/[A-Za-z0-9/_.-]+\.metadata\.json$"

Let glue client be a new glue client (region: glue region).
Let live loose balance cache predicate be "b.balance != 0 OR b.unlimited IS TRUE OR a.feature_type = 'boolean'".

“The Glue pointer advances on every RW sink commit — always read it fresh; a pinned metadata.json 404s within hours once compaction expires it.”
To get current lake metadata location — given table; gives back text (async):
  Send glue client (a new get table command (database name: glue database and name: table)), and call the result response.
  Let location be response's table's parameters' metadata location.
  If location is missing or location does not match a metadata location pattern (table):
    Fail with an error: "[refreshCeBalancesCache] unexpected metadata_location from Glue for {table}: {location}".
  Give back location.

“Aggregate once here (~1s/feature at query time otherwise); expiry is baked at refresh, which the 5-min staleness window already covers. granted ≈ allowance + adjustment (quantity lives only in PG). remaining/granted sums cover FINITE rows only; usage covers ALL rows (unlimited rows track real deductions, so −balance = their usage). The ORDER BY clusters row groups so per-feature top-N prunes. Reads the lake in one pass: the `ce_balances` intermediate this replaced was 114M rows rewritten per run for a table nothing else ever queried.”
Ce balance totals SQL — given ce metadata locations and totals table (default "ce_balance_totals"); gives back text:
  Give back "
	CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE main.{totals table} AS
	WITH b AS (
		{ce metadata locations, after these steps}
	)
	SELECT
		b.internal_customer_id,
		b.internal_feature_id,
		COALESCE(BOOL_OR(b.unlimited), false) AS is_unlimited,
		COALESCE(SUM(b.balance) FILTER (WHERE b.unlimited IS NOT TRUE), 0) AS total,
		COALESCE(SUM(COALESCE(a.allowance, 0) + COALESCE(b.adjustment, 0))
			FILTER (WHERE b.unlimited IS NOT TRUE), 0) AS granted_total,
		COALESCE(SUM(CASE
			WHEN b.unlimited IS TRUE THEN -(COALESCE(b.balance, 0) + COALESCE(b.entities_balance, 0))
			ELSE COALESCE(a.allowance, 0) + COALESCE(b.adjustment, 0) - COALESCE(b.balance, 0)
		END), 0) AS usage_total,
		COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE b.unlimited IS NOT TRUE) AS finite_rows
	FROM b
	LEFT JOIN main.ent_allowances a ON a.id = b.entitlement_id
	WHERE (b.expires_at IS NULL OR b.expires_at > epoch_ms(now()))
		AND (
			(
				b.customer_product_id IS NULL
				AND ({live loose balance cache predicate})
			)
			OR b.customer_product_id IN (SELECT id FROM main.cp_active)
		)
	GROUP BY 1, 2
	ORDER BY b.internal_feature_id, is_unlimited DESC, total DESC
".

Let in flight start as nothing.

“Never throws (a failed tick must not crash the cron); returns whether the refresh actually completed so one-shot callers can fail loudly.”
To refresh ce balances cache — given totals table; gives back an object with ok (async):
  If in flight is set:
    Log "[refreshCeBalancesCache] previous refresh still running — skipping tick".
    Give back an object with ok: true.
  Set in flight to the result of a function that:
    Let started at be performance's now.
    Do these at the same time:
      • for every table in ce lake tables, all at the same time → ce metadata locations:
        get current lake metadata location (table)
      • get current lake metadata location (table: "entitlements") → entitlement metadata location
      • get current lake metadata location (table: "customer_products") → customer product metadata location
      • get current lake metadata location (table: "features") → feature metadata location
    Let row count be a with mother duck rw:
      • run: a function that:
        Execute:
          • SQL's raw:
            • "
						CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE main.ent_allowances AS
						SELECT e.id, e.allowance, f.type AS feature_type
						FROM iceberg_scan('{entitlement metadata location}') e
						JOIN iceberg_scan('{feature metadata location}') f
							ON f.internal_id = e.internal_feature_id
					"
        “Statuses must mirror PG's ACTIVE_STATUSES — dead product-history rows otherwise inflate every aggregate (granted by 10-30x).”
        Execute:
          • SQL's raw:
            • "
						CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE main.cp_active AS
						SELECT id
						FROM iceberg_scan('{customer product metadata location}')
						WHERE status IN ('active', 'past_due')
					"
        Execute:
          • SQL's raw (a ce balance totals SQL (ce metadata locations and totals table))
        Execute, and call the result count result:
          • SQL's raw:
            • "SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM main.{totals table, or "ce_balance_totals" if that's missing}"
        Let first be depending on whether count result is a list:
          • if so: the first of count result
          • if not: the first of count result's rows
        Give back first's n, or 0 if that's missing as a number.
    Log "[refreshCeBalancesCache] rebuilt balance cache tables (rowCount = totals rows)" (with type, row count, metadata locations, and duration ms).
  Try the following:
    In flight.
    Give back an object with ok: true.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):

##### server/src/external/connect/attachSandboxStripeAccount.ts
“Per-worker Stripe bring-up for `bun tw` sandboxes — the half of `afterOrgCreated` the warm parent skips (`createStripeAccount: false`). It mints a Stripe Connect sub-account, binds it into the worker's LOCAL db as `test_stripe_connect.default_account_id` (NO `master_org_id`, so `shouldUseMaster` stays false and `createStripeCli` routes through `initMasterStripe({ accountId })`), then registers a webhook endpoint ON THE SUB-ACCOUNT (scoped client, NO `connect: true`) at the legacy route `/webhooks/stripe/<orgId>/<env>`. Because the endpoint lives on the sub-account, Stripe only delivers that sub-account's events there, so every worker stays isolated even though they all share the same hardcoded org id. This is the canonical single-call version, primarily for reference/local use. The orchestrator (see §9a) splits create-vs-bind across the platform key and the worker DB so a worker dying mid-bring-up can't orphan an untracked sub-account.”
To attach sandbox Stripe account — given org, user, env, public URL, and metadata (async):
  “1. Mint the sub-account via the master sandbox key.”
  Create connect account (org, user, and metadata) → account.
  “2. Bind in the LOCAL db — default_account_id only, NO master_org_id. OrgService.update clears the org cache and returns the updated row.”
  Update [OrgService], and call the result updated org:
    • org ID: org's ID
    • updates: an object with:
      • default currency: "usd"
      • test Stripe connect: org's test Stripe connect, or an empty object if that's missing, but with default account ID set to account's ID
  If updated org is missing:
    Fail with an error: "attachSandboxStripeAccount: org {org's ID} not found when binding default_account_id".
  “3. Sub-account-scoped client off the UPDATED org (a stale org would throw "no Stripe account linked" inside createStripeCli).”
  Create Stripe client (org: updated org and env) → Stripe client.
  “4. Webhook ON THE SUB-ACCOUNT, legacy route, NO connect:true. With STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SKIP_VERIFY=true the seeder never reads the signing secret, so we deliberately skip storing it.”
  Create Stripe client's webhook endpoints:
    • URL: "{public URL}/webhooks/stripe/{org's ID}/{env}"
    • enabled events: main Stripe event types, plus sync Stripe event types
  Give back an object with account and org: updated org.

| where isnotempty(['context.api_key_id'])
| summarize last_used = max(_time) by api_key_id = tostring(['context.api_key_id'])".

##### server/src/external/axiom/utils/resultUtils.ts
To get axiom match data — given result; gives back a list of Record:
  If result is set, result is an object, and result has a "matches" key:
    Give back everything in a list of match's data if match's data is set, otherwise an empty list, for each match in result's matches.
  Otherwise:
    Give back an empty list.

Axiom number from — given value:
  If value is a number, give back value.
  If value is text, give back value with /,/g replaced by "" as a number.
  Give back 0.

Axiom string from — given value:
  Give back value if value is text, otherwise "".

To get axiom result debug — given result:
  If result is missing or result is not an object, give back an object with result type: the type of result.
  Let record be result.
  Give back an object with:
    • dataset names: record's dataset names
    • match count: the number of record's matches if record's matches is a list (otherwise nothing)
    • result keys: the keys of result
    • status: record's status

##### server/src/external/aws/ecs/awsTaskIdentity.ts
“Identity of the ECS task this Node process is running in. Applies to server, workers, and cron — used by the blue-green gate (matching on `serviceArn`) and by log/trace tagging. - `serviceArn`: full ECS service ARN constructed at boot from the v4 metadata `Cluster` ARN + `ServiceName`. Stable across deploys, unique per FC blue/green service. **Sole gate signal.** - `imageSha`: from `FC_GIT_COMMIT_SHA` / `IMAGE_TAG` env. Used only for log/trace tagging (which deploy code is running) — NOT a gate signal, to avoid the stale-SHA failure mode. Both may be null on non-ECS hosts (Railway, local). The gate fails open when `serviceArn` is null (`hasAwsTaskIdentity()` returns false).”
Let aws task identity schema be a schema for an object with service arn and image sha.

Type AwsTaskIdentity: a z.infer.
Let cached identity start as nothing.
Let identity resolved mean false.
Let identity promise start as nothing.

“Build the full ECS service ARN from the v4 `Cluster` ARN + a service name. Returns null if the cluster ARN doesn't match the expected format. - Cluster ARN: arn:aws:ecs:<region>:<accountId>:cluster/<clusterName> - Service ARN: arn:aws:ecs:<region>:<accountId>:service/<clusterName>/<serviceName>”
To construct service arn — given cluster arn and service name; gives back text (or nothing):
  Match cluster arn (/^arn:aws:ecs:([^:]+):([^:]+):cluster\/(.+)$/) → match.
  If match is missing, give back nothing.
  Split match into (skip), region, account ID, and cluster name.
  Give back "arn:aws:ecs:{region}:{account ID}:service/{cluster name}/{service name}".

“Reads the ECS task metadata endpoint to resolve this task's identity. Cached for process lifetime — neither field changes for a running task.”
To resolve aws task identity — gives back an AwsTaskIdentity (async):
  If identity resolved is true and cached identity is set, give back cached identity.
  If identity promise is set, give back identity promise.
  Set identity promise to the result of a function that:
    Let image sha be the FC_GIT_COMMIT_SHA environment variable, or the IMAGE_TAG environment variable if that's empty, or nothing if that's empty.
    Let metadata uri be the ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI_V4 environment variable.
    Let service arn start as nothing.
    If metadata uri is set:
      Try the following:
        Fetch ("{metadata uri}/task" and signal: a timeout [AbortSignal] (2000)), and call the result response.
        If response's ok is set:
          Let body be response's JSON.
          If body's service name is text and body's cluster is text:
            Construct service arn (cluster arn: body's cluster and service name: body's service name), and put the result in service arn.
            If service arn is missing, warn "[awsTaskIdentity] Could not parse cluster ARN: {body's cluster}; gate will fail open".
        Otherwise:
          Warn "[awsTaskIdentity] ECS metadata returned {response's status}; gate will fail open".
      If anything fails (call the problem error):
        Warn "[awsTaskIdentity] ECS metadata fetch failed: {error's message if error is an error, otherwise error}; gate will fail open".
    Otherwise, if the NODE_ENV environment variable is "production":
      Warn "[awsTaskIdentity] ECS_CONTAINER_METADATA_URI_V4 unset in production — gate will fail open".
    Set cached identity to an object with service arn and image sha.
    Set identity resolved to true.
    Give back cached identity.
  Give back identity promise.

“Synchronous reader. Returns null until `resolveAwsTaskIdentity` resolves.”
To get aws task identity — gives back an AwsTaskIdentity (or nothing):
  Give back cached identity.

“True iff `serviceArn` is known. The gate uses this — when false, we're either on a non-ECS host (Railway, local) or ECS metadata didn't surface the data we need (rare). Either way → fail open.”
Has aws task identity? — gives back true/false:
  Give back whether cached identity's service arn is set.

“Fire-and-forget at module load so server, workers, and cron all get identity resolved without each entry point having to await explicitly.”
Nothing.

##### server/src/db/executePrepared.ts
Let dialect be a new pg dialect.

“DB spans in this service come only from `instrumentDrizzleClient` in initDrizzle — there is no @opentelemetry/instrumentation-pg. Because this helper goes straight to the pg Pool (see poolOf), Drizzle never sees the call and would emit nothing, so the span is raised by hand here. It deliberately impersonates @kubiks/otel-drizzle rather than taking its own identity. Three panels in the infra-health dashboard filter on `scope.name == '@kubiks/otel-drizzle'`, and spanMetrics.ts derives the `autumn.db.query.duration_ms` histogram's `operation` label from `span.name.slice("drizzle.".length)` — so a different tracer name makes these spans invisible, and a fixed span name silently forks the metric series.”
Get trace tracer ("@kubiks/otel-drizzle") → tracer.

“Leading keyword, for db.operation.”
Operation of — given text:
  Give back the first of trim text start split on /\s+/ in uppercase, or "UNKNOWN" if that's missing.

“Matches the library: `drizzle.${leading keyword, lowercased}`. getFullSubject compiles to text starting with WITH, so these land as `drizzle.with`.”
Span name for — given operation:
  Give back "drizzle.{operation in lowercase}".

“The library capped db.statement at 1000 chars plus a literal "...". Same shape here. Do NOT trim or normalise the text — the leading whitespace is what distinguishes the three getFullSubjectQuery variants in the dashboards.”
Let max statement chars be 1000.

To truncate statement — given text:
  If the number of text is more than max statement chars:
    Give back "{the first max statement chars of text}...".
  Otherwise:
    Give back text.

“Kept under PgBouncer's `max_prepared_statements` (200) so the pooler tracks every statement we mint rather than silently dropping the overflow.”
Let max distinct statements be 100.

“Statement name -> the exact SQL text it was first prepared with. node-postgres caches by name per connection and a name bound to two different texts poisons that connection, so we detect the collision here instead.”
Let prepared texts be an empty lookup table.

Let overflow warned mean false.

Is enabled?:
  Give back whether the PREPARED_STATEMENTS_DISABLED environment variable is not "true".

“node-postgres pool behind a Drizzle client, or null for drivers without one.”
Pool of — gives back a Pool (or nothing):
  Give back the client, or nothing if that's missing.

“Stable, content-addressed statement name. Same SQL always yields the same name across processes and restarts; edited SQL yields a new one.”
Statement name — given label and text:
  Give back "{label}_{the first 16 of update create hash ("sha1") (text)'s digest ("hex")}".

“Executes a Drizzle SQL fragment as a server-side **named** prepared statement. Postgres plans a named statement once per connection and reuses that plan; node-postgres only sends a named Parse when `name` is supplied, so without this every execution re-plans from scratch and PgBouncer's `max_prepared_statements` never sees the statement at all. Callers must keep their SQL text invariant across executions: bind values as parameters, and use `sql.param(list)` for arrays so the text doesn't grow a placeholder per element. `experiments/checkFullSubjectSqlStability.ts` guards this for getFullSubject. Falls back to an unprepared execution rather than failing the request if the driver exposes no pool, the shape count overflows, or preparation is disabled.”
To execute prepared — given query and label; gives back a list of TRow (async):
  Let pool be the pool of .
  If pool is missing or is not enabled, Execute (query), and give back the result.
  From dialect's SQL to query (query), take SQL (as text) and params.
  Let name be a statement name (label and text).
  Let known text be prepared texts' entry for name.
  If known text is missing:
    If prepared texts' size is at least max distinct statements:
      If overflow warned is false:
        Set overflow warned to true.
        Warn (with "[executePrepared] {max distinct statements} distinct statements reached; " plus "further shapes run unprepared. A query is likely emitting unstable SQL text." and label).
      Execute (query), and give back the result.
    Record text under name in prepared texts.
  Otherwise, if known text is not text:
    “Content-addressed names make this unreachable short of a SHA-1 collision; throwing beats poisoning every connection in the pool.”
    Fail with an error: "[executePrepared] name collision for "{name}"".
  Let operation be the operation of text.
  Start tracer active span, and give back the result:
    • the span name for operation
    • kind: span kind's client
    • a function of span that:
      Set span attributes:
        • db.system: "postgresql"
        • db.operation: operation
        • db.statement: truncate statement (text)
        • db.prepared statement name: name
        • autumn.db.label: label
      Try the following:
        “Untyped on purpose: pg constrains its generic to QueryResultRow, which is narrower than the row shapes callers of db.execute() use.”
        Query pool (name, text, and values: params), and call the result result.
        Set span attribute:
          • "db.response.returned_rows"
          • result's row count, or 0 if that's missing
        “The library set OK explicitly; leaving it UNSET flips status.code from "OK" to null in the dataset.”
        Set span status (code: span status code's ok).
        Give back result's rows.
      If anything fails (call the problem error):
        Record span exception (error).
        Set span status:
          • code: span status code's error
          • message: error's message if error is an error, otherwise error as text
        Fail with error.
      Either way, finally:
        End span.

“Statement names minted by this process — for diagnostics and tests.”
Prepared statement names — gives back a list of text:
  Give back a copy of prepared texts' keys.

##### server/src/db/pgHealthMonitor.ts
Enum PgHealth: Healthy and Degraded.

“Number of slow/failed queries within the window to trigger DEGRADED. Conservative: 20 slow queries in 60s is a strong signal, not a blip.”
Let failure threshold be 20.

“Tumbling window size for failure tracking (ms).”
Let failure window ms be 60,000.

“How often to probe the primary when DEGRADED (ms).”
Let probe interval ms be 5000.

“Probe query timeout (ms).”
Let probe timeout ms be 3000.

“How long the primary must be stable before switching back to HEALTHY (ms).”
Let recovery stability ms be 10,000.

Let state start as pg health's healthy.
Let probe interval start as nothing.
Let first probe success at start as nothing.
Let probe client start as nothing.

“Lightweight failure tracking — tumbling window with a counter instead of an array of timestamps. Two numbers, zero allocations per call.”
Let failure count start as 0.

Let window started at start as the current time.

To reset failure window — given now (default the current time):
  Set failure count to 0.
  Set window started at to now.

“Get the current DB health state.”
To get DB health — gives back a PgHealth:
  Give back state.

“Initialize the health monitor with a pg pool for probing. Call once at startup. The probe client should be the critical pool's raw client.”
To init pg health monitor — given client:
  Set probe client to client.
  Log "[PgHealthMonitor] Initialized" (with type).

“Record a successful query against the primary DB. No-op: recovery is driven by the probe, not by application queries.”
To record DB success:
  Do nothing.

“Record a slow or failed query against the primary DB. Called when a critical-pool query exceeds the latency threshold or throws.”
To record DB failure:
  If state is pg health's degraded, stop here.
  Let now be the current time.
  “Reset counter if the window has elapsed”
  If now minus window started at is after failure window ms:
    Set failure count to 0.
    Set window started at to now.
  Increase failure count by 1.
  If failure count is at least failure threshold, Switch to degraded.

To switch to degraded:
  If state is pg health's degraded, stop here.
  Set state to pg health's degraded.
  Log an error "[PgHealthMonitor] ENTERING DEGRADED MODE" (with type, failure count, window ms, and threshold count).
  Reset failure window.
  Start probe.

To switch to healthy:
  If state is pg health's healthy, stop here.
  Set state to pg health's healthy.
  Reset failure window.
  Set first probe success at to nothing.
  Log "[PgHealthMonitor] RECOVERED to HEALTHY" (with type).
  Stop probe.

  If probe interval is set or probe client is missing, stop here.
  Set first probe success at to nothing.
  Set interval, and put the result in probe interval:
    • a function that:
      If probe client is missing, stop here.
      Start with no timeout ID yet.
      Try the following:
        Run race [Promise] (a list of query probe client ("SELECT 1") and a promise).
        Let now be the current time.
        If first probe success at is missing:
          Set first probe success at to now.
          Log "[PgHealthMonitor] Probe succeeded, waiting for stability" (with type).
        If now minus first probe success at is at or after recovery stability ms, Switch to healthy.
      If anything fails:
        If first probe success at is set, warn "[PgHealthMonitor] Probe failed, resetting stability timer" (with type).
        Set first probe success at to nothing.
      Either way, finally:
        Clear timeout (timeout ID).
    • probe interval ms

To stop probe:
  If probe interval is set:
    Clear interval (probe interval).
    Set probe interval to nothing.

“Execute a query with automatic health tracking and replica fallback. - If DEGRADED and a replica exists, queries the replica instead. - Tracks latency on critical pool queries: >=10s counts as a failure signal. - Actual errors always count as failures.”
Let slow query threshold ms be 10,000.

To execute with health tracking — given query and use replica; gives back an object with result and used replica (async):
  Let is degraded mean state is pg health's degraded.
  Let used replica mean any of these is true:
    • is degraded and DB replica is set
    • use replica is true and DB replica is set
  Let effective DB be DB replica if used replica is true, otherwise DB.
  “Only track health for critical pool queries — prevents general pool saturation from falsely triggering degradation while critical pool is fine.”
  Let should track health mean is not degraded and DB is DB critical.
  Let query start be the current time.
  Try the following:
    Execute effective DB (query), and call the result result.
    If should track health:
      Let duration ms be the current time minus query start.
      If duration ms is at least slow query threshold ms:
        Record DB failure.
      Otherwise:
        Record DB success.
    Give back an object with result and used replica.
  If anything fails (call the problem error):
    “Connection drops (DB restart, upgrade) are transient — don't count toward degradation. They resolve on reconnect automatically.”
    If should track health and error is not connection drop, Record DB failure.
    Fail with error.

“Clean up the probe interval (for graceful shutdown).”
To shutdown pg health monitor:
  Stop probe.

“Get monitor state for debug endpoints.”
